Execution therefore requires choosing not only which low-level policy to run, but also which policy-specific goal should be given to it. We formulate this problem as policy orchestration: runtime selection of a policy-goal pair that is likely to remain feasible while tracking the planner target. We develop EPO, an energy-based policy orchestrator for modular goal-conditioned policy families. For each policy, EPO learns a composite energy over low-level goals, where lower energy corresponds to higher feasibility and more accurate target realization. At runtime, EPO refines each policy's goal and executes the lowest-energy policy-goal pair. Because energies are policy-specific, new policies can be incorporated by learning their own energy models, without retraining the existing policies or a centralized scheduler. In simulation, EPO improves the empirical precision-robustness trade-off by refining policy-specific goals before selectively switching among policies based on energy scores. We further demonstrate sim-to-real deployment of the same frozen policies and energy models on real humanoid loco-manipulation tasks. Project website: https://yewr.github.io/epo

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: Camera-Free Object Discovery and Interaction with GazeTags
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Vimal Mollyn, Chris Harrison
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: GazeTags enable camera-free, energy-efficient object discovery and interaction by using infrared signals aligned with head gaze, enhancing user awareness in wearable technology.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: We present GazeTags, a camera- and computer-vision-free approach for worn head-gaze object awareness. Our small electronic tags cost roughly \$2 each and can operate for more than a year on a coin cell battery. They work in concert with a user-worn device (smartglasses, hearables, etc.) that periodically emits a focused infrared signal aligned with the user's head direction. Only GazeTags within that narrow head-oriented beam wake and respond, providing their identity and optional payloads such as object state or live sensor readings. By avoiding cameras and computer vision pipelines, our approach is very energy efficient, able to operate continuously even in battery-constrained wearables, and sidesteps non-trivial privacy issues. We describe our hardware design, characterize our system performance and operating tradeoffs, and demonstrate how GazeTags can enable practical gaze-aware environments.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: Pixel-UMI: Learning Environment-Aware Whole-Body Manipulation from Sensorized Human Demonstrations
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Jason Jingzhou Liu, Tony Tao, Deepak Pathak, Ruslan Salakhutdinov
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: Pixel-UMI learns environment-aware whole-body manipulation policies from sensorized human demonstrations, addressing embodiment differences and improving performance through innovative retargeting and correction techniques.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Sensorized human demonstrations offer scalable data for mobile manipulation, but embodiment differences complicate policy learning. We present Pixel-UMI, a pipeline for learning environment-aware whole-body policies from human data. We first introduce Environment-Aware Retargeting (EAR), which combines reconstructed scene geometry with demonstrated head and gripper trajectories to determine robot posture and generate collision-aware joint and base targets. Delay-calibrated action assignment converts these trajectories into actions. However, kinematic differences can leave residual pose errors, creating viewpoint mismatches between human demonstrations and robot observations. We therefore introduce Retargeting-Error-Aware Masking (REAM), which uses these errors during training to reduce reliance on mismatched views at deployment. Finally, because estimated actions cannot fully capture contact-rich interactions, we collect on-policy human corrections through DAgger to improve performance. We evaluate Pixel-UMI on five challenging tasks spanning articulated-object manipulation, deformable-object handling, constrained-space reaching, whole-body collision avoidance, and contact-rich bimanual coordination, achieving 87.0% average task progress. Video results are available at https://pixel-robot.com/pixel-umi

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: Pixel: A Co-Designed Full-Stack Robot System for Learning General-Purpose Mobile Manipulation
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Tony Tao, Jason Jingzhou Liu, Ruslan Salakhutdinov, Deepak Pathak
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: Pixel is a co-designed full-stack robot system integrating hardware, data collection, control, and learning for effective general-purpose mobile manipulation.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: General-purpose mobile manipulation requires a combination of capable robot hardware, scalable demonstration collection, expressive whole-body control, and effective policy learning. Yet these components are often developed independently, creating mismatches that limit the capabilities of the complete system. We present Pixel, a co-designed full-stack system for learning general-purpose mobile manipulation. Pixel combines a low-cost wheeled humanoid with human-aligned kinematics and compliant grippers, multiple teleoperation and robot-free human data-collection interfaces, a unified whole-body controller, and a common policy learning pipeline across human and robot demonstrations. A hierarchical learning stack further enables language-conditioned visuomotor control and long-horizon task execution. We evaluate the system across hardware, data collection, and policy learning, and demonstrate mobile-manipulation behaviors requiring dexterity, active perception, navigation, and whole-body coordination. We hope that Pixel provides an integrated and extensible foundation for studying how robot hardware, data, control, and learning can be designed together for robot learning. More results at https://pixel-robot.com/pixel

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: Humans' ALMANAC: A Human Collaboration Dataset of Action-Level Mental Model Annotations for Agent Collaboration
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Jiaju Chen, Yuxuan Lu, Jiayi Su, Chaoran Chen, Songlin Xiao
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: The ALMANAC dataset provides action-level mental model annotations from human collaborations, enabling better evaluation and development of LLM agents for effective teamwork.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Recent advances in LLM agents have enabled complex cognitive capabilities, such as multi-step reasoning, planning, and tool use, that increasingly position these agents as collaborative partners in human workflows. Effective collaboration, however, requires collaborators to continuously maintain and align mental models of their own reasoning, partners' intentions, and shared goals during the collaborative process. Today's agents rarely develop such capabilities since they are primarily optimized for task completion rather than for maintaining the underlying mental models required for collaborative processes. Moreover, the community lacks authentic human collaboration data with action-level mental model annotations that could guide agents toward collaborative competence. To bridge this gap, we present ALMANAC, a dataset of Action-Level Mental model ANnotations for Agent Collaboration built from the Map Task, a classic dyadic routing task from social science. ALMANAC contains 2,987 collaboration actions, each paired with theory-informed mental model annotations that record the participants' self-reasoning, perceived partner intent, and perceived team goal. We benchmark six LLMs on predicting humans' next-turn behavior and mental models. Our results demonstrate ALMANAC's utility in evaluating models' ability to simulate human collaborative behaviors and infer their underlying mental models. The project page is available at https://human-agent-collab.hailab.io/almanac.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: RCR-Router: Efficient Role-Aware Context Routing for Multi-Agent LLM Systems with Structured Memory
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Jun Liu, Zhenglun Kong, Changdi Yang, Fan Yang, Tianqi Li
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: The RCR-Router optimizes multi-agent LLM systems by efficiently routing role-relevant context, reducing token usage by 35% and runtime by 38% while enhancing performance.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly organized into multi-agent systems for complex reasoning and decision-making tasks. However, scaling such systems can substantially increase inference cost, especially when multiple agents repeatedly process overlapping or role-irrelevant context. Many existing multi-agent frameworks focus on orchestration and role specialization, but still rely on full-context sharing or static context routing, leading to redundant token consumption, increased runtime, and inefficient memory utilization. We present \emph{Role-Conditioned Context Routing (RCR)}, an execution-time layer that allocates role-relevant shared-memory items to agents under token budgets. Given a structured shared memory and a set of role-specialized agents, RCR selectively routes task-relevant memory items to each agent according to its role, optional task-stage metadata, and token budget. RCR integrates role-conditioned relevance scoring, token-budgeted memory selection, and iterative memory updates to reduce redundant context exposure during multi-agent execution. Experiments on multi-hop QA, embodied reasoning (ALFWorld), and web-based decision-making (WebShop) show that RCR reduces token usage by 35\% on average and runtime by 38\% on average relative to Full-Context, while maintaining or improving task performance.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: CoEnv: Code-Driven Exploration in Real-to-Sim Digital Twins for Multi-Arm Manipulation
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Li Kang, Yutao Fan, Rui Li, Heng Zhou, Yiran Qin
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: CoEnv enables a coding agent to efficiently explore and refine multi-arm manipulation programs in a realistic digital twin, achieving higher success rates than previous methods.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: General-purpose coding agents can now write, debug, and refine entire robot programs, but only if they have somewhere to practice. Physical hardware is a poor practice ground: exploratory rollouts are slow to reset and, when several arms share a workspace, unsafe. Generic simulation benchmarks are safe but do not match the geometry, assets, or viewpoints of the workspace where the robot must actually work. We present CoEx (Code-driven Exploration), which lets the agent practice in an executable digital twin of its own deployment workspace. The twin is built by CoEnv, our real-to-sim framework, which reconstructs the physical scene from multi-view RGBD into a physics simulation. Inside it, a centralized code agent explores at the program level, writing a complete multi-arm program, running it in the twin, and refining it against grounded verification (privileged state checks, checkpoint predicates on risky steps, and adaptive viewpoints against inter-arm occlusion). Verified programs transfer to hardware through collision-checked deployment. On five real-world multi-arm tasks with up to three heterogeneous robots, CoEx reaches 70% average success, against 50% for the same system without the code agent (where a VLM must choose every primitive step by step), outperforms two prior VLM-planning frameworks, and produces verified episodes at 3.8-11.7x the ablated rate. Because every verified rollout is also a demonstration, exploration leaves reusable experience behind: a $π_{0.5}$ policy fine-tuned purely on 200 agent-generated rollouts reaches 100% and 70% real-robot success on two tasks, with no human demonstrations.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: MotorSense: A Video-EMG Dataset of Motoric Representations for Action Understanding
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Eadom Dessalene, Michael Maynord, Amir-Hossein Shahidzadeh, Botao He, Yasamin Tabatabaee
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: MotorSense introduces a large-scale dataset pairing egocentric video with EMG signals, enhancing action recognition and 3D reconstruction through sensorimotor alignment and outperforming traditional learning methods.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Computer vision models learn hand action only from its visual consequences, without access to the underlying embodied motor signals. We address this absence with MotorSense, the first large-scale paired egocentric video and surface electromyography (EMG) dataset. MotorSense pairs bimanual EMG bands with egocentric video and yields synchronized video, bimanual EMG and IMU, and audio across 100 hours of unscripted manipulation. EMG offers a powerful scalable alternative to manual annotation: it captures finger movement, hand configuration, and the forces exerted between hand and environment as a dense signal free of occlusion and labeler bias, whereas manual annotation is costly, subjective, and unreliable under occlusion. We use MotorSense to learn sensorimotor alignment, producing an organization of action that is shared across the visual and motoric spaces, through cross-modal pre-training between video and EMG. The resultant vision models are then transferred to downstream tasks that benefit from sensorimotor alignment: in this case, action recognition, 3D hand reconstruction, and 3D contact reconstruction. We further demonstrate a generative application in which EMG motor signals are used to condition a video diffusion model, yielding videos of fine-grained hand manipulation. Across four action-centric computer vision tasks and eight popular video datasets, we demonstrate that sensorimotor alignment provides a stronger foundation for visual representation learning than conventional self-supervised learning methods over video, outperforming every baseline across all tasks and datasets evaluated.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: Design and Validation of a Robotic Knee Exoskeleton with Musculoskeletal Simulation-Derived Biological Torque Control
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Rajiv V. Joshi, Jimin An, Ilseung Park, Dawit Lee, Inseung Kang
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: This paper presents an open-source knee exoskeleton utilizing a simulation-derived biological torque controller, enabling effective assistance without requiring device-specific data collection.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Data-driven controllers have enabled lower-limb robotic exoskeletons to adapt assistance to the user across many tasks. A leading example is biological torque control, which estimates the user's own joint moment from onboard sensors and assists in proportion to that estimate. However, its estimators are trained on data recorded with the target device, so deploying the controller on new hardware requires collecting new data. Existing open-source efforts release hardware, software, or controllers separately, so this data collection must still be repeated on the assembled device. Here, we present an open-source knee exoskeleton, built from off-the-shelf components and widely available fabrication tools, with a biological torque controller derived entirely from simulation. A muscle-driven imitation policy reproduces squatting motions from an open biomechanics dataset, and the resulting knee moments are distilled into an estimator that uses only onboard sensors, so no training data are recorded on the device. In seven able-bodied participants, assistance reduced peak biological knee extension moment by 21.5% and peak vastus medialis activation by 26.7% during squatting, relative to squatting without the exoskeleton (p<0.05). Our results demonstrate that a biological torque controller derived from simulation can transfer to physical hardware without device-specific data collection. Because the hardware and training pipeline are released together, research groups can train and compare knee exoskeleton controllers on shared hardware without additional data collection overhead.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: Aligning Autoresearch: Co-Improvement between Agents and Humans
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Tianjian Li, Chuanyang Jin, Seungone Kim, Tong Chen, John Hoffman
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: The paper explores co-improvement between autoresearch agents and humans, emphasizing the necessity of human interaction for effective AI research and proposing methods to enhance alignment and communication.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Autoresearch agents can now attempt long-horizon AI research end-to-end, i.e., self-improvement. However, best results are still obtained by research agents interacting with human researchers, and improving AI's ability to perform this co-research will only reinforce this effect---a process termed co-improvement (Weston and Foerster, 2025). Further, aligning with human expectations is likely a safer path for research agents, especially given recent agent reward hacking phenomena (OpenAI, 2026b). In this work we address these issues in four ways: (i) we empirically study the role of humans in directing autoresearch agents, focusing on the domain of benchmark creation, and find humans still play a pivotal role particularly in the ideation phase; (ii) we also develop a benchmark, HackBench, that shows current autoresearch agents are not aligned and are unable to achieve hack localization sufficiently; (iii) we present a method to train agents for improved human interaction by using human simulators as a proxy during reinforcement learning (RL); and finally (iv) we develop a method to improve model text generation, and hence agent communication, by RL with rubrics aligned with human experts. Together, our training and evaluation recipes provide a path toward more capable and aligned (co-)research agents.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: GOFish: Full Field-of-View Gaussian Splatting and Mesh Extraction
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Allen Tu, Meher Gitika Karumuri, Shifan Zhu, Hailing Wang, Yen-Liang Lin
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: GOFish introduces a novel 3D Gaussian Splatting method for fisheye images, enabling full 360° rendering and mesh extraction, outperforming previous techniques in photorealism and accuracy.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Robots, autonomous vehicles, and consumer 360° cameras use fisheye lenses for wide fields of view (FoVs). Simulation-ready digital twins require photorealistic rendering across the full FoV and an aligned collision mesh. However, prior fisheye Gaussian Splatting methods only rasterize up to 180° and do not produce meshes, while Gaussian surface reconstruction methods assume pinhole training images. We present GOFish, the first 3D Gaussian Splatting surface reconstruction method to train directly on fisheye images, rasterize FoVs beyond 180°, and extract an aligned mesh from the same scene. Calibrated densification recovers the surface across the entire FoV, while Calibrated Mip Filtering and Wide-Angle Appearance Modeling keep pixel blur and lens falloff out of the scene and mesh. Across the 200° FIORD and 205° FullCircle benchmarks, GOFish improves PSNR over the best prior method by 2.28 and 1.97 dB, respectively. It also outperforms fisheye rendering baselines within their own FoVs and achieves the highest mesh F-score on FIORD and the main ScanNet++ set. Together, the Gaussian scene and mesh form a LiDAR-free, simulation-ready digital twin that renders in real time, ray traces the full FoV, and provides collision geometry.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: 3DCodeEdit: Benchmarking Instruction-Guided 3D Program Editing
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Binjie Wang, Xinran Zhao, Shoubin Yu, Xiang Li, Silong Yong
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: The paper presents 3DCodeEdit, a benchmark for instruction-guided 3D program editing, revealing low success rates in model performance and the potential of multi-turn feedback to improve outcomes.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Language models increasingly create 3D content through code, with practical workflows often relying on editing existing programs rather than regenerating them, for speed and precise control. Such edits require understanding what a program builds and foreseeing how a change reshapes it, yet prior benchmarks mostly evaluate generation or simple edits against a reference. In this paper, we introduce 3DCodeEdit, a benchmark of 2,592 instruction-guided editing tasks over 108 Blender programs that construct objects entirely in code. Its edits range from parameter to structural changes, style redesign, and scene composition, and are judged from renders against human-reviewed checklists. Across 17 models, the average success rate is only 37%, and even the strongest models complete fewer than 60% of structural and style edits. As models become more capable, their failures shift to geometric foresight, where the code runs but builds the wrong shape. We therefore study whether multi-turn feedback can compensate for this missing foresight. Feedback from a separate reviewer model that describes how the renders differ from the request helps most, more than maximum reasoning effort or an agent harness, and can let a 27B model surpass the single-shot rate of a 2.8T-parameter model.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: Value Function-Guided MPPI for Hierarchical Planning and Control in Off-Road Autonomous Navigation
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Anoushka Alavilli, Raymond Song, Guanya Shi, Jeff Schneider
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: This paper presents a bidirectional hierarchical planning and control framework using a value function-guided MPPI for improved off-road autonomous navigation without explicit cost maps.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Autonomous navigation in off-road terrain is commonly achieved using hierarchical control and planning architectures that rely on explicit cost maps and one-way information flow from a high-level planner to a low-level controller, decoupling planning from the true execution cost experienced during control. We propose a hierarchical planning and control framework in which information flows bidirectionally, allowing the low-level controller to guide trajectory selection at the planning level. The highest level of the hierarchy is a Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control-style planner that determines optimal trajectories and passes these waypoints to a pretrained low-level reinforcement learning (RL) controller. Rather than drawing from an explicit cost map, our MPPI planner leverages the value function of the RL controller as an implicit cost representation. In this formulation, MPPI serves as a trajectory exploration mechanism, while the low-level controller's value function guides the search. To account for the distribution shift seen by the value function between training and evaluation, we propose an online policy evaluation process that adapts the value function to unseen driving experiences, and we demonstrate this adaptation in unseen off-road simulation environments. We evaluate our approach in a high-fidelity off-road driving simulator across a range of challenging terrain conditions and compare its performance against a baseline MPPI controller. The results demonstrate that our method achieves safer and more effective navigation to goal locations while eliminating the need for explicit cost maps and enabling tighter coupling between planning and control.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: UMI-Live for In-The-Wild Bimanual Robotics Data Collection
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Govind Velamoor, Adrian Lin, Sam Jung, Spencer Mateega, Brandon Y. Yang
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: UMI-Live is an open-source bimanual robotics system enabling in-the-wild data collection without external calibration, validated through successful task demonstrations and released datasets.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) devices allow human experts to demonstrate tasks for robot learning without teleoperating physical robots. Using these demonstrations as training data still requires a consistent hardware setup, calibration, and data processing. We present UMI-Live, a full-stack open-source bimanual UMI system for in-the-wild data collection. We design our custom UMI-Live hardware to integrate camera and LiDAR--inertial sensing, onboard compute, and power, without external tracking equipment or calibration within the collection environment. We implement a simple user interface for recording data while an asynchronous pipeline performs parallel SLAM reconstruction and publishes training-ready datasets. We also release software that supports dual-YAM teleoperation and VLA policy training and inference. We validate UMI-Live data quality by fine-tuning $π_{0.5}$ and MolmoAct2, achieving success rates of 10/10 and 8/10, respectively on a bimanual pick-and-place task. Furthermore, we release 40 hours of UMI-Live data across three tasks, and complete hardware designs, software, and reproduction guides at our $\href{https://umi-live.github.io/}{\text{project website}}$.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: Gym-Anything for Robotics: Scaling physical simulations with digital agents
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Pranjal Aggarwal, Sean Welleck
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: The paper presents Gym-Anything for Robotics, a framework enabling coding agents to autonomously create diverse and realistic robotics simulations, enhancing training for embodied AI models.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Realistic, fast robotics simulations could enable large-scale training of embodied AI models that transfer to the real world. However, despite decades of progress, available simulations cover only a narrow range of real-world tasks and physical phenomena. The core bottleneck is that creating better simulations requires significant expert effort and therefore does not scale. To address this, we introduce Gym-Anything for Robotics, a framework in which coding agents create realistic robotics simulations. Our core insight is that simulation creation is a coding agent task, so improvements in coding agents translate directly into richer and more faithful simulations. We select simulations based on U.S. GDP data to cover economically valuable physical work, define what makes a good simulation and a good task, and develop an adversarial creation-audit loop that checks each simulation and task against these definitions. Using this pipeline, we build RoboWorld, a set of 25 simulations with 25 test and 175 training RL environments of varying difficulty. Even the best frontier models fail on every RoboWorld test task, achieving an average reward of only 0.06. Building on RoboWorld, we introduce several new ways for frontier models to improve, including in-context learning across repeated attempts, a privileged teacher that reads the simulator state and teaches a student in context, self-assisted learning from the model's own privileged experience, and code policies that generate demonstrations across varied scenes to train vision-language-action models (VLAs) such as $π_{0.5}$. Each of these substantially improves performance. We release our pipeline, RL environments, and benchmark to facilitate future research. Code and data are available at https://gym-anything.github.io/robotics

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: SymAnt: Grounding Long-Horizon Action Anticipation with Adaptable Symbolic Priors
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Fnu Aryan, Yaqi Xie, Joseph Campbell, Woojun Kim, Kwonjoon Lee
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: SymAnt integrates neural networks with symbolic reasoning to effectively anticipate long-horizon actions from brief observations, allowing for user-editable predictions without retraining.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: As robots and intelligent systems increasingly interact with humans, they must anticipate long sequences of future actions from only brief observations. While purely neural models typically require extensive observations to predict future actions and remain difficult to interpret and adjust, symbolic priors offer a structured alternative. To this end, we introduce SymAnt, a novel neuro-symbolic approach that unifies the expressiveness of neural networks with the structured reasoning of scene and knowledge graphs. Given a short video, SymAnt performs a joint-search over both graphs to construct a symbolic context, enabling unified reasoning over spatial relationships, object attributes, affordances, and associated actions. This symbolic context serves as a prior for an iterative refinement process that progressively generates and improves the sequence of future actions. By grounding predictions in symbolic context, SymAnt anticipates long-horizon actions from short observation windows in a parameter-efficient manner, while enabling users to directly edit the underlying knowledge to adjust predictions without further training. Through our experiments, we demonstrate the effectiveness of SymAnt, particularly when only short observation contexts are available, across five diverse datasets: Breakfast, 50 Salads, EPIC-KITCHENS, EGTEA Gaze+, and Assembly101.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: RPT*: Global Planning with Probabilistic Terminals for Target Search in Complex Environments
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Yunpeng Lyu, Chao Cao, Ji Zhang, Howie Choset, Zhongqiang Ren
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: The paper presents RPT*, a novel approach for solving the HPP-PT problem, optimizing target search paths in complex environments by incorporating probabilistic terminal locations and dynamic programming.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Routing problems such as Hamiltonian Path Problem (HPP), seek a path to visit all the vertices in a graph while minimizing the path cost. This paper studies a variant, HPP with Probabilistic Terminals (HPP-PT), where each vertex has a probability representing the likelihood that the robot's path terminates there, and the objective is to minimize the expected path cost. HPP-PT arises in target object search, where a mobile robot must visit all candidate locations to find an object, and prior knowledge of the object's location is expressed as vertex probabilities. While routing problems have been studied for decades, few of them consider uncertainty as required in this work. The challenge lies not only in optimality ordering the vertices, as in standard HPP, but also in handling history dependency: the expected path cost depends on the order in which vertices were previously visited. This makes many existing methods inefficient or inapplicable. To address the challenge, we propose a search-based approach RPT* with solution optimality guarantees, which leverages dynamic programming in a new state space to bypass the history dependency and novel heuristics to speed up the computation. Building on RPT*, we design a Hierarchical Autonomous Target Search (HATS) system that combines RPT* with either Bayesian filtering for lifelong target search with noisy sensors, or autonomous exploration to find targets in unknown environments. Experiments in both simulation and real robot show that our approach can naturally balance between exploitation and exploration, thereby finding targets more quickly on average than baseline methods.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: Goal2Pixel: Grounding Goals to Pixels for Vision-Language Navigation
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Muyi Bao, Yuxin Cai, Hang Xu, Zongtai Li, Jinxi He
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: Goal2Pixel introduces a pixel-based navigation paradigm for vision-language models, enhancing efficiency and performance in long-horizon navigation by grounding goals to navigable pixels instead of predicting actions.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have become a common foundation for vision-and-language navigation in continuous environments (VLN-CE). Yet most VLM-based methods cast navigation as low-level action prediction, an interface that is ambiguous, tied to short-horizon motion primitives, and inefficient due to repeated VLM querying. We propose Goal2Pixel, a pure pixel-based paradigm that reformulates VLN-CE as navigable pixel grounding. Rather than predicting actions, Goal2Pixel uses the image plane as a unified spatial interface between VLM reasoning and robot motion: the model predicts a visible navigable pixel, which is back-projected into a 3D waypoint for forward navigation. Non-forward actions are encoded by auxiliary left/right/bottom regions for turning and stopping. To support long-horizon navigation, we propose ViKeyMem, a visibility-aware keyframe memory, achieving a favorable performance-efficiency trade-off while reducing training cost by over 50%. To adapt pretrained VLMs to navigable pixel grounding, we introduce semantic embeddings and coordinate-aware auxiliary losses. Among methods trained without external data, Goal2Pixel achieves competitive state-of-the-art performance on R2R-CE and RxR-CE. On R2R-CE Val-Unseen, it achieves 54.1% SR and 52.5% SPL with only 7.75 VLM calls per episode. Compared with direct action prediction, Goal2Pixel improves SR by 21.2 percentage points while requiring 6 times fewer VLM calls. Project Page: https://baobao0926.github.io/Goal2Pixel/.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: From Grasps to Dexterity: Large-Scale Grasp Pretraining for Dexterous Manipulation
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Ying Yuan, Xinyu Liu, Sriram Krishna, David Held
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: This paper demonstrates that large-scale grasp datasets can effectively pretrain controllers for dexterous manipulation tasks, significantly enhancing performance in articulated tool use.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Large-scale dexterous grasp datasets encode rich priors over hand-object interaction, but their use has largely been confined to grasp generation and pick-and-place manipulation. We study whether such data can instead support functional dexterity in articulated tool use, where a robot must acquire a tool, maintain contact, and operate its functional moving parts. We adapt a hierarchical imitation learning framework that combines high-level hand sub-goal prediction with a low-level goal-conditioned controller. We construct a 355k-trajectory grasp-pretraining dataset from large-scale dexterous grasp annotations and use it to pretrain the low-level controller. The controller is then fine-tuned on downstream task demonstrations. To evaluate this setting, we introduce DexCraft, a simulation benchmark with six articulated tool-use tasks requiring coordinated finger motion. Across simulation and real-world experiments, our approach outperforms end-to-end diffusion policy baselines and hierarchical policies trained from scratch. In the real world, it improves full-task success by 33.3 percentage points over DP3. These results show that grasp datasets can serve not only as resources for grasp synthesis, but also as scalable pretraining data for contact-rich dexterous manipulation. Videos are shown on https://yingyuan0414.github.io/grasp2dexterity/ .

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: Executable Archaeology of Programs That Model Programming: Reanimating the Heuristic Compiler (1961) and KBEmacs (1984)
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Jeff Shrager, Kent M. Pitman, Mia Golec
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: This paper reanimates and compares Herbert Simon's Heuristic Compiler and KBEmacs, revealing shared programming theories absent in modern AI coding assistants.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Early AI programs were often also theories of how people think, and programs that wrote programs were, in part, theories of how people program. Here we report on the reanimation of two such programs that offer two seemingly different theories of programming and were developed for quite different purposes. The first, Herbert Simon's Heuristic Compiler (1961), was an experimental model of programming as problem-solving, applying the means-ends analysis methods of the General Problem Solver to investigate the nature of the programming task. The second, KBEmacs (1984), was a working prototype of an intelligent programming assistant developed by MIT's Programmer's Apprentice project, built on the view that expert programmers recognize and combine familiar patterns, or "cliches." It let a programmer build up programs by combining cliches through a stylized English command language. We approach both through the methodology of Executable Archaeology, the study of historical computational systems by running their original code, a process we call "reanimation." Our reanimation of the Heuristic Compiler reproduces the compiled code appearing in Simon's 1963 paper, and our reanimation of KBEmacs reproduces the SQRT sequence of its December 1984 self-test. Examined side by side, the two theories turn out to have much in common: the Heuristic Compiler also works by adapting existing routines, and Simon later argued that search alone requires a large body of programming knowledge. To highlight the reflexivity of this project, we deliberately used a modern AI-assisted programming tool, Anthropic's Claude Code (Opus 5.5), to carry out much of the detailed reanimation work, building on a significant base of existing software. The explicit, executable theories of programming that both systems embodied are largely absent from today's far more capable AI coding assistants.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: CARD: Contact-Anchored Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Cunxi Dai, Botao He, Francois R Hogan, Wei Pan, Rao Fu
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: CARD is a novel framework that enhances robotic dexterity by retargeting human demonstrations while preserving essential contact dynamics and improving task success rates significantly.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Humans are dexterous, but traditional data collection paradigms such as teleoperation, kinesthetic teaching, and wearable exoskeletons force humans to act through the robot embodiment, bottlenecking their dexterity. Retargeting can avoid this. However, existing methods purely translate kinematics and ignore the real-world contact dynamics essential for task success. We present CARD: Contact-Anchored Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation, a simulator and object-free framework that retargets human demonstrations to robot actions by explicitly preserving contact force targets. CARD unifies human data sources including video, motion capture, and tactile gloves via a shared hand--contact representation and generates explicit contact force targets in addition to kinematics. To maintain these contact targets during hardware open-loop replay, CARD also introduces a tactile tracking controller. For video which does not contain an explicit tactile source, we present Vid-HACO, our video-to-contact model that sets a new state of the art. Across our video, glove, motion-capture data and the GRAB dataset, CARD maintains contact on $43$--$78\%$ of contact frames, while kinematic and object-aware retargeting methods maintain contact on $<10\%$ and $22.5\%$ of the frames respectively. Further, integrating our formulation into physics-based retargeting improves strict task success from 12\% to 32\% on GRAB dataset. Finally, we show that our tactile tracker is critical to reproduce demonstrated forces during hardware replay. These results establish that contact preservation via CARD is a scalable interface for transferring human dexterity to robots.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: CASEL: Consequence-Aware Selective Execution for Reliable Long-Horizon Tool-Using Agents
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Yanyan Zhang, Fei Shen, Ting Yan, Hao Zhang
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: CASEL is a model-agnostic runtime policy that optimizes tool-using agents' execution strategies by minimizing harmful side effects through consequence-aware decision-making.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Tool-using language agents increasingly modify external systems, yet most runtime safeguards allocate scrutiny by generic uncertainty scores or coarse mutation heuristics. We introduce CASEL (Consequence-Aware Selective Execution Layer), a model-agnostic runtime allocation policy that combines calibrated failure probability, state-dependent consequence, reversibility, ambiguity, and evidence freshness to choose, for each proposed tool call, among direct execution, verification, sandboxing, clarification, approval, and abstention by minimizing a per-mode cost. We formalize direct execution as selective prediction and state and test the validity conditions of a finite-sample threshold and a trajectory risk ledger. In a controlled simulation over 20 seeds with 120,000 test actions each, in which every method has the same intervention menu and the same compute cost, CASEL reduces harmful-side-effect trajectories from 14.75 percent for an uncertainty-ranked gate to 7.02 percent and mean normalized harm from 0.184 to 0.123. A gate ranked by the product of failure probability and consequence reaches similar harm (5.82 percent, 0.120) but sends 45 percent more actions to human approval, and removing reversibility-aware routing raises the rate to 15.53 percent. A trajectory-level risk budget, in contrast, increases harm at equal cost (11.82 percent). Intervention effectiveness is assumed, not measured: the results rank allocation rules under the simulator's assumptions and do not establish deployment effectiveness.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: Multi-robot Learning-based Informative Path Planning Using Spatio-Temporal Gaussian Process Kalman Filter
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Muqing Cao, Yunwoo Lee, Junbin Yuan, Lorenzo Schenk, Sebastian Scherer
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: This paper presents a spatio-temporal GP-Kalman filtering framework for decentralized multi-robot informative path planning, enhancing target monitoring under uncertainty and communication constraints.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Multi-robot informative path planning (IPP) for persistent target monitoring requires robots to reason about spatial uncertainty, temporal evolution, and practical sensing and communication constraints. Recent learning-based multi-robot IPP methods use Gaussian Processes (GPs) for target uncertainty, but often rely on simplified sensing models and centralized belief updates. We propose a grid-based spatio-temporal GP-Kalman filtering framework for learning-based multi-robot IPP. Instead of maintaining one GP per target, we represent anonymous target presence as a single latent field over a discrete workspace grid. The proposed recursive update assimilates footprint-level camera measurements and supports arbitrary fields of view and range-dependent noise. A GP-derived temporal process update inflates uncertainty over time to account for moving targets. For decentralized deployment, each robot maintains its own mapper and exchanges fixed-size belief summaries rather than raw measurements. Received beliefs are fused using diagonal covariance intersection to remain conservative under unknown inter-robot correlations. We integrate the mapper with a reinforcement-learning policy for graph-based neighbor selection. In simulation, the centralized deployment improves target visitation and attains about 20% lower posterior target uncertainty than learning-based and classical auction/coverage baselines, a large share of which stems from the belief representation itself. A real-world two-UAV experiment demonstrates transfer to outdoor multi-robot search over a large field (>7000 m^2). Code is available at https://github.com/caomuqing/multirobot-ipp.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: Gym-Anything-RT: Scaling Real-Time Environments for Vision-Language Agents
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Pranjal Aggarwal, Sean Welleck
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: Gym-Anything-RT introduces a framework for evaluating vision-language agents' real-time interaction capabilities through 100 generated minigames, revealing significant performance gaps under time constraints.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: AI agents have made substantial progress in domains where they have a non-trivial amount of time to deliberate between actions, such as mathematics, software engineering, and performing tasks on desktop applications. It is less clear how such models fare in settings that demand real-time interaction, such as playing a video game or operating a physical device. In these settings, the environment state may evolve as the agent is reasoning, or even as the underlying model is performing a forward pass. To gain insight into the real-time interaction capabilities of vision-language agents, we introduce Gym-Anything-RT. Our key idea is to construct visual minigames that demand a portfolio of capabilities required for interactive real-time settings. Gym-Anything-RT uses an agentic pipeline to automatically generate such environments based on a taxonomy of six capabilities required for real-time interaction, including the ability to perceive the environment and act under an evolving environment state. A key feature of Gym-Anything-RT is that it allows for controlled comparison of real-time interaction capabilities: we can run the same minigame in real time, or pause or slow down the environment to relax the requirement for real-time actions. We use Gym-Anything-RT to construct 100 real-time minigames and evaluate AI agents on them. We find large capability gaps in real-time interaction. For example, GPT-6 Astra (xHigh) achieves a pass rate of only 9.0% on the real-time minigames, which rises to 75.0% when the environment is paused. We also identify intriguing behaviors by the most powerful frontier agents: for instance, when given the ability to write code, these agents write code that bypasses the need to perceive and act in real time. We publicly release Gym-Anything-RT and the generated minigames to spur further research on AI agents in real-time interactive settings.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: Emergent Neural Automaton Policies: Learning Symbolic Structure from Visuomotor Trajectories
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Yiyuan Pan, Xusheng Luo, Hanjiang Hu, Peiqi Yu, Changliu Liu
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: ENAP introduces a neuro-symbolic imitation learning framework that effectively learns task structures from visuomotor trajectories, enhancing sample efficiency and interpretability in long-horizon robotic tasks.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Scaling robot learning to long-horizon tasks remains a formidable challenge. While end-to-end policies often lack the structural priors needed for effective long-term reasoning, traditional neuro-symbolic methods rely heavily on hand-crafted symbolic priors. We introduce ENAP (Emergent Neural Automaton Policy), a neuro-symbolic imitation learning framework in which a bi-level policy adaptively emerges from visuomotor demonstrations. Specifically, we employ adaptive clustering and an extension of the L* algorithm to learn the task structure from demonstrations as a Mealy state machine, which serves as an interpretable high-level planner capturing latent task modes. This discrete structure then guides a low-level reactive residual network to learn precise continuous control via behavior cloning (BC). By explicitly modeling discrete transitions and continuous residuals, ENAP achieves sample efficiency and interpretability without task-specific labels. Experiments on complex manipulation and long-horizon tasks show that ENAP outperforms state-of-the-art end-to-end vision-language-action (VLA) policies by up to 27% in low-data regimes. ENAP can also distill task structure from the latent space of a pre-trained VLA, surpassing it on CALVIN benchmark with 39% fewer parameters (Fig. 1).

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: Not an Accident: Exploiting Safety Filter Inadequacy in Humanoid Robots
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Tiffany Bao, Shangtao Li, Yifan Sun, Mengwen He, Bowei Li
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: This paper reveals that inadequately configured safety filters in humanoid robots can be exploited through normal interactions, leading to potential safety violations, and introduces SIREN, a tool for identifying such vulnerabilities.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: As humanoid robots move from research laboratories toward deployment in human-centered environments such as homes, hospitals, and warehouses, safe operation around nearby people and objects becomes a fundamental requirement. Safety filters have emerged as a promising technique to address this challenge by providing mathematical guarantees that generated control actions do not result in collisions. This paper shows that these guarantees hold only when the safety parameters are configured correctly. However, correct parameter configurations are task- and environment-specific, and no general method exists to determine them across diverse deployments. As a result, safety filters shipped with humanoid robots can fail after deployment in specific scenarios. We show that attackers can exploit these failures through only normal user interactions without any additional privileges or capabilities. To demonstrate this risk, we present goal insertion attacks and develop SIREN, an automated tool that identifies vulnerable inserting goals for a given task and environment. Experimental results show that SIREN identifies attacks in all vulnerable scenarios in the SPARK dataset. Compared with a baseline approach, SIREN discovers three times as many attacks. We also show that SIREN is able to generate attacks against a real humanoid and cause it to collide while executing tasks. These results demonstrate that current safety filters introduce exploitable vulnerabilities that can cause safety violations, which reveals that existing safety mechanisms can themselves become a source of safety risk for humanoid robots.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: TravSUITE: Traversability via Self-Supervised, Uncertainty-Aware IRL and Terrain Estimation
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Samuel Triest, Amirreza Shaban, David D. Fan, Wenshan Wang, Sebastian Scherer
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: TravSUITE is a self-supervised, uncertainty-aware system that enhances off-road robot navigation by efficiently mapping terrain and predicting traversability without annotations, achieving significant performance improvements.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Traversability analysis in off-road settings remains a fundamental challenge for mobile robots. Key difficulties include constructing an accurate and expressive local map from multimodal sensor data, and using the map to design traversability rules that yield desirable navigation behavior. Importantly, this system must be resilient to the limited sensing regime brought about by complex environments and high speeds. In this paper, we present TravSUITE, a traversability system suitable for high-speed navigation in off-road environments. TravSUITE consists of two major components: 1) an efficient voxel mapper that leverages visual foundation models (VFMs) to build a rich geometric-semantic local map from streams of on-board sensor data, and 2) a unified neural network that jointly predicts traversability-relevant quantities in bird's eye view (BEV), including geometry, semantics, speed and cost. Our training strategy is entirely annotation-free and self-supervised, leveraging tasks such as map inpainting and inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) to learn both map representations and traversability. We perform a thorough ablation study and comparison to state-of-the-art approaches, and the results indicate that cost learning and auxiliary inpainting each contribute significantly to planning quality, and their combination is critical for achieving state-of-the-art performance in off-road path planning. We also design a simple risk adaptation mechanism to leverage our method's uncertainty estimates at deploy-time, and demonstrate that a combination of inpainting and risk estimation can result in 80% fewer navigation errors and 5% faster autonomous traversal speeds in real-world hardware experiments.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: Beyond Imitation: Reinforcement Learning-Based Sim-Real Co-Training for VLA Models
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Liangzhi Shi, Shuaihang Chen, Feng Gao, Yinuo Chen, Kang Chen
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: The paper presents an RL-based sim-real co-training framework that enhances vision-language-action models' real-world performance and generalization through interactive simulation and reinforcement learning.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Simulation offers a scalable and low-cost way to enrich vision-language-action (VLA) training, reducing reliance on expensive real-robot demonstrations. However, most sim-real co-training methods rely on supervised fine-tuning (SFT), which treats simulation as a static source of demonstrations and does not exploit large-scale closed-loop interaction. Consequently, real-world gains and generalization are often limited. In this paper, we propose an RL-based sim-real Co-training (RL-Co) framework that leverages interactive simulation while preserving real-world capabilities. Our method follows a generic two-stage design: we first warm-start the policy with SFT on a mixture of real and simulated demonstrations, then fine-tune it with reinforcement learning in simulation while adding an auxiliary supervised loss on real-world data to anchor the policy and mitigate catastrophic forgetting. We evaluate our framework on four real-world tabletop manipulation tasks using two representative VLA architectures, OpenVLA and $π_{0.5}$, and observe consistent improvements over real-only fine-tuning and SFT-based co-training, including +24% real-world success on OpenVLA and +20% on $π_{0.5}$. Beyond higher success rates, RL co-training yields stronger generalization to unseen task variations and substantially improved real-world data efficiency, providing a practical and scalable pathway for leveraging simulation to enhance real-robot deployment.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: Training Small Language Models for Transferable Tool Selection
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Zhaoyi Zhou, Akshayaa Magesh, Jeongyeol Kwon, Artem Kuriksha, Daniel Jiang
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: The paper demonstrates that a small, open language model can be effectively trained via reinforcement learning for transferable tool selection, outperforming larger models in diverse domains.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: As LLM agents operate over corpora of more than ten thousand tools, selecting the right tool for a complex multi-step user instruction becomes a central bottleneck. Tool descriptions cannot all fit in context, and relevance-based retrievers only rank tools without knowing which are actually needed. Recent work instead leverages proprietary commercial LLMs like Claude or ChatGPT to drive a retriever, decomposing the instruction and selecting over retrieved candidates. We show that a small, open model can be trained via reinforcement learning to perform the same functionality. On ToolBench, a Qwen3-8B model post-trained with our recipe outperforms Llama-4-Maverick (402B). In addition, the trained model transfers directly to different retrievers and generalizes to new tool corpora in different domains.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: Progress Probes $P^2$: Lightweight Runtime Monitoring for Vision-Language-Action Models
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Atiksh Bhardwaj, Edward W. Duan, Junwon Seo, Prithwish Dan, Wei-Chiu Ma
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: The paper presents a method using internal activations of Vision-Language-Action models for lightweight runtime monitoring, outperforming traditional external model-based approaches in detecting task failures.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can perform diverse manipulation tasks directly from visual observations and natural language instructions, but they remain prone to mistakes and unpredictable failures. Deploying these policies without continuous human supervision will require robust runtime monitors that detect when the policy has gone off-course. Existing monitors use external foundation models, such as vision-language models (VLMs) to supervise the policy, introducing significant complexity and computational cost for monitoring at runtime. In this work, we investigate an alternate approach: \textit{can a VLA's own internal activations provide the information needed to monitor its execution?} Our method trains linear probes on policy activations from demonstrations to estimate progress, then flags executions that deviate from expected progress. In experiments with the open-source VLA $π_{0.5}$ and across simulated and real-world manipulation tasks, this approach is competitive with or outperforms VLM-based monitors in task failure detection, as well as methods which require failure data for training. These findings suggest that simple probes of VLA internals can be used to develop reliable runtime monitors, opening a path toward building policies that can act reliably and monitor their execution without external foundation models.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: BrickWright: Agentic Creation of Physically Feasible Brick Builds
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Ava Pun, Kevin Dai, Sally Chen, Maxwell Jones, Ruixuan Liu
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: BrickWright is a framework that enables agents to generate 100% physically feasible LEGO builds from prompts by using a specialized assembly API and validator.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Frontier coding agents are becoming increasingly adept at 3D modeling. Yet, they still face challenges when building objects meant to be assembled in the physical world, often creating invalid assemblies with floating, colliding, or disconnected parts. We argue that providing agents with tools for assembling builds and verifying their physical feasibility is sufficient for them to produce physically valid assemblies that still adhere to input prompts. Focusing on the domain of LEGO brick builds, we present BrickWright, a framework for generating physically feasible brick builds from text or image prompts using pre-trained agents, where a build is physically feasible if it uses only real parts, has no colliding or floating parts, and forms a connected structure if possible. BrickWright guides agents to create builds by writing code with BrickLayer, a Python toolkit with two main components: an ergonomic brick assembly API that halves inference cost compared to working in raw LDraw, and a validator that provides feedback on physical feasibility. Whereas baseline agents achieve physical validity rates ranging from only 9% (GPT-6 Luna) to 69% (GPT-6 Astra), BrickWright-guided agents achieve 100% validity on a sample of 512 prompts, while improving prompt adherence for lightweight agents and maintaining it for stronger agents. Additionally, they outperform specialized models on the text-to-brick task. Code is available on our project page: https://avalovelace1.github.io/brickwright/

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: Dual Exam: Controlled Evaluation of Multimodal Agents and World Models
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Zhefan Rao, Meng Chu, Xuan Zhang, Jingfan Chen, Guohao Cai
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: The paper presents Dual Exam, a framework for evaluating the interaction between Multimodal Agents and World Models across various domains, revealing performance inconsistencies and challenges in reciprocal learning.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: World Models (WMs) can support Multimodal Agents (MAs) through simulated experience, while Agent trajectories can inform World Model refinement. Evaluating this interaction requires separate evidence about action selection and state evolution. We introduce Dual Exam, which tests Agents under fixed environment response mechanisms and World Models under fixed action interventions across physical, digital, social, and scientific domains. The Agent track compares 10 configurations on 1,088 items in 15 reporting categories. The World Model track contains 400 cases across eight scenarios; 15 configurations have full coverage and one covers six scenarios. GPT 6 Astra leads the case-weighted Agent Index at 31.3, and GPT-Image-2 leads the full-coverage WM Overall at 21.7. These scores use different tasks and metrics and are not directly comparable. A 150-case pilot of one coupled pairing records zero task successes and motivates component-level diagnosis. Results reveal uneven task performance and failures to preserve task-relevant state. Their value for predicting coupled success or sustained reciprocal learning remains to be established.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: Energy-Based Transfer for Reinforcement Learning
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Zeyun Deng, Jasorsi Ghosh, Fiona Xie, Kai Cheng, Yuzhe Lu
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: The paper presents an energy-based transfer learning method that enhances reinforcement learning efficiency by selectively guiding exploration based on out-of-distribution detection.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning remains sample inefficient, particularly when agents must adapt over time to related but distinct tasks, as in continual learning settings. Efficiency can be improved by transferring knowledge from a pretrained teacher policy to guide exploration in new but related tasks. However, if the new task sufficiently differs from the teacher's training task, the transferred guidance may be sub-optimal and bias exploration toward low-reward behaviors. We propose an energy-based transfer learning method that uses out-of-distribution detection to selectively issue guidance, enabling the teacher to intervene only in states within its training distribution. We theoretically link energy scores to state-visitation patterns under on-policy reinforcement learning. Empirically, our method improves sample efficiency and performance across both single-task and multi-task settings.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: ExtremControl: Low-Latency Humanoid Teleoperation with Scaled Velocity Feedforward
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Ziyan Xiong, Lixing Fang, Junyun Huang, Kashu Yamazaki, Hao Zhang
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: ExtremControl introduces a low-latency humanoid teleoperation framework that reduces tracking delay by 70ms, enabling advanced reactive behaviors through optimized velocity feedforward control.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Building a low-latency humanoid teleoperation system is essential for collecting diverse reactive and dynamic demonstrations. However, end-to-end latencies in existing approaches consistently hover around 200ms, roughly equal to human reaction time, that severely limits responsiveness and prevents tasks requiring rapid feedback. We identify position-only PD control as the root cause of this latency floor and propose ExtremControl, a low-latency whole-body control framework that: (1) incorporates scaled velocity feedforward in low-level control, reducing tracking delay by approximately 70ms with a provably optimal feedforward ratio; (2) operates directly on SE(3) poses of selected rigid links, primarily humanoid extremities, to avoid joint-space retargeting in the control loop. To minimize retargeting time, we derive a closed-form Cartesian-space mapping that uses a single anthropomorphic calibration step to translate human motion into humanoid link targets, accommodating operators with varying body proportions. Furthermore, we provide a theoretical framework for selecting control hyperparameters, and validate the effectiveness of velocity feedforward control in the reinforcement learning for locomotion setting through experiments in both simulation and the real world. Building on ExtremControl, we implement a teleoperation system supporting both optical motion capture and VR-based tracking, achieving end-to-end latency as low as 50ms --- well beneath the threshold at which system delay adds a full human reaction cycle to the control loop. This enables a qualitatively new class of reactive behaviors, including ping-pong ball balancing, juggling, and real-time return, that are beyond the capability of existing teleoperation systems.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: WARPED: Wrist-Aligned Rendering for Robot Policy Learning from Egocentric Human Demonstrations
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Harry Freeman, Chung Hee Kim, Jenny Wang, George Kantor
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: WARPED synthesizes wrist-view observations from egocentric videos to train visuomotor policies using monocular RGB data, achieving high success rates with significantly reduced data collection time.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Recent advancements in learning from human demonstration have shown promising results in addressing the scalability and high cost of data collection required to train robust visuomotor policies. However, existing approaches are often constrained by a reliance on multiview camera setups, depth sensors, or custom hardware, and are typically limited to policy execution from third-person or egocentric cameras. In this paper, we present WARPED, a framework designed to synthesize realistic wrist-view observations and actions from human demonstration videos to facilitate the training of visuomotor policies using only monocular RGB data. With data collected from an egocentric RGB camera, our system leverages vision foundation models to initialize the interactive scene. A hand-object interaction pipeline is then employed to track the hand and manipulated object and retarget the trajectories to a robotic end-effector. Lastly, photorealistic wrist-view observations are synthesized via Gaussian Splatting to directly train a robotic policy. We demonstrate that WARPED achieves success rates comparable to teleoperation on four of five rigid-object tabletop tasks and one articulated-object task, while requiring 4-9x less data collection time.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: Inference-Time Robot Behavior Steering through Physically-Aware Reconfiguration of Task-Structure
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Yiyuan Pan, Hanjiang Hu, Shangtao Li, Xusheng Luo, Changliu Liu
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: ReStruct enables inference-time steering of robot behaviors by reconfiguring task structures through a neural automaton, enhancing performance in meeting user preferences without retraining.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: A central challenge in deploying learned robot policies is inference-time behavior steering: redirecting a policy at test time to satisfy user preferences not anticipated during training, without retraining. Existing methods fail in two modes: end-to-end methods require fine-tuning or expert-level guidance, while neuro-symbolic methods rely on predefined symbols whose edits can result in logically reasonable but physically infeasible plans. To address this challenge, we propose ReStruct, which builds upon a neural automaton policy that decomposes a visuomotor policy into a high-level state-machine skeleton capturing task structure and a low-level continuous controller represented as a residual policy. Specifically, ReStruct adopts the automaton to represent the preference and incorporates it into the skeleton through a synchronous product, thereby reconfiguring the task structure. With the controller kept frozen, the action priors provided by the skeleton are updated accordingly to enable physically-aware control under a modified task structure. Extensive experiments from simulation and real-world show that ReStruct steers a wide range of preferences, from object-centric specifications to temporal-logic constraints, and after steering surpasses existing methods, exceeding VLA models in both task success and preference-following by up to 25%.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: COWBOY: A Scalable Sim-to-Real Framework for Learning Contextual Whole-Body Manipulation
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Jiahui Yang, Jason Jingzhou Liu, Ray Muxin Liu, Andrew E. Wang, Kenneth Shaw
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: COWBOY is a scalable sim-to-real framework enabling mobile manipulators to adaptively perform contextual whole-body manipulation across diverse, unstructured environments using a vision-based control policy.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Mobile manipulators must adapt not only to objects, but also to the spatial context in which they appear: where to position the base, how to manipulate, and where to look while navigating surrounding scene geometry. To address this, we present COWBOY, a scalable sim-to-real framework for learning such contextual whole-body manipulation. On whole-body dexterous grasping, COWBOY transfers zero-shot to hundreds of objects and diverse in-the-wild scenes, spanning cluttered tabletops, shelves, drawers, and other unstructured settings. Rather than learning scene adaptation directly with RL in simulation, a vectorized environment-aware whole-body controller (WBC) handles reaching in thousands of scenes by coordinating base-arm motion, collision avoidance, and active vision. Then, local RL experts are trained in local scenes for object interaction and can be reused across thousands of full-scene layouts. We distill these composed WBC-RL teachers into a single vision policy that controls the mobile base, arm, dexterous hand, and actuated camera from point-cloud observations. The resulting policy exhibits contextual whole-body behavior, automatically adapting base placement, camera viewpoint, arm trajectory, and grasp strategy to observed scene and object geometry. Videos are available at https://cowboy-manip.com

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: HEHA: Bounded Suboptimal Planning for Constrained Routing and Its Use in Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Exploration of Unknown Environments
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Longrui Yang, Yiyu Wang, Jingfan Tang, Yunpeng Lyu, Shizhe Zhao
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: The paper presents HEHA, a hierarchical planning approach that optimizes multi-robot exploration in unknown environments by efficiently solving constrained routing problems for heterogeneous robots.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: This paper considers the path planning problem for autonomous exploration of an unknown environment using multiple heterogeneous robots such as drones, wheeled, and legged robots, with different capabilities to traverse complex terrains. A key challenge there is to intelligently allocate the robots to the unknown areas to be explored and determine the visiting order of those areas subject to traversability constraints, which leads to a large-scale constrained multiple hamiltonian path problem (mHPP) that needs to be quickly and iteratively solved every time when new space is explored. To address the hallenge, we propose HEHA (Hierarchical Exploration with Heterogeneous Agents) using a recent hierarchical method that decomposes the exploration into global planning and local planning. The major contribution in HEHA is its global planning, where we propose a new routing algorithm RCH (Routing with Constraints and Heterogeneity) that can quickly find bounded sub-optimal solutions for mHPP to minimize the maximum path length (i.e., makespan) among the agents subject to traversability constraints. Additionally, the local planner in HEHA also considers heterogeneity to avoid repeated and duplicated exploration among the robots. The experimental results show, in the presence of heterogeneous traversability, our RCH can solve mHPP with up to 47% smaller makespan than several baselines, and HEHA can reduce the exploration time by up to 30% compared with existing approaches.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: GenXR-Bench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Interactive XR Development
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: William Huang, David Li, Xiang 'Anthony' Chen, Xun Qian, Nels Numan
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: GenXR-Bench is a pioneering benchmark for evaluating coding agents in interactive XR development, assessing their performance across diverse tasks and identifying key failure areas.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Coding agents are rapidly advancing from single-file generation to long-horizon repository-scale engineering, yet the evaluation of their capabilities to author interactive extended reality (XR) applications remains an open challenge. Unlike traditional software, XR applications operate within dynamic 3D physical environments where runtime robustness depends jointly on continuous user motion, spatial input, and environmental sensing. We introduce GenXR-Bench, the first benchmark for the end-to-end evaluation of coding agents in XR software development. GenXR-Bench contains 112 expert-authored tasks spanning 24 feature implementations, 21 bug repairs, and 67 application generation tasks. Held-out tests combine scripted and adaptive interactions with programmatic and visual assertions to evaluate core functionality and runtime behavior. GenXR-Bench's testing suite achieves 96.5% accuracy against blinded expert judgments of 124 candidate applications executed on consumer XR hardware. Evaluating 10 models on GenXR-Bench, we find that the strongest configuration achieves only 50.9% overall Pass@1. Failure analysis identifies recurring misunderstandings in asynchronous sensor lifecycles, physical grounding, and embodied interaction semantics. GenXR-Bench establishes a reproducible testbed for evaluating coding agents in the interactive and physically situated conditions of spatial computing.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: Joint Constraint Aggregation for Qualifier-Sensitive Retrieval-Augmented QA
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Jennifer Hsia, Zachary C. Lipton, Aarti Singh
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: The paper introduces Joint Constraint Aggregation (JCA) to enhance retrieval-augmented QA by ensuring candidates meet all question requirements, improving accuracy against retrieval biases.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Retrieval-augmented QA can fail even when the correct answer is in the retrieved evidence. This can happen when a competing answer satisfies some, but not all, of the question's requirements and is mentioned frequently in the retrieved documents, which can make it appear to be the best-supported answer. To test whether this retrieval skew actually affects the decision, we manipulate it directly: increasing the prevalence of passages that favor the competing answer makes the model more likely to select it. This points to a decision problem that candidate-level support alone cannot resolve. We therefore introduce Joint Constraint Aggregation (JCA), which compares candidates against the same question-derived requirements using the retrieved evidence. Across three evaluation settings and three instruction-tuned backbones, JCA improves overall accuracy, and its advantage grows when retrieval favors a competing answer. Together, these results suggest that when partial matches and retrieval prominence pull models toward a competing answer, comparing candidates against the question's full requirements can make selection more reliable.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: EmbodyHOI: Embodiment-Aware Generation of Hand-Object Interactions for Humanoid Dexterous Manipulation
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Chaitanya Chawla, Kartik Sharma, Ananya Bal, Laszlo A. Jeni, Guanya Shi
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: EmbodyHOI optimizes hand-object interaction generation for humanoid robots by integrating embodiment-aware inverse kinematics, significantly improving trajectory accuracy and task success rates.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Humanoid dexterous manipulation needs reference motions that are both semantically rich and kinematically feasible for the target robot. Text-conditioned hand-object interaction (HOI) generators supply diverse, language-specified demonstrations, but they synthesize motion in human (MANO) space. The embodiment gap is therefore deferred to post-hoc retargeting, where trajectories deployed on the robot can fail to maintain contact with objects and also degrade policy learning. Our key idea is that robot reachability should constrain the interaction trajectories while they are being generated. We present EmbodyHOI, which runs a differentiable inverse-kinematics (IK) solver for a specific humanoid embodiment inside the sampling loop of a frozen flow-matching HOI trajectory generator. We feed back gradients from the embodiment-aware IK solver into the HOI sampler and jointly optimize the position of the humanoid with respect to the object. Because guidance acts only at inference, one HOI trajectory generator trained on human hand poses transfers across humanoid embodiments without retraining. On ARCTIC trajectories with two contrasting humanoids (Unitree G1 and H1-2), our proposed guidance-based method cuts the retargeted wrist error from 8.9 cm to 0.6 cm while leaving text-to-HOI generation quality intact, and raises task success from 68% to 79% on 50 random G1 tasks and from 62% to 76% on a four-task H1-2 suite. Critically, cheaper alternatives for bridging the embodiment gap fail to beat EmbodyHOI. Post-hoc wrist refinement and compute-matched best-of-N selection both reach lower IK energy than our guidance yet train worse policies. For simulation results, see our website: https://embodyhoi.github.io/

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: Automated Multi-Agent Organization Design: From Architecture Search to Organizational Learning
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Shao-Jun Xia, Yuner Zhang, Huixin Zhang, Di Wang, Yifan Jiang
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: The paper introduces Automated Multi-Agent Organization Design (AMOD), a framework for dynamically optimizing multi-agent systems by modeling responsibilities, coordination, and iterative organizational learning.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Agentic system design is increasingly shifting from hand-crafted prompts and workflows toward automated search over agentic programs and interaction structures, with multi-agent systems receiving growing attention. Yet a central question remains unresolved: when does an automatically generated multi-agent structure exhibit a functionally meaningful division of responsibility? We argue that automated multi-agent design should move beyond searching for effective architectures toward identifying which responsibilities are functionally necessary, how they should be allocated, and when they should change. To explore this, we propose Automated Multi-Agent Organization Design (AMOD), which treats organization itself as a first-class design object, explicitly modeling how agent teams are composed, what functional responsibilities the agents assume, how they coordinate, and how collective decisions are made. We formulate AMOD as an execution-driven design loop. For each task, an automated designer instantiates an organization by assigning functional responsibilities and coordination rules to a set of agents. After execution, task outcomes, intermediate artifacts, and interaction traces are examined to identify which responsibilities may be missing, duplicated, or ineffective, and the organization is revised accordingly. We also propose testing discovered responsibilities by removing them, replacing them with generic roles, or changing their assignment under matched resource budgets, with complementary evaluations. AMOD provides a principled foundation for evidence-based and adaptive multi-agent organization design.

卡内基-机器人研究所.title: VLM-Guided Contact Retargeting and Generative Partner Modeling for Humanoid-Human Interaction
卡内基-机器人研究所.authors_text: Yuto Shibata, Kotaro Amaya, Kashu Yamazaki, Lalit Jayanti, Yoshimitsu Aoki
卡内基-机器人研究所.summary: REACT is a framework for humanoid-human interaction that utilizes VLM-guided contact modeling and generative partner-state modeling to enhance performance under occlusion and partial observability.
卡内基-机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Humanoid-human interaction requires robots to operate under severe partial observability: during close physical contact, the human partner is occluded, truncated, or outside the robot's field of view, causing pose estimation to fail and often necessitating external tracking or privileged human state. At the same time, heavy mutual occlusions introduce errors into the human-human motion-capture data used for learning. We present REACT, a framework for learning deployable humanoid-human interaction policies from human-human demonstrations. REACT treats semantic contact structure as the key supervisory signal connecting demonstration processing, interaction learning, and onboard control. First, a VLM-guided contact modeling and retargeting pipeline identifies semantically meaningful contacts and transfers them onto humanoid-human geometry while preserving interaction structure. Using these annotations, privileged interaction policies learn physically grounded behaviors through interaction-aware contact rewards and are then distilled into deployable egocentric depth policies trained entirely from onboard sensing using photorealistic human depth rendering. To address severe partial observability, we introduce generative partner-state modeling objectives that predict partner motion from occluded egocentric views. We evaluate REACT in simulation and on a real Unitree G1 humanoid across five contact-rich interactions.
