However, most existing guardrail mechanisms remain static, relying on fixed rules, prompts, or classifiers that generalize poorly to emerging risks. Here we present EVOLVE, a tool-level self-evolving defense framework that formulates agent security as a process of cumulative security evolution. Inspired by how human societies transform experiences into transferable protective knowledge, EVOLVE externalizes security knowledge into executable guardrail tools that are continuously inherited, independently audited, and iteratively refined through lifelong interaction. Across multiple benchmarks, backbone models, and embodied environments, EVOLVE consistently outperforms existing defenses across diverse risk scenarios with +22\% average F1 score. We further validate the framework in real-world robotic and autonomous agent systems. Our results suggest that scalable agent safety may require continuously evolving defense systems rather than static guardrails.

MReaLLab.title: INTERACT: Learning Interaction-Aware World Dynamics from Driving Videos for Autonomous Driving
MReaLLab.authors_text: Zhan Chen, Songyan Zhang, Wenhui Huang, Zirui Li, Zhidong Wang
MReaLLab.summary: INTERACT is a three-stage framework that learns object-centric world dynamics from driving videos to enhance trajectory planning for safer autonomous driving.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Safe autonomous driving requires more than recognizing the current scene: the ego vehicle must anticipate how surrounding traffic participants will evolve under its own motion. However, existing end-to-end driving models typically encode scenes into dense visual or BEV features, leaving object-level interactions implicit. We propose (INTERACT INTERaction-aware Action-Conditioned Trajectory learning), a three-stage framework that learns a slot-based object-centric world model from unlabeled driving videos and transfers it to trajectory planning. INTERACT first learns recurrent slots that group dense visual features into temporally structured scene-entity representations without object annotations. It then infers latent ego actions from slot context and video transitions, and uses them to condition future slot prediction, capturing how ego motion and surrounding entities co-evolve. Finally, the learned slots, latent actions, and future slot predictions are distilled into a trajectory planner to guide trajectory generation and selection. Extensive experiments on NAVSIM and nuScenes validate the effectiveness of INTERACT. In particular, it achieves state-of-the-art performance on NAVSIM, with improvements in safety-critical collision metrics.

MReaLLab.title: VLALagBench: Understanding When and Why VLA Inference Latency Matters
MReaLLab.authors_text: Qi Wen, Borui Xu, Hussein Amro, Hongshi Tan, Hanmin Lin
MReaLLab.summary: VLALagBench benchmarks VLA inference latency's impact on task success, revealing significant sensitivity to latency and guiding algorithm configurations for optimal performance in robotics.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models offer a promising path toward general-purpose robot manipulation. While inference latency can affect task success in a constantly evolving physical world, the relationship between latency and task success rate remains poorly understood. In this paper, we introduce VLALagBench, a comprehensive benchmark for studying VLA inference latency sensitivity across task types, object speeds, execution modes (synchronous and asynchronous), and VLA policies. Using VLALagBench, we find that even a modest inference latency of 100 ms can nearly halve task success on moving targets, with sensitivity varying substantially across tasks and policies. These differences reflect task-specific requirements for precision and continuous motion. By overlapping inference with action execution, asynchronous execution can recover some of the lost success at the cost of more frequent inference requests. Building on these findings, we develop an empirical model that predicts task success from limited calibration data, achieving root-mean-square prediction errors of only 5.7-7.8% across various VLA policies. Given an inference system's latency and per-robot throughput, these predictions guide the selection of system-specific VLA algorithm configurations to maximize task success. We believe VLALagBench and these findings provide a solid foundation for future robotics algorithm-system co-design.

MReaLLab.title: AnchorComplete: Recovering Complete Scene Meshes from Partial Point Clouds
MReaLLab.authors_text: Weirong Chen, Ismail El-Yamany, Ganlin Zhang, Chuanxia Zheng, Andrea Vedaldi
MReaLLab.summary: AnchorComplete is a novel framework that reconstructs complete scene meshes from partial point clouds, enhancing geometry recovery while maintaining structural consistency across varying scales.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Most image-based 3D reconstructors primarily recover visible surfaces, producing partial point clouds with large holes and leaving unobserved geometry unresolved. To address this limitation, we introduce AnchorComplete, a framework that reconstructs complete scene meshes from partial point clouds while preserving observed geometry and supporting scenes of varying scales. Building on TRELLIS.2, our method combines partial-point conditioning, which integrates global scene tokens with local spatial evidence to anchor generation to the input, and metric-scale coarse-to-fine generation, which progressively refines scene geometry within fixed-size windows while maintaining global structural consistency. Experiments on Replica and SCRREAM demonstrate that AnchorComplete consistently outperforms strong baselines in complete-scene reconstruction, particularly under sparse-view settings.

MReaLLab.title: UAV-DualCog: A Dual-Cognition Benchmark for Grounded UAV Agent-World Reasoning with MLLMs
MReaLLab.authors_text: Like Liu, Zhengzheng Xu, Hongzhe Li, Lin Wang, Dian Shao
MReaLLab.summary: UAV-DualCog introduces a benchmark for evaluating UAV agents' dual cognition capabilities using MLLMs, highlighting significant performance gaps in reasoning about agent and world states.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) perform strongly across vision-language tasks, yet remain insufficiently explored in UAV scenarios. Recent UAV-oriented benchmarks have begun to evaluate MLLMs in aerial scenarios, but typically focus on scene understanding, event recognition, or navigation completion, rather than jointly assessing the dual-cognition capability required for UAV agents: reasoning about the UAV's own position, behavior, and observation state alongside external landmark states under continuously changing viewpoints, supported by explicit spatio-temporal grounding. To address this gap, we present UAV-DualCog, the first benchmark to formulate UAV dual cognition as the coordinated evaluation of Agent-State Reasoning and World-State Reasoning across multi-view images and egocentric videos, with explicit spatial or temporal grounding. The State-aware UAV Simulation Platform (SUSP) and the DualCog-aware Capture System (DCCS) construct 4,096 image and 2,048 video samples from 12 scenes, pairing complementary state questions within shared Agent-Landmark contexts. Extensive evaluations on 45 models show that current MLLMs remain far from reliable in UAV dual cognition: Agent-State Reasoning is generally weaker than World-State Reasoning, semantic answers do not reliably coincide with spatial or temporal grounding, and coordinated abilities remain limited. Thinking-mode comparisons, open-ended analyses, and sim-to-real validation show that these limitations persist across inference settings, formats, and environments. We further construct UAV-DualCog-Train and improve UAV dual-cognition performance through a lightweight optimization probe. Supplementary website, code, and dataset: https://smartdianlab.github.io/UAV-DualCog/

MReaLLab.title: The Strange Attractor Model of Bipedal Locomotion and its Consequences on Motor Control
MReaLLab.authors_text: Carlo Tiseo, Ming Jeat Foo, Kalyana C Veluvolu, Arturo Forner-Cordero, Wei Tech Ang
MReaLLab.summary: This paper introduces a novel deterministic task-space planner for bipedal locomotion, enhancing understanding of human gait dynamics and informing rehabilitation and robotic control strategies.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Despite decades of research, the dynamic mechanisms governing human locomotion remain incompletely understood. Current motor control models only partially capture these complex dynamics, a theoretical gap that likely limits the clinical efficacy of modern lower-limb rehabilitation therapies. Recently, it has been proposed that human locomotion is planned in task-space by explicitly exploiting the gravitational pull acting on the Center of Mass (CoM). Building upon this concept, this paper presents a novel deterministic task-space planner for straight, constant-speed locomotion. Our model formulates the CoM trajectory in the transverse plane as a harmonic oscillator moving at a constant forward velocity, while demonstrating that the vertical CoM trajectory is actively regulated through localized ankle strategies. We derive closed-form equations that successfully generate human-like trajectories for both the CoM and the swing foot. The model's predictive accuracy is empirically validated against the kinematic behavior of 12 healthy subjects walking at three self-selected speeds. Furthermore, the proposed planner is mathematically compatible with an extended formulation of the Passive Motion Paradigm ($λ_0$-PMP), establishing a comprehensive theoretical foundation for decentralized, hierarchical architectures of semi-autonomous controllers in both human motor control and assistive robotics.

MReaLLab.title: Cross-Embodiment Motion Planning by Coupling Body-Agnostic World Model with Differentiable Ego-Dynamics
MReaLLab.authors_text: Zhidong Wang, Zirui Li, Haoran Xu, Yujie Yan, Zitong Shan
MReaLLab.summary: The paper presents Hourglass, a novel architecture for cross-embodiment motion planning that integrates a body-agnostic world model with differentiable ego-dynamics, achieving superior performance across various robotic embodiments.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Motion planning in clutter is embodiment-specific: the feasible free space and reachable commands depend on each robot's geometry and dynamics. Existing cross-embodiment policies output normalized commands that disregard these differences, or compensate through per-robot training and distillation. World models can in principle pool cross-embodiment data, yet command-conditioned models bind their latent dynamics to a single action space, while pose-conditioned models omit the mapping from commands to body-specific motion. On flat ground, however, embodiment affects the planner's observations only through the camera ego-motion. This letter proposes Hourglass, an hourglass-shaped architecture that factorizes cross-embodiment motion planning at this interface: a body-agnostic world model and each robot's differentiable ego-dynamics, which map commands to that ego-motion, are coupled only through it. The world model is trained on data pooled across embodiments and camera mounts; each robot's ego-dynamics is a reduced-order template with identified physical parameters. A generalist parameter-conditioned policy is learned once at this junction: each imagined step rolls out the template and then the world model, and imagination training through each robot's template makes the policy body-aware. On seven simulated robots of five locomotion types, the generalist policy outperforms imitation-learning and diffusion-policy baselines on the same world model by 3.8--10.6 percentage points in success rate and matches per-robot specialists without dedicated training, while approaching its parameter-conditioned MPPI teacher within 1.4--2.8 points without an online map. After three minutes of teleoperated driving for identification, the synthetic-data-trained model transfers zero-shot to a real skid-steer robot unseen in training, navigating unseen indoor scenes.

MReaLLab.title: FrontierMat: Benchmarking Language Models at the Frontier of Materials R&D
MReaLLab.authors_text: Feng Chen, Jianguo Huang, Yushan Xiao, Yue Li, Bijun Tang
MReaLLab.summary: FrontierMat introduces a benchmark of 330 validated research problems to evaluate language models' effectiveness in advanced materials discovery, highlighting significant performance gaps and improvement strategies.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: To accelerate materials discovery, language models must be able to address problems at the research frontier. Yet textbook- and examination-derived benchmarks primarily assess established knowledge, leaving performance on frontier research problems largely untested. We introduce FrontierMat, a benchmark of 330 problems drawn from frontier academic and industrial research in fields including aerospace, semiconductors, embodied intelligence and nuclear fusion. Every problem is validated by leading experimentalists and industry experts in its field. Each problem presents a real study and asks the model to infer a withheld outcome or draw a conclusion from selected experimental evidence. Problems are annotated by functional domain, material system and the scale of the governing mechanism; 130 require cross-scale reasoning. The strongest general-purpose model scores only 53.7%, and on matched problems, cross-scale problems score 8.7 points below single-scale ones. Half of the problems are solved by at most one model, and models fail chiefly by endorsing what is plausible rather than what was observed. A domain-adaptation study with meta-weighted continued pretraining and scale-modular self-distillation raises an open-weight model from 36.7% to 55.4%, matching the strongest proprietary model, with improvements on public materials benchmarks and no decline in aggregate performance on general benchmarks. FrontierMat provides a testbed for measuring progress toward language models that support frontier materials R&D.

MReaLLab.title: Decompose and Reorganize: Planning with Primitives and Visuomotor Policies Learned from Demonstrations
MReaLLab.authors_text: Yizhou Chen, Hang Xu, Dongjie Yu, Yupu Lu, Tengye Xu
MReaLLab.summary: The DR-LfD framework integrates visuomotor policies into TAMP, enabling efficient skill decomposition and reorganization for dexterous bimanual manipulation with fewer demonstrations.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Successfully automating dexterous, long-horizon bimanual manipulation requires frameworks capable of both high-level reasoning and fine-grained execution. Traditional task and motion planning (TAMP), while excellent at symbolic planning, is often brittle in contact-rich operations. Simultaneously, imitation learning (IL), while effective in manipulation tasks with visual feedback, is limited by its low capability in spatial generalization and multi-stage operation. To reconcile their complementary strengths and limitations, we propose DR-LfD (Decomposed and Reorganized Skills Learned from Demonstrations), a framework that integrates visuomotor policies into a TAMP-gated decision-making system. Based on contact relationships, DR-LfD decomposes human demonstrations into atomic skills, which are reproduced as visuomotor policies or object-centric primitives. The initiation, termination, and constraints of the visuomotor policies are carefully modeled and implemented in a TAMP-compatible form, enabling reorganization of skills learned from different sources. DR-LfD transforms the learning problem from one requiring exponential demonstration data over possible skill sequences to one whose demonstration burden scales with the number of distinct skill types, with limited data for each skill. Real-world and simulation benchmarks demonstrate data-efficient skill composition under unseen setups and physical constraints. On two DexMimicGen tasks, DR-LfD with 100 demonstrations outperforms diffusion-based imitation policies with 1000.

MReaLLab.title: Diagnosing the Reference Gap: What Visual Scaffolds Can and Cannot Fix in Multimodal Reasoning
MReaLLab.authors_text: Guizhen Chen, Weiwen Xu, Wotao Yin, Anh Tuan Luu, Hou Pong Chan
MReaLLab.summary: The paper identifies a "reference gap" in multimodal reasoning, demonstrating that task-matched visual references significantly enhance model accuracy, while mismatched references hinder performance.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Multimodal large language models can recognize visual content yet struggle to reason reliably over it across multiple steps. In counting, a model may see all objects but lose track of which ones it has counted. We argue that such failures, commonly attributed to perception, reveal a reference gap: the failure to bind language to the relevant visual entities, regions, or locations. Motivated by the theory of visual routines, we test whether external references such as numbering can narrow this gap. We introduce ReGap-Bench, a paired benchmark of five visual reasoning tasks in which the scene, question, and answer are fixed and only the reference varies. Results show that task-matched references improve accuracy by up to 25\%, while mismatched references provide little benefit or even hurt performance. These findings identify the reference gap as a bottleneck distinct from visual perception and show that constructing task-appropriate visual references can serve as a training-free visual skill for improving multimodal reasoning.

MReaLLab.title: ClueTracer: Question-to-Vision Clue Tracing for Training-Free Hallucination Suppression in Multimodal Reasoning
MReaLLab.authors_text: Gongli Xi, Kun Wang, Zeming Gao, Huahui Yi, Haolang Lu
MReaLLab.summary: ClueTracer is a training-free method that enhances multimodal reasoning models by suppressing hallucinations through effective visual clue tracing, improving performance across various architectures.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Large multimodal reasoning models solve challenging visual problems via explicit long-chain inference: they gather visual clues from images and decode clues into textual tokens. Yet this capability also increases hallucinations, where the model generates content that is not supported by the input image or the question. To understand this failure mode, we identify \emph{reasoning drift}: during clue gathering, the model over-focuses on question-irrelevant entities, diluting focus on task-relevant cues and gradually decoupling the reasoning trace from visual grounding. As a consequence, many inference-time localization or intervention methods developed for non-reasoning models fail to pinpoint the true clues in reasoning settings. Motivated by these insights, we introduce ClueRecall, a metric for assessing visual clue retrieval, and present ClueTracer, a training-free, parameter-free, and architecture-agnostic plugin for hallucination suppression. ClueTracer starts from the question and traces how key clues propagate along the model's reasoning pathway (question $\rightarrow$ outputs $\rightarrow$ visual tokens), thereby localizing task-relevant patches while suppressing spurious attention to irrelevant regions. Remarkably, \textbf{without any additional training}, ClueTracer improves all \textbf{reasoning} architectures (including \texttt{R1-OneVision}, \texttt{Ocean-R1}, \texttt{MM-Eureka}, \emph{etc}.) by $\mathbf{1.21\times}$ on reasoning benchmarks

MReaLLab.title: Breadcrumbing Search Agents: Per-Turn Scheming Over Long-Horizon Trajectories
MReaLLab.authors_text: Xuebin Li, Hanqing Zhao, Siyuan Liang, Kejiang Chen, Weiming Zhang
MReaLLab.summary: The paper presents a method called Authority-Chain Hijack (ACH) that enhances the effectiveness of attacks on LLM-based search agents by coordinating manipulated evidence across their query trajectories.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: LLM-based search agents are widely used for information-seeking tasks, but their reliance on external tool returns introduces a critical security risk: web content retrieved during execution is untrusted, exposing agents to prompt injection and goal hijacking. Prior work on search-agent safety primarily focuses on static web-content injection, but modern agents issue follow-up queries and cross-check competing sources, so a single injected page is often diluted or rejected. We show that the channel delivering search and page observations is a fragile security boundary: beyond exposing the agent to a single poisoned page, a mediated search interface can repeatedly steer how the agent gathers evidence and forms its final answer. Under a constrained tool-intermediary threat model, appending only one controlled result per query can substantially increase attack success when the evidence is coordinated across the agent's trajectory. We study this setting with a strategy-driven long-horizon attack system and introduce Authority-Chain Hijack (ACH), an expert-refined strategy that turns isolated search-result and page-content manipulations into a coherent evidence chain across seemingly corroborating sources. ACH achieves the highest Overall ASR among all baselines, reaching 55.9% / 83.3% ASR / MaxN ASR on the full SafeSearch test split. We further introduce Trace-Guided Strategy Evolution (TGSE), which automatically improves attacker strategies from execution traces, replacing manual redesign with trace-driven refinement; its strongest single setting reaches 71.4% / 95.0% in held-out evaluation. Code is available at https://github.com/MBOSSLESS/Breadcrumbing-Search-Agents.

MReaLLab.title: CAD-WAM: Anticipating Geometry for Text-to-CAD Generation
MReaLLab.authors_text: Zhengyang Li, Weijie Zheng, Yuxin Cui, Sijie Wang, Wenjie Feng
MReaLLab.summary: CAD-WAM enhances text-to-CAD generation by integrating geometry-conditioned action generation with next-state prediction, improving geometric accuracy and output validity over existing methods.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Generating editable computer-aided design (CAD) models from text requires selecting operations that produce the intended changes to the geometry constructed so far. An incorrect operation can compromise subsequent steps, making reliable multi-step generation challenging. Existing methods based on large language models (LLMs) primarily learn to predict commands, without explicit supervision of the geometric states those commands should produce. Inspired by world-action models, we introduce CAD-WAM, which couples geometry-conditioned action generation with next-state prediction. We define complete modeling operations as actions in a CAD domain-specific language (DSL) and encode surface point clouds of intermediate solids into compact latent states using a pretrained variational autoencoder. An LLM backbone generates the next action from the target description and current geometric state, while an auxiliary head on the same backbone predicts the next state to provide geometric supervision during training. We construct step-wise training trajectories from parametric CAD models in the DeepCAD dataset, pairing each trajectory with an expert-level textual description. At inference, each generated action is executed by a CAD kernel, and the resulting solid is re-encoded to inform the next decision. On the DeepCAD test set, CAD-WAM outperforms the task-specific baselines in geometric accuracy and output validity, with larger gains on models requiring more operations, and produces more accurate geometry than general-purpose LLMs prompted with the same DSL. Ablations further show that next-state supervision reduces mean Chamfer distance by 13.2\% relative to an otherwise identical model trained only to predict actions. Code is available at https://github.com/Lzy-1037/CAD-WAM.

MReaLLab.title: Robust Taylor-Lagrange Control for Safety-Critical Systems with Guaranteed Feasibility
MReaLLab.authors_text: Wei Xiao, Christos Cassandras, Anni Li
MReaLLab.summary: The proposed robust Taylor-Lagrange Control method enhances safety in critical systems by ensuring feasibility preservation through higher-order safety function expansions and simplified parameterization.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: The Control Barrier Function (CBF) method has been widely adopted in solving safety-critical control problems. However, the existence of a CBF is only a sufficient condition for system safety. The recently proposed Taylor-Lagrange Control (TLC) method addresses this limitation by providing a necessary and sufficient condition, but it is still vulnerable to the feasibility preservation problem (e.g., due to the inter-sampling effect when time is discretized). In this paper, we propose a robust TLC (rTLC) method to address the feasibility preservation problem and show how to use it to solve optimal control problems. Specifically, the rTLC method expands the safety function to an order higher than its relative degree using Taylor's expansion with Lagrange remainder, which allows the control to explicitly show up at the current time instead of a future time in the original TLC method. This implies that the safety constraint remains satisfied over the entire discretization time interval that follows. Moreover, the rTLC method naturally addresses the feasibility preservation problem with only a single hyper-parameter (the discretization time interval size during implementation), compared to significantly more parameters for its counterparts. Finally, we illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed rTLC method through an adaptive cruise control problem, and compare it with existing safety-critical control methods.

MReaLLab.title: RFW-A: Agentic Procedural Generation of 400K Articulated Assets over 500 Categories
MReaLLab.authors_text: Yuanbo Lyu, Changjian Pan, Saining Zhang, Yi Yang, Peishuo Li
MReaLLab.summary: RFW-A introduces a novel paradigm for generating over 400K articulated assets efficiently by combining agentic synthesis with procedural generation, significantly reducing costs and improving asset validity.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: High-quality articulated assets are essential for embodied perception, simulation, and manipulation, yet constructing them at scale remains difficult. Manual annotation and procedural modeling require substantial human effort. Recent agentic systems automate asset construction through program synthesis, but repeat costly reasoning and refinement for every new asset. Our key observation is that assets within a category can share construction logic despite variations in structure and appearance. Agentic synthesis and procedural generation are therefore complementary: agents can construct reusable programs, while procedural execution reuses the resulting logic across many samples. We therefore present RFW-A, which combines the two in a new articulated-asset generation paradigm. Starting from existing articulated programs, RFW-A organizes reusable components and their dependencies into category-level generators. Agents test and refine these generators across sampled configurations and motion states. Once constructed and validated, the generators produce diverse assets through procedural execution with no further model calls or token charges. The estimated API cost of generator authoring averages $10.62, amortizing to $0.05 per asset over 200 assets, versus $1.24 for the sampled per-asset agentic synthesis baseline. Using RFW-A, we built RFW-A-400K, containing over 400K sim-ready articulated assets across more than 500 categories. Experiments show high structural and kinematic validity and stable execution across physics simulators. Beyond asset validity, training with RFW-A-400K improves part-level articulation estimation on seen and unseen categories, while policies trained in simulation with retrieved and program-edited assets transfer zero-shot to real articulated objects.

MReaLLab.title: TouchBridge: Tactile-Conditioned Human-to-Robot Transfer for Dexterous Manipulation
MReaLLab.authors_text: Haozhe Zhang, Gu Zhang, Zirui Zou, Yuzheng Chen, Jinlong Wu
MReaLLab.summary: TouchBridge enables efficient human-to-robot transfer of dexterous manipulation through tactile-conditioned retargeting, achieving high success rates with faster demonstration collection compared to traditional methods.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Human demonstrations offer an efficient and scalable source of data for dexterous robot manipulation, but differences in sensing and hand morphology complicate the transfer of contact-rich interactions. We present TouchBridge, a hardware--software co-designed framework for human-to-robot data transformation. A wearable human demonstration interface and a corresponding robot interface establish cross-embodiment correspondence in visual and fingertip tactile sensing. We introduce Tac-Retarget, a tactile-conditioned retargeting method that uses measured contact to align fingertip contact patches and preserve their spatial relations within and across hands. Unlike object-aware or simulation-based transfer pipelines, Tac-Retarget requires no object mesh, object-pose estimate, or physics simulation for retargeting, enabling direct and scalable conversion of human demonstrations into robot-domain training data. Combined with visual synthesis and camera-anchored action conversion, TouchBridge produces robot-domain demonstrations for fine-tuning a pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) model. Across four real-world contact-rich tasks, policies fine-tuned solely on TouchBridge-converted human demonstrations achieve a 72.5% average success rate, compared with 77.5% using an equal number of teleoperated robot demonstrations, while human demonstration collection is 7.0x faster. Under the same policy and training setup, Tac-Retarget outperforms DexPilot and UniDex by 25.0 and 42.5 percentage points, respectively.

MReaLLab.title: Probing Spatial State Representations in Visual Foundation Models
MReaLLab.authors_text: Baiqiao Yin, Zhongang Cai, Ruisi Wang, Qiwei Liang, Lei Yang
MReaLLab.summary: This study evaluates visual foundation models' spatial representations, revealing varied capabilities in object persistence, predictive updates, and actionability under dynamic viewing conditions.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: An observer sees only part of the surrounding world, yet must keep track of what lies beyond the current view. Spatial perception therefore involves more than recognizing individual images: it calls for a persistent spatial state that is updated under self-motion and used to guide action. Do visual foundation models provide representations that support such a state? We study this question through four levels of spatial capability---spatial structure, object persistence, predictive spatial update, and actionability---using frozen-feature probes on ten representations under streaming egocentric observations of static indoor environments. The resulting capability profiles vary across tasks, network layers, and prefix lengths: strong readout of the visible scene does not ensure accurate object persistence or future-feature retrieval. Matched controls separate readout accuracy from reliance on visual history and motion. Native future prediction retains recoverable spatial structure, but a spatial reader trained on real features does not transfer to predicted features unchanged. Finally, goal-dependent candidate selection does not establish reliable continuous action utility: predicted actions respond to goal changes, yet supplying the correct goal does not reliably improve progress. Across the four levels, object persistence and actionability build on camera-pose readout, whereas feature prediction builds on visible-scene readout. Together, these findings motivate evaluating spatial representations not only by what can be decoded from them, but by whether that information is maintained beyond observation, updated predictively, and used for goal-directed action.

MReaLLab.title: MarineLife-16K: An Attribute-Rich Video-Text Dataset for Motion-Aware Marine Video Understanding
MReaLLab.authors_text: Quang-Trung Truong, Thanh-Nghia Nguyen, Phu-Phong Vo, Jaeyeon Kim, Cheng Chen
MReaLLab.summary: The MarineLife-16K dataset enhances marine video understanding by providing 2,000 annotated video-text pairs with rich attributes and benchmarking video-LLM models on various tasks.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Marine video understanding is crucial for a wide range of real-world applications. However, existing marine video datasets suffer from limitations, including the limited number of data samples, fine-grained text descriptions, and detailed visual attributes. To address these limitations, we introduce a large-scale, video-text dataset featuring rich, in-the-wild visual attributes tailored for complex marine environments. Our dataset comprises 2,000 video-text pairs annotated with 13 attributes covering up to four objects per scene, object visual/geometric properties, behaviors, environmental context, and camera motion, spanning diverse lighting conditions, times of day, and 7 countries. From these annotations, we generate 16,080 video-question pairs (12,080 multiple-choice, 4,000 open-ended). Furthermore, we benchmark both proprietary and open-source video-LLM models on video question answering and video captioning tasks. We find that (i) proprietary models often achieves superior performances; (ii) VLMs handle object motion well but struggle with complex camera motion; (iii) closed-source models struggle to perceive camera motion; and (iv) VLMs struggle to reason in static cameras.

MReaLLab.title: CAPTURER: A Dexterous Aerial Manipulator for Dynamic and Precise Grasping across Diverse Environments
MReaLLab.authors_text: Meng Wang, Jindou Jia, Sicheng Zhou, Zeshuai Chen, Kexin Guo
MReaLLab.summary: CAPTURER is a dexterous aerial manipulator that achieves centimeter-level grasping accuracy for dynamic targets through advanced perception, motion planning, and disturbance-rejection techniques.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: As a representative form of embodied robotic interaction, aerial grasping requires close coordination between the aerial platform and manipulator. Most existing systems perform aerial grasping with static or slowly moving targets under fixed scenarios. Dynamic and precise grasping across different conditions introduces additional challenges, including target motion, localization drift, dynamic coupling, and external disturbances. In this work, we present CAPTURER, a dexterous aerial manipulator for centimeter-level grasping across diverse environments. To achieve the challenging goal, we first develop an onboard perception system for state estimation and target detection. Drift correction and global pose transformation are introduced to improve target localization during flight. A cooperative motion planner is proposed to coordinate the mobility of the aerial platform with the dexterity of the manipulator according to the relative target state. To maintain grasping accuracy under disturbances, we design a disturbance-rejection controller to compensate for dynamic coupling, model uncertainty, and external disturbances. The capability of CAPTURER is validated through indoor and outdoor experiments with both static and moving targets. The results demonstrate that CAPTURER achieves centimeter-level grasping accuracy for a marker pen measuring only 1.5 cm in diameter at flight speeds exceeding 1.5 m/s.

MReaLLab.title: WorldProbe: When Video World Models Fall Apart under Long-Horizon Spatial Exploration
MReaLLab.authors_text: Minqi Wang, Jie Peng, Hejun Dong, Ruchang Yao, Puyi Wang
MReaLLab.summary: WorldProbe introduces a benchmark revealing that video world models struggle with long-horizon exploration, highlighting inconsistencies in long-range memory despite improved local generation quality.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Video world models generate future visual observations from camera or action inputs, with the goal of synthesizing persistent 3D worlds that can be explored across time and space. Existing benchmarks typically evaluate short interactions or rely on camera trajectories fixed before generation. The performance of video world models under long-horizon exploration with extensive camera motion remains under-explored. We introduce WorldProbe, a diagnostic benchmark that uses a goal-conditioned multimodal agent to adapt camera actions online during generation. WorldProbe comprises 164 test cases across four probing families. Across 10 state-of-the-art models, we generate more than 1,600 rollouts totaling approximately 800 minutes, with horizons up to 180 seconds. Our evaluation across four dimensions reveals both the degradation of local measures and the emergence of long-range inconsistencies. We find that recent models sustain visual and content quality for longer, while long-range memory and evolution remain weak. These results expose a gap between locally stable generation and persistent world consistency that is largely missed by existing benchmarks. Code and benchmark resources are available at https://github.com/Untitled-W/WorldProbe.

MReaLLab.title: MLLM-GS: Multimodal Large Language Model Prior-Guided Fast Novel View Synthesis in Extreme Environments
MReaLLab.authors_text: Zhiliang Wu, Xinye Zheng, Kun Li, Fei Wang, Hao Guo
MReaLLab.summary: MLLM-GS introduces a multimodal large language model framework for efficient novel view synthesis in extreme environments, enhancing degraded views and optimizing 3D reconstruction processes.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Novel view synthesis (NVS) in degraded scenes aims to reconstruct 3D scenes from multi-view observations affected by various degradations, and to generate clear and photorealistic images at unseen viewpoints. Despite recent advances, existing methods often rely on degradation-specific models, limiting their generalization across diverse extreme environments. Generative models provide rich visual priors, but their outputs often suffer from pixel misalignment and color deviations, which can propagate into the reconstructed 3D scene and compromise reconstruction quality. Furthermore, the high computational and memory costs of 3D reconstruction hinder the practical application of NVS in extreme environments. To this end, we propose MLLM-GS, a multimodal large language model (MLLM) prior-guided framework for fast NVS in extreme environments. MLLM-GS consists of two branches: MLLM prior-guided view enhancement and fast 3D scene reconstruction. The former leverages the rich visual priors of a frozen MLLM to enhance views under different severe degradations and introduces a lightweight correction network to reduce pixel shifts and color distortions in MLLM outputs. With supervision from only a few paired clean views, this branch produces reliable enhanced views for all degraded observations, providing pseudo-GT views for subsequent 3D reconstruction. The latter improves 3DGS efficiency by optimizing rasterization, Gaussian memory layout, and parameter updates, reducing redundant computation, memory-access overhead, and optimization costs. Extensive experiments on multiple degraded scenes demonstrate that MLLM-GS effectively handles various severe degradations and achieves high-quality NVS with significantly lower reconstruction time and memory consumption. Project Page: https://wzlwlm13.github.io/MLLM-GS

MReaLLab.title: Video Generation Meets Agent Harness: Agentic Video Generation, Agentic World Modeling and Recursive Self-Improvement
MReaLLab.authors_text: Liaoyuan Fan, Yuhao Zheng, Dongxing Mao, Hangyu Ran, Siyuan Hu
MReaLLab.summary: The paper explores agentic video generation and world modeling through an agent harness, emphasizing recursive self-improvement and essential capabilities for autonomous video production.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Video generation is shifting from end-to-end synthesis toward agentic generation, where planning, tool use, and feedback enable coherent, controllable multi-shot videos. In parallel, video world models provide action-conditioned observations and predicted futures, serving as interactive environments for agents. We study their intersection through the agent harness: an executable runtime that constructs context, exposes tools, maintains state, routes feedback, and manages budgets around video models. This report examines three directions. First, agentic video generation, where harnesses coordinate scripting, shot planning, asset management, production, and editing, alongside the evaluation challenges of these systems. Second, agentic world modeling, where harnesses mediate observation, control, execution, and state. We discuss hybrid designs in which game engines or agent-written programs maintain world state while video models render observations, and how agents and world models can mutually evaluate and improve one another. Third, recursive self-improvement (RSI) in video model development, distinguishing output revisions, updates to harness state, generator parameters, and evaluators, and changes to the improvement procedure itself. We identify how these improvements feed back into subsequent development. Across these directions, we analyze essential agent capabilities, including audiovisual perception, long-horizon planning, memory, code-based interaction, feedback-guided control, skill reuse, and multi-agent coordination. We conclude with challenges in autonomous video production, lifelong memory, programmable hybrid control, autonomous model development, provenance, cost accounting, and evaluation linking video quality and task performance to sustained improvements in models and harnesses.

MReaLLab.title: S3KF: Spherical State-Space Kalman Filtering for Panoramic 3D Multi-Object Tracking
MReaLLab.authors_text: Zhongyuan Liu, Shaonan Yu, Jianping Li, Pengfei Wan, Xinhang Xu
MReaLLab.summary: The S3KF framework utilizes spherical state-space Kalman filtering for accurate, real-time panoramic 3D multi-object tracking, enhancing performance in dynamic environments with LiDAR and camera integration.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Panoramic multi-object tracking is important for industrial safety monitoring, wide-area robotic perception, and infrastructure-light deployment in large workspaces. In these settings, the sensing system must provide full-surround coverage, metric geometric cues, and stable target association under wide field-of-view distortion and occlusion. Existing image-plane trackers are tightly coupled to the camera projection and become unreliable in panoramic imagery, while conventional Euclidean 3D formulations introduce redundant directional parameters and do not naturally unify angular, scale, and depth estimation. In this paper, we present $\mathbf{S^3KF}$, a panoramic 3D multi-object tracking framework built on a motorized rotating LiDAR and a quad-fisheye camera rig. The key idea is a geometry-consistent state representation on the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^2$, where object bearing is modeled by a two-degree-of-freedom tangent-plane parameterization and jointly estimated with box scale and depth dynamics. Based on this state, we derive an extended spherical Kalman filtering pipeline that fuses panoramic camera detections with LiDAR depth observations for multimodal tracking. We further establish a map-based ground-truth generation pipeline using wearable localization devices registered to a shared global LiDAR map, enabling quantitative evaluation without motion-capture infrastructure. Experiments on self-collected real-world sequences show decimeter-level planar tracking accuracy, improved identity continuity over a 2D panoramic baseline in dynamic scenes, and real-time onboard operation on a Jetson AGX Orin platform. These results indicate that the proposed framework is a practical solution for panoramic perception and industrial-scale multi-object tracking.The project page can be found at https://kafeiyin00.github.io/S3KF/.

MReaLLab.title: Goal2Pixel: Grounding Goals to Pixels for Vision-Language Navigation
MReaLLab.authors_text: Muyi Bao, Yuxin Cai, Hang Xu, Zongtai Li, Jinxi He
MReaLLab.summary: Goal2Pixel introduces a pixel-based navigation paradigm for vision-language models, enhancing efficiency and performance in long-horizon navigation by grounding goals to navigable pixels instead of predicting actions.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have become a common foundation for vision-and-language navigation in continuous environments (VLN-CE). Yet most VLM-based methods cast navigation as low-level action prediction, an interface that is ambiguous, tied to short-horizon motion primitives, and inefficient due to repeated VLM querying. We propose Goal2Pixel, a pure pixel-based paradigm that reformulates VLN-CE as navigable pixel grounding. Rather than predicting actions, Goal2Pixel uses the image plane as a unified spatial interface between VLM reasoning and robot motion: the model predicts a visible navigable pixel, which is back-projected into a 3D waypoint for forward navigation. Non-forward actions are encoded by auxiliary left/right/bottom regions for turning and stopping. To support long-horizon navigation, we propose ViKeyMem, a visibility-aware keyframe memory, achieving a favorable performance-efficiency trade-off while reducing training cost by over 50%. To adapt pretrained VLMs to navigable pixel grounding, we introduce semantic embeddings and coordinate-aware auxiliary losses. Among methods trained without external data, Goal2Pixel achieves competitive state-of-the-art performance on R2R-CE and RxR-CE. On R2R-CE Val-Unseen, it achieves 54.1% SR and 52.5% SPL with only 7.75 VLM calls per episode. Compared with direct action prediction, Goal2Pixel improves SR by 21.2 percentage points while requiring 6 times fewer VLM calls. Project Page: https://baobao0926.github.io/Goal2Pixel/.

MReaLLab.title: Multi-Agent Relay Thinking
MReaLLab.authors_text: Xu Liu, Jungang Qiao, Guikun Chen, Xiaojuan Qi, Wenguan Wang
MReaLLab.summary: The paper presents Multi-Agent Confidence-guided Relay (MACR), a framework for dynamic relay collaboration among agents that enhances accuracy and efficiency in multi-agent reasoning tasks.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Existing multi-agent collaboration (MAC) methods have primarily explored a group thinking collaboration topology, where agents independently generate solutions and aggregate their outputs. In this work, we investigate an alternative relay thinking topology, where reasoning ownership is dynamically transferred across agents, allowing subsequent agents to inherit and refine an evolving reasoning trajectory. We introduce Multi-Agent Confidence-guided Relay (MACR), a framework that enables dynamical relay collaboration among agents. The key challenge is determining when reasoning should be relayed and which agent should continue the process. method addresses this challenge through confidence-guided relay triggering and a bidding mechanism that selects the next agent based on its confidence. Experiments on four benchmarks show that method outperforms the strongest single-model strategies in accuracy, e.g., +3.3% on MathVista and +3.9% on MMStar, and remains on par with multi-agent strategies while consuming 6.0x less token overhead on HallusionBench and MMStar. Further analysis demonstrates that relay collaboration enables heterogeneous agents to progressively integrate complementary insights, combining heterogeneous capabilities across reasoning stages. Our source code is available at https://github.com/67L1/MACR.

MReaLLab.title: TOPS: Reshaping Flow Source and Transport for Multi-Task Robot Manipulation
MReaLLab.authors_text: Tuo An, Chuhao Zhou, Jiahua Dong, Jingliang Li, Jiaqi Bai
MReaLLab.summary: TOPS enhances multi-task robot manipulation by adapting flow source priors and schedules for distinct tasks, improving success rates and efficiency without altering network architecture.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Flow-based policies for language-conditioned multi-task manipulation commonly share a single $\textit{Gaussian}$ source prior and a common linear transport path across tasks. However, reliably executing multiple tasks with distinct motion requirements remains challenging for a shared policy. We introduce $\textbf{TOPS}$ ($\textbf{T}$ask-$\textbf{O}$riented $\textbf{P}$riors and $\textbf{S}$chedules), which adapts the flow source prior and interpolation schedule to each task without modifying the network architecture. TOPS first constructs multimodal task sources from reverse-mapped expert action sequences, allowing language instructions to select where generation begins. Guided by source-target covariance mismatch, it then slows the transition toward expert actions early in denoising and accelerates it later along directions requiring expansion. Under a $\textit{Gaussian}$ endpoint model, our analysis shows that this schedule adjustment can lower an upper bound on velocity-prediction risk. Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and CALVIN demonstrate improved performance across in-distribution, perturbation and cross-environment settings, alongside better data efficiency. Using one integration step, TOPS raises LIBERO-10 success from $53.44\%$ to $69.67\%$ compared with ten-step Standard Flow Matching (FM), while reducing inference time to approximately one-sixth of the baseline. TOPS also yields consistent gains when transferred to the large-scale flow-based $π_{0.5}$ policy across all four evaluated settings. Real-world experiments further demonstrate improved task success, including an increase from $20\%$ with standard FM to $80\%$ with TOPS on the upper-drawer opening task.

MReaLLab.title: OmniGlimpse: Asymmetric Identity Memory for Online Multi-View Tracking
MReaLLab.authors_text: Rangya Zhang, Jiaping Xiao, Yujing Shang, Yuhang Zhang, Mingsheng Li
MReaLLab.summary: OmniGlimpse introduces an asymmetric framework for online multi-view tracking, enhancing identity maintenance through adaptive associations and stable memory consolidation without offline training.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Multi-view tracking extends visual coverage beyond a single camera, providing complementary observations when targets are occluded or leave the view. This raises a question: how can observations from different views be matched to the correct identities without offline scene-specific training or camera calibration? Progress toward this goal remains limited because many offline formulations assume such deployment-specific knowledge, while online adaptation can amplify association errors. We study this problem as online multi-view identity maintenance (OMIM): targets are initialized once per view, with no further identity labels provided after each initialization. To this end, we introduce OmniGlimpse, an asymmetric propose-verify framework that separates adaptive association from stable identity consolidation. At the representation level, short-term local and cross-view evidence is mapped into target-specific adaptive spaces to propose associations, whereas long-term identity distributions are maintained for verification in a canonical space defined by a frozen encoder. At the update level, short-term evidence may guide current associations, whereas, after bootstrapping, only verified observations may update persistent memory or drive adaptation. Under a unified target-specified evaluation protocol, OmniGlimpse improves over the best evaluated online baseline for each metric by 9.1 IDF1 and 22.1 CVIDF1 points on M3Track. The corresponding gains on MvMHAT are 20.3 and 26.2 points. Despite using no offline scene-specific training, it outperforms offline-trained references in IDF1 and remains competitive in cross-view association. These results support an approach to online identity maintenance that adapts to changing appearances while consolidating reliable evidence into stable identity anchors.

MReaLLab.title: GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latents as a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents
MReaLLab.authors_text: Bingchao Wang, Yongcheng Jing, Shunyu Liu, Chengyu Wang, Jun Huang
MReaLLab.summary: GUI-JEPA introduces a novel decoder-free policy for mobile GUI agents, significantly improving action selection speed and efficiency using a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Mobile GUI agents are typically fine-tuned 7B-scale vision-language models (VLMs) that generate each action as text. However, these VLMs decode every action token by token, and even agents that score candidate actions keep a large language model or VLM in the loop, making them slow and memory-hungry. To address these issues, we propose GUI-JEPA, to our knowledge the first decoder-free GUI agent policy built on a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA), which selects actions in the latent space of a JEPA encoder pretrained on unlabelled GUI screenshots. Its action- and region-conditioned latent predictor turns the screen latent into one latent per candidate action, letting lightweight heads score all candidates against the instruction in a single batched pass, without decoding a token. We further show that the scorer relies on this latent pathway and that the predictor is trained for the decision itself: a randomly initialised predictor does just as well as one pretrained on screen dynamics. On AndroidControl, GUI-JEPA is 2.8-4.0x faster on the same GPU than a Qwen2.5-VL-7B agent we fine-tune with the same inputs, while reaching 86-92% of its in-distribution accuracy with 6% of its parameters. Code is available at https://github.com/bcwang-sjtu/GUI-JEPA

MReaLLab.title: Keeping Contact: Task-Adaptive Friction Margins for Bimanual Non-Prehensile Manipulation
MReaLLab.authors_text: Qian Ying Lee, Lin Yang, Domenico Campolo
MReaLLab.summary: This paper presents a method for adaptive friction margins in bimanual non-prehensile manipulation, optimizing contact forces to prevent slip and maintain stability during tilting tasks.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Maintaining contact in non-prehensile manipulation requires more than nominal friction cone feasibility: a force barely inside the cone and one well inside it are both feasible, but they provide different margins against slip and contact loss. This paper uses signed friction distance to measure friction margin in force space and derives a task-adaptive margin from the force correction needed to balance pivot moment deviations in bimanual tilting. The resulting contact margins are embedded in a sequence of second-order cone programs (SOCPs), each giving a globally optimal contact force solution at a tilt angle. The optimizer balances the object about an environmental pivot while keeping robot and pivot contact forces away from the nominal friction boundary. Optimizer-level results show interpretable force redistribution and adaptation to object property changes. Real-world experiments demonstrate successful execution under object property variations and model mismatch, while fixed margin and no-margin comparisons illustrate the importance of adapting the margin to task demand. These results support signed friction distance margins as a force planning mechanism for maintaining contact in bimanual non-prehensile manipulation. Project page: https://keeping-contact.github.io/

MReaLLab.title: Ego-CEVR: Learning Cross-Embodiment Visual Representations from Human Egocentric Videos
MReaLLab.authors_text: Keru Zhou, Zhirui Fang, Xinrun Xu, Yaopeng Lou, Zeyuan He
MReaLLab.summary: Ego-CEVR is a framework that leverages egocentric videos to learn hierarchical visual representations for robot manipulation, enhancing task understanding and action alignment.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: As egocentric video becomes increasingly available for embodied learning, an important research question is how to turn this low-cost, scalable source of data into robot manipulation capabilities. Egocentric videos naturally provide rich context for high-level task understanding, while real-robot demonstrations with wrist observations and action annotations provide supervision for fine-grained action alignment. We present Ego-CEVR, a data-native framework for hierarchical visual representation learning that assigns distinct learning objectives to global and interaction representations. The global module learns object relations, task state, and temporal progress through future prediction on egocentric video. The Interaction module interprets wrist observations in global context and learns local alignment and contact cues through robot action supervision. Separate residual paths expose both representations to the action policy, preserving direct access to task context alongside fine-grained execution information. Ego-CEVR supports independent pretraining of its global video module on large-scale human egocentric videos and videos from diverse robot embodiments, without requiring robot action labels or paired wrist observations.

MReaLLab.title: MemPrism: Task-Conditioned Relational Memory Views for Long-Horizon Agents
MReaLLab.authors_text: Bingfan Zeng, Zhisheng Chen, Zhengwei Xie, Bangde Cao, Yuxuan Li
MReaLLab.summary: MemPrism introduces a task-conditioned relational memory framework that enhances long-horizon agent performance by dynamically constructing relevant memory views for decision-making.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Long-horizon agents performing multi-step Web tasks must reuse earlier page observations and interactions to support subsequent actions. However, preserving relevant history does not ensure that it exposes the relations needed for the current decision. We call this gap representation mismatch. To this end, we propose MemPrism, a task-conditioned relational memory framework that separates persistent experience storage from decision-time working memory. MemPrism records interactions as the event stream and dynamically constructs relational views according to the current task context. A lightweight view policy selects the relation structure, evidence range, outcome condition, and granularity, while a deterministic composer and renderer transform historical facts into a temporary optical working-memory view for a frozen task policy. Experiments on long-horizon embodied and web-agent benchmarks show that MemPrism consistently improves the task performance, especially as trajectories become longer, while reducing memory token consumption. Furthermore, the learned view policy transfers across different VLMs without additional adaptation, demonstrating the effectiveness of task-conditioned relational views as a general memory interface for agents.

MReaLLab.title: VideoLVR: Latent Visual Reasoning over Grounded Video Evidence
MReaLLab.authors_text: Shilong Li, Xingyuan Bu, Hao Shi, Yun Xing, Weixin Feng
MReaLLab.summary: VideoLVR enhances multimodal large language models' video understanding by integrating latent visual evidence during reasoning, improving accuracy without significantly increasing context size.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Chain-of-thought reasoning has substantially advanced video understanding in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, language-based reasoning traces do not provide a reliable mechanism for models to revisit relevant visual evidence, leading to visual forgetting and impairing their ability to reason over video content. Existing approaches maintain visual grounding during reasoning in two main ways: they either refer to evidence using textual coordinates, which specify symbolic locations rather than the visual content itself, or reinsert cropped regions or frames into the multimodal context, preserving visual details at the cost of substantial context expansion. To address these limitations, we introduce VideoLVR, which constructs latent visual evidence from local regions at relevant video moments, thereby providing visual support for intermediate reasoning steps. To supervise latent visual evidence generation, we introduce a visual token prediction objective that formulates visual token reconstruction as prediction over a vocabulary derived from the input video, thereby unifying visual evidence reconstruction and text generation within the same token prediction framework. This shared prediction framework enables MLLMs to reason over interleaved text tokens and latent visual states while integrating evidence from different moments. We further extend VideoLVR to reinforcement learning by treating sampled visual tokens as actions alongside text tokens and jointly optimizing the policy using final-answer rewards. By efficiently revisiting task-relevant visual information during reasoning, VideoLVR improves video understanding without substantially expanding the multimodal context. Experiments on multiple video benchmarks demonstrate its effectiveness, especially on tasks requiring fine-grained visual evidence.

MReaLLab.title: 4DMemory: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Spatiotemporal Memory with Harness-Augmented Agents
MReaLLab.authors_text: Yanhao Jia, Yi Zhu, Yiran Zhong, Weigao Sun, Feida Zhu
MReaLLab.summary: The paper introduces the 4DMemory framework and LongVideo dataset to benchmark and enhance long-horizon spatiotemporal reasoning in agents, revealing significant performance improvements with the 4DMemory Harness.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Humans efficiently process multimodal streams spanning hours to years, building persistent, fine-grained spatiotemporal memories that support reasoning about and predicting long-horizon events. In contrast, existing benchmarks focus on short- and medium-context tasks, and most foundation models struggle to preserve fine-grained information over long horizons. To evaluate and improve long-horizon spatiotemporal reasoning, we introduce the LongVideo dataset and the 4DMemoryBench. LongVideo comprises about 900 hours of video and over 5,000 manually reviewed questions covering visual, textual, and spatiotemporal reasoning across diverse context lengths. We further develop the 4DMemory Harness, which integrates four complementary skills, 22+ specialized tool models, and a model-specific retrieval-augmented generation system. Evaluating 13 leading models, we find that standalone foundation models struggle with long-horizon tasks, while the 4DMemory Harness improves all of them by over 50\%. Compared to previous benchmark, the same models exhibit a performance drop of more than 10\% on 4DMemoryBench. We hope 4DMemory will facilitate the development of spatiotemporal agents capable of addressing complex, long-horizon tasks.

MReaLLab.title: Unified Condition-Action Modeling for Accurate One-Step Action Generation
MReaLLab.authors_text: Xinyu Zhou, Zikun Cai, Kuangji Zuo, Gen Li, Boyu Ma
MReaLLab.summary: UCA-Flow introduces a unified condition-action modeling framework that enhances one-step action generation accuracy and speed by jointly representing conditions and actions in a shared token space.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Robot manipulation requires policies that are both accurate and efficient, as robot control must respond to changing observations under tight latency constraints. Recent diffusion and flow policies are promising, but they often treat conditions as auxiliary signals rather than jointly evolving them with action trajectories. We find that this limitation can be effectively mitigated by a simple yet effective unified condition-action modeling design that represents conditions and actions in a shared token space, allowing a compact model to achieve high performance while improving both inference speed and accuracy. Therefore, we propose UCA-Flow, a unified condition-action modeling framework for accurate one-step action generation. Our method unifies observation conditions, timestep conditions, interval conditions, and action tokens into a single sequence, and processes them with a Unified Condition-Action Transformer for joint condition-action representation learning. As a result, condition representations are dynamically reconstructed according to the current generation stage, highlighting information most relevant for action refinement. Furthermore, we introduce an improved dual-pass supervision scheme over $u$ and $v$ for stronger optimization of unified condition-action modeling. UCA-Flow achieves an average success rate of 86.4%, improving over the strongest baseline by 7.5 percentage points, with a task-averaged inference latency of $3.0$ ms. It achieves $43.9\times$ and $32.2\times$ speedups over DP3 and Simple DP3, and remains $4.2\times$ and $2.2\times$ faster than one-step FlowPolicy and MP1, respectively. Project page: https://uca-policy.github.io/UCA.github.io/

MReaLLab.title: FlowCritic: Bridging Value Estimation with Flow Matching in Reinforcement Learning
MReaLLab.authors_text: Shan Zhong, Shutong Ding, He Diao, Xiangyu Wang, Kah Chan Teh
MReaLLab.summary: FlowCritic introduces a generative approach to value estimation in reinforcement learning by utilizing flow matching to model and sample complex value distributions.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Reliable value estimation serves as the cornerstone of reinforcement learning (RL) by evaluating long-term returns and guiding policy improvement, significantly influencing the convergence speed and final performance. Existing works improve the reliability of value function estimation via multi-critic ensembles and distributional RL, yet the former merely combines multi point estimation without capturing distributional information, whereas the latter relies on discretization or quantile regression, limiting the expressiveness of complex value distributions. Inspired by flow matching's success in generative modeling, we propose a generative paradigm for value estimation, named FlowCritic. Departing from conventional regression for deterministic value prediction, FlowCritic leverages flow matching to model value distributions and generate samples for value estimation.

MReaLLab.title: Dual-Arm Box Manipulation via Online Inertial Estimation and Convex Wrench Optimization
MReaLLab.authors_text: Kenzhi Iskandar Wong, Lin Yang, Qian Ying Lee, Domenico Campolo
MReaLLab.summary: This paper introduces a dual-arm manipulation framework that employs online inertial estimation and convex optimization to stably lift and transport objects with unknown mass and center of mass.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Dual-arm robotic manipulation often requires lifting and transporting objects whose mass and center of mass are not known in advance. These uncertainties affect the force-moment balance required for stable lifting, and improper regulation of contact wrenches can lead to slip, object drop, orientation deviation, or excessive squeezing. This paper presents a friction-aware dual-arm box-manipulation framework for objects with unknown inertial properties. The framework combines online inertial estimation with convex contact-wrench optimization. The inertial estimation module estimates the object mass and center of mass from measured contact wrenches, while the optimization module computes friction-feasible contact forces and torsional moments through a second-order cone program (SOCP) under ellipsoidal friction-limit-surface constraints. An offline trajectory refinement stage is also included to reduce undesired object-environment contact when geometric constraints are present. By enforcing friction feasibility as a hard constraint and minimizing contact effort within the feasible region, the framework achieves stable lifting without treating slip avoidance and excessive squeezing as separately tuned objectives. Experiments on a real dual-arm robotic system under different center-of-mass configurations demonstrate that the method lifts objects with unknown inertial properties while maintaining stable frictional contact.

MReaLLab.title: MoRE: Motion-Regularized Encoding for Articulated 3D Generation
MReaLLab.authors_text: Guantian Zheng, Shan Jin
MReaLLab.summary: MoRE introduces a motion-regularized encoding method for generating articulated 3D objects from images, enhancing joint attribute reconstruction and motion accuracy compared to existing approaches.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Generating an articulated object from a single image requires recovering both its appearance and the mechanism governing its parts. A compact encoding of joint attributes does not by itself ensure that reconstruction preserves the resulting motion. We present MoRE, Motion-Regularized Encoding for articulated 3D generation. MoRE represents coordinate-aligned joint lines with axis classification and two axis-orthogonal Plücker moment coefficients, removing the arbitrary choice of an origin along the axis. During representation learning, decoded joint hypotheses are used to move corresponding three-dimensional anchors, and their motions are compared with those of annotated joints. A differentiable expectation over joint types and axis directions couples attribute reconstruction to the motion it induces. An image-conditioned flow learns the resulting functional latents, while a multi-state-adapted Gaussian model supplies appearance. At inference, recovered part assignments and joints articulate a single set of rest-pose Gaussians without regenerating the object for each state. Experiments on PartNet-Mobility and ACD show stronger part-box agreement, articulated-state geometry and visual similarity than the compared baselines, while joint prediction reduces axis, origin and range errors relative to ArtiLatent. Controlled ablations support the joint-line encoding and show that motion supervision reduces anchor-motion error. Code and pretrained checkpoints will be released in the future.

MReaLLab.title: DeXplicit: Making Physical State Explicit in Dexterous Manipulation World Models
MReaLLab.authors_text: Adam Lee, Mutian Xu, Yukang Cao, Shulin Tian, Ziwei Liu
MReaLLab.summary: DeXplicit introduces a 3D dynamics network for dexterous manipulation, enhancing object motion prediction and video generation efficiency while improving accuracy and fidelity in scene rendering.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Before acting on an object, a robot needs to anticipate how its hand motion will change the physical world and what the resulting scene will look like. Existing approaches typically entangle action-conditioned dynamics, camera motion, and visual synthesis within a video generation model, or represent dynamics as point trajectories without explicit object structure. We introduce DeXplicit, a dexterous manipulation world model that instead predicts how the world evolves explicitly in metric 3D before rendering its visual consequences. Given an initial scene and a future hand trajectory, a lightweight 3D dynamics network predicts object-centric motion and deformation, providing structured and geometrically grounded future world states. These predictions then serve as a strong scaffold for video generation: appearance is transported through the predicted 3D motion and projected into future views, allowing the renderer to focus on completing uncertain and newly visible content rather than implicitly learning world dynamics from pixels. This explicit-3D-first decomposition also enables efficient causal generation, requiring only two denoising steps per block while conditioning on generated history. Across HOT3D, OakInk2, and PhysTwin, DeXplicit reduces moved-point error by 27-40% relative to PointWorld and improves object fidelity IoU+ by 47% on HOT3D under a shared renderer. Our design with two-step causal generation achieves a 57x speedup from our 14B bi-directional configuration in video synthesis.

MReaLLab.title: SkillFlow: Flow-Driven Recursive Skill Evolution for Agentic Orchestration
MReaLLab.authors_text: Mingda Zhang, Tiesunlong Shen, Haoran Luo, Wenjin Liu, Zikai Xiao
MReaLLab.summary: SkillFlow introduces a flow-based framework for agentic task orchestration, enhancing skill evolution and credit assignment while outperforming existing methods across various complex tasks.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: In recent years, a variety of powerful LLM-based agentic systems have been applied to automate complex tasks through task orchestration. However, existing orchestration methods still face key challenges, including strategy collapse under reward maximization, high gradient variance with opaque credit assignment, and unguided skill evolution whose decisions are typically made by directly prompting an LLM to judge rather than derived from principled training signals. To address these challenges, we propose SkillFlow, a flow-based framework that takes a trainable Supervisor as the agent and a structured environment with dynamic skill library and frozen executor, automating task orchestration through multi-turn interaction. SkillFlow employs Tempered Trajectory Balance (TTB), a regression-based flow-matching loss that samples trajectories proportional to reward, preserving diverse orchestration strategies rather than collapsing to a single mode. The same flow objective yields a jointly learned backward policy that provides transparent per-step credit assignment at zero additional inference cost. Building on these flow diagnostics, a recursive skill evolution mechanism determines when to evolve, what skills to create or prune, and where decision gaps lie -- closing the loop from training signal to autonomous capability growth. Experimental results on 14 datasets show that SkillFlow significantly outperforms baselines across question answering, mathematical reasoning, code generation, and real-world interactive decision making tasks. Our code is available at https://github.com/beita6969/SkillFlow.

MReaLLab.title: Demonstration-Based Robotic Feeding Using Dynamic Movement Primitives
MReaLLab.authors_text: Kenzhi Iskandar Wong, Kitti Thamrongaphichartkul, Sri Harsha Turlapati, Yanshuo Lu, Kanichi Doi
MReaLLab.summary: This paper introduces a robotic feeding framework that utilizes human demonstrations and Dynamic Movement Primitives for motion planning, integrating vision-based perception and control for effective task execution.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: This paper presents a demonstration-based robotic feeding framework that integrates human demonstration, Dynamic Movement Primitive-based motion planning, vision-based scene perception, and robot control. A human operator first demonstrates the scooping and feeding motions while the position and Euler-angle orientation of the spoon are recorded using a motion-capture system. The recorded trajectory is segmented into scooping and feeding motions, which are encoded using separate Dynamic Movement Primitives. Before task execution, an RGB-D camera estimates the participant's mouth position, while two AprilTags are used for robot-frame registration and tray localization. The detected tray pose is used to position the scooping motion, whereas the detected mouth position defines the positional goal of the feeding motion. The approach, scooping, and feeding trajectories are then executed sequentially by a Kinova Gen3 manipulator through a ROS~2-based framework. A real-world experiment demonstrates the feasibility of the integrated pipeline and shows that the learned spoon motions can be reproduced within the detected experimental scene.

MReaLLab.title: HiP3R: Hierarchical Pose Graphs for Long-Horizon 3D Reconstruction
MReaLLab.authors_text: Zunnan Xu, Shangchen Zhou, Yihang Luo, Chen Change Loy
MReaLLab.summary: HiP3R introduces a hierarchical pose graph approach that optimizes camera trajectories and 3D reconstruction by balancing global consistency and local flexibility in long video sequences.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Feed-forward models accurately estimate camera motion and 3D geometry from short video windows. However, computational and memory costs prevent direct inference on sequences containing thousands of frames. Long videos must therefore be processed as overlapping chunks. This division produces independent local reconstructions with inconsistent coordinate frames and duplicate estimates of shared cameras. Achieving global consistency requires propagating constraints from adjacent overlaps and distant revisits across the sequence. This requirement naturally motivates pose graph optimization. However, the choice of graph level creates a trade-off. Chunk-level graphs efficiently resolve scale drift and close large loops. Yet, their rigid transformations cannot correct internal errors or conflicting frame predictions. Conversely, frame-level optimization offers local flexibility, but scaling it globally is computationally expensive and can break metric scale. HiP3R resolves this trade-off using a hierarchical pose graph. HiP3R first optimizes a robust chunk-level $\mathrm{Sim}(3)$ graph to establish the global layout and scale. It then holds this layout fixed and estimates one shared $\mathrm{SE}(3)$ camera per frame, turning overlapping window predictions into a single trajectory. Experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of HiP3R in improving camera trajectories and 3D reconstruction. Our method applies to both chunk-based and streaming backends without additional training or fine-tuning. The codes are available at https://kkakkkka.github.io/HiP3R.

MReaLLab.title: DailyBench: A Unified Benchmark for AI-Generated and Manipulated Images from Modern Generative Models
MReaLLab.authors_text: Xin Jiang, Hao Tang, Junyao Gao, Zijie Yang, Meiqi Cao
MReaLLab.summary: DailyBench is a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate AI-generated image detectors' effectiveness against modern synthesis and manipulation techniques, revealing significant robustness gaps in current detection methods.
MReaLLab.debug_abstract: Recent advances in generative models have shifted AI-generated image detection from identifying easily distinguishable, fully synthetic images to identifying highly realistic content generated by both modern generation and manipulation pipelines. However, existing detection benchmarks are often built with outdated generative models and primarily emphasize full-image synthesis, creating a growing mismatch between benchmark data and the images encountered in real-world generation and editing scenarios. To bridge this gap, we introduce DailyBench, a high-quality unified benchmark for evaluating whether AI-generated image detectors can generalize across both modern full-image synthesis and object-level manipulation. DailyBench contains two complementary subsets: FakeBench, which includes high-quality images synthesized by recent open-source and commercial generative models, and ManipulationBench, which introduces challenging object-level edits applied to real images using advanced image-conditional models. This design makes DailyBench a realistic testbed for studying both generator-level generalization and manipulation-aware detection under subtle local edits. Experiments on DailyBench reveal substantial robustness gaps in current detectors: methods reporting 91-96% balanced accuracy on GenImage drop to 52-79% on FakeBench and 43-67% on ManipulationBench. These results show that existing detectors remain poorly generalized to realistic synthesis and manipulation, highlighting DailyBench as a rigorous testbed for developing robust and manipulation-aware AI-generated image detection methods. The project is available at https://dailybench.github.io/

MReaLLab.title: Dual Exam: Controlled Evaluation of Multimodal Agents and World Models
MReaLLab.authors_text: Zhefan Rao, Meng Chu, Xuan Zhang, Jingfan Chen, Guohao Cai
MReaLLab.summary: The paper presents Dual Exam, a framework for evaluating the interaction between Multimodal Agents and World Models across various domains, revealing performance inconsistencies and challenges in reciprocal learning.
