机器人控制实验室.summary: The Stateful Harness framework enhances world models by decoupling state evolution from video rendering, enabling rule-governed interactions that effectively handle hidden states.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Existing world models can generate action-conditioned video from a single image. Many focus on camera movement, allowing users to explore the generated scene. However, navigation alone does not ensure that an action follows persistent rules when its outcome depends on state that is invisible in the current frame. We present Stateful Harness, a framework that separates world evolution from video rendering to support stateful and rule-governed interaction. It maintains an evolving world state under specified rules, renders each resulting event with a frozen video model, and uses the generated clip to update the world state for the next turn. At each turn, the harness resolves the action selected by the user and compiles the resulting event into an instruction, while a preview clip from an editable 3D scene provides spatial and camera guidance. To evaluate rule compliance, we build WorldState-Bench, a benchmark of 50 counterfactual twin pairs that share an initial frame and action but differ in hidden state and required outcome. Under rule-only prompting, the best of the 11 evaluated video backends produces the required endings for both cases in 32% of pairs. For MiniMax-H3, specifying the required endings raises this rate from 32% to 64%, while the full harness reaches 92% with the same frozen model. These results support separating rule execution from video rendering for world interactions with hidden state.

机器人控制实验室.title: GPT-6 Astra Is a Native Visuo-Tactile Policy for Contact-Rich Manipulation
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Chen Yang, Linzhe Shi, Hang Zhang, Mu Xu, Jiansheng Fan
机器人控制实验室.summary: GPT-6 Astra demonstrates effective visuo-tactile manipulation by interpreting tactile images for contact-rich tasks, outperforming specialist policies and suggesting potential for joint visual-tactile pretraining.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Recent advances in multimodal models have enabled GPT-6 Astra to perform robotic manipulation through in-context learning. Yet contact-rich control and tactile perception are often regarded as strengths of specialist policies, leaving open whether Astra can directly understand and use tactile observations. We provide, to our knowledge, the first demonstration that Astra directly interprets vision-based tactile images and uses their contact cues for manipulation. Tactile RGB images enter through its existing visual interface, enabling few-shot closed-loop control on nineteen simulated UniVTAC and OpenViTac tasks with 210 sampled scene seeds per setting. With visuo-tactile input, Astra achieves mean success rates of 93.8% and 81.8%, exceeding the strongest reported specialist baselines in our comparison by 22.9 and 13.1 percentage points, respectively. Vision-only performance also leads these baselines, reaching 76.3% and 80.6%. Trajectory analysis reveals active probing, cautious grasping, contact-guided alignment, and recovery, alongside difficulties with tangential loading and corrective execution. Our findings challenge the exclusivity of specialist policies in contact-rich manipulation and show that fine-grained vision can partially compensate for missing touch. They also identify vision-based tactile sensing as an interface for scaling contact understanding with foundation models and reveal signs of benchmark saturation. These results motivate joint visual-tactile pretraining, harder contact-rich evaluations, and physical-robot validation.

机器人控制实验室.title: Ropedia W0: Scaling Loco-Manipulation World Models across Embodiments with Human Experience
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Tianqi Liu, Hanfei Zhao, Qifeng Liang, Hui En Pang, Jiarui Xu
机器人控制实验室.summary: Ropedia W0 introduces a unified loco-manipulation world model leveraging extensive egocentric data to enhance performance across diverse human and robotic embodiments in real-time interactions.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: World models enable embodied agents to anticipate action consequences, yet jointly modeling locomotion and manipulation across diverse embodiments remains challenging due to heterogeneous action spaces and limited multimodal supervision. We present Ropedia W0, the first egocentric loco-manipulation world foundation model spanning humans and robots with diverse embodiments. We curate Xp-Data, comprising 10k hours of egocentric human data and 3k hours of robot data with unified multimodal annotations and systematic quality control. A unified kinematic representation encodes locomotion through camera poses and manipulation through projected skeletons, with robot skeletons combining embodiment-specific forward kinematics with extensive manual keypoint annotation and correction. We also introduce Xp-Teleop, a long-horizon loco-manipulation benchmark based on high-quality dexterous humanoid teleoperation data. Evaluations demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across five cross-embodiment benchmarks (DreamDojo, $Ψ_0$, $ω$-HOME, Xp-Teleop, and AgiBot) and on held-out human egocentric video, from zero-shot inference to few-shot and full-data post-training. Scaling human pre-training data improves performance on both human and robot evaluations. After distillation, our model supports real-time, minute-long rollouts, enabling live VR interaction. Applications in policy evaluation, model-based planning, and world-action modeling further demonstrate the model's utility for embodied decision-making.

机器人控制实验室.title: GazeAgent: VLM-Guided Implicit Gaze Calibration from Egocentric Multimodal Behavior for AI Glasses
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Yuhong Zhang, Khanh An Nguyen, Xinyu Tian, KungYi Chang, Abraham Padua
机器人控制实验室.summary: GazeAgent is a VLM-guided framework that enhances gaze calibration in AI glasses by adaptively utilizing multimodal behavior without user interruption, significantly improving accuracy.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: AI glasses typically require explicit, user-specific eye-tracker calibration, and accuracy can drift when the device shifts during use. We present GazeAgent, a VLM-guided framework that continuously and adaptively improves gaze-calibration accuracy from naturally occurring behavior without asking users to interrupt their activities. GazeAgent identifies precise visual attention (PVA) events from multimodal streams of inertial measurement unit (IMU), gaze, and wearer-hand signals, validates their task relevance, and localizes functional targets as pseudo-calibration targets. In a 10-participant scripted study, the system detected all 820 predefined PVA opportunities and, under device disturbance, reduced median gaze error by 44.1% compared with explicit calibration. In a five-participant case study, autonomous calibration produced the lowest workload and interruption ratings, and all participants preferred it for routine use. By deriving task-critical targets from natural multimodal behavior, GazeAgent demonstrates the potential for continuous, adaptive, and low-burden gaze interaction on egocentric AI glasses.

机器人控制实验室.title: Latent-WAM: Latent World Action Modeling for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Linbo Wang, Yupeng Zheng, Qiang Chen, Shiwei Li, Yichen Zhang
机器人控制实验室.summary: Latent-WAM introduces a novel autonomous driving framework utilizing spatially-aware latent representations for improved trajectory planning, achieving state-of-the-art results with fewer resources.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: We introduce Latent-WAM, an efficient end-to-end autonomous driving framework that achieves strong trajectory planning through spatially-aware and dynamics-informed latent world representations. Existing world-model-based planners suffer from inadequately compressed representations, limited spatial understanding, and underutilized temporal dynamics, resulting in sub-optimal planning under constrained data and compute budgets. Latent-WAM addresses these limitations with two core modules: a Spatial-Aware Compressive World Encoder (SCWE) that distills geometric knowledge from a foundation model and compresses multi-view images into compact scene tokens via learnable queries, and a Dynamic Latent World Model (DLWM) that employs a causal Transformer to autoregressively predict future world status conditioned on historical visual and ego status representations. Extensive experiments on NAVSIM v2 and HUGSIM demonstrate new state-of-the-art results: 89.3 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 and 28.9 HD-Score on HUGSIM, surpassing the best prior perception-free method by 3.2 EPDMS with significantly less training data and a compact 104M-parameter model. The code and model weights have been open-sourced at https://github.com/yukki555/Latent-WAM.

机器人控制实验室.title: MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Junxi Wang, Te Sun, Jiayi Zhu, Chen Zhang, Siyuan Li
机器人控制实验室.summary: MemForest is a memory compression framework that efficiently partitions and merges agent memory, achieving significant storage reduction and retrieval speedup while maintaining high performance.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Agent memory systems have demonstrated significant potential in long-term dialogue, personalized assistants, and video understanding. However, continuously accumulated memory introduces substantial storage and retrieval costs during inference. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{MemForest}, a general memory compression framework adaptable to various agent memory systems. Specifically, MemForest partitions historical memory into event-centric units by leveraging global semantic similarity and local temporal continuity. For each unit, it constructs a maximum spanning tree, termed an EventTree, and progressively merges redundant memory nodes by selecting high-weight edges, reducing storage overhead. Furthermore, we introduce an anchor-guided propagation retrieval mechanism that retrieves relevant memory nodes from the temporal neighborhoods of key nodes, improving retrieval accuracy. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of MemForest. Under the unimodal Mem0 framework, MemForest retains \textbf{97.1%} of the original performance while compressing \textbf{50%} of historical memory across three benchmarks (LoCoMo, LongMemEval, and PersonaMem), achieving a \textbf{1.89x} retrieval speedup. Under the multimodal M3-Agent framework, it preserves \textbf{99.7%} of the original performance with a \textbf{50%} compression ratio across two benchmarks (M3-Bench-robot and M3-Bench-web), achieving a \textbf{2.24x} retrieval speedup. \textcolor{RoyalBlue}{\textit{Our code is available at [https://github.com/Celina-love-sweet/MemForest.}}](https://github.com/Celina-love-sweet/MemForest.}})

机器人控制实验室.title: MVISTA-4D: View-Consistent 4D World Model with Test-Time Action Inference for Robotic Manipulation
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Jiaxu Wang, Yicheng Jiang, Tianlun He, Jingkai Sun, Qiang Zhang
机器人控制实验室.summary: MVISTA-4D introduces a view-consistent 4D world model for robotic manipulation, enabling comprehensive scene dynamics prediction and optimized action inference from single-view RGBD inputs.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: World-model-based imagine-then-act becomes a promising paradigm for robotic manipulation, yet existing approaches typically support either purely image-based forecasting or reasoning over partial 3D geometry, limiting their ability to predict complete 4D scene dynamics. This work proposes a novel embodied 4D world model that enables geometrically consistent, arbitrary-view RGBD generation: given only a single-view RGBD observation as input, the model imagines the remaining viewpoints, which can then be back-projected and fused to assemble a more complete 3D structure across time. To efficiently learn the multi-view, cross-modality generation, we explicitly design cross-view and cross-modality feature fusion that jointly encourage consistency between RGB and depth and enforce geometric alignment across views. Beyond prediction, converting generated futures into actions is often handled by inverse dynamics, which is ill-posed because multiple actions can explain the same transition. We address this with a test-time action optimization strategy that backpropagates through the generative model to infer a trajectory-level latent best matching the predicted future, and a residual inverse dynamics model that turns this trajectory prior into accurate executable actions. Experiments on three datasets demonstrate strong performance on both 4D scene generation and downstream manipulation, and ablations provide practical insights into the key design choices.

机器人控制实验室.title: Benchmarking the Limits of In-Context Reinforcement Learning for Ad-Hoc Teamwork
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Yuheng Jing, Kai Li, Ziwen Zhang, Jiajun Zhang, Zeyao Ma
机器人控制实验室.summary: The paper introduces the ICRL4AHT benchmark to evaluate In-Context Reinforcement Learning's limitations in Ad-Hoc Teamwork, revealing poor adaptation in multi-agent scenarios despite success in single-agent tasks.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: In-Context Reinforcement Learning (ICRL) has enabled foundation agents to adapt instantaneously to novel tasks, yet its efficacy in Ad-Hoc Teamwork (AHT)-where coordination with unknown partners is required-remains unexplored. To rigorously evaluate this, we introduce a large-scale benchmark ICRL4AHT, built upon a high-throughput JAX implementation of Overcooked-V2. Our benchmark includes a large, diverse teammate suite spanning both RL and heuristic policies, enabling controlled train-test shifts, and provides a reproducible end-to-end pipeline for teammate generation, learning-history collection, dataset construction, and online multi-episode evaluation. We evaluate representative history-conditioned ICRL algorithms, including Algorithm Distillation (AD) and Decision-Pretrained Transformer (DPT), across millions of transitions. Results reveal notable limitations: contrary to their success in single-agent domains, these baselines fail to exhibit robust test-time adaptation in multi-agent settings. Specifically, these methods frequently underperform random baselines across both unseen teammate and unseen layout tracks, with no clear in-context improvement over long horizons. These findings highlight the challenges of strategic inference under partial observability within the OvercookedV2 AHT protocol, establishing our benchmark as a critical testbed for next-generation coordination algorithms.

机器人控制实验室.title: ELAN4D: Embodiment-Centric 4D Supervision for Vision-Language-Action Models via Plug-and-Play Adaptation
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Zeyuan He, Bowen Yang, Zhirui Fang, Keru Zhou, Lei Jiang
机器人控制实验室.summary: ELAN4D enhances Vision-Language-Action models by integrating 4D predictive supervision from robot keypoint tracks, improving robustness and generalization in robotic manipulation tasks.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown promise for robotic manipulation, yet most existing policies operate reactively by directly regressing actions from current observations, without explicitly modeling future dynamics. This limits their ability to generalize under out-of-distribution perturbations. To address this issue, we propose ELAN4D, an embodiment-centric, 4D-aware training framework that enhances VLA policies with future robot keypoint tracks as predictive spatio-temporal supervision. Using only forward kinematics from proprioceptive states, we derive 3D displacement tracks of robot keypoints, such as joints and the end-effector, with negligible preprocess cost. These tracks provide metric and compact supervision without requiring external trackers or reconstruction. A plug-and-play auxiliary branch with a lightweight track decoder injects this 4D signal into the action expert while preserving the pretrained vision-language backbone through gradient isolation. The track decoder is discarded during inference, leaving the base policy interface unchanged. Extensive experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin2.0 and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate that ELAN4D consistently improves over strong VLA baselines, achieving the best overall performance and substantial gains under out-of-distribution perturbations, including camera, background, and layout shifts. These results highlight the effectiveness of embodiment-centric 4D supervision for building more robust and generalizable manipulation policies.

机器人控制实验室.title: When Seeing Is Not Believing -- A Benchmark for Search-Grounded Video Misinformation Detection
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Tao Yu, Yujia Yang, Shenghua Chai, Jinshuai Zhang, Haopeng Jin
机器人控制实验室.summary: The paper presents EVID-Bench, a benchmark for detecting video misinformation through cross-video comparison, revealing significant challenges in current multimodal models' accuracy.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Video misinformation increasingly operates at the semantic and evidential level: authentic footage may be selectively edited, temporally reordered, spliced across sources, or augmented with AI-generated content to construct false narratives. Such evidence-dependent manipulations cannot be reliably verified from the input video alone, because the missing, reordered, replaced, or recontextualized evidence lies outside the video itself. We introduce \textbf{EVID-Bench}, a benchmark for search-grounded video misinformation detection, where a system must search the open web for related videos and identify what information is false through cross-video comparison. EVID-Bench comprises 222 videos spanning 9 manipulation types across 3 categories: AI generation, single-source editing, and multi-source editing. All samples are verified to be undetectable by frontier models through visual inspection alone. We evaluate nine frontier multimodal models using a retrieval-augmented verification baseline. The best system achieves only 61.43\% point-level accuracy and 43.24\% video-level accuracy, while AI-generated manipulations remain especially challenging. Error analysis reveals recurring challenges: models fixate on irrelevant anchors, misattribute synthetic content to editorial splicing, and terminate search prematurely before fully explaining the manipulation.

机器人控制实验室.title: Humanoid Badminton: Learning Dynamic Racket Skills from Limited Human Motion Data
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Jingzhi Cui, Zhexiong Wang, Bangjie Xu, Pengyu Zhao, Youyuan Li
机器人控制实验室.summary: This paper presents a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework enabling humanoid robots to perform dynamic badminton skills and engage in multi-skill rallies with humans.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: High-speed racket sports provide a demanding testbed for humanoid robots, requiring time-critical decisions, precise striking, and dynamic whole-body coordination. In badminton, fast-changing shuttle trajectories require timely contact decisions, while successful returns demand precise racket pose and velocity within a brief contact window and across a broad three-dimensional striking workspace. Human motion data provide valuable priors for such athletic skills, but usable badminton references are limited and imperfect. Direct tracking provides insufficient executable variation for diverse shuttle conditions, while purely task-driven optimization may produce unnatural motion. We therefore present a three-stage hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for dynamic humanoid badminton. First, task-randomized motion augmentation expands sparse annotated hitting events into executable target-conditioned stroke variations, forming a continuous latent skill space. Second, a high-level planner outputs continuous latent skill codes to compose these skills online according to the observed shuttle state. Third, a context-conditioned adversarial regularizer encourages more natural planner-level skill usage while preserving return performance. In real-world deployment, our system sustains multi-skill rallies with human players, including forehand, backhand, and highly dynamic jump returns. This is the first real-world humanoid racket-sport system to demonstrate multi-skill human--robot rallies including highly dynamic jump returns.

机器人控制实验室.title: ActiveMem: Dynamic Latent Memory Trees for Long-Horizon Agents
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Song-Li Wu, Jingyi Wang, Zhaocheng Du, Weinan Gan
机器人控制实验室.summary: ActiveMem introduces a hierarchical memory framework that enhances long-horizon reasoning in agents by organizing experiences into dependency-aware trees, improving task completion and memory efficiency.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on external memory to support long-horizon reasoning and decision making. Existing memory systems typically retrieve historical trajectories or summaries as independent context fragments, overlooking the procedural dependencies underlying multi-step execution. As memory scales, such flat retrieval introduces context fragmentation and cross-task interference, leading to structurally inconsistent reasoning trajectories. We propose ActiveMem, a hierarchical memory framework that recursively organizes agent experiences into dependency-aware latent execution trees. ActiveMem abstracts trajectories into reusable subtask nodes while explicitly preserving execution transitions, enabling coherent reasoning-path retrieval conditioned on the current execution state. To support continual adaptation, ActiveMem further learns dynamic memory expansion, retrieval, and pruning policies through reinforcement learning. Experiments across various agent benchmarks demonstrate that ActiveMem consistently improves task completion, reasoning stability, and memory efficiency over existing memory-based agents. Moreover, ActiveMem enables compact open-weight models to achieve competitive performance with substantially larger proprietary systems.

机器人控制实验室.title: VeriCUA: Learning Proactive Verification for Reliable GUI Agent Rewards
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Zhizhou Wang, Yaxi Lu, Zhong Zhang, Zikun Hu, Xin Cong
机器人控制实验室.summary: VeriCUA introduces a proactive reward agent that optimizes verification strategies for GUI agents, significantly improving task success and efficiency over existing methods.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning for computer-use agents increasingly relies on proactive reward agents that interact with the post-execution GUI environment to verify what recorded screenshots cannot reveal. The reliability of such verification hinges on two coupled decisions: what to check and when to stop. Existing methods leave these decisions to prompted foundation models. However, neither scaling up the model nor providing few-shot examples reliably improves verification: prompted Judges ranging from 4B to GPT-5.4 all plateau at 68%-70% macro-average agreement. This is because the value of a check depends on the environment rather than the task alone, and becomes apparent only through execution. Learning from execution is itself constrained, as the Actor's terminal state cannot be faithfully replicated during training, allowing only one verification attempt per state. We introduce VeriCUA, a proactive reward agent that learns its verification strategy from these single attempts. A trainable Judge decides what to check and when to stop, while a frozen Probe executes the checks in the live environment. Online reinforcement learning optimizes the Judge for both verdict correctness and efficient Probe use, with returns normalized across terminal states. Trained only on OSWorld and evaluated without further training on MobileWorld and WebArena-Verified, VeriCUA achieves the highest reward agreement across all three benchmarks and lies on the agreement-cost Pareto frontier among proactive verifiers. It surpasses few-shot GPT-5.4 by 5.36 points with 47.6%-59.8% fewer Probe tokens, and even a 1B VeriCUA exceeds every prompted Judge. As the reward for Actor RL, it raises task success by 3.21 points overall and 5.40 points on held-out multi-application tasks. These results identify the verification strategy, not verifier scale, as the key to reliable GUI rewards.

机器人控制实验室.title: PrismWAM: Decoupling State Representations in World Action Models
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Tianyu Xin, Wanqi Zhong, Bowen Hu, Zhangchi Guo, Lijie Wang
机器人控制实验室.summary: PrismWAM decouples semantic and physical state representations in World Action Models, enhancing manipulation performance by focusing on action-driven world evolution without extensive pretraining.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) typically represent the world through latent embeddings from pretrained video models, which entangle heterogeneous aspects of the world, from how it looks (e.g., texture and color) to how it is physically configured (e.g., occupancy and pose). This raises an underexplored question: $\textbf{what should constitute the state of a WAM?}$ We argue that the world state should separate how the world appears from how the world evolves under action: the former captures semantic context, while the latter is governed by physical state. To this end, we propose $\textbf{PrismWAM}$, which decouples physics from semantics while jointly modeling state and action. PrismWAM factorizes an embodied task into a $\mathrm{Semantic\ Planning}\rightarrow\mathrm{Physical\ Rollout}\rightarrow\mathrm{Executable\ Action}$ pipeline: given only the initial RGB observation, semantic planning learns to predict the final goal image, while physical rollout predicts the fine-grained evolution toward this goal in depth space; executable actions are then generated from the depth rollout. Without any embodied action pretraining or additional data augmentation, PrismWAM achieves strong manipulation performance in both simulation and the real world. Notably, PrismWAM even surpasses a broad range of models with large-scale embodied action pretraining (e.g., OpenWAM-$α$). More broadly, we reframe World Action Models from modeling how the world looks to how it responds to action, paving the way for action-centric world models grounded in occupancy, flow, tactile sensing, proprioception, and beyond.

机器人控制实验室.title: HAF-VLA: Hierarchical Action Flow Framework for Humanoid Vision-Language-Action Control
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Langzhe Gu, Chengkai Hou, Meng Li, Xinhua Wang, Xinyuan Lv
机器人控制实验室.summary: HAF-VLA is a hierarchical framework that enhances humanoid robots' vision-language-action control by progressively refining locomotion and manipulation actions through cross-stage conditioning.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Humanoid robots hold great promise as general-purpose agents in human-centered environments, yet adapting generalist vision-language-action (VLA) policies to real-world humanoid loco-manipulation remains challenging. Unlike fixed-base or wheeled manipulators, humanoids must coordinate locomotion, posture, gaze, and dual-arm manipulation over a high-dimensional whole-body action space, where inaccurate base or waist motions can easily induce unstable and aggressive upper-body compensation. We propose HAF-VLA, a hierarchical action-flow framework for humanoid VLA control. Built upon a pretrained flow-matching VLA, HAF-VLA inherits the vision-language prefix encoder and action expert weights, and adapts them to humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation with learnable stage embeddings and cross-stage KV-cache conditioning. Instead of generating the full action chunk in a single pass, HAF-VLA progressively denoises a shared whole-body action space: first locomotion and head commands, then waist refinement, and finally full-body manipulation. To preserve structural dependencies across stages, we introduce a cross-stage KV cache conditioning mechanism, enabling subsequent action generation stages to refine and augment their outputs based on the action representations from preceding stages. Experimental results across six real-world tasks demonstrate that our framework significantly enhances the performance of existing models in humanoid loco-manipulation tasks, demonstrating an effective pathway for adapting strong mobile-manipulation VLAs to humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation.

机器人控制实验室.title: Drive2Gauss: FeedForward 4D Gaussian Reconstruction from Multimodal Generative Driving Videos
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Tong Zhao, Zhiyuan Han, Lin Chen, Bowen Xie, Yunxi Qiao
机器人控制实验室.summary: Drive2Gauss introduces a feedforward framework for dynamic 4D Gaussian scene reconstruction from multimodal driving videos, enhancing efficiency and rendering capabilities without optimization.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Generating reusable driving environments requires both controllable future observations and an explicit representation that supports rendering from different viewpoints, yet existing methods still recover explicit scenes from generated RGB videos through optimization for each sequence. To overcome these limitations, we present Drive2Gauss, a feedforward framework that converts jointly generated RGB, metric depth, and dynamic flow into dynamic 4D Gaussian scenes. A Multimodal Video Generator predicts the three modalities from reference multiview images and future control signals. Furthermore, we introduce a Gaussian Query Decoder that uses depth to initialize sparse 3D queries and flow to associate the queries across time, and integrates appearance information through spatiotemporal feature aggregation and iterative query refinement. The reconstruction stage operates in a single feedforward pass without optimization for each scene. Extensive results on nuScenes demonstrate that our approach attains an FID of 6.38 and an FVD of 12.43 for future RGB generation, a PSNR of 29.91 dB when reconstructing its generated observations, and supports both direct rendering under lateral camera shifts and downstream video fixing. Code and more visualizations are available at https://zttt04. github.io/Drive2Gauss_page/.

机器人控制实验室.title: SPACE: Swarm Pheromone Fields for Adaptive Collision-Aware Exploration
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Haohua Que, Haojia Gao, Mingkai Liu, Qian Zhang, Jiajun Sun
机器人控制实验室.summary: SPACE introduces a pheromone-based system for robot swarms that enhances collision avoidance and efficiency in exploration, significantly reducing inter-robot contacts while maintaining coverage.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Massive robot swarms can explore unknown environments quickly, but adding robots eventually stops helping. Doorways and dense traffic create congestion, increasing inter-robot contacts and reducing the value of each additional robot. We study this safety-efficiency tradeoff for ground swarms of tens to hundreds of robots. We present SPACE, Swarm Pheromone Fields for Adaptive Collision-Aware Exploration. Inspired by ant foraging, SPACE maintains a shared environmental field with an attractive frontier pheromone, a repellent explore pheromone, and a fast robot-density field. Robots use local field guidance on a synchronized shared map. We evaluate SPACE on real building floorplans, namely sixteen home layouts from the HouseExpo dataset and eight campus floors from the KTH dataset, with swarms of up to two hundred and fifty-six robots. At congested swarm sizes, SPACE attains the lowest inter-robot contact rate on HouseExpo and lies on the empirical Pareto frontier on KTH, together with handed lane formation at sizes where Lane has fewer contacts. Relative to a greedy nearest-frontier planner, SPACE reduces the contact rate by four to seventeen times while keeping coverage time within about two percent. The results indicate that, at this scale, coordination mainly improves safety rather than coverage time.

机器人控制实验室.title: EgoTac: In-the-wild Tactile Prediction from Egocentric Vision
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Wenkang Zhang, Chengbo Yuan, Zicheng Zhang, Zhengxue Cheng, Yang Gao
机器人控制实验室.summary: EgoTac is a model that predicts tactile information from egocentric videos, achieving high accuracy and enabling tactile-aware robot learning without direct tactile data collection.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Touch is fundamental to dexterous manipulation, yet most egocentric human data increasingly used for robot learning lacks tactile information. Directly collecting large-scale tactile data is challenging due to sensor limitations, while human video data is abundant, contact-rich, and easily scalable. This motivates a natural question: can tactile signals be inferred purely from vision? To address this, we introduce EgoTac, a generalizable model that predicts rich tactile information directly from egocentric human videos. EgoTac is trained on a unified corpus of over 5.7M image-tactile pairs, covering both continuous force measurements and binary contacts. By learning from this diverse dataset, EgoTac captures nuanced touch dynamics across varied interactions. Experiments demonstrate strong performance: in-domain prediction achieves an average force error below 0.06N. On out-of-domain contact prediction benchmarks, EgoTac consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art contact estimator. It also captures the rise and fall patterns of real tactile data and enables zero-shot predictions on unconstrained real-world videos. Scaling analyses further reveal that both data diversity and volume improve performance steadily. Overall, EgoTac provides a scalable pathway to extract tactile priors from egocentric human videos, enabling broadly applicable tactile-aware robot learning. Related resources can be found at https://egotac.github.io/ .

机器人控制实验室.title: Event-STVG: Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding for Long-Form Event Reasoning
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Yizhe Zhang, Xujia Wang, Songqi Tang, Xujie Tang, Leo Jiahao Jiang
机器人控制实验室.summary: Event-STVG introduces a novel spatio-temporal video grounding task focused on event-level reasoning, supported by a large-scale benchmark, highlighting challenges for multimodal large language models.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding (STVG) aims to jointly localize a target in space and time given a natural-language query. Despite continued advances, existing STVG benchmarks remain largely centered on localizing targets through instance-specific descriptions, leaving them largely decoupled from long-form reasoning increasingly emphasized in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). In this paper, we introduce Event-STVG, a task that shifts STVG from locating what is described toward event-level reasoning by unifying long-form context, repeated-event reasoning, event localization, role inference, and multi-target grounding. To facilitate research on Event-STVG, we construct a large-scale benchmark comprising 4,016 annotated event occurrences across soccer and seven additional domains. Experiments with state-of-the-art MLLMs reveal substantial difficulty, with the strongest model achieving only 5.4% m-vIoU at the 10-minute horizon. Across domains, we consistently observe confusion among repeated same-type events, spatial grounding bottlenecks, and rare success in jointly grounding all required roles. Event-STVG establishes a new challenge for visual understanding in MLLMs, calling for future models that can jointly reason about complex events across space and time. Code and annotations are available at https://github.com/THU-KEG/EventSTVG

机器人控制实验室.title: World Action Critic (WAC) Model: Joint Foresight and Criticism for Policy Learning
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Xiangteng Zhang, Haoyuan Liu, Yang Guan, Jingliang Duan, Yao Lyu
机器人控制实验室.summary: The World Action Critic (WAC) Model enhances sequential decision-making by jointly learning future predictions and action evaluations, improving policy learning in autonomous driving.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: World models have shown considerable promise in sequential decision-making by anticipating the consequences of actions and providing predictive foresight for policy learning. However, learning to reason about counterfactual actions remains challenging, since predictive objectives may underemphasize information critical for action evaluation, while unexecuted actions lack observed futures for direct supervision. To address these challenges, we propose the World Action Critic (WAC) Model, which proposes multimodal action candidates and jointly learns candidate-conditioned future prediction and consequence evaluation. In our proposed framework, critic supervision directly shapes intermediate predictive representations during rollout, encouraging them to retain information needed to distinguish action quality. Observed futures supervise prediction for executed actions, while external task-quality targets provide evaluation signals for counterfactual candidates. Through joint optimization, critic signals from these candidates propagate into predictive representations without requiring their observed futures. Our theoretical analysis characterizes critic-guided feature retention and bounds candidate-selection regret. Applied to autonomous driving, WAC achieves 93.4 PDMS on NAVSIM-v1, demonstrating the effectiveness of jointly learning predictive foresight and consequence evaluation.

机器人控制实验室.title: Batched Contextual Reinforcement II: Does RLVR Need Long Rollout Windows?
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Bangji Yang, Hongbo Ma, Ruihan Guo, Jiajun Fan, Xi Zhu
机器人控制实验室.summary: The paper introduces Concurrent Constraint Reinforcement (CCR), which optimizes reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards by using shorter rollout windows while maintaining accuracy and reducing training costs significantly.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Long rollout windows make reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) expensive, yet simply shortening them can remove the correctness signal: when every single-problem rollout truncates before an answer, group-relative accuracy advantages vanish. As a technical continuation of Batched Contextual Reinforcement (BCR), we study how concurrent rewards relax this dependence on long windows. Concurrent Constraint Reinforcement (CCR) places three independently verifiable problems in one capped training completion. Correct answers completed before truncation retain credit, while a shared budget encourages shorter useful reasoning without an explicit length penalty. We connect this mechanism to conditional reward- and update-variance analyses and study 4B and 8B mathematical reasoning models. Against single-problem GRPO with a 32k window, CCR with an 8,000-token window reduces tokens per training step from 975,464 to 174,957 on 4B and from 793,832 to 165,788 on 8B, saving 82.1% and 79.1%, respectively. An 8B training trace shows increasing accuracy reward alongside shorter completions. Single-problem evaluations provide supporting evidence of retained reasoning quality. These results identify reward-preserving training structure as a practical route to lower per-step cost in short-window RLVR.

机器人控制实验室.title: DiffusionRVGE: Reinforcement Learning via Regression-Based Value Gradient Estimation
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Jiayuan Wang, Tongyao Pang
机器人控制实验室.summary: DiffusionRVGE introduces an efficient reinforcement learning method for diffusion models, enhancing training speed and performance by regressing rewards on denoised images without requiring reward derivatives.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning improves diffusion models using rewards on generated images, but repeated denoising and gradient estimation make training expensive. We introduce \method, an efficient method that constructs useful update directions by regressing centered rewards on centered final denoised images. It requires neither reward derivatives nor adjoint backpropagation through the sampling trajectory. A unified first-variation formulation identifies the value-gradient target with or without a trajectory-KL penalty. A population analysis under Gaussian noising explains the regression geometry, while a subspace analysis motivates clean-image coordinates. The implementation adapts rollout bandwidth and query weights to reward continuity: local rollouts suit smooth rewards, whereas broader groups provide informative contrasts for discrete rewards. Trained jointly on five rewards, one SD3.5-Medium model matches or exceeds DiffusionNFT's joint model on seven of eight metrics, reaching GenEval $0.94$, OCR $0.92$, and PickScore $23.82$ at about one fifth of its estimated training compute. In single-reward training, \method reaches matched reward thresholds $2.1$--$6.7\times$ faster than reproduced DiffusionNFT on identical hardware. Ablations support the clean-image estimator, direct direction transfer, and reward-dependent rollout choices. Code is available at https://github.com/jy-wang-tsinghua/DIFFUSIONRVGE.

机器人控制实验室.title: Robotic Spatiotemporal Editing: A Unified Interface for Controllable Action Generation via Masked Action Reconstruction
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Yanbang Li, Bu He, Yi Tian, Yu-Chiao Huang, Chenyu Zhang
机器人控制实验室.summary: The paper presents the MAP interface for spatiotemporal control in robotic action generation, enabling precise behavior editing through a novel inpainting approach.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Generative policies can synthesize robot behaviors, yet controlling and editing them through diverse spatiotemporal references remains challenging. In the real world, human intent requires robot behaviors that satisfy constraints on where, when, and how actions are executed. Our key insight is that spatiotemporal control references, such as keypoints, flows, orientations, and keyposes, can be viewed as partial specifications of the same temporal Cartesian action space. We introduce the MAP (Masked Action Space) interface to unify these action references and formulate controllable manipulation as an action inpainting problem. Our Inpainting Policy (IP) reconstructs missing action dimensions of the end-effector, combining progress-guided alignment with multi-mask training to support unseen action-constraint combinations. We further adopt a training-free RePaint variant that iteratively inpaints the action during denoising to reduce control error. On ManiSkill and LIBERO-10, our policy achieves average task success rates of 92.67% and 64.67%, respectively.Real-world experiments demonstrate spatiotemporal control with average positional and rotational errors of 44.3 mm and 7°, respectively, showing that our policy can use diverse references to guide executable robot behaviors.

机器人控制实验室.title: Agentic In-Context Learning: What Algorithms Can Transformers Learn in Closed-Loop Interaction?
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Shiguang Wu, Yaqing Wang, Quanming Yao
机器人控制实验室.summary: This paper introduces Agentic In-Context Learning, exploring how Transformers learn through interactive decision-making and reward structures, demonstrating distinct behavioral outcomes based on reward alignment.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: The learning algorithm view of in-context learning (ICL) studies how fixed-parameter Transformers learn from supplied examples. Language model agents extend this setting through interaction: their actions determine what evidence enters context next. We call this regime Agentic In-Context Learning (Agentic ICL). Existing studies largely depend on externally supplied contexts or reward-bearing interaction histories, while work on general tool-using agents lacks a learning algorithm view. We represent an interactive learner by its state, update, and decision rule, covering active learning, bandits, and online reinforcement learning (RL). For expressivity, we construct causal Transformers that approximate these algorithms over a finite horizon, and bound the resulting loss in return. For training, we characterize when optimizing process rewards preserves behavior that maximizes the final outcome. Distillation experiments show that Transformers can learn to execute three representative recursions. We then train models from outcome or process rewards without oracle action or state targets, as in RL post-training. Different rewards yield distinct decision policies. Improving the alignment of process supervision with outcome-optimal action preferences shifts learned decisions accordingly. Such behavioral differences persist in a pretrained language model across textual paraphrases.

机器人控制实验室.title: Rethinking GRPO for Large Reasoning Model Safety Alignment
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Jiawei Chen, Yi Zhang, Jiawei Du, Zhonghou Lv, Tairan Chen
机器人控制实验室.summary: The paper introduces Beacon, a framework enhancing safety alignment in large reasoning models by addressing GRPO's limitations through Safety Signal Recovery and Safety-Utility Decoupled Alignment, significantly improving safety performance.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) exhibit strong reasoning capabilities but remain vulnerable to unsafe outputs. While Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) is widely used for safety alignment, its group-relative optimization may provide insufficient safety-directed learning signals. In this paper, we identify two failure modes: advantage collapse, where homogeneous rollout groups yield vanishing advantages, and unsafe diversification, where unsafe behaviors persist and become increasingly diverse. Our theoretical analysis reveals that behavioral consistency weakens within-group safety contrasts, while entropy regularization can diversify unsafe responses when relative signals vanish. To address these challenges, we propose Beacon, comprising Safety Signal Recovery (SSR) and Safety-Utility Decoupled Alignment (SUDA). SSR combines advantage-guided trajectory filtering and safe reference supervision to recover effective safety learning signals, while SUDA employs category-aware rewards and benign-only KL anchoring to mitigate over-refusal without compromising safety. Experiments across four Qwen3 and DeepSeek-R1-Distill variants and eight benchmarks show that our framework achieves the best average safety and reasoning performance, reducing average safety error by up to 32.83 percentage points while maintaining low over-refusal.

机器人控制实验室.title: CrystalReasoner: Reasoning and RL for Property-Conditioned Crystal Structure Generation
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Yuyang Wu, Stefano Falletta, Delia McGrath, Sherry Yang
机器人控制实验室.summary: CrystalReasoner (CrysReas) is an LLM framework that integrates reasoning and reinforcement learning to generate valid, stable, and property-conditioned crystal structures from natural language instructions.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Generative modeling has emerged as a promising approach for crystal structure discovery. However, existing LLM-based generative models struggle with low-level atomic precision, while diffusion-based methods fall short in integrating high-level scientific knowledge. As a result, generated structures are often invalid, unstable, or do not possess desirable properties. To address this gap, we propose CrystalReasoner (CrysReas), an end-to-end LLM framework that generates crystal structures from natural language instructions through reasoning and alignment. CrysReas introduces physical priors as thinking tokens, which include crystallographic symmetry, local coordination environments and predicted physical properties before generating atomic coordinates. This bridges the gap between natural language and 3D structures. CrysReas then employs reinforcement learning (RL) with a multi-objective, dense reward function to align generation with physical validity, chemical consistency, and thermodynamic stability. For property-conditioned tasks, we design task-specific reward functions and train specialized models for discrete constraints (e.g., space group) and continuous properties (e.g., elasticity, thermal expansion). Empirical results demonstrate that compared to prior works and baselines without thinking traces or RL, CrysReas obtains better performance on diverse metrics, triples S.U.N. ratio, and achieves better performance for property conditioned generation. CrysReas also exhibits adaptive reasoning, increasing reasoning lengths as the number of atoms increases. Our work demonstrates the potential of leveraging thinking traces and RL for generating valid, stable, and property-conditioned crystal structures.

机器人控制实验室.title: WebCoder: Scaling General Frontend Development with Artifact-Grounded Agentic Reinforcement Learning
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Zijun Dou, Zhen Yang, Xijun Liu, Dongzhuoran Zhou, Aohan Zeng
机器人控制实验室.summary: WebCoder leverages artifact-grounded reinforcement learning to enhance frontend development by improving task requirement satisfaction and evaluation through a shared executable environment.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Real-world frontend development requires agents to compose reproduction, generation, modification, and repair over an evolving application state. Learning a general policy for this process requires translating heterogeneous execution feedback into task-aligned rewards and effective credit assignment across long sequences of interdependent actions. We introduce WebCoder, a general frontend development agent trained with artifact-grounded agentic reinforcement learning. Our key idea is to assess diverse development activities through their effects on a shared executable artifact and its satisfaction of task requirements. We build Webdev-World, an executable environment that integrates code editing, application execution, browser inspection, and on-demand skills while preserving project state across interactions. An independent verifier evaluates the final application against task requirements to provide terminal rewards, while changes in intermediate artifact progress redistribute the resulting rollout advantage across development segments. Context compaction and message-tree sample construction support training on trajectories beyond a single context window while avoiding repeated loss computation on shared generated history. We further introduce Webdev-Bench to evaluate composed development requirements within a single project. On Webdev-Bench, WebCoder-27B raises requirement satisfaction from 64.8 for its Qwen3.8-27B base model to 72.8, exceeding Claude-Opus-4.8 (65.1) and GPT-5.4 (59.6); on Vision2Web, it improves the average visual and functional score from 41.1 to 62.4, on par with Claude-Opus-4.8. Ablation studies confirm the contributions of artifact-grounded credit assignment and long-horizon training.

机器人控制实验室.title: FloodVLM-Pix: Language-Guided Pixel-Level Flood Understanding
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Chengyang Zhang, Zhihao Wang, Zhiyu Long, Xueqian Wang, Quanming Yao
机器人控制实验室.summary: FloodVLM-Pix is a novel model leveraging a large-scale benchmark for enhanced language-guided flood understanding and pixel-level segmentation, addressing existing performance limitations.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: As climate change intensifies, floods are becoming more frequent and destructive, making accurate flood understanding an urgent priority. However, existing vision-language models perform poorly on flood-related tasks, suffering from attentional bias and inaccurate descriptions of flood magnitude. To bridge this gap, we construct the first large-scale remote sensing flood multi-modal benchmark that supports language-level flood understanding and pixel-level flood segmentation. The benchmark contains 131,200 flood image patches and corresponding 443,100 textual descriptions for flood severity and evolution. Based on this benchmark, we propose FloodVLM-Pix, a language-guided pixel-level flood understanding model that includes a flood prior module and a multi-temporal flood pixel decoder to achieve accurate flood understanding. The flood prior module automatically distills sub-region flood spatial priors and inputs priors into FloodVLM-Pix, solving the attentional bias problem in flood language understanding. The flood pixel decoder introduces a novel general-specific feature fusion mechanism to address performance degradation caused by interference (e.g., clouds or mountain shadows) during flood segmentation. Experiments on FloodVL-Pix demonstrate that FloodVLM-Pix improves both flood description quality and pixel-level flood segmentation performance compared with state-of-the-art VLMs and flood segmentation models. Our code and data will be released at https://github.com/Haomiaoyanmeng/FloodPix.

机器人控制实验室.title: RL-Guided Temporal Localization for Dual-Channel Retrieval in Long-Horizon Agent Memory
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Dabin Sheng, Zhe Wu, Jinming Zhao, Junliang Xing, Yuanchun Shi
机器人控制实验室.summary: TIDER introduces a reinforcement learning framework for time-aware retrieval in long-horizon memory, enhancing accuracy by optimizing temporal window localization to improve evidence selection.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Time-aware retrieval is crucial for long-horizon LLM agents to effectively leverage ever-growing long-term memory. Existing methods focus on lexical or semantic similarity, leading to target memories being crowded out by temporally mismatched yet semantically similar candidates. Even time-aware approaches inject temporal cues only during memory organization or answer generation, overlooking temporal constraints at the retrieval stage, where candidate selection occurs - the root cause of the displacement. Inspired by the temporal contiguity effect in human episodic memory, we propose TIDER (Temporal Interval-driven Dual-channel Evidence Retrieval), a time-aware agentic retrieval framework. Central to TIDER is a reinforcement learning (RL)-trained temporal interval locator that infers the temporal windows in which the evidence lies. RL optimizes window localization as a discrete, non-differentiable retrieval decision, using composite rewards to convert sparse answer supervision into fine-grained retrieval feedback. These temporal windows first define the temporal retrieval channel; the retrieved candidates are then merged with results from the semantic channel and reranked by proximity to the windows. This temporal grounding enables TIDER to retrieve temporally aligned evidence that would otherwise be drowned out by the volume of semantically similar yet temporally mismatched memories. With a lightweight 1.7B locator, TIDER achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on both long-horizon memory benchmarks - 61.52% on LifeBench (+8.82%) and 78.96% on LoCoMo (+3.66%) - which indicates that temporal cues are crucial for pinpointing target evidence amid a vast pool of semantically similar historical events in long-term daily-life memory.

机器人控制实验室.title: Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Yuze He, Bin Tan, Zelin Gao, Yujun Shen, Yong-Jin Liu
机器人控制实验室.summary: PPMem introduces a compact persistent 3D memory using plane primitives in video world models, enhancing video quality and geometric consistency while reducing memory requirements.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Video world models that generate and explore environments at scale need a persistent 3D memory of what they have produced. Plane primitives offer a natural candidate: a compact set of oriented planes captures the dominant structural elements (e.g., walls, floors, facades) of indoor and outdoor scenes, while requiring only 7 parameters per primitive. We present PPMem, a video world model that adopts plane primitives as its persistent 3D memory. PPMem augments a video diffusion transformer with a planar prediction head and a Depth Token Fusion (DTF) module: each autoregressive chunk jointly produces RGB video and planar geometry, which merges into a persistent plane memory that conditions subsequent chunks via rendered depth. The resulting memory is three orders of magnitude more compact than per-pixel point clouds (~100K primitives, 5MB for a full scene), geometrically explicit (metric depth, normals, exportable surfaces), cross-view consistent (jointly predicted by the shared backbone), and adaptive (refined by the merging procedure as generation proceeds). On DL3DV and RealEstate10K, PPMem outperforms prior 3D-grounded world models in video quality while jointly producing metric-scale depth, surface normals, and exportable planar geometry, sustaining coherence across hundreds of frames under large viewpoint changes. Project page: https://hyzcluster.github.io/ppmem.

机器人控制实验室.title: R$^2$Orch: Recursive Self-Improvement for Agent Orchestration via Self-Play within a Skill-Internalization Loop
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Mingda Zhang, Yun Huang, Qiang Huang, Yanjin Li, Rui Qian
机器人控制实验室.summary: R$^2$Orch introduces a recursive self-play framework for agent orchestration that enhances skill learning and evaluation, outperforming traditional methods across various complex tasks.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: In recent years, agentic orchestration has been widely applied to solve complex human tasks. However, existing orchestration learning still faces key challenges, including hand-designed curricula, advantage collapse when a task's rollouts all reach the same outcome, and unreliable evaluation signals that judge each skill by one noisy score. To address these challenges, we propose R$^2$Orch, a new paradigm of Recursive Self-Play Orchestration: an inner loop of self-play that improves the orchestrator on self-chosen tasks, and an outer loop that improves how the inner loop improves. To support this paradigm, we introduce Recursive Learnability, a training objective that rewards a Proposer for choosing tasks whose rollouts keep reaching different outcomes as skills are withdrawn. Built on this objective, we further propose Skill Withdrawal, in which the outer loop withdraws each skill once a controlled evaluation within self-play shows that the orchestrator performs as well without it. Moreover, the two loops form one cycle: failures are distilled into skills, skills into parameters, and withdrawals lead the Proposer to new failures, so the orchestrator moves toward zero-skill deployment. Experimental results on twelve datasets show that R$^2$Orch consistently outperforms baselines across question answering, math, code, and interactive tasks.

机器人控制实验室.title: PASS-VLN: Passability-Aware Local-Command Vision-and-Language Navigation
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Cong Zou, Xiangsheng Shi, Xuanhui Wang, Fubin Wang, Guangjun Ge
机器人控制实验室.summary: PASS-VLN introduces a benchmark and model for vision-and-language navigation that emphasizes passability and collision-free execution, improving local command success in robotic navigation.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Reliable vision-and-language navigation (VLN) requires not only understanding instructions but also determining whether and how a robot can physically execute them. However, existing VLN benchmarks typically assume executable instructions and focus on long-horizon tasks. This leaves body-dependent local execution, including passability and collision-free execution, largely unexamined. Evaluating these factors within long-horizon tasks would entangle local physical execution with task planning and long-term spatial memory, making navigation failures difficult to attribute. We therefore focus on grounding local navigation commands in executable motion under environmental and robot body constraints. We present PASS-VLN, a passability-aware local-command VLN benchmark and model. The benchmark holds the scene, instruction, start pose, and reference route fixed while varying robot body width, requiring target completion when the instructed passage is feasible and stopping before blockage otherwise. Our model encodes body width through obstacle inflation in a depth-derived local bird's-eye view, fuses geometry with visual and linguistic context, and predicts discrete latent action codes for continuous closed-loop execution. Experiments show that PASS-VLN improves collision-free success by approximately 12 percentage points over a strong VLN model fine-tuned on our benchmark, while adapting reach-versus-stop behavior to body constraints and generalizing to unseen body widths. When integrated with a high-level planner, PASS-VLN achieves higher success with fewer local commands, while real-world deployment further demonstrates its effectiveness as a low-level executor. The benchmark and model will be released.

机器人控制实验室.title: SenseSwarm: Swarm Exploration via Neural Structure Estimation with Shared World-Anticipation for Rapid Mapping
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Haohua Que, Haojia Gao, Mingkai Liu, Hoiian Au, Qian Zhang
机器人控制实验室.summary: SenseSwarm enhances swarm exploration efficiency by using a shared neural map predictor, enabling faster and more accurate mapping of unknown environments compared to traditional methods.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: A robot swarm covers a building faster with more robots, but the map is only as complete as the space the robots have physically visited. We target the amount of an unknown building a decentralized swarm knows at each instant, ahead of physical coverage. SenseSwarm serves a lightweight learned map predictor on the swarm's shared occupancy map and folds the predicted structure back into a stigmergic guidance field. Its 709K-parameter predictor is fine-tuned on the swarm's own multi-front observations, which we show is necessary: a single-robot predictor collapses on such views. We build a benchmark of twelve real building floors from HouseExpo, HKUST, and KTH, up to 24,000 square meters, and run 1,620 simulations across nine coordination methods, swarm sizes 32 to 512, and three seeds. On physical coverage the swarm is near parity with a greedy frontier planner, as expected. On map reconstruction, every non-predictive baseline needs 1.3 to 1.9 times longer to reach an 80 percent known map, and SenseSwarm holds an equal-time area lead of about 670 square meters, up to 1,359. Folding the prediction into the shared field matters: the same predictor applied per robot matches our speed but suffers a 6.9 times higher inter-robot contact rate at 512 robots. The prediction is computed once per shared map, so its cost stayed flat from 32 to 512 robots.

机器人控制实验室.title: Reliability-Consistent Appearance Modeling for RGB-Infrared Multi-Object Tracking
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Bingyang Wang, Jiazuo Yu, Lu Zhang, Lihe Zhang, Huchuan Lu
机器人控制实验室.summary: RCA-MOT enhances RGB-infrared multi-object tracking by maintaining separate appearance states for reliability control, achieving state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Recent RGB-infrared multi-object tracking (MOT) methods have substantially improved cross-modal representation learning and multimodal information integration. However, most existing methods compress RGB and infrared evidence into a unified descriptor. When one modality is temporarily degraded, the tracker can no longer regulate its contribution separately; unreliable evidence may distort association and contaminate appearance memory. We therefore propose RCA-MOT, a reliability-consistent appearance modeling framework that preserves cross-modal complementarity while retaining post-representation evidence controllability. RGB-specific, infrared-specific, and fused identity representations are maintained as jointly accessible appearance states. For each detection, a simple training-free target-scene estimator produces branch-wise appearance reliability used across the two temporal roles of appearance: relative reliability regulates different identity branches, absolute reliability calibrates borderline candidates near the ReID acceptance boundary, and the same branch-wise reliability controls how strongly matched descriptors update historical appearance memory. The individual components are intentionally simple, focusing evaluation on reliability-controllable appearance organization rather than elaborate fusion or learned reliability-estimation modules. RCA-MOT sets new SOTA results on VT-MOT and UniRTL, improving the previous best HOTA by 5.402/6.075 points and IDF1 by 11.549/12.789 points, respectively, while post-hoc analyses further validate reliability as an informative control signal. Code will be released upon acceptance.

机器人控制实验室.title: Not All Actions Contribute Equally: Learning Precise Progress Estimation from Imprecise Demonstrations
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Huanqian Wang, Boshi Tang, Botong Xiao, Jie Zhang, Yang Yue
机器人控制实验室.summary: The paper introduces PRIME, a novel progress estimator that improves task progress assessment in robotic manipulation by distinguishing meaningful advancements from human errors using a weighted graph approach.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Progress estimators play an essential role in providing dense reward signals for reinforcement learning in robotic manipulation, but accurately assessing task progress can be much challenging. Existing methods heavily rely on expert data and naively assume that all actions within a demonstration contribute to task success. This assumption often breaks down in real-world scenarios, especially in high-precision manipulation, where subtle geometric errors can lead to task failure. Therefore, these methods can erroneously interpret human mistakes as meaningful progress, further corrupting progress learning. We argue that a key limitation is the lack of a global prior regarding task evaluation criteria, which is crucial for distinguishing meaningful progress from human mistakes. To this end, we propose PRIME, a novel progress estimator capable of learning precise progress estimation from imprecise demonstrations by aggregating experience across trajectories. PRIME constructs a weighted graph over observed states, connecting states across trajectories based on spatial proximity and visual consistency. Edge weights encode spatial distances as transition costs, and shortest-path search approximates the geodesic distance to success. Changes in this distance naturally distinguish advancement, stagnation, and setbacks without assuming monotonic progress over time. Extensive experiments in both simulation and real world on precise manipulation tasks show that PRIME is consistently effective across diverse tasks, and robust to data with varying degrees of suboptimality. Notably, the advantage of PRIME gets more pronounced in higher-precision scenarios, yielding up to a \(5\times\) improvement in policy success rate over the SFT baselines on charger insertion.

机器人控制实验室.title: Revisiting Embodied Chain-of-Thought for Generalizable Robot Manipulation
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Nan Sun, Yuan Zhang, Yongkun Yang, Wentao Zhao, Peiyan Li
机器人控制实验室.summary: This paper introduces ERVLA, a vision-language-action model that enhances robot manipulation by integrating grounded linguistic reasoning, achieving state-of-the-art performance while addressing autoregressive instability.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Embodied chain-of-thought (CoT) aims to bridge linguistic reasoning with robotic control, yet its effective form and integration remain underexplored. In this paper, we revisit embodied CoT for robotic control at an unprecedented scale. We curate the largest embodied CoT corpus to date, comprising 978,743 trajectories, 226.3M samples, and 2592.5 hours of data. Through extensive experiments, we show that effective CoT must ground high-level semantic understaning in concrete linguistic action guidance -- such as end-effector movement and image-space trajectories -- whereas high-level reasoning alone yields marginal gains. More importantly, we identify that explicit CoT does not scale reliably as an autoregressive action prefix, suffering from compounding errors during inference. To address these challenges, we propose ERVLA, a vision-language-action (VLA) model that effectively leverages linguistic reasoning in generalizable robot manipulation. ERVLA is trained using a CoT-dropout strategy, allowing the model to leverage rich reasoning traces during training while predicting actions directly without CoT during inference to bypass autoregressive instability. This approach enables reliable scaling with increasing pre-training data. ERVLA achieves state-of-the-art results on LIBERO-Plus with an 86.9\% success rate and reaches 53.2\% on VLABench, showcasing superior performance in out-of-distribution settings. Furthermore, ERVLA outperforms competitive state-of-the-art baselines in real-robot experiments, especially in handling semantic ambiguity and long-horizon tasks. Code, data, and model checkpoints are available on the project website: https://taoshuaiz.github.io/ERVLA/.

机器人控制实验室.title: CQDC-Warp: GPU-Accelerated Differentiable Quasi-Dynamic Simulation for Contact-Rich Manipulation
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Yanchen Ding, Jiayi Chen, Jianfeng Xu, Wei Zhao, Li Yi
机器人控制实验室.summary: CQDC-Warp is a GPU-accelerated differentiable simulator that enhances contact-rich trajectory optimization for robots, achieving higher success rates and significantly faster planning times.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Efficient synthesis of contact-rich manipulation trajectories is essential for downstream robot learning. Gradient-based planning offers a promising approach, but jointly optimizing motion and contact decisions remains challenging. Meanwhile, many existing planners run on CPUs with limited throughput. We present CQDC-Warp, a GPU-accelerated differentiable quasi-dynamic simulator for batched model predictive control (MPC). We use it to study contact-guided trajectory optimization, in which intended robot--object contacts are specified before planning and encouraged through soft costs, while the simulated dynamics determine contact geometry and frictional response without a prescribed contact-mode schedule. Across $17{,}408$ trials on the $17$-object Allegro in-hand rotation benchmark, our framework achieves $79.8\%$ success, compared with $73.7\%$ for CFree and $65.2\%$ for IMPACT, and reduces mean trajectory-generation time by factors of $27.0$ and $50.2$, respectively. On a single NVIDIA RTX 4090 with $2{,}048$ parallel worlds, forward and backward throughput reach $2.06\times10^5$ and $2.25\times10^5$ world-steps per second, respectively. Further experiments cover manipulation with LEAP and Shadow hands, environmental contact exploitation, bimanual manipulation, whole-body control, and real-world trajectory replay on a Sharpa hand.

机器人控制实验室.title: Robo2Process: Benchmarking and Learning Process-Aware Understanding in Vision-Language Robotic Manipulation
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Dayu Xia, Yue Shi, Yao Mu, Huiting Ji, Chaofan Ma
机器人控制实验室.summary: Robo2Process introduces a framework for process-aware supervision in robotic manipulation, enhancing vision-language models' understanding through structured QA and diagnostic benchmarking.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) used as robotic critics, reward generators, and failure detectors must understand how manipulation unfolds, not only whether it succeeds. Yet fine-grained process supervision is not readily available in a unified form, and existing evaluations do not systematically diagnose these abilities. We introduce Robo2Process, a trace-grounded framework for scalable construction of process-aware supervision from heterogeneous robotic execution data. It aligns visual observations with source-native signals and annotations, extracts local process units (LPUs), and generates structured QA supervision through task-specific sampling, deterministic label construction, and ambiguity filtering. We instantiate this framework as RoboProcessBench, a diagnostic benchmark with 12 question families spanning \emph{static monitoring} and \emph{dynamic reasoning}, and ProcessData, a corpus of 57,892 QA pairs across four data sources and 260 manipulation tasks, split into ProcessData-SFT and ProcessData-Eval. Evaluation of a broad suite of VLMs reveals uneven process understanding. Supervision from ProcessData-SFT improves \textit{Qwen2.5-VL-7B} and \textit{InternVL-3-8B} on local state, motion, progress, and primitive-aware cues. External evaluation on RoboRewardBench shows Robo2Process enables out-of-distribution process-aware reasoning abilities. Overall, Robo2Process provides a source-aware pipeline, diagnostic benchmark, and learnable substrate for process-aware understanding in robotic manipulation.

机器人控制实验室.title: Predict Before You Modify: Learning Improvement Dynamics for Self-Evolving Agents
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Zixuan Xie, Chang Xu, Yuhua Jiang, Li Zhao
机器人控制实验室.summary: The paper presents a predictive self-evolution model for agents that enhances task performance by anticipating modification outcomes, leading to significant improvements across various domains.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Self-evolving agents improve through repeated cycles of modification and evaluation. However, existing methods receive feedback on modifications only after costly evaluations, and aggregate scores may obscure distinctions between failures that require different repairs. We introduce predictive self-evolution through an editable Improvement Dynamics Model (IDM). Before evaluation, the IDM predicts task-level outcomes of a proposed modification and guides an optional revision. After evaluation, past modifications and their observed outcomes are used to improve the IDM, allowing predictive knowledge to accumulate across generations. The system can thus improve how it solves tasks, proposes modifications, and predicts their effects. Building on HyperAgents, we evaluate this approach across multilingual coding, paper review, robotics reward design, and Olympiad-level mathematical grading. Our approach outperforms HyperAgents across all four domains, with up to 46% higher average performance over generations. Gains also persist under matched token budgets that include both agent evolution and task evaluation, and extend to held-out tasks. Forecast accuracy improves as the IDM evolves, and the learned predictive knowledge transfers to improve evolution in a new domain.

机器人控制实验室.title: LoopWAM: Closed-Loop Generalist Policy Improvement from Deployment Rollouts
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Wenxuan Guo, Yingping Liang, Zhaoguo Wang, Ziyuan Li, Angyuan Ma
机器人控制实验室.summary: LoopWAM enhances generalist robot policies by leveraging mixed-quality deployment rollouts for closed-loop learning, achieving significant performance improvements across multiple benchmarks.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Scaling expert demonstrations alone does not enable generalist robot policies to improve from deployment. Real-world rollouts contain successes, suboptimal behavior, and failures: imitating every recorded action can reinforce poor behavior, while filtering out failures discards evidence of physical interactions and their consequences. We introduce LoopWAM, a closed-loop world-action model that learns directly from this full quality spectrum, using rollouts from both itself and other deployed policies. Source-dependent noise sampling unifies behavior learning and action-conditioned world modeling, while quality steering and quality-weighted supervision retain full video supervision across qualities and regulate action imitation. Video and action tokens interact throughout parallel denoising, allowing learned consequences to inform action generation directly. On RoboChallenge Table30-V2, three deployment-and-training rounds raise success from 23.67% to 43.33%, a 19.7-percentage-point gain, with a final score of 56.80. LoopWAM also achieves 94.5% average success on RoboTwin 2.0 and 49.5% overall success on RoboCasa365 without additional embodied pretraining, obtaining the best overall results among the compared methods across all three benchmarks. On challenging shirt folding task, two rounds of deployment-driven improvement after single-task post-training raise success from 13.20% to 55.56%. These results demonstrate closed-loop improvement from mixed-quality experience under both multi-task learning and single-task post-training. Project page: https://loop-wam.github.io/

机器人控制实验室.title: Full-Duplex Interaction with Speech, Expressions and Gestures
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Siyin Wang, Wenyi Yu, Terumi Chiba, Xianzhao Chen, Xiaohai Tian
机器人控制实验室.summary: The ELLSA 2 model enhances full-duplex dialogue by integrating speech, gestures, and expressions, optimizing multimodal interaction through advanced synthesis and evaluation techniques.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Human face-to-face conversation requires coordinating speech, gestures and expressions across both speaking and listening. We present ELLSA 2, an end-to-end full-duplex dialogue model that jointly optimizes speech interaction and streaming gesture-expression generation. An autoregressive, chunk-wise synthesizer combines pretrained acoustic features with distinct listening and speaking hidden states from the dialogue backbone and speech synthesizer, enabling continuous non-verbal generation even when the model is verbally silent. To translate dialogue understanding into vivid semantic gestures, we introduce contextual semantic calls and template guidance, separating whether to invoke an available semantic gesture from how to realize it. We also establish a curated data and evaluation pipeline for dialog-aware co-speech gesture generation and investigate reference-based multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as automatic judges. Experiments show that ELLSA 2 remains highly competitive with open-source full-duplex speech interaction models and outperforms cascaded baselines across dialog-aware gesture and expression metrics. Semantic template guidance further significantly improves semantic gesture quality. Strong system-level correlations with human judgments support these reference-based scores as useful preliminary metrics for full-duplex and semantic gesture assessment. Together, these results advance dialogue modeling from spoken responses toward coordinated multimodal interaction.

机器人控制实验室.title: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Flow-Based Vision-Language-Action Models
机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Lichao Ni, Yuhan Liu, Pengfei Li, Guanghuan Fang
机器人控制实验室.summary: The paper presents a two-level on-policy distillation framework that enhances flow-based vision-language-action models by consolidating domain-specific skills through multi-teacher supervision, achieving significant success-rate improvements across multiple tasks.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Specialized vision-language-action (VLA) policies acquire strong domain-specific skills, yet consolidating these skills into one shared policy remains challenging. On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers teacher knowledge on inputs induced by the student, addressing the distribution mismatch encountered during deployment. For flow-based VLAs, this mismatch arises at two levels: environment observations and intermediate action-generation states. We propose a two-level on-policy distillation framework that couples student-driven environment interaction with teacher velocity supervision along student-generated action flow trajectories. Frozen domain specialists jointly supervise one student. After each update, the student collects new environment experience and generates fresh action-flow trajectories. Starting from a joint supervised fine-tuning (SFT) initialization, Velocity Loss OPD yields absolute success-rate gains of 22.55% on LIBERO-40, 33.4% on CALVIN five-instruction sequences, and 22.6% on Meta-World MT50. Compared with Action Loss OPD and Teacher-rollout SFT, it achieves absolute success-rate gains of 6.4-9.5% on LIBERO-40, 9.7-18.3% on CALVIN, and 3.2-4.2% on Meta-World MT50. Analysis by sequence length further shows larger success-rate gains on longer CALVIN sequences. These results demonstrate effective multi-domain capability consolidation through two-level on-policy supervision, with a single student deployed across domains.

机器人控制实验室.title: Anchor3DGS: Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting with Compact Anchor-Based Representation
