机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) robustness is commonly summarized by aggregate task success, which obscures how individual executions change under distribution shifts and where failures emerge in long-horizon tasks. We introduce \textbf{RoboCasa-Shift}, a diagnostic robustness benchmark built on RoboCasa365 that combines controlled single-factor shifts, matched clean-perturbed rollouts in which each pair shares the same underlying settings and differs only in the target shift, and simulator-grounded stage-aware diagnostics. We evaluate GR00T N1.5 on four long-horizon tasks that pass a predefined clean-performance gate under four perturbation factors and three calibrated severity levels, including conditions that drive the evaluated policy to complete task failure, totaling 1,040 formal rollouts. Robustness responses vary substantially across factors and tasks, and increasing severity does not always produce monotonic degradation. For example, one camera condition yields $Δ\mathrm{SR}=0$ despite 8 of 80 matched episodes changing outcome. Stage-aware analysis further shows that the same end-to-end degradation can correspond to different execution-depth profiles. Camera $L_2$ and Gaussian blur $L_1$ both yield $Δ\mathrm{SR}=0.188$, yet their first-stage failure rates are 19.0\% and 36.4\%, respectively. Our findings suggest that VLA robustness should be viewed as a multi-dimensional property of execution rather than a single end-to-end performance measure, motivating evaluation protocols that jointly capture outcome degradation, paired outcome sensitivity, and failure progression. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/HaochengWang23/RoboCasa-Shift.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: Learn to Modify: Self-evolving Multi-agent Refinement Framework for Conversational Text-to-Motion Generation
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Jianan Li, Jiawei Zhao, Yangtao Zhou, Zhifu Zhao, Shaoxin Wu
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: The paper presents SMART, a self-evolving multi-agent framework for conversational text-to-motion generation that enables efficient, localized motion refinements based on user feedback.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Despite rapid progress in text-to-motion generation, existing methods are commonly designed for single-shot generation. When users are dissatisfied with specific motion details, they are often forced to regenerate the entire sequence from scratch, which is computationally inefficient and potentially destroys previously established kinematic context. A practical generation system should instead support iterative user feedback and refine only the affected spatio-temporal regions while preserving the remaining motion. Therefore, we introduce a conversational motion generation paradigm that requires the system to coordinate instruction understanding, motion generation, localized editing, and quality assessment. Recent advances in LLM-driven multi-agent systems provide a promising foundation for such role-specialized coordination. To tackle these challenges, a Self-evolving Multi-Agent RefinemenT Framework (SMART) is proposed for conversational motion generation. Within SMART, to preserve semantic consistency, we design a semantic-guided masked motion editing mechanism, which precisely grounds natural language feedback into spatiotemporal motion regions to enable localized refinements without altering unedited regions. To reduce redundant exploration, we propose a memory-based self-evolving strategy that dynamically accumulates motion editing knowledge from interaction history and reuses past successful experience. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SMART effectively supports multi-turn conversational motion generation and enables efficient motion refinement.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: HAVANA: A Hierarchical Video-Action Model for Vision-Language Navigation
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Dongzhihan Wang, Yi Du, Chen Wang, Xiuxian Li, Liang Xu
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: HAVANA introduces a dual-system video-action model for vision-language navigation, decoupling predictive reasoning from local planning to enhance adaptability and performance in diverse environments.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) requires long-horizon instruction-consistent planning and short-horizon local planning in current geometry. Video-action models (VAMs) offer a promising way to learn predictive representations for navigation. However, existing VAMs jointly predict visual futures and local trajectories in a single process, even though they operate at different paces: future prediction remains stable across multiple updates while local trajectories must react to fresh observations. To bridge this gap, we introduce HAVANA, a dual-system VAM that decouples predictive reasoning from reactive local planning. A slow system produces a compact language-conditioned latent plan from observation history, while a fast system combines the latest plan with the current observation to generate local trajectories. Their asynchronous execution enables rapid adaptation without repeated future prediction, and no future video is generated during inference. Experiments on OmniNavBench demonstrate state-of-the-art navigation performance over prior baselines, while real-world deployments further show robust generalization to unseen environments across different robot embodiments. Our code and checkpoints will be available at https://github.com/Anastasiawd/HAVANA.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: AffordanceWAM: Affordance-Aware Joint World-Action Modeling for Robot Manipulation
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Jiadi You, Qize Yu, Yue Chen, Minghong Cai, Zhide Zhong
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: AffordanceWAM is a generative model that enhances robot manipulation by integrating affordance-aware predictions from diverse human videos and robot actions for improved interaction and performance.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Generalizable robot manipulation requires predicting how a scene will evolve, identifying where interactions are feasible, and determining how to act. Action-labeled robot videos directly supervise control but are costly and limited in diversity, whereas egocentric human videos capture diverse interactions but lack robot actions and differ in embodiment and appearance. We introduce AffordanceWAM, an affordance-aware generative World Action Model that represents object-centric spatiotemporal affordance through Scalar Affordance and Affordance Heatmap, within the generated future World. This representation grounds visual prediction in task-relevantant objects and interaction regions for action generation, and provides shared interaction targets across human and robot videos. Built on a pretrained video diffusion Transformer, AffordanceWAM uses separately parameterized World and Action Experts, coupled through Masked Joint Self-Attention, to jointly predict future RGB observations, Scalar Affordance fields, Affordance Heatmaps, and continuous robot actions under a unified flow-matching objective. Human videos supervise all three future-World streams, whereas robot trajectories additionally provide action supervision, enabling transfer without human action labels or retargeting. Experiments on RoboCasa, CALVIN ABC$\rightarrow$D, and real-world manipulation demonstrate consistent gains over RGB-only and robot-data-only baselines. Under fixed robot supervision, RoboCasa performance improves monotonically as affordance-annotated human video scales. These results support affordance as an effective interface for both vision-language-action learning and human-to-robot transfer.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: When Does Backpropagating Through Policy Memory Matter? Separating Representation Credit from Closed-Loop Credit
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Xingjian Li, Jianhua Z. Huang, Junli Duan
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: The study investigates the impact of memory credit routes in policy training, revealing that representation credit is crucial under noisy conditions, while closed-loop credit can be selectively truncated.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: When a policy with memory is trained through a differentiable simulator, credit can reach what it stores along two routes: \emph{representation credit} teaches the network that writes the memory what to summarize, while \emph{closed-loop credit} travels back through the physical states that earlier actions produced and that the memory later stored. Stopping gradients at stored history, as truncated backpropagation and Transformer-XL do, removes both routes at once. Keeping every forward computation identical and removing one route at a time, we trained Transformer policies for quadrotor tracking to determine when each route matters. Credit through memory improved learning only when velocity observations were noisy or hidden. When velocity was hidden, mildly decaying the gradient between consecutive physical states ($γ= 0.8$) eliminated the truncation cost of removing closed-loop credit while leaving representation credit essential, a separation that held in 14 of 16 new seeds. Two further systems bound this result: in a fixed-wing aircraft, representation credit could replace closed-loop credit on its own, leaving no cost to separate, and in a cart-pole, training with full state-edge credit was too unstable to compare the routes. In both the quadrotor and a fully observed vessel model, static gradient norms failed to predict which cut cost more, so memory truncation choices are best guided by short training runs.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: CoworkEnv: Synthesizing Training Environments for Long-Horizon Cowork Agents
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Zhongwei Xie, Yiming Du, Jiaxin Bai, Baixuan Xu, Chunyang Li
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: CoworkEnv synthesizes executable training environments for AI coworkers, enhancing coordination and communication capabilities through structured tasks and validation, leading to improved performance in long-horizon tasks.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: AI coworkers must coordinate tools, communicate across turns, and act on changing workspace state while respecting workflow constraints. Constructing training experience for these capabilities requires coherent requests, service records, tool interfaces, and grading checks. We present CoworkEnv, a capability-guided framework for synthesizing executable training environments for AI coworkers. Workflow requirements guide task construction, and programmatic validation with feedback repair checks generated specifications and grading behavior. Teacher executions yield curated demonstrations for supervised fine-tuning (SFT), while student interactions provide rollouts and rewards for reinforcement learning (RL). Using these resources, we train compact PocketWorker models. For Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, SFT raises the mean score from 46.6 to 64.1 on Claw-Eval, including a 31.9-point gain on Multi-turn tasks. An SFT-only extension to ClawMark demonstrates applicability across coworker benchmarks. We further compare RL training dynamics across configurations that vary reward processing and credit assignment. Improving training rewards provide preliminary evidence that the constructed environments support policy optimization.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: TrajWAM: An Efficient Trajectory-Guided World Action Model for Dynamic Robotic Manipulation
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Haohan Geng, Sha Zhang, Weishuo Sun, Guanting Ye, Wenhao Yu
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: TrajWAM introduces a trajectory-guided world action model that enhances dynamic robotic manipulation by predicting target motion and enabling efficient one-step action inference.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Dynamic object manipulation requires robots to anticipate target motion while replanning fast enough to avoid executing outdated actions. Existing approaches either rely on fast reactive control without an explicit future target state or encode anticipated motion only implicitly. World Action Models (WAMs) offer a promising alternative by coupling future visual prediction with action generation, but scene-level video objectives may underrepresent target dynamics that are critical for manipulation, while iterative video-action denoising introduces substantial latency. We present TrajWAM, a trajectory-guided world action model for efficient dynamic robotic manipulation. Our key insight is to explicitly ground future visual imagination in predicted target-object motion and use the resulting future representation to condition action generation, while preserving this anticipation pathway after acceleration. Given a short history of object masks, a history-conditioned motion predictor forecasts future masks encoding the target object's trajectory. A lightweight Trajectory ControlNet then steers a pretrained video model toward trajectory-consistent futures. The resulting future representation conditions an action expert to predict executable action chunks. To enable one-step inference without breaking this interface, we introduce a decoupled distillation scheme that combines distribution matching for the video backbone, Trajectory ControlNet realignment, and action rollout distillation to support accurate one-step action prediction conditioned on the compressed future representation. Comprehensive evaluations in simulation and the real world show that TrajWAM achieves state-of-the-art performance on dynamic object manipulation tasks while enabling efficient one-step video-action inference. Project page: https://kevingeng3.github.io/TrajWAM/.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: AeroIntent: A Synchronized Multimodal Benchmark for UAV Mission Intent Recognition
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Yutong Chen, Jingxin Mao, Zhiwei Wei, Bing Li, Jianzhong Ni
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: AeroIntent introduces a multimodal benchmark for UAV mission intent recognition, featuring 990 sequences and the AeroMIR model, achieving significant accuracy improvements over existing methods.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Reliable recognition of mission-level UAV intent from multimodal observations is essential for low-altitude airspace surveillance and security. Existing multimodal UAV datasets primarily support detection, tracking, and localization, leaving limited support for evaluating mission-intent recognition across held-out trajectory programs and incomplete radar histories. We introduce AeroIntent, a simulation-based benchmark comprising 990 synchronized multimodal sequences generated by 22 trajectory programs across five mission intents. The benchmark provides radar, RGB, infrared, and depth observations, together with program-disjoint, radar-gap, and observation-prefix evaluation protocols. Building on this benchmark, we propose AeroMIR, a structured Multimodal Intent Reasoner that integrates radar trajectories, derived behavioral features, selected visual evidence, and task knowledge for candidate-based UAV intent recognition. Under a strict program-disjoint protocol evaluating unseen tactical realizations, AeroMIR achieves a mean accuracy of 71.56% and a mean Macro-F1 of 69.84% across three seeds, outperforming the strongest trajectory-only baseline by 7.79 Macro-F1 points and a conventional radar-RGB late-fusion baseline by 19.32 points. AeroMIR also demonstrates strong performance under controlled radar gaps and early intent recognition settings. AeroIntent and AeroMIR provide a reproducible foundation for multimodal UAV intent recognition. The benchmark is available at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/AeroIntent

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: Learning Wheel Motion Uncertainty for Degeneracy-Aware LiDAR-Inertial Odometry on Quadrupedal Wheel-Legged Robots
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Hairuo Wei, Yunfan Ren, Renda Yang, Qiangsheng Huang, Zhongyu Li
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: This paper presents a LiDAR-inertial odometry framework for quadrupedal wheel-legged robots that learns motion uncertainty, significantly improving accuracy in challenging environments.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Wheel kinematics can support odometry for quadrupedal wheel-legged robots when LiDAR geometry provides weak motion constraints. However, slip and contact loss make rolling predictions unreliable, and contact state alone cannot determine their reliability across motion directions. We propose a tightly coupled LiDAR-inertial-kinematic odometry framework that retains analytical rolling predictions and learns per-wheel, direction-dependent process covariances from proprioceptive history. The estimator maintains moving wheel-center states, allowing the learned uncertainty to regulate the influence of rolling predictions through forward-kinematic corrections. Degeneracy-aware projection (DAP) complements this mechanism by suppressing LiDAR constraints along geometrically weak directions. The learned covariance network (CovNet) is trained through a differentiable filter using simulated velocity supervision and deployed on the real robot without fine-tuning. On the six room sequences with the highest degeneracy ratios in our indoor dataset, the method reduces mean per-sequence position root mean square error (RMSE) by 66.2% relative to FAST-LIO2 and by 31.0% relative to a fixed-covariance variant. In a severely degenerate corridor run, it achieves an endpoint position error of 0.198 m, compared with 7.531 m for FAST-LIO2. These results demonstrate robust odometry under challenging geometric and wheel-motion conditions. We plan to publicly release our code and multimodal dataset. Project website: https://weihairuo.github.io/wheel-motion-uncertainty/

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: Beyond Omni: A Unified MLLM for Embodied Sensory Understanding
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Shiyun Xiong, Dongming Wu, Peiwen Sun, Bokang Yang, Jiaxu Wang
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: Unisense is a unified MLLM framework that enhances embodied sensory understanding by integrating diverse modalities through a two-stage training process, outperforming existing models.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Recent embodied systems increasingly build on multimodal large language models (MLLMs) for their pretrained understanding and reasoning capabilities, but their perception of the physical world remains largely limited to basic modalities such as vision and audio. However, broadening MLLMs to more diverse sensory modalities from the physical environment is challenging: their representations are often weakly connected to the MLLM and vary substantially in structure and statistics, while their interpretation still requires shared high-level understanding and reasoning. We therefore propose Unisense, a unified embodied MLLM framework that supports diverse physical sensory modalities within a shared multimodal architecture. Unisense follows a two-stage training process: (i) aligning sensory representations with language to establish a language-accessible interface; and (ii) tuning modality-specific experts within the shared LLM to provide specialized processing for different sensory modalities. To support broad sensory learning, we curate Unisense-1M, a large-scale embodied sensory training corpus comprising 1M samples across 8 sensory modalities. We further evaluate Unisense on 12 benchmarks spanning depth, point cloud, IMU, tactile, thermal, radar, motion, and smell understanding. Across these heterogeneous sensing tasks, Unisense achieves strong performance and outperforms both generalist and specialized models on most benchmarks, demonstrating the potential of pretrained MLLMs as unified models for embodied sensory understanding.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: Mise-en-Video: Fine-Grained 3D Control for Multi-Shot Video Generation
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Yingshuang Zou, Xiaoyu Shi, Yawen Luo, Ziang Li, Qinghe Wang
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: Mise-en-Video introduces a controllable multi-shot video generation framework that enhances narrative consistency and spatial control through hierarchical attention and 3D layout guidance.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Recent advances in text-to-video generation have enabled high-fidelity single-shot synthesis, yet practical storytelling creation requires multi-shot videos with both strong inter-shot consistency and fine-grained controllability. Existing multi-shot video generation approaches achieve strong consistency but still fall short in controllability. In this paper, we propose Mise-en-Video (MeV), a highly controllable multi-shot video generation framework that allows video creators to conduct staging the multi-shot in the 3D space and then generate the corresponding multi-shot video. To achieve this, our framework combines a hierarchical attention mechanism for multi-level narrative consistency with 3D-aware layout guidance for precise, per-shot spatial control. To support training and evaluation, we develop standardized annotation pipelines and construct a 160K-video dataset with hierarchical multi-shot texts and oriented 3D bounding boxes. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MeV consistently outperforms strong baselines in video quality, inter-shot consistency, and subject-level controllability.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: Can It Actually Work? Synthesizing Functional CAD Mechanisms
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Wenqian Zhang, Yangyi Huang, Zigeng Xu, Weiyang Liu, Zhen Liu
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: The paper presents FunCAD-Harness, a framework that improves functional CAD design by translating abstract requirements into physical tests, enhancing mechanism success rates through simulation feedback.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: While LLM agents can generate visually plausible CAD assemblies, these designs often fail to fulfill their intended physical functions. We study functional CAD design, a setting where agents interpret underspecified requests to construct and iteratively revise mechanisms that satisfy functional requirements in physical simulation. Verifying these requirements is nontrivial: different candidate mechanisms may realize the same function through entirely different components, controls, and operating sequences. To bridge this gap, we propose FunCAD-Harness, a framework that translates abstract requirements into candidate-specific physical tests and uses simulation feedback to guide design revisions. To systematically evaluate this capability, we introduce FunCADBench, a benchmark spanning 46 mechanism families with interdependent and multi-step operations. Experiments across frontier LLM agents show that FunCAD-Harness exposes subtle mechanical failures invisible to visual inspection, substantially improving functional success rates over standard simulation-augmented baselines. Ultimately, our work marks a step toward CAD agents capable of translating human intent into working mechanisms.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: EVA: Aligning Video World Models with Executable Robot Actions via Inverse Dynamics Rewards
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Ruixiang Wang, Qingming Liu, Yueci Deng, Guiliang Liu, Zhen Liu
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: EVA enhances video generative models for robotic planning by aligning visual outputs with executable actions through inverse dynamics rewards, reducing artifacts and improving task success.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Video generative models offer a promising basis for robotic planning by predicting future visual rollouts from observations and task instructions. However, their training objectives typically lack explicit constraints on robot executability. Generated rollouts can exhibit embodiment-related artifacts, including arm deformation and temporal discontinuities, while the actions decoded from these rollouts may be unstable or violate robot motion limits. We term this mismatch between generated robot behavior and embodiment-specific execution requirements the executability gap. We introduce Executable Video Alignment (EVA), a post-training framework that uses action-space feedback to improve both the visual integrity of generated robot motion and the feasibility of decoded actions. EVA trains an inverse dynamics model (IDM) on robot demonstrations and freezes it to decode actions from generated videos. We compute a reward from these actions that penalizes non-smooth motion and violations of velocity and acceleration limits, and use it to guide reinforcement-learning updates to the video generator. By feeding decoded-action constraints back into video generation, EVA links visual and action-level improvements through a shared alignment signal. Experiments on RoboTwin, LIBERO, and a real bimanual robot show that EVA reduces embodiment-related visual artifacts and improves task success when executing IDM-decoded actions. Further experiments show that video models fine-tuned with EVA generate more effective video--action pairs for training downstream VLAs.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: AffordanceVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model Empowering Action Generation through Affordance-Aware Understanding
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Qize Yu, Jiadi You, Yuran Wang, Jiaqi Liang, Bowen Ping
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: AffordanceVLA introduces a structured affordance learning framework that enhances vision-language-action models for improved robotic manipulation through precise perception-action mappings.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models leverage the rich world knowledge of pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) to enable instruction-following robotic manipulation. However, the structural mismatch between VLM semantic spaces and embodied control policies often hinders the learning of precise perception-action mappings. To address this challenge, we propose AffordanceVLA, a scalable, unified framework that introduces structured affordance learning as a task-oriented and object-centric intermediate representation to establish a more precise and robust perception-action mapping. Specifically, we progressively model manipulation priors through three complementary components - Which2Act, Where2Act, and How2Act - which jointly produce spatially grounded, semantically conditioned, and action-coupled intermediate representations, thereby naturally bridging vision, language, and action. We integrate these modules into a Mixture-of-Transformer (MoT) architecture and adopt a three-stage progressive training curriculum that leverages 8.8M affordance-centric grounding and pointing samples, translating scalable vision-language supervision into improved robotic manipulation. To overcome the scarcity of dense affordance labels in robotic datasets, we also develop a robust automated data augmentation pipeline. Extensive experiments on ID & OOD simulation and real-world demonstrate that AffordanceVLA outperforms strong VLA baselines across diverse manipulation scenarios, validating structured affordance learning as a scalable and robust bridge that integrates multi-source vision-language supervision while connecting pretrained VLM semantics to embodied robot control.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: EndoVLA-OOV: Language-Conditioned Out-of-View Target Acquisition in Robotic Endoscopy
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Chi Kit Ng, Yidong Zhang, Tianchun Wu, Zhiqing Tang, Hanlin Zhao
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: EndoVLA-OOV is a language-conditioned policy for robotic endoscopy that enhances out-of-view target acquisition, achieving up to 93.3% success through advanced vision-language-action integration.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: The scan-then-revisit workflow of upper gastrointestinal endoscopy requires bringing a previously observed suspicious region back into view for closer inspection. Acquiring such targets requires translating anatomical and appearance descriptions into camera motions from partial observations of a confined, deformable environment. We present EndoVLA-OOV, a language-conditioned vision-language-action policy for out-of-view target acquisition in robotic endoscopy. The policy adapts a pretrained backbone to continuous two-degree-of-freedom distal bending commands and combines initial, intermediate, and current images to guide search. To support policy learning, we provide an open-source VLA dataset containing 1,050 episodes across six tasks and approximately 262k observation-action pairs. Physical evaluation spans wet-lens and low-light conditions, two unseen stomach phantoms, and cross-embodiment transfer to an unseen ex-vivo environment. In the cross-embodiment evaluation, the full-data policy achieves 93.3% target acquisition success (28/30). In a controlled training-data comparison, expanding the corpus from 312 to 1,050 episodes increases acquisition success from 40.0% to 90.0% under the same model, training, and test configuration. Instruction and observation interventions further support the use of language and temporal context in the evaluated acquisition tasks. These results support language-guided endoscopic revisitation across the evaluated environments and robot embodiments and demonstrate the benefit of expanded task-specific demonstrations.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: Map2Vid: Embodied Navigation Video Generation with Human-Friendly Motion Control
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Yulin Dai, Yuqian Fu, Tianwen Qian, Zhen Xing, Bojia Zi
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: Map2Vid introduces a novel framework for generating navigation videos from BEV maps, enhancing human-friendly control and evaluation through a large-scale dataset and integrated signals.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Controllable video generation has recently achieved impressive visual quality, yet existing control paradigms remain poorly suited to embodied navigation. Text prompts are spatially ambiguous, while camera-trajectory control relies on low-level motion specifications that are unintuitive for human users and difficult to manipulate. In this work, we introduce Map2Vid, a novel task that reformulates embodied navigation video generation as a BEV-map-to-video synthesis problem, together with a large-scale benchmark for systematic evaluation. By using BEV maps, which provide a visual representation of global scene layout and intended navigation routes, Map2Vid enables human-friendly navigation video generation. To support this task, we construct a dedicated dataset with over 100K navigation sequences across 61 indoor scenes, each paired with egocentric videos, BEV maps, camera trajectories and language instructions. We further develop a unified framework that integrates multiple control signals, together with a curriculum training strategy that progressively weakens non-map inputs, enabling flexible inference under both full conditioning and map-only input. Extensive experiments across multiple foundation generation models demonstrate that controllable navigation video generation via BEV map is a viable and promising direction.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: MotionShift: Environment-Compatible Motion Transfer via Planner-Evaluator Synergistic Adaptation
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Yanchen Liu, Junyao Gao, Yanan Sun, Wensheng Chen, Guangming Lu
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: MotionShift introduces a planner-evaluator framework using LLMs and VLMs for high-fidelity, physically compatible motion transfer in diverse scenes without requiring additional training.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Existing motion transfer methods excel at exact, rigid motion replication from reference videos to target scenes, whereas they often fail to account for the compatibility between the transferred motion and the target scene environment in accordance with physical laws. In this work, we propose MotionShift, a novel motion transfer framework that achieves high-fidelity motion transfer while ensuring physical compatibility with the target scene. In particular, we design a planner--evaluator iterative motion adaptation mechanism, in which a Large Language Model (LLM) acts as the planner to generate motion trajectories by leveraging its strong semantic reasoning capabilities, while a Vision-Language Model (VLM) serves as the evaluator to rectify the motion based on its superior visual perception and scene understanding. Through this planner--evaluator synergistic reasoning process, the motion is adapted to the target scene in a training-free manner. The adapted motion is then used as a generative condition for an image-to-video (I2V) model to render videos in the target scene. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MotionShift achieves high-fidelity and physically compatible motion transfer across diverse and complex scenes. Moreover, we show that MotionShift can be readily integrated into existing trajectory-conditioned I2V models, endowing them with realistic motion transfer capabilities.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: MCSplat: Multi-View Photometric and Geometric Consistent Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting for Driving Scenes
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Yifei Wang, Wei Tian, Wenhua Bao, Jia Zhou, Hanshi Wang
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: MCSplat introduces a multi-view Gaussian splatting framework that enhances driving scene reconstruction by decoupling geometry from camera-specific appearance and improving local geometric reliability.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Driving-scene reconstruction via feed-forward Gaussian splatting from sparse multi-view images remains challenging due to two factors. First, cross-camera photometric inconsistency, caused by variations in exposure, ISP, and illumination, can be incorrectly absorbed into Gaussian geometry. Second, unreliable local geometric supervision arises from normal-based constraints near depth discontinuities. To address these issues, we present \textbf{MCSplat}, a multi-view consistent feed-forward Gaussian splatting framework for driving scenes. MCSplat constructs a canonical appearance space from depth-guided multi-camera correspondences to decouple geometry learning from camera-specific appearance. A multi-scale Bilateral Grid Transformer restores raw camera appearance from canonical renderings, enabling photometric supervision without contaminating Gaussian geometry. To improve local geometric reliability, we estimate Fisher-information-based uncertainty from photometric sensitivity and use it to adaptively weight surface-oriented self-supervision. Extensive experiments demonstrate improved reconstruction quality and generalization across driving datasets. Geometry-oriented evaluations further reveal enhanced cross-view depth consistency and local surface-normal agreement, while qualitative results show fewer geometric artifacts and more coherent structures across overlapping views.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: MVISTA-4D: View-Consistent 4D World Model with Test-Time Action Inference for Robotic Manipulation
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Jiaxu Wang, Yicheng Jiang, Tianlun He, Jingkai Sun, Qiang Zhang
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: MVISTA-4D introduces a view-consistent 4D world model for robotic manipulation, enabling comprehensive scene dynamics prediction and optimized action inference from single-view RGBD inputs.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: World-model-based imagine-then-act becomes a promising paradigm for robotic manipulation, yet existing approaches typically support either purely image-based forecasting or reasoning over partial 3D geometry, limiting their ability to predict complete 4D scene dynamics. This work proposes a novel embodied 4D world model that enables geometrically consistent, arbitrary-view RGBD generation: given only a single-view RGBD observation as input, the model imagines the remaining viewpoints, which can then be back-projected and fused to assemble a more complete 3D structure across time. To efficiently learn the multi-view, cross-modality generation, we explicitly design cross-view and cross-modality feature fusion that jointly encourage consistency between RGB and depth and enforce geometric alignment across views. Beyond prediction, converting generated futures into actions is often handled by inverse dynamics, which is ill-posed because multiple actions can explain the same transition. We address this with a test-time action optimization strategy that backpropagates through the generative model to infer a trajectory-level latent best matching the predicted future, and a residual inverse dynamics model that turns this trajectory prior into accurate executable actions. Experiments on three datasets demonstrate strong performance on both 4D scene generation and downstream manipulation, and ablations provide practical insights into the key design choices.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: ELAN4D: Embodiment-Centric 4D Supervision for Vision-Language-Action Models via Plug-and-Play Adaptation
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Zeyuan He, Bowen Yang, Zhirui Fang, Keru Zhou, Lei Jiang
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: ELAN4D enhances Vision-Language-Action models by integrating 4D predictive supervision from robot keypoint tracks, improving robustness and generalization in robotic manipulation tasks.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown promise for robotic manipulation, yet most existing policies operate reactively by directly regressing actions from current observations, without explicitly modeling future dynamics. This limits their ability to generalize under out-of-distribution perturbations. To address this issue, we propose ELAN4D, an embodiment-centric, 4D-aware training framework that enhances VLA policies with future robot keypoint tracks as predictive spatio-temporal supervision. Using only forward kinematics from proprioceptive states, we derive 3D displacement tracks of robot keypoints, such as joints and the end-effector, with negligible preprocess cost. These tracks provide metric and compact supervision without requiring external trackers or reconstruction. A plug-and-play auxiliary branch with a lightweight track decoder injects this 4D signal into the action expert while preserving the pretrained vision-language backbone through gradient isolation. The track decoder is discarded during inference, leaving the base policy interface unchanged. Extensive experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin2.0 and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate that ELAN4D consistently improves over strong VLA baselines, achieving the best overall performance and substantial gains under out-of-distribution perturbations, including camera, background, and layout shifts. These results highlight the effectiveness of embodiment-centric 4D supervision for building more robust and generalizable manipulation policies.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: Humanoid Badminton: Learning Dynamic Racket Skills from Limited Human Motion Data
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Jingzhi Cui, Zhexiong Wang, Bangjie Xu, Pengyu Zhao, Youyuan Li
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: This paper presents a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework enabling humanoid robots to perform dynamic badminton skills and engage in multi-skill rallies with humans.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: High-speed racket sports provide a demanding testbed for humanoid robots, requiring time-critical decisions, precise striking, and dynamic whole-body coordination. In badminton, fast-changing shuttle trajectories require timely contact decisions, while successful returns demand precise racket pose and velocity within a brief contact window and across a broad three-dimensional striking workspace. Human motion data provide valuable priors for such athletic skills, but usable badminton references are limited and imperfect. Direct tracking provides insufficient executable variation for diverse shuttle conditions, while purely task-driven optimization may produce unnatural motion. We therefore present a three-stage hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for dynamic humanoid badminton. First, task-randomized motion augmentation expands sparse annotated hitting events into executable target-conditioned stroke variations, forming a continuous latent skill space. Second, a high-level planner outputs continuous latent skill codes to compose these skills online according to the observed shuttle state. Third, a context-conditioned adversarial regularizer encourages more natural planner-level skill usage while preserving return performance. In real-world deployment, our system sustains multi-skill rallies with human players, including forehand, backhand, and highly dynamic jump returns. This is the first real-world humanoid racket-sport system to demonstrate multi-skill human--robot rallies including highly dynamic jump returns.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: Drive2Gauss: FeedForward 4D Gaussian Reconstruction from Multimodal Generative Driving Videos
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Tong Zhao, Zhiyuan Han, Lin Chen, Bowen Xie, Yunxi Qiao
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: Drive2Gauss introduces a feedforward framework for dynamic 4D Gaussian scene reconstruction from multimodal driving videos, enhancing efficiency and rendering capabilities without optimization.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Generating reusable driving environments requires both controllable future observations and an explicit representation that supports rendering from different viewpoints, yet existing methods still recover explicit scenes from generated RGB videos through optimization for each sequence. To overcome these limitations, we present Drive2Gauss, a feedforward framework that converts jointly generated RGB, metric depth, and dynamic flow into dynamic 4D Gaussian scenes. A Multimodal Video Generator predicts the three modalities from reference multiview images and future control signals. Furthermore, we introduce a Gaussian Query Decoder that uses depth to initialize sparse 3D queries and flow to associate the queries across time, and integrates appearance information through spatiotemporal feature aggregation and iterative query refinement. The reconstruction stage operates in a single feedforward pass without optimization for each scene. Extensive results on nuScenes demonstrate that our approach attains an FID of 6.38 and an FVD of 12.43 for future RGB generation, a PSNR of 29.91 dB when reconstructing its generated observations, and supports both direct rendering under lateral camera shifts and downstream video fixing. Code and more visualizations are available at https://zttt04. github.io/Drive2Gauss_page/.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: R$^2$ Flow: Recursive Self-Improvement via Recursive Skill Evolution
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Mingda Zhang, Qiang Huang, Yanjin Li, Zijia Wang, Qika Lin
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: R$^2$ Flow introduces a recursive self-improvement framework for LLM-based agents that enhances task accuracy and skill evolution through flow-based training and evidence verification.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: LLM-based agents can improve themselves across tasks by reusing and revising the skills they orchestrate into executable procedures. Flow-based training fits this loop: it samples procedures in proportion to reward, and the flow through each skill credits it for the next library revision. Three obstacles stand in the way of making this self-improvement reliable: flow training suffers strategy collapse over tree-structured histories; nonnegative flow-based credit rewards frequent use as if it were benefit; and library edits rest on the task reward the policy optimizes. We introduce R$^2$ Flow, a recursive self-improvement framework that alternates policy learning, independent verification, and versioned skill-library updates on a shared-state orchestration graph. The graph merges histories that differ only in the order of independent steps, allowing flow training to pool evidence across equivalent executions. A flow-share readout of the trained flow, invariant to the backward policy, and a separate signed utility rank which skills to change, verifier evidence decides whether an edit is warranted, and a residual-variance plateau sets when to update. Committed edits reshape the graph the next policy learns on, realizing recursive skill evolution. Across question answering, mathematical reasoning, interactive decision making, and code generation, R$^2$ Flow improves task accuracy and library-edit precision over heuristic orchestration, reinforcement learning, and skill-evolution baselines, and transfers across executors. Code is available at https://github.com/beita6969/r2flow.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: NativeMEM: Native Memory Compression for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Ziye Wang, Modi Shi, Chaojun Ni, Jiazhi Yang, Mengdi Li
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: NativeMEM introduces an efficient memory compression method for Vision-Language-Action models, enhancing long-horizon robotic manipulation performance while reducing latency and memory usage.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: How can pretrained Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models retain long-horizon visual histories with high-frequency updates without sacrificing efficiency? Existing approaches rely on external memory management, which restrains either the memory horizon or the reactiveness of pretrained policies. To this end, we present NativeMEM, a VLA policy that features long-term and real-time updated memory. At its core is an efficient memory encoding scheme, Native Memory Compression, which repurposes the VLA's own vision encoder to compress each historical frame from each camera view into a single token. Appended to the input sequence, these memory tokens enable the pretrained VLA to attend over long-term history with negligible latency overhead, requiring neither an external planner nor a freshly initialized memory module. To align the memory tokens with the pretrained policy, we first develop a generic memory tokenizer under the supervision of a frozen VLA on memory-demanding data, and then unfreeze the VLA for task-specific fine-tuning. NativeMEM consistently outperforms prior methods, boosting success rates from 32.4% to 84.0% in simulation and up to 98.7% on real robots, while maintaining low inference latency and GPU memory usage. Notably, NativeMEM exhibits high data efficiency by achieving competitive results with prior arts using only 20% of the training data.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: Learning to Discriminate Scene Structures Makes Self-Supervised Depth Learning Scalable
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Mengtan Zhang, Yuchuan Cui, Yu Ma, Zizhan Guo, Wei Ye
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: The MaSS framework enhances self-supervised monocular depth estimation by decoupling structural representations from contextual features, improving scalability and generalizability across diverse datasets.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Self-supervised monocular depth estimation is appealing for its potential to scale with unlabeled data, yet existing methods often degrade when trained on diverse scenes. This study finds that, under self-supervision, models tend to encode dataset-specific structural biases rather than transferable scene geometry, leading to cross-domain optimization conflicts. To address this issue, this study proposes the MaSS framework, aiming to make self-supervised depth learning scalable to diverse data. MaSS introduces a dedicated structural representation pathway explicitly decoupled from contextual features, which is guided by a novel scene-structure discrimination objective to learn generalized, layout-aware structural representations for depth decoding. Trained and evaluated on four diverse datasets, both individually and jointly, MaSS substantially outperforms prior self-supervised methods and is the first to consistently benefit from mixed-domain training. Zero-shot evaluation on eight additional datasets further demonstrates its remarkable generalizability, particularly on those entirely out-of-distribution scenes. The source code is publicly available at https://mias.group/MaSS.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: FlexPart: Text-Controlled Semantics-Aware 3D Part Segmentation at Flexible Granularity
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Yiqun Zhao, Jiachen Xu, Yihao Zhi, Yunfei Zhao, Zibo Zhao
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: FLEXPART is a novel framework for text-controlled 3D mesh segmentation that enables flexible, semantics-aware part extraction, outperforming existing models in accuracy and granularity.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: A 3D asset admits multiple valid part decompositions, while semantics-aware segmentation should reflect both the desired granularity and the parts a user wants to extract. Ideally, a practical segmentation model should strive for a simple principle: what you ask for is what you get. However, realizing this goal is hindered by two core obstacles: the lack of multi-granularity training data and the absence of a holistic control mechanism. We propose FLEXPART, a unified framework for text-controlled 3D mesh segmentation. To establish flexible control, we introduce a holistic control prompt comprising semantic part names with location and shape clauses. To support this mechanism, we utilize an automated Vision-Language Model (VLM) pipeline to construct a large-scale dataset of multi-granularity partitions and their corresponding prompts. Driven by this data, FLEXPART generates a view-independent part-identity field in native 3D space, directly assigning discrete part IDs to mesh faces. To compel the model to respect semantic conditions rather than rely on geometric priors, we train the model using randomized background dropping. Furthermore, an inference-time VLM planner can automatically complete descriptive clauses from 2D renderings, allowing users to simply name the desired parts in ordinary words. FLEXPART with planner-completed prompts outperforms the strongest evaluated baseline by 15% in mIoU, even when that baseline receives ground-truth guidance. On our held-out FLEXPARTBENCH, FLEXPART leads at each granularity and improves average mIoU by 22% over the strongest baseline. With only the requested part names supplied by the user, it also improves IoU by 35% over the strongest click-driven baseline on selective segmentation.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: R$^2$Orch: Recursive Self-Improvement for Agent Orchestration via Self-Play within a Skill-Internalization Loop
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Mingda Zhang, Yun Huang, Qiang Huang, Yanjin Li, Rui Qian
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: R$^2$Orch introduces a recursive self-play framework for agent orchestration that enhances skill learning and evaluation, outperforming traditional methods across various complex tasks.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: In recent years, agentic orchestration has been widely applied to solve complex human tasks. However, existing orchestration learning still faces key challenges, including hand-designed curricula, advantage collapse when a task's rollouts all reach the same outcome, and unreliable evaluation signals that judge each skill by one noisy score. To address these challenges, we propose R$^2$Orch, a new paradigm of Recursive Self-Play Orchestration: an inner loop of self-play that improves the orchestrator on self-chosen tasks, and an outer loop that improves how the inner loop improves. To support this paradigm, we introduce Recursive Learnability, a training objective that rewards a Proposer for choosing tasks whose rollouts keep reaching different outcomes as skills are withdrawn. Built on this objective, we further propose Skill Withdrawal, in which the outer loop withdraws each skill once a controlled evaluation within self-play shows that the orchestrator performs as well without it. Moreover, the two loops form one cycle: failures are distilled into skills, skills into parameters, and withdrawals lead the Proposer to new failures, so the orchestrator moves toward zero-skill deployment. Experimental results on twelve datasets show that R$^2$Orch consistently outperforms baselines across question answering, math, code, and interactive tasks.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: Reward Engine: Reward-Centric Self-Evolution for Open-Ended Tool Agents
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Litong Feng, Ji Qi, Yiran Cheng, Shaowu Pan, Xinyu Zhang
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: The Reward Engine constructs a stable, experience-based reward system for open-ended tool agents, improving execution consistency and aligning closely with benchmark evaluations.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Open-ended tool agents can complete the same objective through different tool paths, and their quality depends jointly on the interaction trace, environment state, and final artifacts, so such tasks rarely admit an executable ground-truth reward. The central challenge is therefore to construct a reward from existing experience that exposes the current policy's failures while remaining stationary during optimization. We introduce Reward Engine, which, like a self-motivated student, first works out what success requires and then optimizes toward it. From the task and initial trajectories, it builds a RewardPack of testcases for required correctness and rubrics for graded quality, each executed as a check that returns a judgment with evidence. The frozen RewardPack then guides the agent to revise and select its outputs, and can also serve as a reward for reinforcement learning. On WorkBuddy Bench Office and Claw-Eval, the constructed reward largely agrees with the benchmark graders, not reversing their ordering on 82.3\% and 80.5\% of candidate pairs. Used to revise executions, it raises three-run consistency ($\mathrm{Pass}^{3}$) over Baseline from 45.0\% to 54.0\% and from 78.4\% to 83.7\%.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: Referring Multi-Object Tracking with Diverse Dynamic Expressions
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Yani Zhang, Dongming Wu, Wencheng Han, Xingping Dong, Shengcai Liao
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: This paper introduces referring multi-object tracking (RMOT) to enhance object localization using diverse language expressions and a novel Transformer-based framework, TempRMOT, achieving state-of-the-art results.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Referring understanding is a fundamental task that bridges natural language and visual content by localizing objects described in free-form expressions. However, existing works are constrained by limited language expressiveness, lacking the capacity to model object dynamics in spatial numbers and temporal states. To address these limitations, we introduce a new and general referring understanding task, termed referring multi-object tracking (RMOT). Its core idea is to employ a language expression as a semantic cue to guide the prediction of multi-object tracking, comprehensively accounting for variations in object quantity and temporal semantics. Along with RMOT, we introduce a RMOT benchmark named Refer-KITTI-V2, featuring scalable and diverse language expressions. To efficiently generate high-quality annotations covering object dynamics with minimal manual effort, we propose a semi-automatic labeling pipeline that formulates a total of 9,758 language prompts. In addition, we propose TempRMOT, an elegant end-to-end Transformer-based framework for RMOT. At its core is a query-driven Temporal Enhancement Module that represents each object as a Transformer query, enabling long-term spatial-temporal interactions with other objects and past frames to efficiently refine these queries. TempRMOT achieves state-of-the-art performance on both Refer-KITTI and Refer-KITTI-V2, demonstrating the effectiveness of our approach. The source code and dataset is available at https://github.com/zyn213/TempRMOT.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: GRASP: Global-Local Representation Alignment and Spatial-Physical Grounding for Bimanual Robotic Manipulation
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Zeyuan Ren, Guanxun Zhao, Qi Li, Hao Wang, Wenlong Liao
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: The paper presents a training framework for bimanual robotic manipulation that aligns global-local representations and incorporates spatial-physical grounding to enhance task success and adaptability.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models that directly regress joint-space actions avoid the deployment-time cost of inverse kinematics. However, their training objectives remain misaligned with task success, as joint-space losses ignore the unequal physical consequences of joint errors and visual conditioning lacks explicit focus on hand-object interaction regions. To address these issues, we propose a training-phase prior injection framework for fine-grained bimanual manipulation. First, a physics-grounded flow-matching loss maps the implicit clean-action estimate at every noise level through differentiable forward kinematics (FK) and supervises the resulting Tool Center Point (TCP) pose and inter-arm relative pose, with a bounded noise-level weighting that compensates gradient decay. Second, we introduce a global prediction query group distilled from a frozen DINOv3 teacher through future-frame feature prediction, together with a local interaction query supervised by Grounding DINO at the attention level. Both teachers are removed at inference, and the deployment pipeline is that of a standard joint-space flow policy, adding only the learned query pathway. Simulation and real-robot experiments on long-horizon bimanual tasks show that the two priors are complementary across different deployment settings. The full model excels in in-distribution deployment, while the distilled query branch is preferable under strong visual randomization.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: RoPE-Flow: Monocular Vision-based Robot Pose Estimation via 2D Graph-Conditioned 3D Flow Matching
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Liangjing Shao, Wanhao Liu, Zhiwei Fang, Rulin Zhou, Quanlu Zhang
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: RoPE-Flow introduces an end-to-end framework for monocular robot pose estimation using flow matching, enhancing accuracy and consistency through innovative feature extraction and loss functions.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Camera-to-robot pose estimation from a monocular image is significant for vision-based robot navigation and control. However, recovering 3D structural features from 2D observations remains a challenging task. Existing camera-to-robot pose estimation methods either rely on time-consuming iterative rendering or involve sophisticated 2D-3D registration which suffers from projection ambiguity, accumulated errors for distal joints and imbalanced learning for different joints. In this work, we propose RoPE-Flow, an end-to-end flow matching-based framework for camera-to-robot pose estimation. From the predicted 2D heatmaps, we propose a Keypoint-centered Feature Extractor to obtain positional features along with contextual representations from keypoints-centered multi-scale patches. Moreover, we introduce Graph-guided Condition Generator, which embeds a learnable adjacency map to generate condition for flow matching based on correlation among keypoints. Besides, we introduce Bone Length Loss and Ray-Depth Loss for topological consistency and scale stability, with joint-wise weighting to mitigate varied prediction difficulty across joints. The proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods for pose estimation across different types of robots with mutiple cameras. Besides, we establish a novel cross-scene benchmark to demonstrate the outstanding performance of RoPE-Flow on zero-shot cross-scene robot pose estimation. Meanwhile, animated visualizations are shown on the website: ropeflow.netlify.app

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: Anvil: Scaling Embodied Spatial Intelligence through Knowledge Recirculation
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Weilin Ruan, Bohan Zhou, Jinghao Li, Yangkai Wei, Wenqian Li
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: Anvil is a unified framework enhancing embodied spatial intelligence through innovative data generation, training, and benchmarking, significantly outperforming existing models in various benchmarks.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Embodied spatial intelligence requires more than visual recognition: models must localize entities, reason about their relations, and express this knowledge in action-relevant forms. Yet joint training can conflate the knowledge needed at different stages because supervision is fragmented across incompatible geometric and semantic outputs. We introduce Anvil, a unified framework for data generation, training, and benchmarking for embodied spatial intelligence. (1) Anvil-Gen is a heterogeneous data flywheel that combines form-specific generation, cross-stage consistency verification, and failure-driven recollection across 11 Ground--Relation--Act forms. (2) Anvil-Ben provides scene-aligned supervision for learning diverse embodied spatial capabilities and scene-linked assessments that distinguish stage competence from error propagation. (3) Anvil-MOPD is a 9B student that consolidates heterogeneous spatial knowledge through distillation from specialist teachers. Semantic-first-fault routing targets teacher supervision to the student's earliest decisive failure, while stage normalization controls the loss scale across native outputs of different lengths. We construct 5.8M source-grounded records spanning 160K images, reserving 580K spatial records for held-out evaluation and using the remaining 5.22M records for training. On average across seven public benchmarks, Anvil-MOPD outperforms Qwen3.5-9B and RynnBrain-8B by 9.29 and 11.03 percentage points, respectively, while reaching 80.67% on VABench-Point. Controlled studies support targeted coverage, selective transfer, and feedback-guided repair as complementary framework components.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: BridgeAfford: Bridging Query-Target Gap for Generalizable 3D Affordance Grounding
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Yijie Su, Yakun Zhu, Yi Bin, Pengpeng Zeng, Liang Chen
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: BridgeAfford enhances 3D affordance grounding by aligning interaction regions and refining query attention, significantly improving generalization to unseen objects.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Language-guided 3D affordance grounding aims to localize functional regions on 3D objects according to interaction intents. However, existing methods exhibit poor generalization to unseen objects. One challenge is the query-target gap: a semantic discrepancy between query features encoding interaction intents and target-region features, leading to inaccurate grounding. End-to-end training favors query representations tailored to seen objects, limiting their compatibility with shifted target-region features on unseen objects. To address this issue, we propose BridgeAfford, a framework that reduces the query-target semantic gap from two complementary perspectives. First, Interaction Region Alignment (IRA) promotes cross-object alignment among geometrically similar interaction regions during training. This enables structures on unseen objects that resemble previously observed ones to produce representations similar to those learned during training, facilitating target-region recognition. Second, Visual Evidence Aggregation (VEA) leverages a 2D affordance model to refine the attention distribution and guide the query toward the correct region, yielding more target-aware queries. Extensive experiments on the LASO and PIAD datasets demonstrate that BridgeAfford outperforms existing methods, particularly on unseen objects, highlighting its robust generalization ability.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Hongchang Liu, Jian Liu, Yujuan Ding, Liang Peng, Xun Jiang
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: GeoState introduces a view-decoupled geometry representation for 3D world modeling, enhancing predictive accuracy by separating scene dynamics from camera variations.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Recent 3D world models increasingly use features from geometry foundation models (GFMs) as predictive world states, benefiting from their rich geometric priors. However, the view dependence of these features entangles scene dynamics with camera-induced variation, making the resulting state evolution harder to predict. We propose GeoState, a view-decoupled geometry representation for predictive 3D world modeling that separates scene-state evolution from camera-dependent observation. Specifically, a scene tokenizer aggregates multi-view GFM features into a view-decoupled scene state, which a geometry decoder queries using camera rays. An autoregressive world model then predicts future scene states, while camera motion is modeled separately. The predicted states can therefore be decoded under either predicted or externally specified cameras, while retaining a single context-derived scale throughout the rollout without per-frame scale alignment. Experiments show that GeoState outperforms prior 3D world models on Waymo, supports geometrically consistent cross-view querying, and generalizes zero-shot to KITTI and nuScenes. Project page: https://hongchang-liu.github.io/GeoState-project-page/

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: CoDA: Co-Evolution of Data Engines and Action Policies
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Tianjiao Yu, Zhilin Ou, Yifan Shen, Xinzhuo Li, Yuanzhe Liu
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: CoDA is a co-evolution framework that enhances robot training by integrating simulation data engines and action policies through a shared memory of failures and learning progress, significantly improving out-of-distribution success rates.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Generative simulation can automate robot environment construction, but physically valid environments are not necessarily useful for training. The challenge is to identify environments that address a policy's failures and supervision that helps it overcome them. We introduce CoDA, a framework in which a simulation data engine and an action policy co-evolve through a shared heterogeneous memory of environment construction, policy failures, and learning progress. The memory compiles validated diagnoses from a vision-language critic into generation programs that recreate difficulties and training programs that help the policy overcome them. We further propose Text2potential to convert these diagnoses into staged potentials for action-chunk value learning, providing dense supervision for policy updates while preserving the task's optimal policy under standard shaping assumptions. Measured learning progress guides further generation and program refinement. Across four manipulation task families, CoDA improves out-of-distribution success from 5.3% after supervised fine-tuning to 27.6%, exceeding the strongest closed-loop baseline by 9.5 percentage points with the same generation budget. On LIBERO-Pro, 15 rounds of generation and training raise success from 25% to 84% under position perturbations and from 1% to 76% under instruction perturbations.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: Affordance-Aware Interactive Decision-Making and Execution for Ambiguous Instructions
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Hengxuan Xu, Fengbo Lan, Zhixin Zhao, Shengjie Wang, Mengqiao Liu
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: The AIDE framework enhances robot interaction with ambiguous instructions by integrating vision-language reasoning and interactive exploration, achieving high success rates in task planning and execution.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Enabling robots to explore and act in unfamiliar environments under ambiguous human instructions by interactively identifying task-relevant objects (e.g., cups or beverages for "I'm thirsty") remains challenging for existing vision-language model (VLM)-based methods, due to inefficient reasoning and limited environmental interaction. These factors hinder real-time task planning and execution. To address this, we propose Affordance-Aware Interactive Decision-Making and Execution for Ambiguous Instructions (AIDE), a human-inspired dual-stream framework that integrates interactive exploration with vision-language reasoning: mirroring the complementary deliberative and intuitive processes of human cognition, Multi-Stage Inference (MSI) serves as the decision-making stream and Accelerated Decision-Making (ADM) as the execution stream, enabling zero-shot affordance analysis and interpretation of ambiguous instructions. Experiments in simulation and real-world settings show that AIDE achieves over 80% task planning success rate and more than 95% closed-loop continuous execution accuracy at 10 Hz, surpassing existing VLM-based methods in diverse open scenarios.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: LIBERO-Industry: Benchmarking Robotic Manipulation under Industrial Process Constraints
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Ming Shin Cindy Sung, Duan Leijiahao, Haoxiang Wang, Boning Tan, Liangna Fu
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: LIBERO-Industry introduces a benchmark for evaluating robotic manipulation under industrial constraints, revealing performance degradation with increasing complexity across various task scenarios.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Industrial manipulation in flexible manufacturing, e.g., high-mix, low-volume (HMLV) electronics assembly, requires robot policies to adapt to changing products and production conditions. Such settings impose industrial process constraints, including product variants, moving material flows, finite execution windows, and tight geometric tolerances. However, existing evaluation frameworks do not systematically capture these constraints when assessing generalist robot policies. To address this gap, we introduce LIBERO-Industry, a novel benchmark built on the widely used robot learning benchmark LIBERO, that translates the aforementioned industrial constraints into controllable task conditions and measurable success criteria. Specifically, LIBERO-Industry comprises three classic task scenarios: Static-to-Dynamic (S2D) loading, Dynamic-to-Static (D2S) unloading, and Dynamic-to-Dynamic (D2D) transfer. The suites contain 216 tasks in total that systematically vary object geometry, conveyor speed, interaction-window duration, and geometric acceptance region size. Extensive experiments across five generalist robot policies (including vision-language-action models and world-action models) show that performance progressively degrades as industrial constraints are introduced and combined. Under a shared fine-tuning and evaluation protocol, the LIBERO-Industry co-training condition achieved higher observed target-transfer completion than the original-LIBERO condition.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: Reinforcement Learning-driven Diffusion Models: Language, Vision, and Beyond
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Zhiyuan Ma, Jiabao Wei, Tianyu Wang, Hanqing Wang, Jiadong Pan
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: This paper reviews and analyzes the integration of reinforcement learning into diffusion models, addressing limitations and proposing strategies for improved goal-directed generation across various applications.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Diffusion models (DMs) have steadily demonstrated outstanding performance in high-fidelity, controllable generation across diverse scenarios, following the "pretraining-finetuning" paradigm established in LLMs. Despite these advances, conventional DMs still face critical limitations in sophisticated reasoning, autonomous exploration of generation pathways, and adaptability to complex, human-aligned objectives. Inspired by RLHF's success in LLMs, RL has recently emerged as a pivotal post-training mechanism to iteratively refine DMs through reward-driven trajectory optimization. This paper presents the first comprehensive review of RL-driven DMs and an empirical analysis of how RL reshapes the diffusion process towards experience-centric, goal-directed generation. We propose a novel technical panorama elucidating RL's multifaceted roles in diffusion-based language, multimodal, robotic, and scientific models, with a granular focus on diffusion trajectory optimization and reward engineering. Through extensive experiments on multiple task-specific benchmarks, we systematically evaluate representative methods to intuitively highlight the advantages of different RL post-training strategies. Furthermore, we reveal and dissect three crucial bottlenecks that currently hinder the real-world deployment of RL-driven DMs: reward design fragility, exploration-exploitation trade-off in high-dimensional generation spaces, and training instability under sparse rewards. Based on these perspectives, we provide a principled roadmap for the integration of RL into DMs and outline promising future research directions for robust, interpretable RL-diffusion systems. We also construct a public repository to continuously track the latest developments in this rapidly evolving field: https://github.com/MAIR-Lab-HUST/Awesome-RL-for-Diffusion-Models.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: Provably Efficient Risk-Sensitive Offline Reinforcement Learning via Optimized Certainty Equivalents
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Hanzhen Wang, Boxiang Lyu, Zhongxiang Dai, Siyang Gao, Dake Zhang
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: This paper presents novel offline reinforcement learning algorithms using optimized certainty equivalents, establishing theoretical bounds and addressing risk sensitivity in decision-making under uncertainty.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Risk-sensitive reinforcement learning (RL) addresses decision-making under uncertainty and adverse outcomes. Learning risk-sensitive policies from fixed datasets is important when additional interaction with the environment is costly. Existing work on risk-sensitive RL focuses on online settings or specific risk measures, leaving a general theoretical understanding of its offline setting underdeveloped. In this work, we investigate efficient offline risk-sensitive RL using the optimized certainty equivalent (OCE), a general class of risk measures. We consider two formulations: dynamic-OCE RL, which applies OCE recursively at each step, and static-OCE RL, which applies a single OCE to the cumulative rewards. Under the tabular setting, we develop pessimistic value-iteration algorithms for both formulations and establish tight sublinear suboptimality bounds, explicitly capturing how risk sensitivity, encoded by utility functions, affects learning difficulty. Moreover, we establish minimax suboptimality lower bounds to characterize the problem's fundamental limits. To handle large state spaces, we further develop pessimistic least-squares value-iteration algorithms that incorporate the general OCE risk criterion into linear function approximation. We establish utility-dependent sublinear guarantees with explicit dependence on the feature dimension $d$. To our knowledge, we provide the first offline algorithms along with the first upper and lower suboptimality bounds for both dynamic- and static-OCE RL.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: SteerDistill: Quantizing LLM Agents via Closed-Loop Teacher Steering
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Genming Cui, Xiangyu Li, Zixu Hao, Xin Ding, Yunxin Liu
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: SteerDistill enhances low-bit quantized LLM agents by employing closed-loop teacher steering to correct behavioral divergences, improving task success and efficiency across multiple benchmarks.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Low-bit quantization reduces the inference cost of LLM agents but can compromise task success. Examining failed rollouts, we find that quantized agents overlook task requirements or environmental conditions, producing environment transitions that diverge from successful full-precision references. Correcting these behavioral divergences remains difficult: offline data may miss the student's failure contexts, while its own rollouts may provide few correct responses in those contexts. We introduce SteerDistill, a quantization-aware distillation method in which a full-precision teacher guides the student to revise failed responses and iteratively refines its guidance using feedback from student execution. This closed-loop teacher steering produces locally verified behavioral corrections. We internalize these corrections by training the student without guidance to match the steered student's predictions at corrected turns and the full-precision teacher's at other turns, enabling unassisted inference. Across five agentic benchmarks and three models, SteerDistill exceeds the strongest quantized baseline by 1.67--2.18 points in average score under W4A16 and stays within one point of BF16. On $τ^2$-Bench, it outperforms QeRL by 1.84 percentage points in success rate using 67% fewer training GPU hours and produces shorter successful trajectories than the quantized baselines.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: CIALLO: Learning Shared Intent Representations for Cross-Embodiment Manipulation
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Choo Sin Wai, Dake Zhong, Jingye Zhang, Zhifang Liu, Siyao Xiao
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: CIALLO introduces a shared action codec for cross-embodiment manipulation, enabling efficient transfer of manipulation knowledge across different robot control interfaces with high success rates.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Robot demonstrations contain reusable manipulation knowledge, but transferring this knowledge across embodiments requires representations that bridge differences in control interfaces. Action reconstruction alone does not ensure that similar behaviors across robots share a representation. To address this gap, we introduce CIALLO, an action codec that aligns actions, visual changes, and observation-grounded language in a shared space of short-horizon behavioral intent. An embodiment-conditioned decoder maps this intent back to robot-specific actions, allowing a shared representation to support different control interfaces. After pretraining on eight embodiments, CIALLO adapts to a new robot from one recording of at most 10 seconds by updating only its embodiment embeddings. The calibrated codec then remains frozen while a policy learns to predict intent from observations and instructions. We instantiate this policy with Qwen3.5-4B to form Qwen-CIALLO, whose backbone requires no large-scale robot-action pretraining before policy finetuning. With 20 demonstrations per task, Qwen-CIALLO achieves 76.7\% average success across real SO-101 and single-arm Piper robots, compared with 70.0\% for fully finetuned $π_0$. In simulation, we additionally finetune the action decoder, achieving 97.3\% success on LIBERO and 52.7\% on RoboTwin 2.0. The LIBERO policy also achieves 80.8\% on LIBERO-Plus without further finetuning. Together, these results support a shared action codec as a transferable control interface that separates embodiment calibration from task learning.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: LandslideFM: A Foundation Model Towards Unified Landslide Perception and Understanding
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Shanwen Wang, Sirui Wang, Xin Sun, Jungong Han
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: LandslideFM is a novel foundation model that enhances landslide detection by integrating visual tasks with contextual understanding through semi-supervised learning and a new benchmark, LandslideVL.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Intelligent landslide detection is essential for disaster prevention. However, existing models primarily focus on isolated visual tasks, require extensive labeled data, and lack deep analytical and scene-understanding capabilities. To address these limitations, we propose LandslideFM, the first unified foundation model that connects visual perception tasks with contextual interpretation of landslides. Specifically, LandslideFM adapts to multiple visual tasks via a Source-Agreement Graduated Trust semi-supervised learning framework that leverages limited labeled data alongside abundant unlabeled data. Furthermore, predicted landslide regions provide explicit spatial guidance to a Vision-Language Model adapted through parameter-efficient fine-tuning, enabling comprehensive landslide reasoning.
