智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: HITCH: Teaching a Vision-Language Model to Operate a Humanoid through a Whole-Body Harness
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Qingzhou Lu, Chenxin Liu, Xinming Wang, Liu Cao, Yanjiang Guo
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: HITCH enables vision-language models to effectively control humanoid robots through a whole-body harness, enhancing task success via accurate perception and execution of commands.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Enabling vision-language models (VLMs) to control humanoid robots requires both reliable whole-body interfaces and knowledge of how to use the body that carries over across tasks. We present HITCH (Harness Interfaces To Command Humanoids), a harness in which perception returns the 3D position of any point the VLM selects in its image, and execution turns commands for the pelvis, torso, hands, walking, and gaze into whole-body motion with a learned tracker. We find that both measuring the scene and executing commands accurately raise task success. We then fine-tune a VLM on trajectories in which teacher policies solve five base tasks through HITCH, so that it learns how to operate the humanoid. Without task-specific trajectories, the fine-tuned model completes 51% of SIMPLE episodes and 42.5% of HumanoidArena episodes, and adding five trajectories per SIMPLE task raises its SIMPLE success to 95%. On a real G1, it carries a box and walks to a goal without real training data.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Detecting Silent Faults at the Environment-Trainer Boundary in Reinforcement Learning
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Zuo Gou, Chenhao Lu
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The paper proposes a wire protocol for detecting silent faults at the environment-trainer boundary in reinforcement learning, demonstrating effective fault identification through step ledgers and episode records.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Robot reinforcement learning increasingly runs environments outside the trainer: in another process, on another machine, in another language. Many faults at this boundary raise no error. We make the boundary a wire protocol and ask what notices a fault in it. On Pendulum, HalfCheetah, Hopper and a 7-joint arm (Pusher), we injected up to 23 faults into what crosses the wire and 2 into the trainer's log, from one value to every value. Unless every value was wrong, a learning-curve threshold caught at most one run in ten, and a comparison with ten fault-free seeds at most 21%. A clean evaluation of all 1,060 final policies agreed with the curves: of the 728 boundary-fault runs both curve checks passed, 723 scored no more than three standard deviations below fault-free seeds, though nearly all ended on other weights and, for reward faults, logged other returns. Checks of the run itself, not of its outcome, saw every fault. A step ledger kept on both sides and compared step by step caught and located every fault that crossed, on Pendulum, Hopper and Pusher on one machine and on Pendulum across two, with no fault-free run and, on Pendulum, a median 3% more training time. An episode record kept at the environment caught the faults in the trainer's log. We list such faults found in practice, in Gymnasium 1.3 and our own code and, reported by others, in five multi-agent libraries, and recommend a step ledger and episode counts kept at the environment.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: MASBench: Benchmarking LLM-based Multi-Agent Collaboration under Partial Observability
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Qizhi Chu, Zekai Yu, Sijie Wen, Yang Liu, Chen Qian
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: MASBench is a benchmark for evaluating LLM-based multi-agent collaboration under partial observability, featuring structured tasks and metrics to assess collaboration mechanisms.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have progressively evolved into the core of autonomous agents. Building on this progress, LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) coordinate multiple agents into a synergistic team to accomplish complex tasks that exceed the capabilities of individual agents. The effectiveness of such systems depends not only on the agents themselves, but also on how collaboration mechanisms are designed and organized. Note that real-world collaboration is typically partially observable, where each agent can only access partial information about the environment due to physical or privacy-related constraints. However, many existing multi-agent benchmarks assume global observability, and leave limited support for systematically evaluating collaboration mechanisms. To bridge this gap, we introduce MASBench, a multi-agent collaboration benchmark designed under partially observable constraints. It is organized into three progressive task categories: Reasoning, Scheduling, and Game. Through this structure, we progressively evaluate three representative collaboration mechanisms: Protocol, Memory, and Routing. MASBench further provides deterministic evaluation metrics, including performance score, communication cost, and cost effectiveness, to characterize both collaboration outcomes and communication overhead. Experiments across diverse LLM backbones and mechanism configurations offer empirical guidance for effective MAS design. Code is available at: https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/MASBench

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: SleuthVLM: Do We Really Need Audio-in-Video for Omni Video Understanding?
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Peiran Wu, Fangfei Gou, Zhaoxi Mu, Changhao Zhang, Jian Liu
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: SleuthVLM demonstrates superior video understanding by utilizing transcribed audio instead of direct audio input, achieving higher accuracy than existing models and emphasizing the importance of agentic ability.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Omni models answer questions about videos by jointly processing sampled frames and audio in one turn, with progress driven largely by scaling model size and omni training data. We ask whether a model needs to hear the audio directly at all, and present SleuthVLM, an agent harness built on a VLM that never hears the audio directly: speech will be transcribed into text, and the VLM will sleuth the video on its own without any predefined workflow. On four omni benchmarks with videos up to 90 minutes, SleuthVLM achieves the best average accuracy: \textbf{75.0%}, 2.6 points above Gemini 3.8 Flash, and it also tops the Video-MME-v2 leaderboard with \textbf{77.8%}; with an open-source 27B VLM, it beats all open-source omni models. We draw three findings: SleuthVLM beats a model that glances; hearing is not the bottleneck, agentic ability is; omni understanding needs better agentic ability, not just more omni data for modality alignment. So we provide a simple but effective starting point for doing omni video understanding. Omni understanding needs better agents, not just bigger models that hear.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: ModalSearcher: Weaving Visual Evidence into Autonomous Cross-Modal Deep Search
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Zhihan Yin, Ruyi Li, Chengyu Fang, Yifeng Yao, Nonghai Zhang
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: ModalSearcher enhances multimodal large language models by enabling autonomous cross-modal search, integrating visual evidence dynamically, and achieving significant accuracy improvements in knowledge-intensive tasks.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Static and incomplete parametric knowledge limits the performance of multimodal large language models on novel-knowledge and knowledge-intensive tasks, especially those requiring multi-hop evidence acquisition. Existing multimodal agentic search methods often fix visual evidence at the input or a predefined trajectory position, making it difficult for agents to select search modalities as their information needs evolve and to handle complex real-world queries. We define this capability as autonomous cross-modal search: an agent chooses among direct reasoning, text-to-text search, text-to-image search, and reverse-image search, actively introduces visual evidence when appropriate, and switches between and integrates modalities across multiple hops. We propose ModalSearch-Pipeline, a scalable procedure for constructing an interleaved multimodal knowledge graph. It samples paths with diverse depths and modality compositions and uses backward question construction to obscure entity names and image targets that would expose reasoning shortcuts while retaining necessary disambiguating clues, yielding text-only, image-initialized, and arbitrarily interleaved multi-hop problems. We train the ModalSearcher Agent with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning in a live Web environment, and construct ModalSearch-Bench. Experiments show that ModalSearcher-8B improves average accuracy by 16.2 points over Qwen3-VL-8B under the same agentic workflow across five multimodal knowledge-intensive QA benchmarks, with consistent gains on independently constructed active visual-search benchmarks.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Yuetong Liu, Zhehao Zhou, Yitong Zhang, Haorui Chen, Jia Li
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: Coca-Cola introduces a continuous latent context compression model for LLM agents, significantly reducing token consumption and runtime while enhancing task performance through action-preserving training.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents typically append raw tool outputs to their context. Over multi-step interactions, long and noisy observations incur substantial context overhead and dilute the agent's attention to task-relevant information. Existing token pruning and summarization methods remain constrained by discrete text representations, limiting the achievable compression ratios. In this work, we challenge the prevailing assumption that agents must consume tool observations as explicit text tokens. To this end, we propose Coca-Cola, a continuous latent context compression model for LLM agents. Coca-Cola compresses tool observations into latent tokens and embeds them into the input embedding space of the agent. We further introduce Action-Preserving Training, which aligns the agent's next-action distributions under full and compressed observations. This trains the compression model to learn action-sufficient latent tokens that retain decision-critical information. Experiments with web-search agents on four QA benchmarks and two model families show that Coca-Cola reduces the agent's token consumption by 70.01%-89.24% and end-to-end runtime by 24.45%-55.97%, while consistently improving task performance. These results suggest that Coca-Cola offers a promising approach for context compression in agents. Our code is available at https://github.com/THU-Agent/Coca-cola.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Compression Forcing: Hierarchical History Tokenization Enables Flexible World Models
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Siqiao Huang, Partha Kaushik, Michael Chen, Hengkai Pan, Kaiwen Geng
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The paper introduces Compression Forcing, a framework that enhances world modeling by aligning history compression with predictive objectives through Dynamics-Aware Tokenization and Hierarchical History Guidance.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Effective world modeling requires compressing salient history information that facilitates future prediction. However, most existing approaches inherit tokenization and conditioning mechanisms from video generation, where objectives are centered around perceptual realism rather than predictive utility. This discrepancy limits the world model's effectiveness, especially in environments dominated by visual nuisances or task-irrelevant background details. To this end, we introduce Compression Forcing (CF), a general framework that aligns history compression with the predictive objective of world modeling. Compression Forcing features Dynamics-Aware Tokenization (DAT), a novel tokenization method that compresses history observations into a sequence ordered by decreasing dynamics saliency. Built on a diffusion backbone, this structure enables Hierarchical History Guidance (HG-H), allowing selective amplification of dynamics-salient information during inference. Extensive experiments across various environments demonstrate improved prediction fidelity, physical realism, and downstream decision-making performance, establishing Compression Forcing as a highly flexible and effective approach for world modeling.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: ReflexArc: Bottom-Up Integration of Instantaneous Tactile Reflexes into Whole-Body Humanoid Control
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Mingyu Wang, Si Li, Ziqing Chen, He Wang, Li Yi
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The ReflexArc framework integrates instantaneous tactile reflexes into humanoid robot control, significantly enhancing responsiveness and safety in hazardous contact situations.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Humanoid robots operating in cluttered environments must react to unexpected contacts before the first impact peak, which arrives within tens of milliseconds. Learned whole-body policies running at 50 Hz introduce a policy-cycle delay and may suppress a protective withdrawal as a tracking error. To address these challenges, we propose ARC (Ascending Reflex Control), a bottom-up framework that integrates instantaneous tactile reflexes with learned whole-body control. ARC consists of two components: an instantaneous reflex pathway and bottom-up reflex integration. The reflex pathway detects hazardous contacts from full-body tactile sensing, solves a whole-body withdrawal pose, and delivers it directly to the motors within 10 ms. Bottom-up reflex integration combines reflex-in-the-loop policy learning, reflex-transparent policy alignment, and reflex-informed policy adaptation to sustain the withdrawal, maintain balance, and complete longer-horizon recovery. We deploy ARC on a Unitree G1 and evaluate three categories of hazardous contact. Compared with an otherwise identical reflex delayed by 20 ms, ARC reduces the first force peak by 34.1% and reduces the contact impulse from 0.2632 N s to 0.1225 N s (a 2.15x ratio). We further demonstrate protected motion tracking, teleoperation, and vision-free obstacle traversal guided by foot tactile sensing. Project page: https://minusmodulo.github.io/reflexarc-website/

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Spectrally Routed Diffusion Policy for Multi-Task Robotic Manipulation
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Mingcong Li, Yihan Zhou, Jiayu Qu, Xueyang Guo, Yilin Mo
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The Spectrally Routed Diffusion Policy (SR-DP) enhances multi-task robotic manipulation by improving visual encoding and reducing interference, achieving superior success rates compared to existing methods.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Diffusion-based policies have achieved strong performance on single-task robotic manipulation. However, a single model trained jointly on multiple tasks consistently underperforms the per-task specialists trained on the same demonstrations. We focus on two challenges. First, the convolutional encoders commonly used in diffusion-based policies produce visual conditions that are not discriminative enough. Second, gradients from incompatible action modes update the shared denoiser's dense parameters along the same directions, causing destructive interference during joint training. To address both, we propose SR-DP (Spectrally Routed Diffusion Policy). A frozen VGGT encoder with a spatial-compression adapter produces compact multi-scale semantic-geometric tokens, a task-discriminative visual condition for tasks that share a workspace. We first train the denoiser as a standard diffusion policy, then decompose selected linear layers by SVD into a frozen basis of orthogonal rank-one experts, adapted through spectral routing and Householder input rotations. On six RoboTwin tasks, SR-DP averages a 68.4% success rate, surpassing multi-task VO-DP by 21.8 points and the strongest per-task baseline by 3.8 points. On four real-world bimanual tasks, Stage 2 reaches a 43.0% average success rate and improves over Stage 1 by 19.0 points.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Beyond Local Refinement: Wide-Area Precise Cross-View Localization
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Qingguo Hu, Xinyu Ma, Yujie Lin, Yaoxiang Wang, Qi Shi
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The paper presents RingMatch, a framework for precise cross-view localization over large areas, addressing challenges of spatial disparity and visual ambiguity using predictive uncertainty and a novel depth ring representation.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Fine-grained cross-view localization aims to precisely localize a ground camera against geo-referenced aerial imagery, but current methods typically assume a narrow geographic prior, substantially limiting their applicability when upstream localization remains coarse. To bridge this gap, we study this task over much larger aerial regions. However, this seemingly simple extension fundamentally changes the localization problem: the growing disparity in spatial extent between ground and aerial views makes reliable cross-view matching difficult to establish directly, while the increasing number of look-alike locations in larger regions introduces substantial visual ambiguity. To address these challenges, we propose RingMatch, a search-and-verification framework for wide-area cross-view localization. RingMatch first leverages predictive uncertainty to uncover plausible locations and progressively zooms into their surroundings to obtain increasingly fine-grained evidence, yielding a compact set of promising candidates. We then introduce the depth ring, a novel geometric representation that reveals subtle variations in the spatial layout around a location and serves as a view-shared spatial signature for an LVLM verifier to resolve residual ambiguity. To benchmark this setting, we construct VIGOR-Pro by composing VIGOR aerial tiles into contiguous regions with spatial extents of up to 400 m. Experiments show that RingMatch maintains strong localization performance as the aerial region expands, consistently outperforming representative end-to-end and retrieval-based methods.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: ReSI-Math: Exploring Recoverable Capability Frontiers for Efficient Reasoning Improvement
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Yao Cui, Zhen Yang, Yuandong Wang, Yangfu Zhu, Tianyu Wo
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: ReSI-Math enhances mathematical reasoning in language models by exploring recoverable capability frontiers through trajectory-level search and adaptive reinforcement learning, improving problem-solving efficiency.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become an effective approach for improving mathematical reasoning in large language models. However, a fundamental question remains: when a model fails to solve a problem, does it truly lack the underlying capability? In this work, we reveal that direct failure does not necessarily imply inability. Some reasoning failures can be recovered by exploring the model's own trajectories, exposing a recoverable capability frontier: a policy-dependent region where solutions are not reliably generated through direct decoding but can be elicited through trajectory-level search. Based on this observation, we introduce ReSI-Math, a framework that explores recoverable capability frontiers and converts recovered capabilities into data-efficient RLVR supervision. ReSI-Math uses Self-Judge-guided evolutionary search to identify recoverable failures under a fixed policy and adaptively selects frontier problems for sequential RLVR as the policy evolves. On Qwen3-VL-8B, correct-incorrect trajectory crossover produces 272 verifier-confirmed correct offspring from 621 attempts (43.8%). After three sequential one-shot RLVR stages, the MATH500 and WE-MATH average improves from 78.71 to 80.16. Under matched single-problem RLVR, random selection reaches only 53.31 versus 54.16 for frontier-guided Q1.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: VisSearch-Bench: Evaluating Long Horizon Visual Search in Multimodal Agents
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: ZhengXian Wu, Qianhao Nie, Zhuohong Chen, Junjie Gao, Yuyao Zhang
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: VisSearch-Bench evaluates multimodal agents' long-horizon visual search capabilities across diverse tasks, revealing significant challenges in linking visual evidence to search outcomes.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Multimodal agents use web and image tools to answer questions beyond their internal knowledge. Some search tasks use images mainly to identify an initial entity, then rely on text retrieval. These tasks offer limited insight into how agents connect information across images, objects, and search steps. We therefore focus on visual context management. This involves organizing and using visual information and linking it to other findings during search. Visually intensive tasks require agents to combine object appearance, local details, or spatial relations with external information. We introduce VisSearch-Bench, with 204 human-written tasks across 7 main domains and 25 subdomains. It covers Set-wise Visual Search, Sequential Visual Search, Hybrid Wide-Deep Search, Competitive Visual Disambiguation, and Visual-Structure-Guided Search. Each task provides a reference answer, traceable evidence, and scoring rules. Accuracy measures complete task success, while Process Score measures the correctness and completeness of individual results and subquestion answers. Across 16 multimodal models, the best system fully solves only 26.47% of tasks, even with search tools. These results highlight the challenge of linking visual evidence with search results to produce complete answers.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: HiLo-WAM: Decoupling Long-Horizon Task Evolution and Local Dynamics in World Action Models
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Xingyu Wang, Yanjiang Guo, Zhijing Ding, Jiaxin Fang, Zeyu Lai
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: HiLo-WAM enhances robotic manipulation by decoupling long-horizon task evolution from local dynamics, achieving high success rates and efficiency through a dual-DiT architecture.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) improve robotic manipulation by jointly modeling visual dynamics and robot actions. However, most existing WAMs model dense short-horizon visual dynamics, capturing local interactions but providing limited long-range task context. Extending prediction horizons increases uncertainty and computation while entangling task-level evolution with fine-grained local dynamics, obscuring their dependencies and distinct roles in action generation. We propose HiLo-WAM, which decouples long-horizon task evolution from local visual dynamics while jointly modeling their interaction with robot actions. A sparse long-horizon visual stream captures historical task context and future evolution, while a dense local dynamics visual stream models short-horizon robot-object interactions. The two streams operate at different temporal scales within a unified dual-DiT architecture and guide actions through structured cross-stream attention. Progressive inference further reduces unnecessary computation through stream-wise partial denoising, joint denoising, and dynamic skipping. Experiments demonstrate strong long-horizon manipulation performance: HiLo-WAM achieves a 93.70% average success rate on RoboTwin 2.0 and a 17.43 progress score on RoboDojo long-horizon tasks, with robust in-domain and OOD performance on the Fourier GR-3 robot. Ablations confirm the complementary contributions of long-horizon task evolution and local interaction dynamics, while temporal-scale analyses highlight the importance of balancing temporal coverage and resolution. Progressive inference further achieves a 2.93x speedup while improving performance.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Democratizing Robot-Use Agents: A Unified Harness with Open Models
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Jiarui Yuan, Yuxin Zuo, Xiaoyu Huang, Wenbo Zhang, Kwanyoung Park
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The paper presents uni-robot-agent, a unified framework for open-weight Robot-use Agents that enhances zero-shot manipulation and supports further training, outperforming existing models.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Robot-use Agents (RUAs) have shown promising zero-shot manipulation capabilities, but reliance on frontier, proprietary models limits research into further training. To democratize RUA research, we introduce uni-robot-agent, a unified harness for competitive open-weight robot use that supports further training. Without privileged inputs, an out-of-the-box Qwen3.8-Flash-Next achieves a RoboDojo Score of 31.39, surpassing the published GPT-6 Astra-RoboProbe result of 28.97 and many VLA/WAM baselines, and performs competitively on 19 real-world tasks. Our analysis across model generations, families, and sizes links effective robot use to four general capabilities, suggesting that future RUA training should develop them jointly.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: DexArena: A Unified Benchmark for Long-Horizon Dexterous Manipulation
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Haonan Ping, Jianshu Hu, Yimin Wang, Yi Zhu, Pai Liang
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: DexArena is a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating long-horizon bimanual dexterous manipulation in robots, featuring diverse tasks and standardized testing protocols to enhance learning and generalization.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Long-horizon dexterous manipulation remains a fundamental challenge for robot learning, requiring the composition of multiple skills, precise bimanual coordination, generalizable visual understanding, and robust skill transitions. Yet existing manipulation benchmarks largely emphasize isolated skills or support only a limited range of end-effectors, making these capabilities difficult to evaluate systematically. We introduce DexArena, a benchmark designed to evaluate learning and generalization in long-horizon bimanual dexterous manipulation. DexArena features 10 long-horizon tasks and 30 stage-level tasks spanning diverse household and industrial scenarios. Each long-horizon task is composed of explicitly defined stages with physically grounded success conditions, enabling reliable evaluation of both intermediate progress and end-to-end task completion. A unified benchmark interface and verified human-teleoperated demonstrations enable testing different policy learning algorithms, with standardized simulation configurations, scene randomization, trajectory replay, and task-level evaluation. Through extensive baseline experiments, we identify substantial challenges in precise manipulation, generalization to scene variation, and skill composition. DexArena establishes a challenging and reproducible benchmark for developing robot learning methods that move toward generalizable long-horizon dexterous behavior.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: ReconDreamer#: Self-Evolving Closed-Loop Synergy of Reconstruction and Generation for Dynamic Driving Scenes
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Songling Liu, Guosheng Zhao, Xiaofeng Wang, Chaojun Ni, Guan Huang
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: ReconDreamer# is a self-evolving framework that enhances dynamic driving scene reconstruction by iteratively refining generative and reconstruction models, improving fidelity against real-world data.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Dynamic driving scene reconstruction has made remarkable strides in recent years by leveraging generative priors, particularly in the quality of novel trajectory rendering. Nevertheless, a significant gap remains between the generated data and real-world sensor observations, severely hindering further improvements in reconstruction fidelity. In this paper, we present ReconDreamer#, a self-evolving framework that synergizes reconstruction and generation for dynamic driving scenes, which substantially bridges the gap between synthesized novel trajectory data and recorded real-world observations. Within this self-evolving closed-loop framework, the generative and reconstruction models mutually reinforce each other through iterative refinement, ultimately yielding a significant enhancement in the 3D representation capability of the reconstruction model. Additionally, we introduce a geometry-prior-based adaptive ground model to further enhance the rendering quality of the reconstruction model. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, we conduct comprehensive evaluations on Waymo, nuScenes, PandaSet, and EUVS benchmarks. Specifically on Waymo, at a 6-m lateral shift, ReconDreamer# improves NTA-IoU and NTL-IoU by 8.8% and 3.0%, respectively, and reduces FID by 15.1% relative to ReconDreamer++.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: LLM4Robot-Bench: How Far Can GPT-6 Astra Go in Robotic Manipulation? A Hierarchical, Paired Sim-Real Benchmark
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Haibao Yu, Jiaqi Meng, Zijian Zhang, Bowen Jing, Lei Yang
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The LLM4Robot-Bench evaluates GPT-6 Astra's robotic manipulation across 16 tasks, revealing significant performance declines with increasing interaction complexity in both simulated and real environments.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: We introduce LLM4Robot-Bench, a hierarchical, paired Sim-Real benchmark for evaluating physical interaction capabilities in contact-rich manipulation. Its 16 household tasks span three cumulative levels: contact selection and geometric alignment (L1), force regulation within sustained contact (L2), and coordinated contact reconfiguration and force regulation (L3). Each task is instantiated in physically and visually matched simulated and real-world environments, with shared task definitions and success criteria. We evaluate GPT-6 Astra zero-shot with three trials per task in each environment. Real-world success rates decline from 80.0% at L1 to 47.6% at L2 and 0.0% at L3, with corresponding simulation rates of 66.7%, 47.6%, and 0.0%. Ten of the 16 tasks have identical success counts across environments; the remaining six differ by one success out of three trials. Across both environments, recurring difficulties in spatial reasoning, contact selection, force regulation, and coordination often prevent local physical progress from accumulating into task completion. These findings characterize Astra's observed capability boundary across increasing interaction demands and, for this model, support matched simulation as a repeatable, scalable testbed for studying the sustained, coordinated physical interactions that limit reliable manipulation.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: HTCE: Homeomorphism-inspired Topological Cross-Scene Experience Canonicalization and Reuse for Object Navigation
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Xiaoran Xu, Yupeng Wu, Tianyu Xue, Xuanran Dong, Yifan Xu
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: HTCE introduces a topological framework for canonicalizing and reusing object navigation experiences in residential environments, enhancing retrieval efficiency and performance across varying scene representations.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: As embodied agents perform object-goal navigation across residential environments, they accumulate successful experiences whose semantic structure recurs across scenes even when geometric trajectories do not. Reusing such experience is challenging because differences in region naming and observation granularity produce distinct graph representations of similar approaches, while meaningful differences in anchors, branches, and endpoints must stay distinguishable. We introduce HTCE, a homeomorphism-inspired topological framework that canonicalizes and reuses navigation experience. Feature and topology subdivisions characterize representational variations, and their semantically constrained reductions produce comparable semantic sequences and structural signatures while preserving semantic anchors, branching relations, and navigation endpoints. HTCE then retrieves historical successful approaches through subdivision-aware matching as guidance for a frozen vision-language policy. Canonicalization compresses the experience index losslessly, merging 17.7--23.6\% of distinct stored route descriptions while retaining full task performance. Under a single frozen vision-language backbone shared by all compared systems, HTCE attains the best SR and SPL in every setting---59.9\%/31.8\% on HM3D v0.1, 71.0\%/31.5\% on HM3D v0.2, and 46.6\%/16.6\% on MP3D---with SR gains of up to 4.9 points and structured retrieval contributing up to 2.8 SPL points. The code is available in https://github.com/startracker0/htce.git

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Spotter: Let the Embodied Model Lead, and the VLM Reflect for It
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Long Li, Qichao Zhao, Yue Yang, Fan Xu, Zhe Wang
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The Spotter framework enhances embodied models by allowing them to lead while a vision-language model monitors and corrects errors, significantly improving performance and efficiency.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Current embodied models do not respond to their own failures, although what just went wrong could inform a small adjustment on the next attempt, the kind of reflection behind the gains of thinking in language models. We test whether they can repair a known error, which requires producing a correction and judging whether it is right. Stopped at a failure and allowed to retry, they seldom repair it through their own randomness or from a language description of the error, and best-of-N selection cannot pick the successful candidate after a failure. We attribute this to training only on successful demonstrations and to inputs too narrow to show what went wrong, and conclude that reflection must come from a vision-language model (VLM), which takes in far more information, such as the episode history and text, and is more general. Prior VLM-led work has the VLM plan every step and invoke the embodied model as a tool, placing the VLM on the critical path. We propose Spotter, which reverses the roles: the embodied model leads and executes continuously, while the VLM runs in parallel, monitors through a lightweight local screener, intervenes only when an error is detected, reflects on and corrects it, and returns control. We run Spotter with Qwen and with GPT as the VLM, and both improve the embodied models; with GPT, Spotter improves Cosmos Policy and $π_{0.5}$ by 5.6 and 7.5 percentage points on RoboCasa, and raises $π_{0.5}$ from 47.2% to 57.0% on the Hard setting of RoboTwin 2.0 and from 53% to 83% on a real robot. Because the VLM steps in only when an error is confirmed, a successful episode with Qwen takes only 13 to 16 s longer than with the embodied model alone and about 70% less time than with a VLM-led baseline using the same model. Our code is available at https://github.com/zqc3117/Spotter.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: A New Formulation of the Elastica Model with Application to Image Inpainting
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Zuoqiang Shi, Xue-Cheng Tai
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: This paper introduces a new elastica model formulation using binary curves for efficient image inpainting, leveraging FFT and split Bregman iteration for optimization.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Curves and interfaces play a central role in computer vision and image processing, and Euler's elastica energy is one of the most successful tools to model and manipulate them. The elastica energy is usually computed through a level-set or a phase field representation of the curve, in which the curvature term makes the energy nonlinear, non-convex and, in the level-set case, non-differentiable, so that its minimization is notoriously difficult. In this paper, we propose a new formulation of the elastica model based on a binary representation of curves. The key ingredient is a very simple formula for the curvature: if $ϕ$ is the $\pm1$ binary function associated with a curve $Γ$, then along $Γ$ the curvature is given by $-\frac{1}{C_0ε}\left(R_ε*ϕ\right)+O(ε)$, where $R_ε$ is a radial kernel supported in a ball of radius $ε$ and $C_0$ is an explicit constant. No derivative of $ϕ$ is involved and the convolution is evaluated by FFT. The resulting energy is a weighted total variation, so that formally the new formulation is a generalization of the well-known ROF model; a phase field type model is obtained from the same curvature formula. Combining FFT with the split Bregman iteration, which for the present problem coincides with an augmented Lagrangian method (ALM), we obtain efficient algorithms whose subproblems are either linear systems solved by conjugate gradient or explicit pointwise formulas. Numerical experiments on the inpainting of binary images are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: RoboSnap: One-Shot Real-to-Sim Scene Generation for Generalizable Robot Learning and Evaluation
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Shujie Zhang, Jingkun Yi, Weipeng Zhong, Zirui Zhou, Yangkun Zhu
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: RoboSnap enables efficient one-shot generation of simulation-ready scenes from real images, enhancing robot learning and evaluation through a layered design for stability and visual fidelity.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Recovering real-world scenes as interactive simulation environments can enable generalizable robot learning and reproducible policy evaluation. However, constructing scenes that are both physically stable and visually faithful remains slow and expensive. In this work, we present RoboSnap, a real-to-sim framework that turns a single RGB image into a simulation-ready scene. The key idea is a layered design that separates the physics-critical interaction area from the surrounding visual context: collision-aware foreground assets are refined for stable robot interaction, while a 3D Gaussian splatting visual layer preserves faithful background appearance under novel views. Experiments on DROID scenes and real-robot tasks show that RoboSnap achieves reliable trajectory replay in the recovered scenes, supports task-specific synthetic data generation for policy training, and yields meaningful sim-real correlation for policy evaluation. To further support real-to-sim research, we introduce DROID-Sim, a real-to-sim companion dataset constructed from 564 real-world scenes in DROID. Extensive experiments suggest that the value of real-to-sim methods lies not only in high-fidelity visual reconstruction, but in turning real environments into reusable infrastructure for robot learning and evaluation.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Why Koopman Structure Does Not Help Differentiable World Models for Humanoid Whole-Body Tracking
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Haizhou Ge, Mengshuo Wang, Yufei Jia, Lei Han, Lu Shi
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: Koopman structure does not enhance differentiable world models for humanoid tracking, yielding similar performance but slower training compared to MLP models.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: We test whether Koopman structure, linear dynamics in a lifted state space, helps when a humanoid whole-body tracking policy is trained by backpropagating through a differentiable world model, replacing the MLP world model of an otherwise unchanged pipeline for simulated Unitree G1 tracking. It does not: return is at best equal (0.823 versus 0.830), one-step error on identical data is 1.3 to 1.6 times the MLP's, and training is about 15% slower. Lifted rollouts diverge or fail to train a policy; of the schemes tested, re-lifting at every imagined step trains best. Re-lifting never uses the lifted linear dynamics and leaves a model affine in the action, with state-dependent offset and slope; an action-affine MLP also predicts worse, so the cost belongs to this class. At a fixed state, the curvature of the true dynamics in the action explains only part of it. Across states, the policy's actions span a curved region, so an affine model fits policy data only as the tangent at the policy's action, the operating point: on G1, the MLP's tangent there is as accurate as the MLP; at the mean action, 31 times worse. The offset must encode, from the state alone, where the policy acts, whereas an MLP reads the action. Supplying the policy's action removes most of the remaining gap on G1, Ant and Humanoid. The only online repair approaching the MLP feeds the action into the nonlinear lift, giving up the structure. The MLP world model thus remains the better choice here.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: OpenHLM: An Empirical Recipe for Whole-Body Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Yingdong Hu, Haodong Zhu, Boyuan Zheng, Yihang Hu, Tong Zhang
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The paper presents OpenHLM, an open-source framework for whole-body humanoid loco-manipulation, demonstrating superior performance through a novel vision-language-action model and systematic empirical study.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Whole-body humanoid loco-manipulation requires coordinating the robot's entire kinematic chain. However, most existing systems typically decouple the upper and lower bodies into separate controllers, limiting such coordination and yielding behaviors similar to those of a wheeled dual-arm platform. In this paper, we ask what it takes to build a whole-body native vision-language-action (VLA) model that maps language and pixels directly to all of the humanoid's degrees of freedom. We conduct a systematic empirical study organized as a roadmap of one-variable-at-a-time experiments across three phases: whole-body teleoperation, VLA model design, and heterogeneous co-training. Our study yields several intriguing findings: a joint-based whole-body teleoperation interface outperforms alternatives that only partially expose the humanoid's degrees of freedom; a VLA pretrained on static and wheeled dual-arm platforms transfers surprisingly well to a humanoid's full action space; and co-training with HuMI, the humanoid analog of UMI, extends the policy to new objects and instructions without additional whole-body teleoperation on those targets. Following this roadmap yields OpenHLM, an open-source recipe for whole-body humanoid loco-manipulation. In a challenging long-horizon task that spans a wide vertical range of the humanoid, OpenHLM outperforms two state-of-the-art humanoid VLA baselines (GR00T N1.6 and $Ψ_0$) using less than half the total demonstration time. Our code, training data, and model checkpoints are available at [https://openhlm-project.github.io/].

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Gnomon4D: Learning Where and When to Focus for Geometric Motion-Grounded World-Action Modeling
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Lingwei Dang, Yan Zhou, Juntong Li, Zhenhao Zhang, Yiteng Chen
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: Gnomon4D introduces a novel world-action model that integrates geometric motion fields for improved robot action prediction and future video generation, outperforming existing methods significantly.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: World-action models (WAMs) use video-generation priors to jointly predict future observations and robot actions. Yet RGB futures entangle physical state changes with appearance, while frame-wise depth and point maps lack temporal correspondence. Existing 4D approaches either keep motion implicit in visual features or translate predicted traces into actions through a separate interface. We present Gnomon4D, a WAM that jointly generates future video, robot actions, and GeoDelta, a video-aligned 4D geometric motion field encoding the cross-frame image-plane displacement and depth change of embodiment and object points. By placing embodiment motion and object responses in a shared space, GeoDelta exposes their motion relations to the action expert at inference. Interaction-Salient Attention (InSAttn) uses these relations to focus spatial readout on task-relevant interaction regions, while Transition-Anchored Aggregation (TransAgg) aggregates evidence around changes in their relative motion, such as grasp and release. GeoDelta describes surface motion independently of embodiment-specific controls, providing a shared human--robot quasi-action for action-free pretraining on EgoManip-5000H followed by robot mid-training on Robot-30H. Gnomon4D leads on RoboTwin~2.0, VLABench, and RoboDojo, and outperforms the strongest real-robot baseline by 7.0 and 16.0 percentage points under in-distribution and out-of-distribution settings, respectively.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: ReWorld: Multi-Dimensional Reward Modeling for Embodied Video Generation
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Baorui Peng, Wenyao Zhang, Liang Xu, Bohan Li, Hu Zhu
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: ReWorld introduces a reinforcement learning framework that enhances embodied video generation by aligning it with physical realism, task logic, and visual quality through a multi-dimensional reward model.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Current embodied video generation models primarily emphasize visual generative quality while overlooking physical fidelity, dynamic consistency, and task logic, especially for contact-rich manipulation tasks, which limits their applicability to downstream tasks. In this paper, we introduce ReWorld, a framework aimed to employ reinforcement learning to align the video generation with physical realism, task completion capability, embodiment plausibility and visual quality. Specifically, we first construct a large-scale (~235K) video preference dataset and employ it to train a hierarchical reward model designed to capture multi-dimensional reward consistent with human preferences. We further propose a practical alignment algorithm that post-trains flow-based video generators using this reward through a computationally efficient PPO-style algorithm. Comprehensive experiments and theoretical analysis demonstrate that ReWorld significantly improves the physical fidelity, logical coherence, embodiment and visual quality of generated rollouts, outperforming previous methods.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Beyond Policy Patches: Distilling RL Specialists into Vision-Language-Action Policies
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Zhennan Jiang, Tingying Xie, Shilong Ji, Shu'ang Yu, Tianxing Zhou
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The REPAIR framework effectively distills reinforcement learning specialists into vision-language-action policies, achieving 100% success in precision-critical tasks while minimizing action jitter.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies can handle noncritical stages of long-horizon manipulation yet fail during short precision-critical phases. Lightweight reinforcement learning (RL) specialists can address these failures without directly applying RL to the full VLA, but retain auxiliary controllers and switching mechanisms at deployment. We study how to transfer their capabilities into a single flow-matching VLA. Direct imitation of specialist rollouts can reproduce action jitter and leave the VLA unprepared for states encountered during its own execution. We introduce REPAIR, a value-guided distillation framework that combines offline initialization with on-policy refinement. At each critical-phase observation, REPAIR queries the corresponding specialist for multiple action candidates and weights them using its critic to construct a supervision distribution. A shared weighted flow-matching objective trains the VLA first on observations from specialist-assisted rollouts, then on observations collected through its own execution. Specialists provide supervision without taking control during on-policy collection and are removed at deployment. Across six real-robot tasks with 30 evaluation trials per task, REPAIR achieves 100% success on all six tasks, with lower mean end-effector jerk than specialist-assisted execution on every task.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: 3D Gaussian Splatting within Self-Learned Neural View-Dependent Color Fields
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Yixiao Yang, Yu-Shen Liu, Zhizhong Han
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The paper presents a novel approach to 3D Gaussian Splatting using self-learned neural networks for improved radiance field modeling and geometry recovery in novel view synthesis.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has become a vital tool in novel view synthesis. 3D Gaussian functions with attributes like color, opacity, and scale are stacked together to explicitly model a radiance field. However, discrete 3D Gaussians usually produce poor depth with few geometry details but lots of floaters, which hinders the effective modeling of smooth radiance fields. To address this issue, we propose to learn a radiance field within a continuous view-dependent color field parameterized by neural networks. With continuous constraints in color, the bias on low-frequency signals of neural networks can highly encourage the geometry modeling to contribute to high-frequency color variations on images, getting rid of solely relying on the color attribute itself. Moreover, we impose a constraint to improve the Lipschitz continuity of the neural color field, making large changes of each Gaussian's color also match with large changes of its position in terms of a ratio. To this end, we additionally introduce novel self-learning strategies to improve the learning of the neural view-dependent color field without any external knowledge or priors, aiming for better generalization on unseen scenes. Our numerical and visual comparisons on widely used benchmarks justify our idea and show better ability of high fidelity geometry recovery in 3DGS. Project page: https://github.com/yangyixi21/Neural-Color-Fields-3DGS.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Transfer the Style, Not the Semantics: Mitigating Semantic Leakage in Image-Guided Stylization
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Haojun Tang, Qiwei Lin, Tongda Xu, Wenda Zhao, Yian Zhao
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The paper introduces SuRe, a framework that mitigates semantic leakage in image-guided stylization by disrupting key-value correspondence in self-attention mechanisms of diffusion models.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Image-guided zero-shot style transfer enables training-free stylization of arbitrary content images using a reference style. Despite recent progress, existing methods commonly rely on self-attention manipulation to inject style information, which may transfer semantic content from the style image, leading to semantic leakage. In this work, we revisit this phenomenon from the perspective of key--value coupling in the self-attention of diffusion models. Our analysis shows that the native correspondence between style keys and values plays an important role in transferring semantic information from the style image. Motivated by this observation, we propose SuRe, a timestep-aware key--value regulation framework that mitigates semantic leakage by disrupting the native key--value correspondence while progressively restoring it for faithful style transfer. Specifically, we present value shuffle to decouple style keys and values while preserving the empirical distribution of the values, together with a progressive recoupling mechanism that gradually recouples them throughout the stylization process. Experiments against 18 representative methods demonstrate that SuRe maintains competitive style similarity while consistently improving content similarity across SD1.5, SDXL, SD3, and FLUX.1-dev, with natural generalization to multi-style transfer. The code will be publicly available at https://github.com/XinR-Tang/SuRe.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: ArthroCut: Autonomous Policy Learning for Robotic Bone Resection in Knee Arthroplasty
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Xu Lu, Yiling Zhang, Wenquan Cheng, Longfei Ma, Fang Chen
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: ArthroCut enhances robotic knee arthroplasty by integrating multimodal data for autonomous, context-aware decision-making, achieving an 86% success rate in bone resection tasks.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Despite rapid commercialization of surgical robots, their autonomy and real-time decision-making remain limited in practice. To address this gap, we propose ArthroCut, an autonomous policy learning framework that upgrades knee arthroplasty robots from assistive execution to context-aware action generation. ArthroCut fine-tunes a Qwen--VL backbone on a self-built, time-synchronized multimodal dataset from 21 complete cases (23,205 RGB--D pairs), integrating preoperative CT/MR, intraoperative NDI tracking of bones and end effector, RGB--D surgical video, robot state, and textual intent. The method operates on two complementary token families -- Preoperative Imaging Tokens (PIT) to encode patient-specific anatomy and planned resection planes, and Time-Aligned Surgical Tokens (TAST) to fuse real-time visual, geometric, and kinematic evidence -- and emits an interpretable action grammar under grammar/safety-constrained decoding. In bench-top experiments on a knee prosthesis across seven trials, ArthroCut achieves an average success rate of 86% over the six standard resections, significantly outperforming strong baselines trained under the same protocol. Ablations show that TAST is the principal driver of reliability while PIT provides essential anatomical grounding, and their combination yields the most stable multi-plane execution. These results indicate that aligning preoperative geometry with time-aligned intraoperative perception and translating that alignment into tokenized, constrained actions is an effective path toward robust, interpretable autonomy in orthopedic robotic surgery.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Decoupled Predictive Decision Making: A Shared Conditional Predictor for Agents
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Lang Mo, Xingxuan Zhang, Qi Wang, Mingchao Hao, Hao Yuan
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: Decoupled Predictive Decision Making (DPDM) enhances agent decision-making accuracy by leveraging a shared pretrained learner for conditional predictions, improving performance across various tasks.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Agent decisions depend on empirical relationships that deployment observations reveal and task descriptions alone may leave unresolved. We introduce Decoupled Predictive Decision Making (DPDM), an architecture that formulates heterogeneous agent decisions as conditional prediction with a shared pretrained learner. Language models provide semantic representations of current and historical records, while a general-purpose conditional predictor predicts task-defined targets from the represented evidence. Pretraining supplies reusable inference capability; deployment evidence instantiates problem-specific predictions without updating either model's neural parameters. Tool judgments, candidate preferences, and reasoning assessments share an evidence-and-query interface, with predictions mapped to choices by a decision rule. This architecture establishes complementary sources of agent capability: semantic knowledge acquired through language pretraining and empirical inference acquired through structured-data pretraining. A single frozen LimiX-2 predictor serves all five task categories. With Qwen3.5-27B as the semantic encoder, DPDM raises mean accuracy across 50 benchmarks from 78.80% with few-shot prompting to 84.92% under their respective evaluated history budgets, and reaches 82.33% with identical histories and queries. On ToolPRMBench's BFCL and ToolSandbox tasks, absolute accuracy gains are 34.26% and 28.87%, respectively, at the methods' respective evaluated history budgets. Accuracy improves as history grows. With identical imbalanced histories, mean balanced accuracy improves by an absolute 14.51% across five reasoning-step assessment tasks and four encoders. DPDM makes learning from experience an independently improvable foundation-model capability, creating a shared route for advances in conditional prediction to improve decisions across agent tasks.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: OpenZilo: An Open Smart-Ring Platform for Human-Centric Sensing and Interaction with Robots
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Qianggang Ding, Xingyao Wang, Rui Feng, Chi Qin, Weijian Lin
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The OpenZilo smart-ring platform enables effective human-robot interaction through speech and gesture control, achieving high task success rates and efficient response times.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Wearable robot interfaces must connect user input to timely physical action. We present the proposed platform, an open smart-ring platform for studying this connection across task stages. The ring integrates a microphone, an inertial measurement unit, photoplethysmography, and skin-temperature sensing. Its software architecture separates acquisition, event interpretation, interaction policy, and robot execution. We characterize seven operating modes and evaluate speech and gesture control with 10 participants. Across five commands and 250 trials per modality, speech and gestures achieved task success rates of 90.4% and 88.8%, respectively. Recognition accuracy exceeded task success for both modalities. Gaussian hidden Markov models achieved higher accuracy than a support vector machine across three vocabulary sizes, with longer scoring times. Following a shared spoken task start, gesture-based adjustments had shorter median response times than speech. Whole-task success was 70.0% with gestures and 64.0% with speech. We further examine physiological-event-triggered robot interaction using simulated event notifications. Mean notification-receipt-to-arrival times were 11.71 s for the robot and 9.20 s for an on-site person. These descriptive findings support evaluating wearable robot interfaces through both recognition and physical outcomes, with timing measures appropriate to each task stage.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: $π$-StepNFT: Wider Space Needs Finer Steps in Online RL for Flow-based VLAs
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Siting Wang, Xiaofeng Wang, Zheng Zhu, Minnan Pei, Xinyu Cui
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The $π$-StepNFT framework enhances online reinforcement learning for flow-based VLAs by integrating wider stochastic exploration with fine-tuned supervision, significantly improving success rates in various tasks.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Flow-based vision-language-action (VLA) models have emerged as a powerful paradigm for embodied control, but multi-step denoising makes policy-gradient online reinforcement learning (RL) difficult because the final-action likelihood induced by the sampler is not directly tractable. We identify an exploration--supervision mismatch within the denoising trajectory, where stochastic differential equation (SDE) sampling explores a wider local stochastic transition space while supervision derived from the final denoised output does not directly use the adjacent transitions observed during sampling. We propose $π$-StepNFT (Step-wise Negative-aware Fine-Tuning), a flow-native online RL framework that couples wider stochastic exploration with finer step-wise supervision without computing the final-action likelihood. $π$-StepNFT treats observed SDE transitions as supervision units, using variance-normalized transition errors to rank mirrored positive and negative velocity branches and map rollout feedback to local velocity updates. On LIBERO, starting from shared few-shot SFT initializations, $π$-StepNFT raises average success from 57.6\% to 92.0\% for $π_0$ and from 77.1\% to 94.0\% for $π_{0.5}$. On ManiSkill, it achieves the highest reported mean success among the evaluated RL baselines on five test-only visual perturbations. Our project homepage is available at https://wangst0181.github.io/pi-StepNFT/.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: EgoHSI3R: Online 4D Hand-Scene Interaction Reconstruction from Egocentric Video
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Mingzhi Pei, Zhangchen Ye, Ruoqu Chen, Liu Cao, Mengdi Xu
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: EgoHSI3R is a unified framework for online 4D hand-scene interaction reconstruction from egocentric video, achieving superior accuracy and speed in joint estimation of hands, camera, and scene geometry.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Egocentric videos offer an abundant source of hand-scene interactions for embodied learning, which requires recovering hands, camera, and scene consistently in a shared 3D world. Existing methods focus on either camera-frame hands or world-space hand trajectories, without jointly recovering the scene pointmaps or interaction information. Building a complete reconstruction from such specialized predictions therefore typically requires per-sequence optimization. We propose EgoHSI3R, a unified feed-forward framework for online 4D hand-scene interaction reconstruction from egocentric monocular video. To jointly recover these components, it maintains a recurrent scene representation that accumulates geometric evidence over time and provides a shared world space and scale. We introduce hand-centric prompts that fuse pretrained hand priors and local scene context, while MANO vertex queries attend to scene features to predict dense per-vertex contact. These designs enable a single network to jointly estimate camera motion, dense scene geometry, world-space bilateral MANO hands, and per-vertex hand contact. Despite operating causally, EgoHSI3R achieves the lowest world-space hand joint error on ARCTIC among the evaluated methods, while offering faster inference than existing world-space hand reconstruction pipelines and competitive camera and scene reconstruction accuracy.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: HandMimicX: Learning Human-Like Dexterous Manipulation via an Object-Centric Policy from Egocentric Videos
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Zihan Gao, Yufei Liu, Yuhong Zhang, Zhen Yu, Xinhao Huang
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: HandMimicX presents an object-centric framework for learning dexterous manipulation from egocentric videos, enabling generalizable robotic skills through reinforcement learning and natural hand-object interactions.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Learning dexterous manipulation from human videos remains an open challenge, particularly in the context of transferring a single demonstration into a spatially generalizable robotic skill and maintaining physically plausible human-like interactions. Unlike prior works that emphasize hand-motion imitation, we introduce an object-centric framework for acquiring dexterous skills from egocentric human RGB-D videos. Within our framework, we formulate the reinforcement learning (RL) objective in terms of object motion to decouple the underlying skill from the specific hand trajectory and impose constraints on hand-object interaction states to promote more anatomically natural hand configurations. Extensive experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate that our method enables efficient learning from human videos and generalizable skill transfer across novel spatial configurations.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Ask on Demand: Targeted Peer Communication for Parallel Agentic Systems
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Haofu Yang, Hongyang Yin, Ran Bi, Faguo Wu, Peng Xue
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The Ask on Demand framework enhances parallel LLM agent collaboration by enabling targeted peer communication, improving task performance and reducing inference costs through adaptive information sharing.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Parallel LLM agents tackle complex tasks by exploring multiple trajectories, yet useful discoveries remain isolated in individual execution histories. Existing sharing methods often select or summarize information before other agents' needs become clear, potentially overlooking details that become important later. We propose Ask on Demand (AOD), a communication framework that enables agents to seek targeted peer assistance when specific information needs arise. Upon an approved request, AOD retrieves relevant evidence from peer execution histories, selects a suitable peer, and generates a response tailored to the request. To determine when such assistance is worthwhile, we train a lightweight gate using paired team continuations, with supervision derived from final team outcomes and inference cost. Experiments on AppWorld and WebShop demonstrate that AOD consistently improves task performance over independent parallel execution while achieving lower inference cost than existing information-sharing baselines. These findings highlight the benefits of aligning peer communication with agents' evolving information needs to achieve more effective and efficient collaboration.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: When the Simulator Fails, Not the Policy: Auditing Contact Artifacts in Simulated Robot Benchmarks
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Alex Zhou, Junhao Wu, Xueyang Zhou, Yixiao Huo, Hongcheng Gao
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The paper introduces SimuGuard, an auditing tool that identifies and mitigates simulator-induced failures in robot policy evaluations, enhancing success rates in simulated benchmarks.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Simulation benchmarks score robot policies by success rate, and every failed episode counts against the policy. Many of these failures are the simulator's fault, not the policy's; we find the cause and fix it. Testing a vision language action model and a world action model in simulation, we find that the policy often places the object and the simulator then ejects it, and that the benchmark's own scripted demonstrations fail the same way. We present SimuGuard, an auditing plugin for LIBERO, RoboTwin, RoboCasa and RoboDojo. It leaves the evaluation unchanged. At every physics step, it records the state and flags an object that starts moving at a contact faster than the robot's contact or gravity account for. It replays a recorded episode bit for bit, and it reruns the episode with one simulation parameter changed. With it we trace these episodes on RoboTwin to the collision detection of the physics engine: for geometry one to two centimeters apart, the engine reports a penetration of about two centimeters, and the solver throws the object out at several meters per second. The cause is one constant: the distance algorithm discards triangles below a fixed area threshold, which valid triangles fall below at the centimeter scale. With that constant changed and nothing else, episodes with an artifact fall from 12 in 100 to none, and the success rate on five container tasks rises from 89% to 98%. Success rates in simulation thus count failures that the simulator causes. Benchmarks on PhysX 5.3.1 or earlier should rerun in a repaired engine. Where the engine cannot change, they should report the success rate together with the range it spans when every flagged episode fails or passes: 75.8% to 98.5% around a reported 83.1% for LingBot-VA.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: FrontierMat: Benchmarking Language Models at the Frontier of Materials R&D
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Feng Chen, Jianguo Huang, Yushan Xiao, Yue Li, Bijun Tang
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: FrontierMat introduces a benchmark of 330 validated research problems to evaluate language models' effectiveness in advanced materials discovery, highlighting significant performance gaps and improvement strategies.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: To accelerate materials discovery, language models must be able to address problems at the research frontier. Yet textbook- and examination-derived benchmarks primarily assess established knowledge, leaving performance on frontier research problems largely untested. We introduce FrontierMat, a benchmark of 330 problems drawn from frontier academic and industrial research in fields including aerospace, semiconductors, embodied intelligence and nuclear fusion. Every problem is validated by leading experimentalists and industry experts in its field. Each problem presents a real study and asks the model to infer a withheld outcome or draw a conclusion from selected experimental evidence. Problems are annotated by functional domain, material system and the scale of the governing mechanism; 130 require cross-scale reasoning. The strongest general-purpose model scores only 53.7%, and on matched problems, cross-scale problems score 8.7 points below single-scale ones. Half of the problems are solved by at most one model, and models fail chiefly by endorsing what is plausible rather than what was observed. A domain-adaptation study with meta-weighted continued pretraining and scale-modular self-distillation raises an open-weight model from 36.7% to 55.4%, matching the strongest proprietary model, with improvements on public materials benchmarks and no decline in aggregate performance on general benchmarks. FrontierMat provides a testbed for measuring progress toward language models that support frontier materials R&D.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Adaptive-WAM: Quality-Guided Early-Exit Planning from Intermediate Video-Diffusion Features
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Sining Ang, Yuguang Yang, Yan Wang
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: Adaptive-WAM introduces a quality-aware multi-exit planner that optimizes trajectory planning by leveraging intermediate video-diffusion features, achieving superior performance and reduced latency in autonomous driving.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Large video diffusion models provide rich spatiotemporal priors for autonomous driving, but existing world-action models often inherit the cost of iterative future-video generation even though deployment only requires an ego trajectory. We ask a more basic question: how much of a video diffusion model must be executed to make a reliable driving decision? Through a controlled study of video denoising timesteps and Diffusion Transformer (DiT) depth, we find that planning performance is largely insensitive to the tested video-noise levels, whereas strong trajectories can already be decoded from intermediate layers. Based on this observation, we introduce Adaptive-WAM, a quality-aware multi-exit planner built on a Wan2.2-5B backbone. Trajectory diffusion heads are attached to selected DiT blocks, and a lightweight trajectory-quality scorer terminates inference once the best trajectory decoded so far satisfies a quality threshold; otherwise, computation continues from the cached hidden state to a deeper exit. The deployed planner therefore avoids the iterative classifier-free denoising loop and VAE decoding required for future-video synthesis, while dynamically allocating backbone depth according to trajectory quality. On NAVSIM, the adaptive single-trajectory planner achieves 90.8 PDMS; a separate fixed-exit variant reaches 92.6 PDMS with 64 proposals. It further obtains 89.9 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2, yielding the best reported results among the compared front-view video world-model planners. Without target-domain fine-tuning, Adaptive-WAM transfers to nuScenes with 0.88 m average L2 error and a 0.08\% collision rate. On an A100, adaptive routing improves PDMS from 90.62 to 90.79 while averaging 170 ms end-to-end planning latency, approximately 10\% below the 190 ms fixed block-15 planner and 47\% below the 320 ms fixed full-depth planner. Code will be released.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Retrieve in Time, Correct in Frequency
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Yuze Fan, Yue Cao, Pengjie Gao, Haojia Gao, Guangqiu Guo
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The RTCF framework enhances frozen vision-language-action policies by correcting execution errors through memory alignment and low-frequency residual transfers, improving task success rates without model updates.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Frozen vision-language-action (VLA) policies generate temporally extended action chunks, but long-horizon manipulation remains vulnerable to accumulated execution error and visual aliasing across task stages. Successful rollouts provide useful corrective evidence, yet current frame retrieval can return progress-misaligned actions,while direct replay or time-domain fusion can overwrite the reactive structure of the policy proposal. We introduce Retrieve in Time, Correct in Frequency (RTCF), a training-free test-time correction framework that improves frozen VLA performance with low model-side overhead.RTCF separates which experience to retrieve from which part of its action to transfer. Progressive Memory Alignment (PMA) causally aligns the growing visual execution history with complete successful trajectories through incrementally updated monotonic frontiers, jointly identifying a relevant memory and the current aligned memory position without stage labels. From the aligned action chunk,RTCF transfers a coefficient-wise-clipped low-frequency residual on motion channels. Higher-frequency components and gripper decisions remain inherited from the frozen policy. Across four LIBERO suites and 2,000 episodes per condition, RTCF raises aggregate success from 86.4% to 88.4% and improves LIBERO-Long from 61.6% to 68.6%.These gains require no parameter updates, repeated VLA inference, or additional GPU resources: correction can be performed on the client CPU after a single policy invocation, and the median latencies sum to only 10.99 ms per action chunk

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Tracking Task Progress Through Errors and Recovery:A Benchmark and Recurrent Distributional Model
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Chen Wang, Xinze Niu, Zihao Zhu, Keru Zhou, Yicheng Xu
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The paper introduces the ReSTEP dataset for tracking robotic task progress through errors and recovery, and presents REMORA, an advanced progress estimator that outperforms existing models.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Operational strategies for long-horizon robotic tasks require reliable evaluation to determine whether execution is progressing, stalling, regressing, or recovering from errors. Yet real- world robot datasets that capture error recovery and provide frame-level error annotations remain scarce. To address this gap, we introduce and open-source ReSTEP, a dataset of 3,156 episodes across two manipulation tasks with semantic stage labels and frame-level er- ror annotations. ReSTEP supports training and benchmarking progress monitors through successful execution, mistakes, and recovery. Existing progress estimators can struggle to distinguish visually similar task stages and maintain temporally consistent predictions while responding to genuine setbacks. We therefore propose REMORA, an online progress esti- mator that combines recurrent visual memory, distributional prediction, and causal peak selection. Memory retains execution history to help resolve visual ambiguity, while distribu- tional prediction represents alternative progress hypotheses and causal peak selection tracks a supported hypothesis over time. Together, these components enable consistent progress tracking that remains responsive to errors and recovery. Experiments on both ReSTEP tasks demonstrate that REMORA outperforms the state-of-the-art SARM baseline in progress ac- curacy and temporal consistency.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Semantic-Enriched Latent Visual Reasoning
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Tianrun Xu, Yue Sun, Qixun Wang, Jingyi Lu, Yuan Wang
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: SLVR enhances latent visual reasoning by integrating attribute-level semantics and aligning representations across queries, supported by a comprehensive dataset and benchmark for evaluation.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Multimodal latent-space reasoning aims to replace explicit thinking with images by performing visual reasoning directly in a compact latent space. However, existing approaches largely rely on visual supervision and produce latent representations that lack sufficient semantic richness, limiting their ability to support diverse region-level reasoning tasks. In this work, we introduce Semantic-Enriched Latent Visual Reasoning (SLVR), a two-stage learning framework that enriches latent representations with attribute-level visual semantics and aligns them with diverse reasoning objectives. In the first stage, SLVR learns semantically enriched region-centric latents under fine-grained attribute supervision. In the second stage, we design Multi-query Group Relative Policy Optimization (M-GRPO) to align latent representations across multiple queries grounded in the same region. To support this framework, we construct SLV-Set, comprising approximately 400K region-level attribute annotations and 800K multi-query question answering samples, and introduce SV-QA, a benchmark that evaluates latent reasoning under semantic variation. Experiments demonstrate that SLVR improves the robustness and semantic consistency of latent visual reasoning compared to existing baselines.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Utility-WAM: Correcting Future-Induced Action Changes
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Feihong Zhang, Xi Lin, Yulong Shi, Zuxing Lu, Yanghong Mei
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: Utility-WAM mitigates future-induced negative transfer in robot action execution by correcting velocity deltas, enhancing performance and reducing latency in visual prediction tasks.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) can condition robot actions on generated visual futures, but this additional context is neither cost-free nor uniformly beneficial. We examine what a predicted future actually changes: the action delta $Δa$ between the future-conditioned and future-free execution paths of the same model. Under a shared WAM checkpoint, this delta barely shifts average benchmark success ($+0.8$ points on LIBERO, $-0.8$ on RoboTwin~2.0), while generating visual futures increases inference latency by 1.7--1.9$\times$. These aggregate metrics conceal a concentrated failure mode that we term \emph{future-induced negative transfer}: while predictive deltas benefit long-horizon tasks ($+2.4$ points on LIBERO-Long) and remain negligible on most routine manipulations, they induce severe degradation on precision tasks---with \emph{Press Stapler} and \emph{Place Can Basket} losing 54.0 and 34.0 points, recurring as top failure modes across independently trained WAM variants. We introduce \textbf{Utility-WAM} for in-place correction of future-conditioned control. Its primary learning component is a residual adapter that repairs future-induced velocity deltas under a frozen shared WAM by aligning them with ground-truth dynamic guidance and penalizing excess error beyond the future-free baseline. The adapter selectively eliminates the majority of severe task drops (reducing losses to 6.0 and 14.0 points) while preserving long-horizon foresight. To eliminate superfluous video computation, a lightweight pre-generation gate reuses counterfactual action outcomes to selectively bypass video generation on 75.5\% of RoboTwin queries, cutting latency by 38\% while improving average success to 93.3\% on RoboTwin~2.0 and 98.9\% on LIBERO. On physical bimanual manipulation across three real-world tasks, Utility-WAM succeeds in 53 of 60 trials, compared to 43 for FAST-WAM.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: TactoHand: Learning Geometry-Based Dense Hand-Surface Interaction Fields from Video
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Ziheng Xi, Weibo Li, Jiayi Yu, Sipeng Zheng, Wanpeng Zhang
