Existing memory mechanisms typically compress, retrieve, or cache historical observations and reintroduce them into the input context, forcing historical memory and current observations to compete for limited context. We propose MaLoW, a streaming memory framework that instead internalizes historical context into evolving lightweight parameter updates. MaLoW uses a recurrent HyperNetwork to incrementally consolidate incoming video observations into fixed-size LoRA weights, allowing historical information to be carried forward without revisiting the full video stream. In doing so, MaLoW represents history as weights, while keeping the current observation as input. To support training, we further construct MaLoW-Instruct, a large-scale streaming video dataset containing 381K question-answer pairs over 56K videos. We conduct extensive experiments to demonstrate that MaLoW achieves strong performance on OVO-Bench, StreamingBench, and StreamArena. On the backward split of OVO-Bench, MaLoW outperforms prior memory approaches by 3.9% to 11.8% across different video backbones while incurring only modest latency overhead. Beyond streaming video understanding, MaLoW also generalizes to vision-language-action models, improving the action success rate on Simpler WidowX by 9.3%.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: MMSearch-OPD: Easy Made Hard, Hard Made Learnable for Long-Horizon Multimodal Search Agents
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Huanyao Zhang, Jiepeng Zhou, Jiaye Lin, Ontai Tang, Jingtian Hao
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: MMSearch-OPD enhances long-horizon multimodal search agents through targeted data refinement, joint reinforcement learning, and on-policy distillation, improving training and performance.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Multimodal deep search is moving from short queries to long-horizon investigations that continually acquire evidence. However, training such agents remains constrained by limited challenging training questions and insufficient process feedback. We introduce MMSearch-OPD, combining controllable data refinement with joint reinforcement learning (RL) and on-policy distillation (OPD). Our Refine pipeline performs targeted expansion of reasoning chains derived from existing simple multimodal questions. Parameterized transformations control search depth and cross-modal evidence requirements while reusing existing image--question pairs. For training, answer rewards and lightweight behavior penalties guide RL, while the reward gap modulates token-level teacher guidance on imperfect student trajectories. An exponentially decaying distillation coefficient reduces teacher dependence as training proceeds. Experiments show gains from data refinement and further improvements from joint training after SFT, indicating stronger long-horizon multimodal deep search capabilities.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: SceneReVis: A Self-Reflective Vision-Grounded Framework for 3D Indoor Scene Synthesis via Multi-Turn RL
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Yang Zhao, Shizhao Sun, Meisheng Zhang, Yingdong Shi, Xubo Yang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: SceneReVis introduces a self-reflective framework for 3D indoor scene synthesis that utilizes multi-turn reinforcement learning to resolve spatial conflicts and enhance generation fidelity.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Current one-pass 3D scene synthesis methods often suffer from spatial hallucinations, such as collisions, due to a lack of deliberative reasoning. To bridge this gap, we introduce SceneReVis, a vision-grounded self-reflection framework that employs an iterative "diagnose-and-act" loop to explicitly intercept and resolve spatial conflicts using multi-modal feedback. To support this step-wise paradigm, we construct SceneChain-12k, a large-scale dataset of causal construction trajectories derived through a novel reverse engineering pipeline. We further propose a two-stage training recipe that transitions from Supervised Fine-Tuning to Agentic Reinforcement Learning, evolving the model into an active spatial planner. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SceneReVis achieves state-of-the-art performance in high-fidelity generation and goal-oriented optimization, with improved transfer to underrepresented room categories in the dataset and promising potential for extension to out-of-distribution room types.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: LICOA: Learning Instruction-Conditioned Optical Actions for Mobile Spatial Augmented Reality
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Yuchen Deng, Shunkai Zhou, Ruixuan Zhu, Haibin Ling, Bingyao Huang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: LICOA enables mobile spatial augmented reality systems to autonomously project light based on language instructions and visual observations, achieving notable success in real-world tasks.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Spatial augmented reality (SAR) augments physical environments with projected content, but most systems assume that the projector pose, target region, or motion path has been fixed or specified. We instead make projected light an embodied action: given a language instruction and current visual observations, a system must decide how to move and where and at what scale to place the projection. We introduce LICOA to realize this capability. Its differential-drive chassis provides room-scale approach and repositioning, while a steerable mirror with two degrees of freedom (2DoF) and projection scale provide rapid local control of the beam. A shared interface maps synchronized external and onboard RGB cameras with robot control state to physical optical actions across pretrained action models. Because instruction-conditioned optical action lacks dedicated training data and a common evaluation protocol, we construct a matched simulation embodiment and a corpus with 150 tasks and 7,500 rendered episodes, then evaluate models trained only on this corpus in previously unseen real-world environments. Across 480 complete closed-loop real-world execution trials (rollouts) on 12 tasks, the best adapted action model achieves a 57.50% success rate and 40.64% success weighted by path length, compared with 8.33% and 5.15% for the same architecture trained from scratch. A further 150 real-world ablation rollouts support the need for both camera views and coordinated control of the chassis and mirror. These results establish a physical platform, shared perception and optical action interface, corpus, and real-world evaluation protocol for treating projected light as an embodied action.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Reinforcement Learning-driven Diffusion Models: Language, Vision, and Beyond
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Zhiyuan Ma, Jiabao Wei, Tianyu Wang, Hanqing Wang, Jiadong Pan
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: This paper reviews and analyzes the integration of reinforcement learning into diffusion models, addressing limitations and proposing strategies for improved goal-directed generation across various applications.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Diffusion models (DMs) have steadily demonstrated outstanding performance in high-fidelity, controllable generation across diverse scenarios, following the "pretraining-finetuning" paradigm established in LLMs. Despite these advances, conventional DMs still face critical limitations in sophisticated reasoning, autonomous exploration of generation pathways, and adaptability to complex, human-aligned objectives. Inspired by RLHF's success in LLMs, RL has recently emerged as a pivotal post-training mechanism to iteratively refine DMs through reward-driven trajectory optimization. This paper presents the first comprehensive review of RL-driven DMs and an empirical analysis of how RL reshapes the diffusion process towards experience-centric, goal-directed generation. We propose a novel technical panorama elucidating RL's multifaceted roles in diffusion-based language, multimodal, robotic, and scientific models, with a granular focus on diffusion trajectory optimization and reward engineering. Through extensive experiments on multiple task-specific benchmarks, we systematically evaluate representative methods to intuitively highlight the advantages of different RL post-training strategies. Furthermore, we reveal and dissect three crucial bottlenecks that currently hinder the real-world deployment of RL-driven DMs: reward design fragility, exploration-exploitation trade-off in high-dimensional generation spaces, and training instability under sparse rewards. Based on these perspectives, we provide a principled roadmap for the integration of RL into DMs and outline promising future research directions for robust, interpretable RL-diffusion systems. We also construct a public repository to continuously track the latest developments in this rapidly evolving field: https://github.com/MAIR-Lab-HUST/Awesome-RL-for-Diffusion-Models.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Coding Agent Memory Post-Training II: Unlocking the Memory Potential of Pre-trained File Operations for Long-Horizon Tasks via On-Policy Distillation
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Lirui Luo, Kelong Mao, Xinwei Yang, Rongqing Li, Luyu Chen
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper presents CAMP-II, a method enhancing long-horizon task performance in language-model agents through on-policy distillation and file-based memory management in diverse environments.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Language-model agents increasingly tackle long-horizon tasks whose interaction histories exceed the model's active context. They must therefore decide what to write down and what to read back, and when to do either. Recent work has begun to use on-policy distillation (OPD) to make memory control part of the policy, relying on memory tools and compaction protocols that lie outside either model's pre-training. However, this weakens the distillation on both sides: the teacher cannot give useful guidance on an interface it has never used, and the student samples too few meaningful memory actions for that guidance to take effect. To study this problem, we introduce Coding Agent Memory Gym II (CAMG-II), a suite of long-horizon agentic-RL environments spanning Shop, Coding, AutoResearch, General, and Visual. Alongside each environment's native task interface, CAMG-II provides ordinary Bash access and an episode-persistent workspace, enabling the policy to create, revise, search, and reuse files as memory across context replacements. We also introduce Coding Agent Memory Post-Training II (CAMP-II), which trains a single policy jointly across all five environments with fully asynchronous OPD to learn this file-based memory behavior directly from a frozen teacher with a prior for file operations. On CAMG-II, CAMP-II obtains 2.97 times the gain of the strongest OPD baseline. The memory behavior CAMP-II learns generalizes to two external benchmarks, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-Bench Pro V2, with improved success rates.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Stylization as Geodesic Navigation on Diffusion Manifolds
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Yan Li, Zehao Li, Xinlong Sun, Fuchen Long, Xi Chen
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: Stylus is a training-free framework for facial stylization that navigates diffusion manifolds, enabling fine control over style while preserving identity through geodesic energy optimization.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Facial stylization asks for a delicate transformation: the image should look unmistakably artistic, yet the person should remain unmistakably the same. Existing training-free and instruction-driven methods often fail to expose such control, either drifting away from identity or producing only weak stylization. We introduce Stylus, a training-free framework that treats facial style transfer as navigation on the curved latent manifold of a pretrained diffusion model. Rather than interpolating in flat Euclidean space, \method refines the interpolated content--style point by lowering a ratio-weighted discrete geodesic energy under the pullback metric, made tractable by a rank-one power-iteration approximation of the Jacobian. This principle drives two complementary controls: content--style latent interpolation for smooth semantic fusion, and self-attention query optimization for spatially adaptive style injection. The resulting dual-control mechanism provides continuous, fine-grained control over stylization strength while preserving identity-critical facial structure, all without additional training. Experiments show that Stylus achieves the strongest identity and content preservation at competitive stylization strength.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: With Tools or Because of Tools? Tracing Capability Gains in Multimodal Agents
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Jiawei Guo, Donglei Yu, Yu Chen, Xiang Wang, Shuai Li
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The study critiques the assumption that tool-augmented multimodal agents improve capabilities, revealing they often learn tool-calling patterns without significant enhancement in problem-solving abilities.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Tool-augmented multimodal agents show strong benchmark gains, often taken as evidence that agents have learned to use tools. We argue that this interpretation can be premature: a tool-call trace alone does not show whether the tool supplied answer-critical information. We study two representative ``thinking with images'' agents, Thyme and DeepEyesV2, across real-world understanding, OCR, chart understanding, and mathematical reasoning. Each agent is compared with its Tool-Free counterpart and with a Pure-Text Reasoner trained from the same source pool without tool-calling trajectories. Tool access yields little consistent aggregate improvement, does not reliably reduce generated-token cost, and leaves only a small tool-only solved set: 93% of DeepEyesV2's tool-solved problems and 96% of Thyme's are also solved by at least one non-tool setting. Mechanism ablations further show that the full tool-use loop does not consistently outperform either the tool-call format or the returned execution result alone. In the settings we study, the analyzed agents appear to learn tool-calling patterns more reliably than tool-contributed capabilities, suggesting that evaluation should distinguish tool availability from whether tools actually expand what agents can solve.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: MADSNet: A Multi-Scale Axial-Attentive Dense Spiking Network for Spike Camera Image Reconstruction
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Sirui Li, Rui Zhao, Siqi Cai, Haizhou Li, Tiejun Huang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: MADSNet is a novel spiking neural network that enhances image reconstruction from spike camera data, achieving superior fidelity and efficiency compared to existing methods.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Spike cameras encode dynamic scenes into high-temporal-resolution binary spike streams for efficient high-speed vision. Although spiking neural networks (SNNs) can process such signals with sparse and accumulate-only computation, existing SNN-based reconstruction methods are typically shallow and still lag behind ANN-based models in reconstruction fidelity. This paper proposes MADSNet, a Multi-scale Axial-attentive Dense Spiking Network for spike camera image reconstruction. MADSNet adopts a hierarchical spiking encoder--decoder, where a multi-scale spike stem extracts early features, axial spike attention captures long-range dependencies, a dense spiking bottleneck enhances feature reuse, and a spike-to-continuous decoder reconstructs continuous intensity images from spike-domain representations. Experiments on gray-scale and color spike reconstruction show that MADSNet outperforms SSIR by 4.3 dB PSNR and Spk2ImgNet by 1.94 dB on SREDS. Compared with Spk2ImgNet, it achieves about 15$\times$ lower latency and uses only about 1/40 of the estimated energy, demonstrating that carefully designed SNN architectures can improve reconstruction quality while preserving computational efficiency.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: From Questions to Decisions: Benchmarking How LLM Agents Acquire Decision-Relevant Information from Human Beings
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Yuhan Tang, Ke Fan, Xinkai Zou, Baichuan Mo, Kangxin Cui
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper introduces Ask2Decide, a benchmark assessing LLM agents' ability to acquire crucial decision-making information from humans, revealing significant shortcomings in their planning efficacy.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: LLM agents are increasingly asked to make plans for people, such as scheduling drivers or assigning nurses. However, people's requests are often incomplete, and the supporting information for decision-making may be outdated, requiring agents to ask for clarification. Existing benchmarks typically provide fully specified problems or rely on uncalibrated LLM-simulated users, leaving this ability insufficiently tested. We introduce Ask2Decide, a benchmark of 43 planning tasks that evaluates whether agents ask for missing information that matters for their decisions. An operator holds facts absent from the agent's request and records, and optimization solvers determine which facts change the optimal plan. We also include similarly worded facts that leave the optimal plan unchanged to test whether agents distinguish useful information from irrelevant details. We collect 79 interaction sessions from 19 participants and find that, after an incorrect plan, human replies omit the correcting fact far more often than replies from an uncalibrated simulated user (43% versus 7%). Using these interactions, we calibrate a simulated operator that more closely matches human reply patterns. Evaluating four frontier LLMs, we find that their initial plans are infeasible on 58-98% of tasks when information is missing, compared with 5-28% when all facts are provided upfront. Agents uncover facts that change the optimal plan only slightly more often than facts that leave it unchanged (39-52% versus 32-41%). These results show that obtaining decision-relevant information through interaction remains a major bottleneck for LLM planning. This is ongoing work and will be updated. The date of this version is shown on the first page.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Ego Guidance: Enhancing Robot Policy Learning with Action-Free Human Egocentric Videos
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Lin Long, Tianren Ma, Zhong Chu, Di Wu, Maosong Cao
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: This paper presents SPAR, a method leveraging human egocentric videos to enhance robot policy learning through independent visual state predictions, improving performance on diverse tasks.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: In this paper, we investigate how human egocentric videos can benefit robot policy learning without action supervision. Building on a pretrained VLM, we propose Shared Prediction on Action and Representation (SPAR), an MoT architecture in which future visual state prediction can provide independent and complementary learning signals alongside action prediction. We find that representations learned from egocentric videos improve downstream performance on out-of-distribution robot tasks, with further gains as video data scales. We also study the effects of objective choices and data curation, providing insights into how to leverage action-free videos for scalable robot learning.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: A 10K drone image dataset with component-level annotations for rooftop photovoltaic inspection
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Penglei Zhang, Wan Zhang, Ruizhe Deng, Bo Chen, Wenhao Duan
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The PVIS-10K dataset consists of 10,065 annotated drone images for precise component-level inspection of rooftop photovoltaic systems, enhancing localization and counting capabilities.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Component-level information supports rooftop photovoltaic (PV) inspection, but recognizing individual components across complex scenes remains challenging. We present PVIS-10K, a dataset of 10,065 drone images with component-level annotations covering 63,632 physical PV modules across 22 rooftop installations. The high-resolution red-green-blue (RGB) images were acquired by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs, also known as drones) in Ningbo, Shaoxing and Shenzhen, China. Multi-angle oblique observations capture installation-height and scale variation, dense arrangements, occlusion, shadows and reflections. Three-dimensional delineation, reprojection and image-by-image review produced 3,516,675 image-level polygon annotations, stored in Common Objects in Context (COCO) format. Station-disjoint partitions support evaluation on unseen stations within and across cities. Four supervised models and text-prompted zero-shot Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3) provide full-resolution benchmarks of instance matching and foreground coverage. PVIS-10K supports component localization, delineation and image-based counting for drone-based rooftop PV inspection research.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: LaST0.5: A Generalist World Action Model with Interaction-Centric Latent Reasoning
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Xuheng Zhang, Yiming Zhang, Jialin Gao, Hao Chen, Jiaming Liu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: LaST0.5 is a novel World Action Model that enhances robotic manipulation by introducing an interaction-centric latent space for improved action generation and physical reasoning.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) have recently emerged as a promising paradigm for robotic manipulation, endowing policies with strong capabilities for modeling temporal and physical dynamics. Existing WAMs, encompassing both video-first action prediction and joint video-action modeling, directly transfer global physical representations from world models to action generation. However, global scene representations may underemphasize local robot-object interactions, creating a mismatch between representations optimized for world evolution and those required for manipulation. To bridge this gap, we propose LaST0.5, a novel WAM that introduces an interaction-centric physical representation between world modeling and action generation. Specifically, LaST0.5 learns a compact interaction-centric latent space under the supervision of visual interaction cues between the robot and the environment. This reasoning space is instantiated as a latent expert that bridges the world expert and the action expert within a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture. Furthermore, LaST0.5 performs adaptive world-to-action transfer by jointly predicting future representations and progress values, using progress consistency to adjust action execution and trigger future resampling. Finally, we pretrain LaST0.5 on a large-scale robotic data corpus comprising over 14k hours of data, establishing interaction-centric physical reasoning as a scalable and effective paradigm. LaST0.5 achieves 99.5% on LIBERO, surpasses the previous state of the art on ten evaluated RLBench tasks, and demonstrates robust long-horizon execution and precise dexterous manipulation in real-world experiments.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: The World is Not Mono: Enabling Spatial Understanding in Large Audio-Language Models
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Yuhuan You, Lai Wei, Tianshu Qu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper introduces TWNM, a framework enhancing audio-language models with spatial understanding through a structured audio scene analysis approach, achieving notable accuracy on a controlled benchmark.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Large audio-language models have made rapid progress in recognizing what is present in an audio clip, but spatial audio-language understanding still lacks a clear task interface. A model must also decide where sound events occur, which semantic and spatial attributes belong to the same auditory object, how multiple objects are arranged, and whether a scene-level answer is physically plausible. We formalize this capability as audio scene analysis (ASA), a three-level problem spanning atomic perception, relational integration, and cognitive reasoning. We propose The World is Not Mono (TWNM), a framework that equips audio-language models with explicit spatial evidence. TWNM uses physically grounded First-Order Ambisonics (FOA) simulation for controllable supervision, learns slot-regularized spatial representations from multichannel audio, fuses them with semantic audio features, and trains with a progressive curriculum ending in preference optimization over metadata-derived correct answers and auxiliary format/evidence rewards. To operationalize ASA, we build a controlled benchmark from scene metadata, covering localization, attribute binding, spatial comparison, scene abduction, and counterfactual reasoning. On this benchmark, TWNM achieves 70.8% overall accuracy, 66.4% on spatial-family tasks, and 79.76% on mixed $\mathcal{L}_3$ scene-level QA under exact multiple-choice question answering (MCQA) scoring. We also audit monaural and binaural reference systems as diagnostic references with explicit audit labels, since they differ in spatial input, training interface, and output format. The supported claim is that a clearly defined ASA hierarchy, FOA-conditioned spatial representations, and metadata-grounded training enable controlled, auditable spatial audio-language reasoning, with STARSS23 providing a limited real-recording diagnostic.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: LessMimic: Versatile Humanoid-Object Interaction with Unified Distance Field Representations
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Yutang Lin, Jieming Cui, Yixuan Li, Wei Liang, Baoxiong Jia
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: LessMimic introduces a unified framework for humanoid-object interaction that enables versatile, command-steered control based on local geometry, enhancing generalization and skill composition.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Humanoid robots capable of versatile whole-body interaction with everyday objects represent a central goal of embodied intelligence. Existing approaches often rely on motion-reference inputs or task-specific rewards, coupling policies to particular motion scripts, object geometries, and contact timings. This limits geometric generalization and flexible interaction control, where simple commands specify motion intent while object geometry determines how contact should be executed. We introduce LessMimic, a framework for versatile motion-free-at-inference humanoid-object interaction. At inference, a single whole-body policy is steered by root commands and an interaction-type flag instead of motion-reference inputs, and is conditioned on a compact interaction representation built from short histories of distance-field-derived surface distances and local surface directions. This geometry-conditioned interface enables command-steered control while adapting contact behavior to local object geometry. Through visual distillation, LessMimic further enables egocentric-depth-based deployment for MoCap-free sensing. Across object scales from 0.4x to 1.6x, LessMimic maintains robust performance over four interaction tasks, including PickUp, SitStand, Push, and Carry, where motion-conditioned baselines degrade sharply away from the training scale. Beyond single-task evaluation, LessMimic further supports sequential composition of heterogeneous interaction skills, attaining 62.1% success on five-task sequences and retaining 23.5% success at 15 task instances. By grounding interaction control in local geometry rather than motion references, LessMimic provides a path toward geometry-generalizable, command-steerable humanoid-object control with heterogeneous skill composition.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: DAC-MACE: Context-Conditioned Expert Routing for Compact Scene Coordinate Regression in Camera Relocalization
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Dingying Fan, Mingkai Liu, Haohua Que, Haojia Gao, Xianliang Huang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: DAC-MACE improves camera relocalization by enhancing expert routing through contextualized features, achieving the lowest translation error among RGB-only scene coordinate regression methods.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: A camera becomes an absolute pose sensor when its images can be relocalized against a prebuilt map of the scene. On mobile robots and augmented-reality devices, that map must be small and quick to build. Scene coordinate regression (SCR) stores the scene in a compact network that predicts a 3D coordinate for every pixel, and mixture-of-experts (MoE) variants extend its capacity to larger outdoor scenes. In existing MoE-based SCR, however, the router assigns each pixel to an expert from the same local descriptor that the experts regress from, so repeated facades and windows at different locations receive similar routing inputs. We present DAC-MACE, which conditions soft expert routing on recalibrated and contextualized features. A residual context adapter (RCA) reweights the channels and locations of frozen encoder features, a global context encoder (GCE) mixes them with multi-scale self-attention, and an image-level pooled descriptor is added to the router input. A dual-threshold RANSAC--Levenberg--Marquardt estimator recovers the pose. On Cambridge Landmarks, DAC-MACE attains a mean per-scene median translation error of 13.0 cm over three seeds, the lowest among the RGB-only SCR methods compared (GLACE 13.6 cm, MACE 14.4 cm), and reduces the error on the largest scene from 24 to 19 cm relative to MACE. In a cumulative study, the MoE head, GCE, RCA, and the dual-threshold estimator lower the mean error from 17.0 cm to 14.4, 14.0, 13.6, and 13.0 cm. On 7-Scenes, adding GCE to a single ACE head raises Recall@(5 cm, 5$^\circ$) from 86.56% to 87.60%.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Represented but Not Used: Value-Policy Dissociation in LLM Agents
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Yuzhang Luo, Mohamed Aghzal, Liangming Pan, Ziyu Yao
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The study reveals that large language model agents can represent prospective action values but often fail to utilize them effectively in decision-making, highlighting a value-policy dissociation.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents need to choose actions whose consequences unfold over multiple future steps, yet poor decisions do not reveal whether the model failed to represent those consequences or failed to use them. Mechanistic interpretability has studied internal representations of environment state and plans, but sequential decision making also requires evaluating how candidate actions change future outcomes. Reinforcement learning formalizes this as action value. We study this computation in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, and GPT-OSS-20B across a partially observed Grid environment and WebShop, a simulated web shopping environment. We find that the relative values of candidate actions are linearly decodable from intermediate hidden states, including at states where the policy prefers a worse action. We call this gap between value representation and policy choice value-policy dissociation. To investigate how represented value relates to action selection, we compare direct interventions along the value readout direction with Natural Value Transport (NVT), a transformation learned from hidden state changes that naturally result from differences in action value. While readout-direction interventions have limited and inconsistent effects, NVT more consistently influences action preferences, particularly at later layers. We also test a closed-loop controller that uses the value readout as a sensor and NVT as an actuator, observing improvements in task outcomes. These results suggest that LLM agents can represent useful prospective value without reliably translating it into policy choice.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Precise: SDE-Consistent Stochastic Sampling for RL Post-Training of Flow-Matching Models
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Jade Zou, Tao Huang, Weijie Kong, Junzhe Li, Yue Wu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper presents Precise, a novel stochastic sampler for reinforcement learning in flow-matching models that enhances reward optimization stability and efficiency through SDE-consistent design.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become an effective way to improve prompt alignment and perceptual quality in diffusion and flow-matching generators. A critical step for applying online RL to flow matching is turning the deterministic sampling trajectory into a stochastic policy, typically by replacing the reverse-time Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE) with a Stochastic Differential Equation (SDE). The stochastic sampler, controlling the exploration behavior and denoising dynamics, is thus part of the policy, and its design can significantly affect the reward optimization performance. We break down the sampler design into two interdependent components: choosing the right amount of stochastic exploration, and discretizing the resulting SDE faithfully at the small step counts used in RL. To address the first component, we analyze the inherent tension between exploration and stability in denoising and derive an SDE schedule that balances the two. Turning to the discretization challenge, we use a toy example to show that existing samplers can deviate from the flow-matching process, either by introducing excessive discretization noise or by relying on heuristic rules that do not guarantee convergence to the data distribution. To address these issues, we propose Precise, a new stochastic sampler that balances effective exploration with stability. Crucially, Precise keeps the denoising trajectory SDE-consistent through a novel approximation that freezes the clean-latent posterior mean, resolving the excess noise issue in standard samplers. Extensive experiments demonstrate that this formulation leads to significantly faster and more stable reward optimization via reinforcement learning, achieving state-of-the-art alignment scores (e.g., PickScore, HPSv2.1) while requiring 13.1-53.2% less wall-clock training time to match the best in-domain performance of prior samplers.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: MIRAGE: Mobile Agents with Implicit Reasoning and Generative World Models
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Zhichao Yang, Yuanze Hu, Haojie Hao, Longkun Hao, Dongshuo Huang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: MIRAGE introduces a framework for mobile agents that enables efficient internal reasoning and anticipatory modeling through continuous latent representations, significantly reducing token generation and enhancing performance.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Mobile agents are increasingly expected to operate everyday applications from screenshots and language goals, where reliable control requires reasoning over screen affordances, multi-step navigation, and future state changes. However, many agents externalize this computation as long textual chains of thought, which slows interaction, increases supervision cost, and complicates deployment. We introduce MIRAGE, a framework that learns continuous latent reasoning representations from visible textual reasoning traces. MIRAGE transfers explicit reasoning into compact hidden states, enabling the agent to reason internally without decoding long rationales. It also incorporates a generative world-model objective: latent reasoning vectors are aligned with future screenshots, encouraging the agent to anticipate upcoming interface states before acting. This turns hidden computation into both a compressed thought representation and a forward-looking model of environment dynamics. At inference time, MIRAGE reasons in continuous latent space, reducing token generation while improving execution efficiency. On AndroidWorld, MIRAGE matches explicit chain-of-thought supervised fine-tuning in the 4B ablation with a 3-5x lower decoded-token budget and improves a comparable instruction-tuned baseline by 10.2 points; on AndroidControl, it improves action grounding while generating over 75% fewer tokens.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Stabilizing MoE Reinforcement Learning by Aligning Training and Inference Routers
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Wenhan Ma, Hailin Zhang, Liang Zhao, Yifan Song, Yudong Wang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper introduces Rollout Routing Replay (R3) to align routing behaviors in Mixture-of-Experts reinforcement learning, stabilizing training and improving performance by reducing policy divergence.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a crucial approach for enhancing the capabilities of large language models. However, in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, the routing mechanism often introduces instability, even leading to catastrophic RL training collapse. We analyze the training-inference consistency of MoE models and identify a notable discrepancy in routing behaviors between the two phases. Moreover, even under identical conditions, the routing framework can yield divergent expert selections across repeated forward passes. To address this foundational inconsistency, we propose Rollout Routing Replay (R3), a method that records routing distributions from the inference engine and replays them during training. R3 significantly reduces training-inference policy KL divergence and mitigates extreme discrepancies without compromising training speed. Extensive experiments on various settings confirm that R3 succeeds in stabilizing RL training, preventing collapse and outperforming methods such as GSPO and TIS. We believe this work can offer a new solution for stabilizing RL in MoE models.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: TACT: Mitigating Overthinking and Overacting in Coding Agents via Activation Steering
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Yuan Sui, Yulin Chen, Yibo Li, Xue Jiang, Yufei He
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: TACT mitigates agent drift in coding agents by steering activation to reduce overthinking and overacting, improving performance and efficiency in complex software tasks.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: When language model agents tackle complex software engineering tasks, they often degrade over long trajectories, which we define as *agent drift*. We focus on two recurring failure modes *overthinking* and *overacting*, i.e., where the agent repeatedly reasons over information it already has, and where it issues tool calls without integrating recent observations or acquiring new evidence. In this paper, we introduce TACT (Think-Act Calibration via activation Steering), to detect and mitigate agent drift in the residual stream before it surfaces as a behavioral failure. In specific, we label trajectory steps as overthinking, overacting, or calibrated, and find that their hidden states can separate linearly along two *drift axes*, pointing from calibrated behavior toward each failure mode (AUC $\approx$ 0.9). To mitigate agent drift, we project each step's activation onto these axes at test time and pull drifted ones back toward the calibrated region. Experiments show that TACT outperforms unsteered baselines across SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.0, and CLAW-Eval, lifting average resolve rate by $+5.8$ pp on Qwen3.5-27B and $+4.8$ pp on Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it while cutting steps-to-resolve by up to $26\%$. These gains frame agent drift as a steerable direction in the residual stream, and position TACT as a viable handle for reliable long-horizon agents.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Decoupling Ego-Motion from Target Dynamics via Dual-Interval Motion Cues for UAV Detection
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Liuyang Wang, Feitian Zhang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper presents a vision-only framework that improves UAV object detection by decoupling ego-motion from target dynamics using dual-interval motion cues and global motion compensation.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Object detection from Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) is challenged by severe ego-motion, camera jitter, and large scale variations. While modern detectors perform well on static images, their direct application to UAV video often fails, particularly for small objects in dynamic scenes. Existing motion-based methods often rely on computationally expensive optical flow. We propose a vision-only motion-guided detection framework that decouples target motion from camera-induced disturbances. Homography-based Global Motion Compensation (GMC) first aligns adjacent frames. We then introduce a Dual-Interval Motion Extraction strategy that captures both short-term and long-term motion cues. To integrate these cues, a lightweight Dual-Interval Motion Injection (DIMI) module enhances feature representations within a Feature Pyramid Network. Experiments on the VisDrone-VID dataset demonstrate consistent improvements over the YOLOv8n baseline under severe ego-motion. Ablation studies further confirm the effectiveness of the dual-interval design and DIMI.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Reliability-Adaptive Multimodal Relative Pose Tracking for Underwater Leader-Follower Robots
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Mingyang Yang, Zeyu Sha, Xiaorui Wang, Jun Wang, David Chen Wang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: This paper presents a reliability-adaptive multimodal framework for underwater pose tracking, achieving efficient, accurate relative-pose estimation under challenging conditions with significant computational constraints.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Underwater leader-follower formation control requires continuous relative-pose estimation despite degraded sensing conditions and limited onboard computation. This paper presents a reliability-adaptive multimodal perception framework for six-degree-of-freedom relative-pose tracking between two moving underwater robots. The framework integrates complementary visual, acoustic-ranging, and hydrodynamic measurements while accounting for their distinct physical characteristics and time-varying reliability. It adaptively weights modality contributions and models temporal dependencies with linear computational complexity, enabling efficient pose estimation on embedded hardware. Extensive experiments were conducted using a custom-built AUV platform, with 648 pool trials spanning two leader vehicle types, three illumination conditions, and nine trajectory patterns. Evaluation yields an average translational error of 3.8 cm and an average orientation error of 2.4°. On an onboard NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, the fusion network achieves an inference latency of 17.62 ms, providing a 2.69-fold speedup over the evaluated Transformer-based fusion baseline. Closed-loop experiments further demonstrate stable formation maintenance with a moving leader under onboard computational constraints. A multimodal dataset containing measurements from all 648 trials will be made publicly available.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: 3R-Adapter: Retrieval, Rewiring, and Refinement for Efficient Adaptation of 3D Reconstruction Model
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Zixiang Ai, Zhenyu Cui, Xu Zou, Jiahuan Zhou
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The 3R-Adapter enhances 3D reconstruction models' adaptation to challenging scenarios through a novel approach combining retrieval, rewiring, and refinement of relational structures.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models have demonstrated strong generalization under large-scale pre-training, yet they struggle in long-tail scenarios such as low-light reconstruction, joint human-scene reconstruction, and test-time adaptation. We observe relational attention structure collapse, manifested as the failure of cross-view correspondences, as a primary cause of these limitations. While adaptation offers a practical way to bridge this gap, existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) approaches mainly perform channel-wise feature adjustment and lack mechanisms to explicitly adapt relational structures, leaving correspondence failures unresolved. In this work, we formulate adaptation of 3D reconstruction models as a problem of correspondence recovery under domain shift and propose 3R-Adapter, a PEFT paradigm for long-tail 3D reconstruction scenarios. Our method consists of three components: Deformable Retrieval for task-adaptive relation candidate retrieval, Relational Rewiring for reconstructing cross-view relational structures, and Consistency Refinement for injecting the rewired relations into stable predictions. Extensive experiments on low-light reconstruction, joint human-scene reconstruction, and test-time adaptation demonstrate that our approach significantly improves robustness over existing PEFT methods while maintaining efficient lightweight adaptation. Our code is released at https://github.com/PKU-OV3-LAB/3R-Adapter.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Learning Contextual Motion Constraints for Object Rearrangement Exploration
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Lexing Zhang, Zeyu Zhang, Gang Zeng, Hangxin Liu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: MoCo-Net, a two-stream neural network, predicts articulated motion ranges and obstacle heatmaps, enhancing object rearrangement exploration by integrating internal and external constraints.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: The motion of an articulated part in cluttered surroundings is constrained not only by an object's intrinsic joint limits but also by extrinsic obstacles. However, existing approaches primarily consider object articulation properties alone. Here we present Motion Constraint Prediction Network (MoCo-Net), a two-stream neural network that jointly predicts the continuous motion ranges of articulated parts and obstacle heatmaps highlighting potential collision regions from partial-view point cloud observation. By capturing both internal and external motion constraints, MoCo-Net produces more accurate feasible motion range prediction and obstacles recognition, improves generalization for novel objects in new scenes, and enables robots to construct a scene configuration space for efficient exploration of rearrangement actions. Our experiments show that MoCo-Net's two-stream design enhances each other to deliver more accurate predictions, which subsequently form a compact configuration space for a customized planner to efficiently rearrange the scene.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: From Reflection to Co-Evolution: Self-Evolving Agents with Locally Verified Memory
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Xinxiang Yin, Xinglang Zhang, Haodong Chen, Zhiqing Cui, Weidong Tang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper presents Anchor, a self-evolving agent that optimizes memory retention through source decision testing, enhancing performance in long-horizon tasks while reducing redundancy.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: LLM agents have made impressive progress in coding and mathematical reasoning, motivating growing interest in learning from long-horizon interaction. Memory supports this process, but plausible lessons can be redundant or reinforce inappropriate actions. Can a memory's source decision provide a practical test for whether to retain it? We localize consequential trajectory steps, extract candidate memories, and replay each source decision with and without its candidate under the same context. This reveals two properties: most candidates barely shift the probed distribution, and both successful and failed source actions can be reinforced or suppressed. These observations motivate Anchor, which tests shift magnitude and source-role alignment before retention. Admitted memories guide later trajectories, enabling experience-driven improvement under a frozen policy. On held-out ALFWorld and WebShop tasks, Anchor improves success rate and mean score by up to 19.9% and 17.2%, respectively, relative to the strongest baseline for each backbone. With Qwen3.5-27B, it retains 41% fewer ALFWorld cards than unfiltered retention and outperforms all four WebShop cost-comparison baselines while using fewer tokens.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Frequency-Aware Flow Matching for Continuous and Consistent Robotic Action Generation
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Jianing Guo, Fangzheng Chen, Zihao Mao, Wong Lik Hang Kenny, Zhenhong Wu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: Frequency-Aware Flow Matching (FAFM) enhances robotic action generation by enabling continuous, consistent actions from heterogeneous frequency inputs, improving performance across various benchmarks and real-world applications.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Flow matching has emerged as a standard paradigm for robotic manipulation owing to its strong expressive power for modelling complex, multimodal action distributions, alongside similar approaches like diffusion policy. However, existing methods rely on discretized action chunks, making them brittle to demonstrations collected at heterogeneous control frequencies and prone to temporally inconsistent actions that degrade control stability. In this paper, we propose Frequency-Aware Flow Matching (FAFM), which outputs continuous, temporally consistent actions. To handle heterogeneous frequency input, we transform discrete action sequences into the frequency domain with the discrete cosine transform (DCT), perform flow matching over the resulting coefficients, and reconstruct continuous actions via cosine basis expansion. To generate temporally consistent actions, we regularize the first-order temporal derivative to promote smooth actions. This corresponds to a Sobolev-type constraint that suppresses high-frequency errors and discourages abrupt action changes. Our FAFM is simple, introduces no additional network parameters and applies to standalone flow-matching policies and vision-language action models. Across synthetic toy benchmark, obstacle avoidance, LapGym, and LIBERO, FAFM improves success rates, multimodal expressivity, motion smoothness, convergence speed, robustness to mechanical bias and mixed-frequency input. These gains are consistent when deployed on a real-world Franka robot. Code available at https://github.com/gakakulicc/FAFM.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Leveraging Complementary Event Frame and Voxel Representations for RGB-Guided Multimodal Pre-training
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Wentao Wu, Xiao Wang, Yi Wang, Chenglong Li, Yonghong Tian
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The CM3AE 2.0 framework enhances multimodal learning by integrating RGB and event data through innovative spatiotemporal reconstruction and cross-modal generation strategies, improving performance across various tasks.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: In this paper, we propose CM3AE 2.0, a unified RGB Frame and Event-Voxel/-Frame pre-training framework. By jointly learning multimodal spatiotemporal representations and exploiting latent cross-modal dependencies through cross-modal generation, the framework enhances multimodal information interaction and collaborative modeling capabilities. Specifically, we first propose an Event-aware Spatiotemporal Masked Reconstruction (ESMR) strategy to learn unified multimodal spatiotemporal representations. It leverages event responses to guide masking toward dynamically salient regions. Through spatiotemporal masked reconstruction, it learns spatial structures and their temporal variations from continuous RGB-Event observations. In addition, it incorporates multimodal fusion reconstruction and cross-modal contrastive learning to facilitate the modeling of cross-modal complementary information and the learning of shared representations. Building upon this, we further propose a Hierarchical Cross-modal Generation (HCG) strategy to learn latent cross-modal dependencies through visual and language generation. At the visual level, Event-conditioned RGB generation is performed using a pre-trained diffusion model to capture visual associations between the two modalities. At the language level, video-level text description generation based on joint RGB-Event representations establishes connections between multimodal visual features and linguistic semantics, further enriching the learning of cross-modal dependencies. Extensive experiments on four diverse downstream tasks demonstrate that CM3AE 2.0 consistently improves performance, validating the effectiveness and generalization capability of the proposed pre-training framework.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Designing Reinforcement Learning for Diffusion Models: A Unified Path-Space View
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Yixian Xu, Yuanrui Zhang, Shengjie Luo, Kaiyuan Gao, Liwei Wang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: This paper unifies reinforcement learning approaches for diffusion models by deriving a common path-space principle, enhancing performance through a novel variance-reduced value-gradient estimator.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training provides a direct way to align diffusion models with human preferences and task-specific rewards. However, current RL algorithms for diffusion models remain fragmented: reverse-trajectory methods rely on discretized likelihood ratios, whereas forward-matching methods train on reward-labeled noising versions of the rollout samples. This paper shows that these seemingly different losses arise from a single path-space principle. Starting from the regularized diffusion-RL objective, we use importance sampling between sampling SDEs to obtain an explicit policy-gradient estimator on trajectory space. The estimator contains the stochastic Itô integral underlying Flow-GRPO-type updates; we derive an equivalent variance-reduced value-gradient form that recovers the forward-matching structure of AWM and DiffusionNFT. This identifies the empirical gap between these method families as a variance-reduction effect rather than a difference in RL principle. The derivation yields a unified design space organized by value-gradient estimation, weight functions, and sampling choices. Within this space, we propose a multi-sample KDE value-gradient estimator that reuses rollout groups, together with scale-bounded weight families that retain stable existing recipes while excluding singular ones. Experiments on SD3.5-M and Qwen-Image models validate the variance-reduction explanation and show that the resulting recipe improves over prior diffusion-RL baselines.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: CoDiMAD: Diffusion-Based Privileged Distillation for Communication-Free Multi-Robot Coordination
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Jiyue Tao, Shunheng Xin, Tongsheng Shen, Dexin Zhao, Feitian Zhang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: CoDiMAD introduces a diffusion-based privileged distillation framework for decentralized multi-robot coordination, effectively addressing multi-modal action distributions and outperforming traditional methods.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Decentralized multi-robot coordination under partial observability remains challenging, especially when agents act solely on local sensing without communication. Privileged policy distillation provides a promising approach by transferring knowledge from a globally informed oracle to sensor-constrained students. However, in multi-agent systems, the same local observation may correspond to multiple global configurations requiring qualitatively different cooperative actions, making the conditional action distribution inherently multi-modal. Standard deterministic distillation collapses these modes to their mean, often yielding invalid or hesitant actions. To address this issue, we propose CoDiMAD, a three-stage framework that trains a privileged oracle with MAPPO, constructs an offline dataset of local-observation-oracle-action pairs, and distills the oracle into decentralized students parameterized as conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic models. By approximating the conditional oracle-action distribution through the diffusion reverse process, CoDiMAD samples decisive actions from coherent coordination modes rather than averaging across them. Theoretical analysis characterizes the mode-averaging failure of deterministic distillation and the distributional recovery property of diffusion-based distillation. Experiments on three cooperative tasks show that CoDiMAD consistently outperforms direct local MARL and deterministic distillation baselines. The source code will be made publicly available upon acceptance.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: PVDepth: Panoramic Video Depth Estimation via Geometry-Aware Spatiotemporal Adaptation
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Chuanxin Song, Peixi Peng
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper introduces PVDepth, a framework for panoramic video depth estimation that overcomes data scarcity and ERP challenges using a novel dataset and geometric adaptations.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Panoramic video depth estimation is pivotal for applications such as Virtual Reality and World Models. However, advancements in this field are impeded by two primary obstacles: the scarcity of large-scale training data and the unique spatiotemporal challenges of Equirectangular Projection (ERP), which hinder the direct transfer of perspective models. In this paper, we first present PanoCARLA, a large-scale synthetic RGB-D panoramic video dataset, featuring natural motion trajectories and drone-like roaming perspectives. Building on this foundation, we propose PVDepth, an end-to-end framework adapted from perspective video depth models. To tackle ERP-specific geometric distortions and consequent non-linear temporal dynamics, we introduce two core mechanisms: (1) A Progressive Sphere-aware Noise Initialization strategy that anneals the noise distribution from planar to spherical, guiding the model to adapt to non-uniform information density; and (2) A Cube-rectified Temporal Modeling module that incorporates an auxiliary cubemap temporal branch to rectify non-linear temporal dynamics in the ERP domain. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PVDepth achieves superior performance, generating geometrically accurate and temporally consistent depth sequences. Code and data will be released at https:// github.com/ChuanxinSong/PVDepth.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: AffordJEV: Affordance Grounding by Confirming Candidate Regions
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Jincheng Li, Yutian Zhang, Jianyu Zhang, Xinshun Wang, Mengyuan Liu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: AffordJEV introduces a novel framework for affordance grounding using a System One model that directly evaluates candidate regions, outperforming traditional methods in efficiency and accuracy.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Affordance grounding asks which visible part of an object performs a requested operation, a basic capability for embodied manipulation and human--robot interaction. Most existing methods follow a System Two paradigm: a multimodal language model first writes a chain of thought and then turns its conclusion into a box or points for a segmenter. This incurs considerable inference cost, gives the semantic decision little direct control over the extent of the final region, and makes mistakes hard to correct. Yet locating an affordance is essentially a perceptual judgment that need not be argued out in words. We therefore propose, in which frozen segmenters propose candidate regions and a System One model decides directly which of them perform the operation, generating no text and reading each decision from a single forward pass. Our contributions are twofold. (1) An inference framework that confirms candidate regions level by level, from object to part to sub-part, with evidence passed between the levels in both directions so that the levels correct one another. (2) A System One model trained for this framework: existing System One models are built for general-purpose decisions, judge one candidate per request and are ill-suited to the framework's region questions, so ours learns directly from the requests the framework itself produces and judges all candidates of a level at once. Trained only on InstructPart and evaluated with definition-aligned operation words, outperforms chain-of-thought methods in domain and in zero-shot transfer to UMD and IIT-AFF, is better overall than existing System One models run in the same framework, and needs fewer judge requests. To our knowledge, is the first approach to bring System One models to affordance grounding.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: USB Gym: A Gymnasium Testbed for Closed-Loop Ultrasound View Matching
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Thanapong Intharah, Zhichao Gao, Yiliang Liu, Hao Dong
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: USB Gym is a testbed that evaluates ultrasound guidance methods, revealing that combining existing techniques does not significantly improve probe positioning accuracy.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Background and Objective: Our main goal is ultrasound guidance: moving a probe until its image matches a target view. Published methods for each part of a guide are evaluated in separate simulators. We asked whether these methods, combined into one guide, are good enough. Methods: We built USB Gym, a testbed whose standard engine simulates ultrasound from public patient CT, with a network drawing organ textures from CT labels. Its guide has three replaceable parts (slots), an organ segmenter, a controller and a reward, which received 20 published methods, each run on the same 60 episodes of six held-out patients. In each slot, a published method replaced ours only if detectably better on these patients. The better of this combination and our original guide on 20 new CTs is the benchmark baseline. A pose oracle, reading the exact probe pose available only in simulation, set the reference. The results below are exploratory. Results: On these CTs, the probe started on average 16.0 mm from the target view; the pose oracle brought it to 1.5 mm. Of the results known when the combination was fixed, only an image-similarity reward (SSIM) was slightly but detectably better, so the combination was our guide with that reward. This combination was the benchmark baseline, ending at 13.7 mm (16% of the oracle's progress). Conclusions: Combining untuned published methods with ours did not guide the probe near the target view; the task remains under-explored. The testbed accepts new methods; no guide was tested on hardware.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: EvoDesign: Agentic Editable Diagram Creation via Design Expertise Evolution
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Tianfu Wang, Leilei Ding, Ziyang Tao, Yi Zhan, Zhiyuan Ma
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: EvoDesign introduces an agentic framework for editable diagram creation, enhancing control and usability through a machine-actionable canvas schema and design expertise evolution.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: High-fidelity diagram creation requires coordinated visual-spatial decisions over semantic topology, visual styling, and geometric layout. Existing methods face a representation gap: pixel-based generation offers limited object-level control, while code-based synthesis provides executable structure at the cost of intuitive manipulation. We introduce EvoDesign, an agentic framework for editable diagram creation through an intermediate canvas schema that is both machine-actionable and directly manipulable by users. EvoDesign first constructs a diagram manifest through coordinated structure, style, and layout agents, and then renders the manifest in a diagnostic verification environment. This environment produces objective defect signals and VLM-based critique, enabling localized refinement of the current diagram while also providing evidence for long-term design expertise evolution. The evolution mechanism distills refinement traces into a three-tier design expertise memory, where candidate strategies are linked to the verification evidence that supports them and are promoted into broader guidelines and principles only through repeated cross-context support. We further define CanvasBench, a canvas-recoverable benchmark and evaluation protocol with content, visual, and cognitive dimensions. Experiments across pixel, code-based, agentic, one-shot schema, and canvas-native methods show that EvoDesign provides the strongest overall balance across content fidelity, visual organization, and cognitive usability. Our code is available at https://github.com/GeminiLight/EvoDesign.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: PSGAgent: Enhancing MLLMs' Dynamic Visual Perception for Panoptic Scene Graph Generation via Agentic Reasoning
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Qingyun Liu, Yuankun Liu, Jiaye Feng, Jie Huang, Zonghong Dai
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: PSGAgent enhances Multimodal Large Language Models' dynamic visual perception for Panoptic Scene Graph generation through agentic reasoning and innovative tools, achieving state-of-the-art performance.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Panoptic Scene Graph generation (PSG) requires holistic yet fine-grained reasoning over complex relations among objects. However, current Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) applied to PSG suffer from a perception bottleneck: they function as static observers limited by fixed-resolution views. As a result, models often overlook critical relations involving small or peripheral objects and struggle to differentiate ambiguous predicates in complex scenes. To address these limitations, we propose PSGAgent, an agentic framework that enhances visual perception for PSG through a think-act-observe loop. PSGAgent allows MLLMs to dynamically refine their visual perception using two tools: a Region Zoom-In Tool for local exploration of small or boundary relations and a Visual Highlight Tool for relation-focused segmentation that filters out irrelevant contextual noise. To optimize decision-making, we construct a two-stage training pipeline. First, we create a high-quality, error-aware Multimodal Chain-of-Thought (M-CoT) dataset that provides robust supervision for cold-start learning. Then, we design a novel hierarchical reward mechanism integrated with Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO) to enable strategic and adaptive tool usage. Extensive experiments on the PSG benchmark show that PSGAgent achieves SOTA performance, demonstrating strong capability in both holistic and fine-grained scene understanding.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Learning the Task or Learning the Verifier? Rethinking Criteria Exposure in Embodied Self-Improvement
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Wenbo Huang, Jianxin Bi, Shunyu Yang, Ruiyang Si, Rui Ni
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper critiques Criteria Exposure in self-improving embodied agents, revealing it leads to overfitting rather than genuine task improvement, and advocates for instruction-faithful evaluation metrics.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Self-improving embodied agents are increasingly being developed and compared on robot simulation benchmarks. Several recent works expose the benchmark's success criteria to the learning agent, a practice we call Criteria Exposure (CE). These criteria, originally written to verify policies trained by imitation learning, often demand more than the corresponding language instructions, so a score from such a verifier may not faithfully reflect whether the instructed task was completed, especially for robot-control programs written by an agent. As embodied coding agents report ever higher benchmark scores, a natural question arises: when a coding agent is exposed to the benchmark's criteria, does it generate code that better performs the instructed task, or code that simply overfits to the verification criteria? We conduct controlled experiments with a self-improving agent with and without CE, and find that with CE the agent quickly produces code with a higher success rate under the given criteria, but this advantage disappears when the criteria are changed slightly without departing from the original instructions. More importantly, the skills the agent develops under CE transfer poorly across tasks. We further propose instruction-faithful criteria and show that they better reflect the performance of agent-generated programs.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: ModalSearcher: Weaving Visual Evidence into Autonomous Cross-Modal Deep Search
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Zhihan Yin, Ruyi Li, Chengyu Fang, Yifeng Yao, Nonghai Zhang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: ModalSearcher enhances multimodal large language models by enabling autonomous cross-modal search, integrating visual evidence dynamically, and achieving significant accuracy improvements in knowledge-intensive tasks.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Static and incomplete parametric knowledge limits the performance of multimodal large language models on novel-knowledge and knowledge-intensive tasks, especially those requiring multi-hop evidence acquisition. Existing multimodal agentic search methods often fix visual evidence at the input or a predefined trajectory position, making it difficult for agents to select search modalities as their information needs evolve and to handle complex real-world queries. We define this capability as autonomous cross-modal search: an agent chooses among direct reasoning, text-to-text search, text-to-image search, and reverse-image search, actively introduces visual evidence when appropriate, and switches between and integrates modalities across multiple hops. We propose ModalSearch-Pipeline, a scalable procedure for constructing an interleaved multimodal knowledge graph. It samples paths with diverse depths and modality compositions and uses backward question construction to obscure entity names and image targets that would expose reasoning shortcuts while retaining necessary disambiguating clues, yielding text-only, image-initialized, and arbitrarily interleaved multi-hop problems. We train the ModalSearcher Agent with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning in a live Web environment, and construct ModalSearch-Bench. Experiments show that ModalSearcher-8B improves average accuracy by 16.2 points over Qwen3-VL-8B under the same agentic workflow across five multimodal knowledge-intensive QA benchmarks, with consistent gains on independently constructed active visual-search benchmarks.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Marathoner: Ultra-Long-Horizon Autonomous Intelligence
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Ruiyang Zhang, Jinpeng Ou, Yifan Xie, Jingang Zhou, Lirui Pan
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: Marathoner is an autonomous model designed for ultra-long-horizon task execution, leveraging advanced synthesis, chaining, and reinforcement learning to outperform existing models in complex challenges.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Humans naturally possess the ability to work persistently toward long-term goals. Given a challenging task, humans can continuously work for months or even years to accomplish a specific objective. In this paper, we propose Marathoner, an autonomous agentic model possessing the ability of ultra-long-horizon execution. Specifically, we propose a comprehensive post-training pipeline to instill this critical capability into base model. For Ultra-Long-Horizon Task Synthesis, we leverage major release PRs containing 1000+ lines of new code from diverse GitHub repositories as the primary source for synthesizing challenging task-level data. Additionally, we introduce Multi-Task Chaining, which chains multiple generated tasks into a single more challenging task, enabling the synthesis of tasks with frontier-level difficulty. For rejection sampling finetuning, we combine strong teacher model with diverse harnesses to generate trajectories on our synthesized tasks and conduct supervised finetuning on base model with rejection sampled trajectories. For reinforcement learning, cold-started model performs real-world execution through harnesses in independent sandboxes during rollout process, effectively facilitating the acquisition of genuine ultra-long-horizon execution capability. We further propose a novel reward strategy, Later Stage Bonus Reward, which explicitly encourages model to perform meaningful maneuvers during later stages of execution. Through extensive evaluation on 5 benchmarks containing ultra-long-horizon tasks, Marathoner achieves consistent and substantial performance improvements over base model and even surpasses performance of strong proprietary model. Further analysis shows that Marathoner can consistently work for 10+ hours and conduct 1000+ tool calls on highly challenging tasks.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: SimForcing: Distilling Simulation Motion Priors into Real-Domain Robot World Models
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Xiaodong Wang, Tianle Li, Chuanxin Song, Junliang Xie, Zhanmi Zhong
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: SimForcing is a simulation-guided framework that distills motion knowledge to enhance robot world models, improving real-domain video generation without additional pretraining.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Action-conditioned robot world models must respond precisely to robot trajectories while preserving realistic visual dynamics, yet learning both from heterogeneous robot videos remains challenging. Simulation offers structured motion supervision, but appearance differences hinder direct transfer, and inaccurate simulation predictions can misguide real-video generation. We present SimForcing, a simulation-guided framework that uses simulation both as a source of transferable motion knowledge and as a controllable reference for prediction. First, we transfer motion knowledge from a simulation teacher through latent-motion distillation, aligning temporal changes in latent space to internalize motion priors while mitigating the influence of appearance differences. Second, we introduce multi-block simulation conditioning with condition dropout to exploit predicted simulation trajectories without relying excessively on their accuracy. Our simulation-conditioning classifier-free guidance scheme unifies these two ideas by balancing predictions based on internalized motion knowledge with those additionally guided by simulation latents. The jointly trained student generates both simulation conditions and real-domain videos, requiring no additional world model at inference. On Bridge, SimForcing achieves the best PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and FVD among the compared methods without external embodied pretraining. Evaluation on InternData-A1 further supports its applicability across robot datasets. Moreover, using our trained world model to initialize a vision-language-action model improves LIBERO success, suggesting its utility for downstream policy learning. https://github.com/Wang-Xiaodong1899/SimForcing

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Playing Soccer Like Humans Do: Learning Versatile and Agile Humanoid Soccer via Latent Motion Priors
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Haoyu Shao, Yunshen Wang, Jingze Zhang, Shaohang Zhu, Yong-Lu Li
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper presents "soccerbot," a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that enables humanoid robots to perform versatile, agile soccer skills with human-like motion using latent motion priors.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Humanoid soccer requires a robot to seamlessly combine agile locomotion, ball manipulation, and impact-rich contact dynamics across a continuous, dynamic behavioral spectrum. Yet existing approaches either cover only a limited set of skills, or forego motion priors entirely and produce unnatural behaviors, leaving the combination of a unified skill set and human-like motion quality unaddressed. We present soccerbot, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that resolves both limitations through a structured latent motion prior distilled from large-scale human soccer motion capture data. By constraining policy learning within this dynamically plausible motion manifold, a single skill-conditioned policy naturally learns to perform moving, dribbling, trapping, and kicking in a unified formulation, while inherently producing human-like motion and fluid transitions during commanded skill switching. Augmented by robustness-oriented simulation design, soccerbot transfers zero-shot to the Unitree G1 humanoid robot, demonstrating agile, natural, and robust execution of the full soccer skill repertoire under real-world conditions.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Turns Matter: Advancing Streaming Video RL via Turn-Level Credit
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Shuai Dong, Kanghui Tian, Linghan Chen, Wenqi Shao, Hongrui Wu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: TurnWise introduces a turn-level GRPO framework for streaming video RL, enhancing decision-making by aligning learning with individual interactions and reducing redundant responses.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Streaming video understanding requires models to repeatedly decide whether to respond or continue observing. Recently, Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) has been applied to this setting, with existing approaches emphasizing reward design while retaining a single trajectory-level advantage across turns. Such shared credit can reinforce redundant replies after earlier successes and discourage useful follow-ups after earlier failures. We propose TurnWise, a turn-level GRPO framework that aligns learning with individual streaming decisions. TurnWise addresses the mismatch between trajectory-level feedback and turn-level interaction, promoting informative responses and reducing redundancy. Specifically, turn-level credit assignment uses silence-completed prefix scoring to construct group-relative advantages from each decision's remaining return, separating its learning signal from earlier rewards. Turn-mean policy optimization averages token losses within each turn and then across turns, giving response and waiting decisions equal weight regardless of output length. These complementary designs improve streaming policy learning without a learned critic or additional rollouts. Extensive experiments show our method outperforms prior RL approaches for streaming video understanding.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: PyRUA-REAL: Robot Exploration and Adaptive Learning through RSI in the Real World
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Qiang Wang, Jianxin Bi, Shulong Jiang, Ruiyang Si, Wenbo Huang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The PyRUA-REAL framework enables robots to enhance capabilities through embodied recursive self-improvement, achieving high success rates in real-world tasks via persistent memory and skill reuse.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Coding agents powered by models such as GPT-6-Astra connect spatial reasoning with executable robot behavior, raising the question of how such agents can produce lasting improvements in robot capabilities from physical interaction. In this work, we study embodied recursive self-improvement (RSI) through real-world exploration, code refinement, and deployment using PyRUA-REAL, a framework in which coding agents retain interaction experience as persistent memory and reusable executable skills that inform subsequent exploration and improvement. Our empirical study places physical manipulation at the center of the improvement process, examining how agents collaborate, what kinds of execution feedback support effective code refinement, and how task specifications and previously acquired skills influence robustness and task transfer. We further investigate the efficiency and capability of the resulting programs when deployed without involving an online agent for decision-making. Across eight real-world tasks, PyRUA-REAL achieves an average success rate of 91.1%. In complementary evaluation on 42 tasks from the RoboDojo benchmark, it achieves an average success rate of 84.4%.
