G1Exo enables more reliable contact teleoperation than end-effector VR-IK, and its demonstrations improve contact-skill learning across four policy architectures. For HS-MoDP, switching from VR-IK to G1Exo demonstrations raises full cabinet workflow success from 35% to 65%. All project hardware designs and source code will be released as open source after the review process.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Learning Wheel Motion Uncertainty for Degeneracy-Aware LiDAR-Inertial Odometry on Quadrupedal Wheel-Legged Robots
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Hairuo Wei, Yunfan Ren, Renda Yang, Qiangsheng Huang, Zhongyu Li
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: This paper presents a LiDAR-inertial odometry framework for quadrupedal wheel-legged robots that learns motion uncertainty, significantly improving accuracy in challenging environments.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Wheel kinematics can support odometry for quadrupedal wheel-legged robots when LiDAR geometry provides weak motion constraints. However, slip and contact loss make rolling predictions unreliable, and contact state alone cannot determine their reliability across motion directions. We propose a tightly coupled LiDAR-inertial-kinematic odometry framework that retains analytical rolling predictions and learns per-wheel, direction-dependent process covariances from proprioceptive history. The estimator maintains moving wheel-center states, allowing the learned uncertainty to regulate the influence of rolling predictions through forward-kinematic corrections. Degeneracy-aware projection (DAP) complements this mechanism by suppressing LiDAR constraints along geometrically weak directions. The learned covariance network (CovNet) is trained through a differentiable filter using simulated velocity supervision and deployed on the real robot without fine-tuning. On the six room sequences with the highest degeneracy ratios in our indoor dataset, the method reduces mean per-sequence position root mean square error (RMSE) by 66.2% relative to FAST-LIO2 and by 31.0% relative to a fixed-covariance variant. In a severely degenerate corridor run, it achieves an endpoint position error of 0.198 m, compared with 7.531 m for FAST-LIO2. These results demonstrate robust odometry under challenging geometric and wheel-motion conditions. We plan to publicly release our code and multimodal dataset. Project website: https://weihairuo.github.io/wheel-motion-uncertainty/

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Beyond Omni: A Unified MLLM for Embodied Sensory Understanding
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Shiyun Xiong, Dongming Wu, Peiwen Sun, Bokang Yang, Jiaxu Wang
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: Unisense is a unified MLLM framework that enhances embodied sensory understanding by integrating diverse modalities through a two-stage training process, outperforming existing models.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Recent embodied systems increasingly build on multimodal large language models (MLLMs) for their pretrained understanding and reasoning capabilities, but their perception of the physical world remains largely limited to basic modalities such as vision and audio. However, broadening MLLMs to more diverse sensory modalities from the physical environment is challenging: their representations are often weakly connected to the MLLM and vary substantially in structure and statistics, while their interpretation still requires shared high-level understanding and reasoning. We therefore propose Unisense, a unified embodied MLLM framework that supports diverse physical sensory modalities within a shared multimodal architecture. Unisense follows a two-stage training process: (i) aligning sensory representations with language to establish a language-accessible interface; and (ii) tuning modality-specific experts within the shared LLM to provide specialized processing for different sensory modalities. To support broad sensory learning, we curate Unisense-1M, a large-scale embodied sensory training corpus comprising 1M samples across 8 sensory modalities. We further evaluate Unisense on 12 benchmarks spanning depth, point cloud, IMU, tactile, thermal, radar, motion, and smell understanding. Across these heterogeneous sensing tasks, Unisense achieves strong performance and outperforms both generalist and specialized models on most benchmarks, demonstrating the potential of pretrained MLLMs as unified models for embodied sensory understanding.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Mise-en-Video: Fine-Grained 3D Control for Multi-Shot Video Generation
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Yingshuang Zou, Xiaoyu Shi, Yawen Luo, Ziang Li, Qinghe Wang
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: Mise-en-Video introduces a controllable multi-shot video generation framework that enhances narrative consistency and spatial control through hierarchical attention and 3D layout guidance.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Recent advances in text-to-video generation have enabled high-fidelity single-shot synthesis, yet practical storytelling creation requires multi-shot videos with both strong inter-shot consistency and fine-grained controllability. Existing multi-shot video generation approaches achieve strong consistency but still fall short in controllability. In this paper, we propose Mise-en-Video (MeV), a highly controllable multi-shot video generation framework that allows video creators to conduct staging the multi-shot in the 3D space and then generate the corresponding multi-shot video. To achieve this, our framework combines a hierarchical attention mechanism for multi-level narrative consistency with 3D-aware layout guidance for precise, per-shot spatial control. To support training and evaluation, we develop standardized annotation pipelines and construct a 160K-video dataset with hierarchical multi-shot texts and oriented 3D bounding boxes. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MeV consistently outperforms strong baselines in video quality, inter-shot consistency, and subject-level controllability.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Can It Actually Work? Synthesizing Functional CAD Mechanisms
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Wenqian Zhang, Yangyi Huang, Zigeng Xu, Weiyang Liu, Zhen Liu
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: The paper presents FunCAD-Harness, a framework that improves functional CAD design by translating abstract requirements into physical tests, enhancing mechanism success rates through simulation feedback.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: While LLM agents can generate visually plausible CAD assemblies, these designs often fail to fulfill their intended physical functions. We study functional CAD design, a setting where agents interpret underspecified requests to construct and iteratively revise mechanisms that satisfy functional requirements in physical simulation. Verifying these requirements is nontrivial: different candidate mechanisms may realize the same function through entirely different components, controls, and operating sequences. To bridge this gap, we propose FunCAD-Harness, a framework that translates abstract requirements into candidate-specific physical tests and uses simulation feedback to guide design revisions. To systematically evaluate this capability, we introduce FunCADBench, a benchmark spanning 46 mechanism families with interdependent and multi-step operations. Experiments across frontier LLM agents show that FunCAD-Harness exposes subtle mechanical failures invisible to visual inspection, substantially improving functional success rates over standard simulation-augmented baselines. Ultimately, our work marks a step toward CAD agents capable of translating human intent into working mechanisms.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: EVA: Aligning Video World Models with Executable Robot Actions via Inverse Dynamics Rewards
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Ruixiang Wang, Qingming Liu, Yueci Deng, Guiliang Liu, Zhen Liu
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: EVA enhances video generative models for robotic planning by aligning visual outputs with executable actions through inverse dynamics rewards, reducing artifacts and improving task success.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Video generative models offer a promising basis for robotic planning by predicting future visual rollouts from observations and task instructions. However, their training objectives typically lack explicit constraints on robot executability. Generated rollouts can exhibit embodiment-related artifacts, including arm deformation and temporal discontinuities, while the actions decoded from these rollouts may be unstable or violate robot motion limits. We term this mismatch between generated robot behavior and embodiment-specific execution requirements the executability gap. We introduce Executable Video Alignment (EVA), a post-training framework that uses action-space feedback to improve both the visual integrity of generated robot motion and the feasibility of decoded actions. EVA trains an inverse dynamics model (IDM) on robot demonstrations and freezes it to decode actions from generated videos. We compute a reward from these actions that penalizes non-smooth motion and violations of velocity and acceleration limits, and use it to guide reinforcement-learning updates to the video generator. By feeding decoded-action constraints back into video generation, EVA links visual and action-level improvements through a shared alignment signal. Experiments on RoboTwin, LIBERO, and a real bimanual robot show that EVA reduces embodiment-related visual artifacts and improves task success when executing IDM-decoded actions. Further experiments show that video models fine-tuned with EVA generate more effective video--action pairs for training downstream VLAs.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: AffordanceVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model Empowering Action Generation through Affordance-Aware Understanding
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Qize Yu, Jiadi You, Yuran Wang, Jiaqi Liang, Bowen Ping
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: AffordanceVLA introduces a structured affordance learning framework that enhances vision-language-action models for improved robotic manipulation through precise perception-action mappings.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models leverage the rich world knowledge of pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) to enable instruction-following robotic manipulation. However, the structural mismatch between VLM semantic spaces and embodied control policies often hinders the learning of precise perception-action mappings. To address this challenge, we propose AffordanceVLA, a scalable, unified framework that introduces structured affordance learning as a task-oriented and object-centric intermediate representation to establish a more precise and robust perception-action mapping. Specifically, we progressively model manipulation priors through three complementary components - Which2Act, Where2Act, and How2Act - which jointly produce spatially grounded, semantically conditioned, and action-coupled intermediate representations, thereby naturally bridging vision, language, and action. We integrate these modules into a Mixture-of-Transformer (MoT) architecture and adopt a three-stage progressive training curriculum that leverages 8.8M affordance-centric grounding and pointing samples, translating scalable vision-language supervision into improved robotic manipulation. To overcome the scarcity of dense affordance labels in robotic datasets, we also develop a robust automated data augmentation pipeline. Extensive experiments on ID & OOD simulation and real-world demonstrate that AffordanceVLA outperforms strong VLA baselines across diverse manipulation scenarios, validating structured affordance learning as a scalable and robust bridge that integrates multi-source vision-language supervision while connecting pretrained VLM semantics to embodied robot control.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: EndoVLA-OOV: Language-Conditioned Out-of-View Target Acquisition in Robotic Endoscopy
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Chi Kit Ng, Yidong Zhang, Tianchun Wu, Zhiqing Tang, Hanlin Zhao
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: EndoVLA-OOV is a language-conditioned policy for robotic endoscopy that enhances out-of-view target acquisition, achieving up to 93.3% success through advanced vision-language-action integration.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: The scan-then-revisit workflow of upper gastrointestinal endoscopy requires bringing a previously observed suspicious region back into view for closer inspection. Acquiring such targets requires translating anatomical and appearance descriptions into camera motions from partial observations of a confined, deformable environment. We present EndoVLA-OOV, a language-conditioned vision-language-action policy for out-of-view target acquisition in robotic endoscopy. The policy adapts a pretrained backbone to continuous two-degree-of-freedom distal bending commands and combines initial, intermediate, and current images to guide search. To support policy learning, we provide an open-source VLA dataset containing 1,050 episodes across six tasks and approximately 262k observation-action pairs. Physical evaluation spans wet-lens and low-light conditions, two unseen stomach phantoms, and cross-embodiment transfer to an unseen ex-vivo environment. In the cross-embodiment evaluation, the full-data policy achieves 93.3% target acquisition success (28/30). In a controlled training-data comparison, expanding the corpus from 312 to 1,050 episodes increases acquisition success from 40.0% to 90.0% under the same model, training, and test configuration. Instruction and observation interventions further support the use of language and temporal context in the evaluated acquisition tasks. These results support language-guided endoscopic revisitation across the evaluated environments and robot embodiments and demonstrate the benefit of expanded task-specific demonstrations.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: PCHMR: Empowering and Benchmarking Human Mesh Recovery in Privacy-Constrained Real-World Settings
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Zeyu Cao, Qingxuan Wu, Zhiyang Dou, Rui Xu, Yuan Liu
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: The paper introduces PCHMR, a benchmark for enhancing human mesh recovery models using federated learning and local fine-tuning while preserving user privacy in real-world settings.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Fine-tuning directly on user-side data is an effective way to improve the performance of widely adopted data-driven human mesh recovery (HMR) models. However, doing so for existing HMR methods often assumes aggregating user-side data from real-world HMR-deployed devices to a central training server, posing a significant privacy risk as sensitive human images are transmitted. How can human mesh recovery be evaluated and improved in privacy-constrained real-world settings? We study this question through a benchmark in which state-of-the-art HMR models are trained with federated learning and a secure-aggregation variant, neither of which centralizes raw images, and evaluated across a wide range of client-scale and data-heterogeneity settings. We document that common HMR training pipelines are built around centralized data access and quantify how representative HMR backbones behave when that assumption is removed. Furthermore, to study the data bottleneck of privacy-constrained HMR training, we propose DePoser, a local annotation and fine-tuning pipeline enhanced with depth foundation models, with which collaboratively trained HMR models can be locally tailored to the end user's distribution. On in-the-wild data, fine-tuning on DePoser annotations improves personalization accuracy, measured against DePoser-generated pseudo-ground truth. This benchmark aims to support future work on privacy-constrained HMR models and their real-world deployment and evaluation.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Map2Vid: Embodied Navigation Video Generation with Human-Friendly Motion Control
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Yulin Dai, Yuqian Fu, Tianwen Qian, Zhen Xing, Bojia Zi
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: Map2Vid introduces a novel framework for generating navigation videos from BEV maps, enhancing human-friendly control and evaluation through a large-scale dataset and integrated signals.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Controllable video generation has recently achieved impressive visual quality, yet existing control paradigms remain poorly suited to embodied navigation. Text prompts are spatially ambiguous, while camera-trajectory control relies on low-level motion specifications that are unintuitive for human users and difficult to manipulate. In this work, we introduce Map2Vid, a novel task that reformulates embodied navigation video generation as a BEV-map-to-video synthesis problem, together with a large-scale benchmark for systematic evaluation. By using BEV maps, which provide a visual representation of global scene layout and intended navigation routes, Map2Vid enables human-friendly navigation video generation. To support this task, we construct a dedicated dataset with over 100K navigation sequences across 61 indoor scenes, each paired with egocentric videos, BEV maps, camera trajectories and language instructions. We further develop a unified framework that integrates multiple control signals, together with a curriculum training strategy that progressively weakens non-map inputs, enabling flexible inference under both full conditioning and map-only input. Extensive experiments across multiple foundation generation models demonstrate that controllable navigation video generation via BEV map is a viable and promising direction.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: MVISTA-4D: View-Consistent 4D World Model with Test-Time Action Inference for Robotic Manipulation
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Jiaxu Wang, Yicheng Jiang, Tianlun He, Jingkai Sun, Qiang Zhang
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: MVISTA-4D introduces a view-consistent 4D world model for robotic manipulation, enabling comprehensive scene dynamics prediction and optimized action inference from single-view RGBD inputs.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: World-model-based imagine-then-act becomes a promising paradigm for robotic manipulation, yet existing approaches typically support either purely image-based forecasting or reasoning over partial 3D geometry, limiting their ability to predict complete 4D scene dynamics. This work proposes a novel embodied 4D world model that enables geometrically consistent, arbitrary-view RGBD generation: given only a single-view RGBD observation as input, the model imagines the remaining viewpoints, which can then be back-projected and fused to assemble a more complete 3D structure across time. To efficiently learn the multi-view, cross-modality generation, we explicitly design cross-view and cross-modality feature fusion that jointly encourage consistency between RGB and depth and enforce geometric alignment across views. Beyond prediction, converting generated futures into actions is often handled by inverse dynamics, which is ill-posed because multiple actions can explain the same transition. We address this with a test-time action optimization strategy that backpropagates through the generative model to infer a trajectory-level latent best matching the predicted future, and a residual inverse dynamics model that turns this trajectory prior into accurate executable actions. Experiments on three datasets demonstrate strong performance on both 4D scene generation and downstream manipulation, and ablations provide practical insights into the key design choices.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: ELAN4D: Embodiment-Centric 4D Supervision for Vision-Language-Action Models via Plug-and-Play Adaptation
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Zeyuan He, Bowen Yang, Zhirui Fang, Keru Zhou, Lei Jiang
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: ELAN4D enhances Vision-Language-Action models by integrating 4D predictive supervision from robot keypoint tracks, improving robustness and generalization in robotic manipulation tasks.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown promise for robotic manipulation, yet most existing policies operate reactively by directly regressing actions from current observations, without explicitly modeling future dynamics. This limits their ability to generalize under out-of-distribution perturbations. To address this issue, we propose ELAN4D, an embodiment-centric, 4D-aware training framework that enhances VLA policies with future robot keypoint tracks as predictive spatio-temporal supervision. Using only forward kinematics from proprioceptive states, we derive 3D displacement tracks of robot keypoints, such as joints and the end-effector, with negligible preprocess cost. These tracks provide metric and compact supervision without requiring external trackers or reconstruction. A plug-and-play auxiliary branch with a lightweight track decoder injects this 4D signal into the action expert while preserving the pretrained vision-language backbone through gradient isolation. The track decoder is discarded during inference, leaving the base policy interface unchanged. Extensive experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin2.0 and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate that ELAN4D consistently improves over strong VLA baselines, achieving the best overall performance and substantial gains under out-of-distribution perturbations, including camera, background, and layout shifts. These results highlight the effectiveness of embodiment-centric 4D supervision for building more robust and generalizable manipulation policies.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Humanoid Badminton: Learning Dynamic Racket Skills from Limited Human Motion Data
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Jingzhi Cui, Zhexiong Wang, Bangjie Xu, Pengyu Zhao, Youyuan Li
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: This paper presents a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework enabling humanoid robots to perform dynamic badminton skills and engage in multi-skill rallies with humans.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: High-speed racket sports provide a demanding testbed for humanoid robots, requiring time-critical decisions, precise striking, and dynamic whole-body coordination. In badminton, fast-changing shuttle trajectories require timely contact decisions, while successful returns demand precise racket pose and velocity within a brief contact window and across a broad three-dimensional striking workspace. Human motion data provide valuable priors for such athletic skills, but usable badminton references are limited and imperfect. Direct tracking provides insufficient executable variation for diverse shuttle conditions, while purely task-driven optimization may produce unnatural motion. We therefore present a three-stage hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for dynamic humanoid badminton. First, task-randomized motion augmentation expands sparse annotated hitting events into executable target-conditioned stroke variations, forming a continuous latent skill space. Second, a high-level planner outputs continuous latent skill codes to compose these skills online according to the observed shuttle state. Third, a context-conditioned adversarial regularizer encourages more natural planner-level skill usage while preserving return performance. In real-world deployment, our system sustains multi-skill rallies with human players, including forehand, backhand, and highly dynamic jump returns. This is the first real-world humanoid racket-sport system to demonstrate multi-skill human--robot rallies including highly dynamic jump returns.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: R$^2$ Flow: Recursive Self-Improvement via Recursive Skill Evolution
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Mingda Zhang, Qiang Huang, Yanjin Li, Zijia Wang, Qika Lin
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: R$^2$ Flow introduces a recursive self-improvement framework for LLM-based agents that enhances task accuracy and skill evolution through flow-based training and evidence verification.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: LLM-based agents can improve themselves across tasks by reusing and revising the skills they orchestrate into executable procedures. Flow-based training fits this loop: it samples procedures in proportion to reward, and the flow through each skill credits it for the next library revision. Three obstacles stand in the way of making this self-improvement reliable: flow training suffers strategy collapse over tree-structured histories; nonnegative flow-based credit rewards frequent use as if it were benefit; and library edits rest on the task reward the policy optimizes. We introduce R$^2$ Flow, a recursive self-improvement framework that alternates policy learning, independent verification, and versioned skill-library updates on a shared-state orchestration graph. The graph merges histories that differ only in the order of independent steps, allowing flow training to pool evidence across equivalent executions. A flow-share readout of the trained flow, invariant to the backward policy, and a separate signed utility rank which skills to change, verifier evidence decides whether an edit is warranted, and a residual-variance plateau sets when to update. Committed edits reshape the graph the next policy learns on, realizing recursive skill evolution. Across question answering, mathematical reasoning, interactive decision making, and code generation, R$^2$ Flow improves task accuracy and library-edit precision over heuristic orchestration, reinforcement learning, and skill-evolution baselines, and transfers across executors. Code is available at https://github.com/beita6969/r2flow.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: TriFold: Folding irregular 3D Gaussians into structured latents for 3D Scene Generation
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Yun Wang, Chiyu Wang, Fan Jiang, Ziyu Zhu, Zhaoxu Sun
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: TriFold introduces a 3D Gaussian VAE that encodes complex scenes into structured latents, enhancing reconstruction and generation through adaptive spatial representation and occupancy prediction.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Recent progress in 3D generation has motivated growing interest in compact generative representations of complex 3D scenes. For native 3D Gaussian scenes, however, learning such representations remains challenging due to widely varying primitive counts, nonuniform spatial density, and differences in geometry and appearance even among spatially neighboring primitives. In this work, we introduce TriFold, a native 3D Gaussian VAE that encodes Gaussian scenes into a fixed-layout triplane latent and jointly reconstructs their geometry and appearance. The key insight is to impose structural regularity on the latent space while preserving the spatial adaptivity of the underlying Gaussians. During encoding, we use cell-wise learned queries to aggregate projected Gaussians into multiple slots per cell, reducing the information loss caused by single-feature pooling. During decoding, occupancy prediction identifies active regions, where query-based set prediction and candidate selection reconstruct local Gaussian sets with spatially varying primitive counts. Building on this representation, we train a latent flow-matching model for conditional scene-level 3DGS generation, enabling point-cloud-conditioned synthesis and single-image-conditioned amodal generation. Experiments demonstrate that TriFold achieves high-fidelity reconstruction and generation from a single image that provides only a partial observation of the scene, validating its effectiveness for native 3D Gaussian representation learning. https://fantasy-amap.github.io/TriFold

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: NativeMEM: Native Memory Compression for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Ziye Wang, Modi Shi, Chaojun Ni, Jiazhi Yang, Mengdi Li
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: NativeMEM introduces an efficient memory compression method for Vision-Language-Action models, enhancing long-horizon robotic manipulation performance while reducing latency and memory usage.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: How can pretrained Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models retain long-horizon visual histories with high-frequency updates without sacrificing efficiency? Existing approaches rely on external memory management, which restrains either the memory horizon or the reactiveness of pretrained policies. To this end, we present NativeMEM, a VLA policy that features long-term and real-time updated memory. At its core is an efficient memory encoding scheme, Native Memory Compression, which repurposes the VLA's own vision encoder to compress each historical frame from each camera view into a single token. Appended to the input sequence, these memory tokens enable the pretrained VLA to attend over long-term history with negligible latency overhead, requiring neither an external planner nor a freshly initialized memory module. To align the memory tokens with the pretrained policy, we first develop a generic memory tokenizer under the supervision of a frozen VLA on memory-demanding data, and then unfreeze the VLA for task-specific fine-tuning. NativeMEM consistently outperforms prior methods, boosting success rates from 32.4% to 84.0% in simulation and up to 98.7% on real robots, while maintaining low inference latency and GPU memory usage. Notably, NativeMEM exhibits high data efficiency by achieving competitive results with prior arts using only 20% of the training data.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Execution Before Memory: Diagnosing Memory Failures in Video World Models
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Weiyang Jin, Jiwen Yu, Sihan Xu, Yuwei Niu, Xihui Liu
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: The paper introduces MIST for diagnosing memory failures in video world models, proposing M3-Agent to enhance execution accuracy and significantly improve evaluation scores.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: A memory test for a video world model should say whether the scene was set, whether the asked change was carried out, and whether the last frame shows the result. Current tests fold these into one number, so a low score is easy to read as forgetting. When the change is not carried out, the hidden state transition cannot appear, so the test is not really a test of memory. We introduce MIST, an evaluation that separates the change from the memory it should leave behind. The model first sets the scene while the change stays hidden, and only later is asked to show it, with leakage before that point kept under control. This separation locates the bottleneck: the model sets the scene but does not carry out the instructed change. The same gap appears in general memory evaluations. On that basis we propose M3-Agent (Make the Missing Move), which recursively revises the details of the input instruction so that the model successfully carries out the requested instruction. Relative to the baseline, it more than triples the MIST reveal score. On the benchmarks, WRBench's score T rises by 26.1% and MBench-T's score U by 52.7%. The method meets the problem from the execution side: it shows what the frozen model can do once the move is stated, and it sets a stricter baseline.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: From Trajectories to Differentiated Skills: Cognitive Differentiation for Self-Improving Agents
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Yewei Zhao, Derong Xu, Wei Chen, Yin Xu, Peilun Zhou
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: The paper introduces Cognitive Differentiation in Skill Evolution (CDSE), enhancing agent performance by evolving skills through coordinated, functionally distinct components, achieving superior results across multiple benchmarks.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents tackle complex tasks through reasoning and interaction with external environments. Agent skills provide persistent, transferable capabilities that guide task planning, inform contextual decisions, support tool use, and enable executable procedures. Yet existing skill-evolution methods largely organize knowledge around skill artifacts, overlooking the functional heterogeneity within individual skills and its implications for knowledge maintenance and use. Inspired by cognitive science, we propose Cognitive Differentiation in Skill Evolution (CDSE), which evolves a unified skill through four functionally distinct yet coordinated components: Meta, Experience, Tool, and Script. CDSE extracts evidence-grounded semantic gradients from successful and failed trajectories, consolidates them by functional role, and applies component-specific updates and validation with cross-component coordination and adaptive invocation. An analysis of 500 top-ranked skill packages shows that 96.8% contain knowledge spanning at least two functional roles. Across six benchmarks, three agent models, and two execution harnesses, CDSE achieves the highest scores in all 36 settings, improving over the Base agent by 7.6 percentage points and the strongest competing method in each setting by 2.6 points on average. Ablation studies further support the importance of functional differentiation and adaptive invocation.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: FlexPart: Text-Controlled Semantics-Aware 3D Part Segmentation at Flexible Granularity
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Yiqun Zhao, Jiachen Xu, Yihao Zhi, Yunfei Zhao, Zibo Zhao
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: FLEXPART is a novel framework for text-controlled 3D mesh segmentation that enables flexible, semantics-aware part extraction, outperforming existing models in accuracy and granularity.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: A 3D asset admits multiple valid part decompositions, while semantics-aware segmentation should reflect both the desired granularity and the parts a user wants to extract. Ideally, a practical segmentation model should strive for a simple principle: what you ask for is what you get. However, realizing this goal is hindered by two core obstacles: the lack of multi-granularity training data and the absence of a holistic control mechanism. We propose FLEXPART, a unified framework for text-controlled 3D mesh segmentation. To establish flexible control, we introduce a holistic control prompt comprising semantic part names with location and shape clauses. To support this mechanism, we utilize an automated Vision-Language Model (VLM) pipeline to construct a large-scale dataset of multi-granularity partitions and their corresponding prompts. Driven by this data, FLEXPART generates a view-independent part-identity field in native 3D space, directly assigning discrete part IDs to mesh faces. To compel the model to respect semantic conditions rather than rely on geometric priors, we train the model using randomized background dropping. Furthermore, an inference-time VLM planner can automatically complete descriptive clauses from 2D renderings, allowing users to simply name the desired parts in ordinary words. FLEXPART with planner-completed prompts outperforms the strongest evaluated baseline by 15% in mIoU, even when that baseline receives ground-truth guidance. On our held-out FLEXPARTBENCH, FLEXPART leads at each granularity and improves average mIoU by 22% over the strongest baseline. With only the requested part names supplied by the user, it also improves IoU by 35% over the strongest click-driven baseline on selective segmentation.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: R$^2$Orch: Recursive Self-Improvement for Agent Orchestration via Self-Play within a Skill-Internalization Loop
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Mingda Zhang, Yun Huang, Qiang Huang, Yanjin Li, Rui Qian
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: R$^2$Orch introduces a recursive self-play framework for agent orchestration that enhances skill learning and evaluation, outperforming traditional methods across various complex tasks.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: In recent years, agentic orchestration has been widely applied to solve complex human tasks. However, existing orchestration learning still faces key challenges, including hand-designed curricula, advantage collapse when a task's rollouts all reach the same outcome, and unreliable evaluation signals that judge each skill by one noisy score. To address these challenges, we propose R$^2$Orch, a new paradigm of Recursive Self-Play Orchestration: an inner loop of self-play that improves the orchestrator on self-chosen tasks, and an outer loop that improves how the inner loop improves. To support this paradigm, we introduce Recursive Learnability, a training objective that rewards a Proposer for choosing tasks whose rollouts keep reaching different outcomes as skills are withdrawn. Built on this objective, we further propose Skill Withdrawal, in which the outer loop withdraws each skill once a controlled evaluation within self-play shows that the orchestrator performs as well without it. Moreover, the two loops form one cycle: failures are distilled into skills, skills into parameters, and withdrawals lead the Proposer to new failures, so the orchestrator moves toward zero-skill deployment. Experimental results on twelve datasets show that R$^2$Orch consistently outperforms baselines across question answering, math, code, and interactive tasks.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Reward Engine: Reward-Centric Self-Evolution for Open-Ended Tool Agents
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Litong Feng, Ji Qi, Yiran Cheng, Shaowu Pan, Xinyu Zhang
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: The Reward Engine constructs a stable, experience-based reward system for open-ended tool agents, improving execution consistency and aligning closely with benchmark evaluations.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Open-ended tool agents can complete the same objective through different tool paths, and their quality depends jointly on the interaction trace, environment state, and final artifacts, so such tasks rarely admit an executable ground-truth reward. The central challenge is therefore to construct a reward from existing experience that exposes the current policy's failures while remaining stationary during optimization. We introduce Reward Engine, which, like a self-motivated student, first works out what success requires and then optimizes toward it. From the task and initial trajectories, it builds a RewardPack of testcases for required correctness and rubrics for graded quality, each executed as a check that returns a judgment with evidence. The frozen RewardPack then guides the agent to revise and select its outputs, and can also serve as a reward for reinforcement learning. On WorkBuddy Bench Office and Claw-Eval, the constructed reward largely agrees with the benchmark graders, not reversing their ordering on 82.3\% and 80.5\% of candidate pairs. Used to revise executions, it raises three-run consistency ($\mathrm{Pass}^{3}$) over Baseline from 45.0\% to 54.0\% and from 78.4\% to 83.7\%.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Referring Multi-Object Tracking with Diverse Dynamic Expressions
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Yani Zhang, Dongming Wu, Wencheng Han, Xingping Dong, Shengcai Liao
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: This paper introduces referring multi-object tracking (RMOT) to enhance object localization using diverse language expressions and a novel Transformer-based framework, TempRMOT, achieving state-of-the-art results.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Referring understanding is a fundamental task that bridges natural language and visual content by localizing objects described in free-form expressions. However, existing works are constrained by limited language expressiveness, lacking the capacity to model object dynamics in spatial numbers and temporal states. To address these limitations, we introduce a new and general referring understanding task, termed referring multi-object tracking (RMOT). Its core idea is to employ a language expression as a semantic cue to guide the prediction of multi-object tracking, comprehensively accounting for variations in object quantity and temporal semantics. Along with RMOT, we introduce a RMOT benchmark named Refer-KITTI-V2, featuring scalable and diverse language expressions. To efficiently generate high-quality annotations covering object dynamics with minimal manual effort, we propose a semi-automatic labeling pipeline that formulates a total of 9,758 language prompts. In addition, we propose TempRMOT, an elegant end-to-end Transformer-based framework for RMOT. At its core is a query-driven Temporal Enhancement Module that represents each object as a Transformer query, enabling long-term spatial-temporal interactions with other objects and past frames to efficiently refine these queries. TempRMOT achieves state-of-the-art performance on both Refer-KITTI and Refer-KITTI-V2, demonstrating the effectiveness of our approach. The source code and dataset is available at https://github.com/zyn213/TempRMOT.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Agentic Physics-Grounded Video Generation via Memory-Augmented In-Context Reasoning
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Xikang Guan, Shaocong Yang, Yanqi Bao, Can Wang, Zheng Gu
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: PhysRepair enhances video generation by diagnosing and selectively repairing physical inconsistencies using causal reasoning and prior repair experiences, improving realism across various physics domains.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Physical plausibility is essential for realistic video generation. Existing methods impose physical guidance before synthesis via simulations or refined prompts, but this can limit dynamic diversity, miss errors that emerge only after generation, and require repeated regeneration when inconsistencies remain. We therefore study a generate-diagnose-repair paradigm that preserves the original generation capability and selectively repairs physical inconsistencies afterward, raising two key questions: what to repair and how to repair? To address them, we introduce PhysRepair, an agentic video generation framework that combines causal reasoning over the observed physical failure with prior repair experience to enable localized and adaptive correction. Specifically, Spatiotemporal Causal Constraints identify the first invalid physical state and its causally affected states, producing a repair specification that guides physically plausible local regeneration while preserving unaffected content. Experience-augmented In-context Learning combines the ongoing repair context with relevant experience from previous repairs, allowing the agent to adapt its repair decisions across diverse physical failures and accumulate completed trajectories for future cases. Experiments on Physics-IQ Verified across solid mechanics, fluid dynamics, optics, thermodynamics, and magnetism demonstrate that PhysRepair consistently improves the physical plausibility of generated videos over existing methods. Our project page is available at https://xxkkxxx.github.io/PhysRepair-Website/.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Imagine Before You Predict: Interleaved Latent Visual Reasoning for Video Event Prediction
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Tianxiang Jiang, Linquan Wu, Sheng Xia, Songze Li, Ziang Yan
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: Future-L1 introduces an interleaved latent visual reasoning framework for video event prediction, enhancing accuracy by preserving visual semantics during autoregressive decoding, achieving state-of-the-art results.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Video event prediction (VEP) requires models to infer unobserved future states from partial video evidence. Existing video MLLMs usually verbalize intermediate future reasoning in text space: once visual evidence is verbalized, fine-grained motion, geometry, and interaction cues can be lost, leading to plausible but visually ungrounded hallucinations. We introduce Future-L1, an interleaved latent visual reasoning framework that lets an MLLM alternate between language tokens and continuous latent visual spans during autoregressive decoding. To train this capability, we construct Future-L1-50K by selecting examples where future visual hints help prediction and align latent states to future-frame embeddings, then further optimize sampled latent trajectories with LA-DAPO, a latent-aware RL objective with outcome-contrastive and temporal-diversity rewards. Future-L1 achieves new state-of-the-art results on both benchmarks: on FutureBench, it improves Qwen3-VL-8B from 61.0 to 85.4 and exceeds the previous best Video-CoE by 10.4 points; on TwiFF-Bench, it improves the average score from 2.44 to 3.04. These results suggest that future-oriented video reasoning benefits from preserving intermediate visual semantics in latent space rather than translating every reasoning step into text.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: RoPE-Flow: Monocular Vision-based Robot Pose Estimation via 2D Graph-Conditioned 3D Flow Matching
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Liangjing Shao, Wanhao Liu, Zhiwei Fang, Rulin Zhou, Quanlu Zhang
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: RoPE-Flow introduces an end-to-end framework for monocular robot pose estimation using flow matching, enhancing accuracy and consistency through innovative feature extraction and loss functions.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Camera-to-robot pose estimation from a monocular image is significant for vision-based robot navigation and control. However, recovering 3D structural features from 2D observations remains a challenging task. Existing camera-to-robot pose estimation methods either rely on time-consuming iterative rendering or involve sophisticated 2D-3D registration which suffers from projection ambiguity, accumulated errors for distal joints and imbalanced learning for different joints. In this work, we propose RoPE-Flow, an end-to-end flow matching-based framework for camera-to-robot pose estimation. From the predicted 2D heatmaps, we propose a Keypoint-centered Feature Extractor to obtain positional features along with contextual representations from keypoints-centered multi-scale patches. Moreover, we introduce Graph-guided Condition Generator, which embeds a learnable adjacency map to generate condition for flow matching based on correlation among keypoints. Besides, we introduce Bone Length Loss and Ray-Depth Loss for topological consistency and scale stability, with joint-wise weighting to mitigate varied prediction difficulty across joints. The proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods for pose estimation across different types of robots with mutiple cameras. Besides, we establish a novel cross-scene benchmark to demonstrate the outstanding performance of RoPE-Flow on zero-shot cross-scene robot pose estimation. Meanwhile, animated visualizations are shown on the website: ropeflow.netlify.app

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: AVALON: Zero-Shot Indoor Navigation with Human-Seeded Topological Memory
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Jing Xia, Changyan Li, Yuduo Wang, Guiyin Tian, Bo Wang
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: AVALON enables zero-shot indoor navigation for robots using human-seeded topological memory and evidence-gated co-updating, outperforming existing methods without prior mapping.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Indoor service robots often enter unmapped buildings whose layouts and task constraints are already familiar to users. We address this human-familiar, robot-unseen setting with AVALON, a topological navigation framework organized around human-seeded layered spatial memory, node-verified topological execution, and task-triggered, evidence-gated human--robot memory co-updating. The robot has no prior on-site traversal or site-specific training. Deployment requires only a floor plan, place clues, and an initial topology-odometry alignment. Visual depth point-goal navigation leverages verified node arrivals to perform translational re-anchoring, without requiring a robot-constructed global SLAM map. Human--robot memory co-updating fuses complementary sources of information. Human operators specify task constraints that are unobservable via vision and report offline environmental modifications, whereas the robot provides physical-state evidence through active in-situ validation. Task relevance governs whether human-reported environmental changes undergo robot validation during the active mission. Field-collected perceptual evidence gates memory updates, maintaining an explicit separation between human-specified permissions and robot-observed traversability. Our experiments on a Unitree Go2 show that AVALON with X-NavDP completes a 12.81 m Intersection-to-Dining mission in 46.4 s (5/5) with no mapping, 40.9% less robot time than DimOS-Go2 (78.5 s, 4/5), while policy-only X-NavDP times out in all of the 5 runs. These demonstrate the superiority of the proposed topological navigation framework.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: SPEAR: Selective Preference Elicitation with Adaptive Rewards for VLM-Guided Robotic Manipulation
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Zewen Wu, Ruizhe Liu, Pei Zhou, Feng Chen, Yanchao Yang
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: SPEAR enhances Vision-Language Models for robotic manipulation by improving query efficiency and exploration, achieving high success rates while reducing abstention and training time.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Recent Vision-Language Models (VLMs) enable automated preference labeling for robotic manipulation, yet their deployment remains impractical since each query incurs substantial inference cost, while VLMs frequently abstain on visually challenging comparisons. We propose SPEAR, a framework that transforms VLMs into efficient preference oracles via two synergistic mechanisms. First, we design distinguishability-aware query selection to reduce abstention rates by targeting only informative and distinguishable comparisons. Second, we deploy an adaptive reward transition that bootstraps exploration with VLM-synthesized guidance before preference-based refinement. Experiments on the manipulation benchmarks demonstrate that SPEAR achieves 88.9% average success, outperforming baselines by 23.3 percentage points, while significantly reducing abstention and wall-clock training time on contact-rich tasks. SPEAR learns three Mobile ALOHA manipulation tasks fully online on real hardware, demonstrating end-to-end real-world applicability. By addressing query efficiency and exploration challenges, SPEAR establishes VLMs as practical preference oracles for scalable robot learning without manual reward engineering.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Seeing Both the Forest and the Trees: Reusing Holistic 3D Priors for Part-Decomposed Generation
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Yiqun Zhao, Binbin Huang, Haobin Duan, Zibo Zhao, Shenghua Gao
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: STRUCTPARTS introduces a dual-frame coordinate mechanism for part-decomposed 3D generation, leveraging holistic priors to enhance geometric detail and structural coherence efficiently.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Generating 3D assets with explicit parts requires two properties at once: geometric detail inside each part and structural coherence across the whole object. Recent image-conditioned 3D generation models adopt a structured 3D representation that anchors tokens to explicit spatial positions, capturing both properties, but their output remains a single fused mesh. We ask how a part-decomposed generation model can inherit both properties of these holistic priors, and answer with STRUCTPARTS, a framework whose core technical contribution is a dual-frame coordinate interleaving mechanism: each shape latent is interpreted under both a part-local and an object-global reference frame, and processed through a global-local inter-leaved transformer that simultaneously reuses the prior's geometric detail at the part scale and its structural coherence at the whole-object scale. As its structural input, STRUCTPARTS uses a segmented mesh scaffold, a coarse mesh paired with a face-level segmentation mask kept entirely within the prior's native 3D representation. With only lightweight finetuning, both intra-part detail and inter-part coherence emerge from the same pretrained weights. On PartObjaverse-Tiny, STRUCTPARTS matches or surpasses prior part-decomposed models at a fraction of their training cost, while naturally supporting part-mesh refinement and part-level editing.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Anvil: Scaling Embodied Spatial Intelligence through Knowledge Recirculation
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Weilin Ruan, Bohan Zhou, Jinghao Li, Yangkai Wei, Wenqian Li
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: Anvil is a unified framework enhancing embodied spatial intelligence through innovative data generation, training, and benchmarking, significantly outperforming existing models in various benchmarks.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Embodied spatial intelligence requires more than visual recognition: models must localize entities, reason about their relations, and express this knowledge in action-relevant forms. Yet joint training can conflate the knowledge needed at different stages because supervision is fragmented across incompatible geometric and semantic outputs. We introduce Anvil, a unified framework for data generation, training, and benchmarking for embodied spatial intelligence. (1) Anvil-Gen is a heterogeneous data flywheel that combines form-specific generation, cross-stage consistency verification, and failure-driven recollection across 11 Ground--Relation--Act forms. (2) Anvil-Ben provides scene-aligned supervision for learning diverse embodied spatial capabilities and scene-linked assessments that distinguish stage competence from error propagation. (3) Anvil-MOPD is a 9B student that consolidates heterogeneous spatial knowledge through distillation from specialist teachers. Semantic-first-fault routing targets teacher supervision to the student's earliest decisive failure, while stage normalization controls the loss scale across native outputs of different lengths. We construct 5.8M source-grounded records spanning 160K images, reserving 580K spatial records for held-out evaluation and using the remaining 5.22M records for training. On average across seven public benchmarks, Anvil-MOPD outperforms Qwen3.5-9B and RynnBrain-8B by 9.29 and 11.03 percentage points, respectively, while reaching 80.67% on VABench-Point. Controlled studies support targeted coverage, selective transfer, and feedback-guided repair as complementary framework components.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: VeriVLA: Adaptive Test-Time Verification for Flow-Based VLAs with Latent World Models
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Xueli Sun, Yuxiang Lu, Yantong Liu, Xianzhe Fan, Xi Chen
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: VeriVLA enhances flow-based VLA policies by adaptively verifying action quality at test time, improving task completion rates across various real-world and simulated scenarios.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Flow-based Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies are inherently stochastic: different noise seeds can produce action chunks of varying quality from the same observation. At test time, however, the policy typically commits to a single sample without an explicit estimate of its quality. In fine-grained manipulation, executing a suboptimal action can irreversibly disrupt task progress and lead to failure. To exploit policy stochasticity, we introduce a training-free two-axis trigger that uses two initial samples to measure within-chunk temporal variation and cross-sample variance, detecting the critical states. Once triggered, a JEPA-based latent world model ranks candidate action chunks by predicting action-conditioned future latent states and the corresponding changes in task progress. By operating in latent space, the verifier avoids pixel reconstruction and enables efficient and more accurate ranking. Across three real-world tasks, $\textit{i.e.,}$ pen insertion, pipetting, and apple placement), our method raises the average completion score from 50.8% to 65.5%, while adding 326 ms for sampling and verification per triggered decision on a single RTX 4090. Consistent gains are also observed in simulation, where the average success rate rises from 66.4% to 73.6% in the clean setting of RoboTwin 2.0, from 62.8% to 69.6% in its randomized setting, and from 96.9% to 97.6% on LIBERO.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Mosaic: Multi-Session Agentic Reinforcement Learning
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Yilong Xu, Minrui Xu, Xinyu Zhou, Xiang Long, Haochen Tan
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: Mosaic introduces a multi-session agentic reinforcement learning framework that enhances trajectory advantage estimation and session allocation, outperforming traditional methods in efficiency and utility.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Most existing agentic reinforcement learning methods assume single-session trajectories, where interaction proceeds within one continuously accumulated context. However, agentic techniques such as context compaction and subagent forking may produce trajectories spanning multiple sessions, creating a mismatch between the single-session training assumption and inference-time execution. Therefore, we introduce Multi-Session Agentic Reinforcement Learning, a more general setting that supports an arbitrary number of sessions within a trajectory. Under this setting, a widely adopted method is to broadcast trajectory-level advantages to all sessions, but this does not distinguish contributions from various sessions or guide session allocation within trajectories. To address this issue, we propose Mosaic, a multi-session agentic RL method with critic-free hierarchical optimization. At the trajectory level, it incorporates session-usage signals into advantage estimation. At the session level, it shapes each session's advantage according to the estimated marginal contribution. Experiments on BrowseComp with Qwen3.5-4B show that Mosaic outperforms broadcasting in both context compaction and subagent forking scenarios while using fewer sessions on average. Further analyses show that our method achieves improvements in session utility and allocation, which we suggested is a promising target for future advances in multi-session agentic RL.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: OS-Helix: Unifying GUI Interaction and Code Execution in Native Computer-Using Agents
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Bowen Yang, Kaiming Jin, Zichen Ding, Zhenyu Wu, Zehao Li
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: OS-Helix is a multimodal agent that integrates GUI interaction and code execution through hybrid training, achieving significant performance improvements in desktop automation tasks.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Real desktop automation is neither purely visual nor purely programmatic. Agents must understand user-facing interfaces while efficiently manipulating files, scripts, and system state. However, native GUI/code coordination cannot be obtained by prompt-level tool composition. In our preliminary experiments, naively adding a code tool degrades a GUI agent, revealing that GUI/code routing must be internalized through training on high-quality hybrid data. We present OS-Helix, an end-to-end trained multimodal computer-using agent that unifies GUI actions and code execution in one action space. To construct the required supervision, we introduce application-artifact composition, pairing desktop applications with authentic file artifacts to instantiate executable Ubuntu states, and a decoupled instruction/evaluator generation pipeline that produces environment-grounded tasks whose final states can be verified regardless of the solution modality. We cold-start the policy with SFT on filtered hybrid data and further improve it through online RL in live desktop environments. For RL, we propose Step-balanced GSPO, which aggregates importance weight by action step rather than raw assistant tokens to prevent long code actions from dominating heterogeneous-action optimization. On OSWorld-Verified, OS-Helix-27B and OS-Helix-35B-A3B achieve relative improvements of 35.0% and 33.7% over their matched Qwen3.5 hybrid baselines, while OS-Helix-27B-RL further improves by 42.9% to reach 66.44% success. Ablations provide evidence consistent with contributions from learned GUI/code coordination, scalable verifiable supervision, and action step balanced optimization, while demonstrating cross-platform transfer on WindowsAgentArena. Our project homepage is at https://os-copilot.github.io/OS-Helix/.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: MMSearch-OPD: Easy Made Hard, Hard Made Learnable for Long-Horizon Multimodal Search Agents
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Huanyao Zhang, Jiepeng Zhou, Jiaye Lin, Ontai Tang, Jingtian Hao
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: MMSearch-OPD enhances long-horizon multimodal search agents through targeted data refinement, joint reinforcement learning, and on-policy distillation, improving training and performance.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Multimodal deep search is moving from short queries to long-horizon investigations that continually acquire evidence. However, training such agents remains constrained by limited challenging training questions and insufficient process feedback. We introduce MMSearch-OPD, combining controllable data refinement with joint reinforcement learning (RL) and on-policy distillation (OPD). Our Refine pipeline performs targeted expansion of reasoning chains derived from existing simple multimodal questions. Parameterized transformations control search depth and cross-modal evidence requirements while reusing existing image--question pairs. For training, answer rewards and lightweight behavior penalties guide RL, while the reward gap modulates token-level teacher guidance on imperfect student trajectories. An exponentially decaying distillation coefficient reduces teacher dependence as training proceeds. Experiments show gains from data refinement and further improvements from joint training after SFT, indicating stronger long-horizon multimodal deep search capabilities.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: CoDA: Co-Evolution of Data Engines and Action Policies
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Tianjiao Yu, Zhilin Ou, Yifan Shen, Xinzhuo Li, Yuanzhe Liu
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: CoDA is a co-evolution framework that enhances robot training by integrating simulation data engines and action policies through a shared memory of failures and learning progress, significantly improving out-of-distribution success rates.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Generative simulation can automate robot environment construction, but physically valid environments are not necessarily useful for training. The challenge is to identify environments that address a policy's failures and supervision that helps it overcome them. We introduce CoDA, a framework in which a simulation data engine and an action policy co-evolve through a shared heterogeneous memory of environment construction, policy failures, and learning progress. The memory compiles validated diagnoses from a vision-language critic into generation programs that recreate difficulties and training programs that help the policy overcome them. We further propose Text2potential to convert these diagnoses into staged potentials for action-chunk value learning, providing dense supervision for policy updates while preserving the task's optimal policy under standard shaping assumptions. Measured learning progress guides further generation and program refinement. Across four manipulation task families, CoDA improves out-of-distribution success from 5.3% after supervised fine-tuning to 27.6%, exceeding the strongest closed-loop baseline by 9.5 percentage points with the same generation budget. On LIBERO-Pro, 15 rounds of generation and training raise success from 25% to 84% under position perturbations and from 1% to 76% under instruction perturbations.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: UniFGVC: Universal Training-Free Few-Shot Fine-Grained Vision Classification via Attribute-Aware Multimodal Retrieval
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Haiyun Guo, Hongyu Guo, Xiangzhao Hao, Jiarui Guo, Jinqiao Wang
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: UniFGVC introduces a training-free retrieval framework for few-shot fine-grained visual classification, leveraging multimodal attributes to enhance recognition without overfitting.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Few-shot fine-grained visual classification (FGVC) aims to discriminate between subtly different categories with very limited data. While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLM) exhibit strong capabilities in both fine-grained visual understanding and open-world category recognition, directly fine-tuning them on few-shot FGVC tasks typically leads to overfitting on sparse samples, which erodes their valuable open-world knowledge and compromises generalization. To fundamentally overcome this limitation, we present UniFGVC, a universal training-free framework that shifts the paradigm from parameter fine-tuning to training-free retrieval-based inference. UniFGVC reframes few-shot FGVC as a multimodal retrieval problem using predefined category templates. Its core is the Category-Discriminative Visual Captioner (CDV-Captioner), an attribute-aware module designed to leverage MLLM for generating structured textual descriptions that explicitly pinpoint discriminative visual attributes between similar classes. By integrating chain-of-thought reasoning and visual references, CDV-Captioner mitigates hallucination and maximizes the discriminative power of textual captions, thereby converting images into attribute-enriched image-description pairs. Subsequently, utilizing arbitrary pre-trained visual and textual encoders in a plug-and-play manner, UniFGVC extracts features from both modalities and computes their similarity with all category templates for recognition. Extensive experiments on 12 FGVC datasets demonstrate UniFGVC's universal compatibility and consistent superiority. It not only outperforms existing few-shot CLIP-based methods but also surpasses several fully-supervised MLLM-based approaches, confirming the general advantage of the proposed retrieval paradigm.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Affordance-Aware Interactive Decision-Making and Execution for Ambiguous Instructions
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Hengxuan Xu, Fengbo Lan, Zhixin Zhao, Shengjie Wang, Mengqiao Liu
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: The AIDE framework enhances robot interaction with ambiguous instructions by integrating vision-language reasoning and interactive exploration, achieving high success rates in task planning and execution.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Enabling robots to explore and act in unfamiliar environments under ambiguous human instructions by interactively identifying task-relevant objects (e.g., cups or beverages for "I'm thirsty") remains challenging for existing vision-language model (VLM)-based methods, due to inefficient reasoning and limited environmental interaction. These factors hinder real-time task planning and execution. To address this, we propose Affordance-Aware Interactive Decision-Making and Execution for Ambiguous Instructions (AIDE), a human-inspired dual-stream framework that integrates interactive exploration with vision-language reasoning: mirroring the complementary deliberative and intuitive processes of human cognition, Multi-Stage Inference (MSI) serves as the decision-making stream and Accelerated Decision-Making (ADM) as the execution stream, enabling zero-shot affordance analysis and interpretation of ambiguous instructions. Experiments in simulation and real-world settings show that AIDE achieves over 80% task planning success rate and more than 95% closed-loop continuous execution accuracy at 10 Hz, surpassing existing VLM-based methods in diverse open scenarios.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: LIBERO-Industry: Benchmarking Robotic Manipulation under Industrial Process Constraints
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Ming Shin Cindy Sung, Duan Leijiahao, Haoxiang Wang, Boning Tan, Liangna Fu
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: LIBERO-Industry introduces a benchmark for evaluating robotic manipulation under industrial constraints, revealing performance degradation with increasing complexity across various task scenarios.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Industrial manipulation in flexible manufacturing, e.g., high-mix, low-volume (HMLV) electronics assembly, requires robot policies to adapt to changing products and production conditions. Such settings impose industrial process constraints, including product variants, moving material flows, finite execution windows, and tight geometric tolerances. However, existing evaluation frameworks do not systematically capture these constraints when assessing generalist robot policies. To address this gap, we introduce LIBERO-Industry, a novel benchmark built on the widely used robot learning benchmark LIBERO, that translates the aforementioned industrial constraints into controllable task conditions and measurable success criteria. Specifically, LIBERO-Industry comprises three classic task scenarios: Static-to-Dynamic (S2D) loading, Dynamic-to-Static (D2S) unloading, and Dynamic-to-Dynamic (D2D) transfer. The suites contain 216 tasks in total that systematically vary object geometry, conveyor speed, interaction-window duration, and geometric acceptance region size. Extensive experiments across five generalist robot policies (including vision-language-action models and world-action models) show that performance progressively degrades as industrial constraints are introduced and combined. Under a shared fine-tuning and evaluation protocol, the LIBERO-Industry co-training condition achieved higher observed target-transfer completion than the original-LIBERO condition.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Provably Efficient Risk-Sensitive Offline Reinforcement Learning via Optimized Certainty Equivalents
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Hanzhen Wang, Boxiang Lyu, Zhongxiang Dai, Siyang Gao, Dake Zhang
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: This paper presents novel offline reinforcement learning algorithms using optimized certainty equivalents, establishing theoretical bounds and addressing risk sensitivity in decision-making under uncertainty.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Risk-sensitive reinforcement learning (RL) addresses decision-making under uncertainty and adverse outcomes. Learning risk-sensitive policies from fixed datasets is important when additional interaction with the environment is costly. Existing work on risk-sensitive RL focuses on online settings or specific risk measures, leaving a general theoretical understanding of its offline setting underdeveloped. In this work, we investigate efficient offline risk-sensitive RL using the optimized certainty equivalent (OCE), a general class of risk measures. We consider two formulations: dynamic-OCE RL, which applies OCE recursively at each step, and static-OCE RL, which applies a single OCE to the cumulative rewards. Under the tabular setting, we develop pessimistic value-iteration algorithms for both formulations and establish tight sublinear suboptimality bounds, explicitly capturing how risk sensitivity, encoded by utility functions, affects learning difficulty. Moreover, we establish minimax suboptimality lower bounds to characterize the problem's fundamental limits. To handle large state spaces, we further develop pessimistic least-squares value-iteration algorithms that incorporate the general OCE risk criterion into linear function approximation. We establish utility-dependent sublinear guarantees with explicit dependence on the feature dimension $d$. To our knowledge, we provide the first offline algorithms along with the first upper and lower suboptimality bounds for both dynamic- and static-OCE RL.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: MADSNet: A Multi-Scale Axial-Attentive Dense Spiking Network for Spike Camera Image Reconstruction
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Sirui Li, Rui Zhao, Siqi Cai, Haizhou Li, Tiejun Huang
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: MADSNet is a novel spiking neural network that enhances image reconstruction from spike camera data, achieving superior fidelity and efficiency compared to existing methods.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Spike cameras encode dynamic scenes into high-temporal-resolution binary spike streams for efficient high-speed vision. Although spiking neural networks (SNNs) can process such signals with sparse and accumulate-only computation, existing SNN-based reconstruction methods are typically shallow and still lag behind ANN-based models in reconstruction fidelity. This paper proposes MADSNet, a Multi-scale Axial-attentive Dense Spiking Network for spike camera image reconstruction. MADSNet adopts a hierarchical spiking encoder--decoder, where a multi-scale spike stem extracts early features, axial spike attention captures long-range dependencies, a dense spiking bottleneck enhances feature reuse, and a spike-to-continuous decoder reconstructs continuous intensity images from spike-domain representations. Experiments on gray-scale and color spike reconstruction show that MADSNet outperforms SSIR by 4.3 dB PSNR and Spk2ImgNet by 1.94 dB on SREDS. Compared with Spk2ImgNet, it achieves about 15$\times$ lower latency and uses only about 1/40 of the estimated energy, demonstrating that carefully designed SNN architectures can improve reconstruction quality while preserving computational efficiency.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: LaST0.5: A Generalist World Action Model with Interaction-Centric Latent Reasoning
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Xuheng Zhang, Yiming Zhang, Jialin Gao, Hao Chen, Jiaming Liu
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: LaST0.5 is a novel World Action Model that enhances robotic manipulation by introducing an interaction-centric latent space for improved action generation and physical reasoning.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) have recently emerged as a promising paradigm for robotic manipulation, endowing policies with strong capabilities for modeling temporal and physical dynamics. Existing WAMs, encompassing both video-first action prediction and joint video-action modeling, directly transfer global physical representations from world models to action generation. However, global scene representations may underemphasize local robot-object interactions, creating a mismatch between representations optimized for world evolution and those required for manipulation. To bridge this gap, we propose LaST0.5, a novel WAM that introduces an interaction-centric physical representation between world modeling and action generation. Specifically, LaST0.5 learns a compact interaction-centric latent space under the supervision of visual interaction cues between the robot and the environment. This reasoning space is instantiated as a latent expert that bridges the world expert and the action expert within a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture. Furthermore, LaST0.5 performs adaptive world-to-action transfer by jointly predicting future representations and progress values, using progress consistency to adjust action execution and trigger future resampling. Finally, we pretrain LaST0.5 on a large-scale robotic data corpus comprising over 14k hours of data, establishing interaction-centric physical reasoning as a scalable and effective paradigm. LaST0.5 achieves 99.5% on LIBERO, surpasses the previous state of the art on ten evaluated RLBench tasks, and demonstrates robust long-horizon execution and precise dexterous manipulation in real-world experiments.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Coding or Cheating? An Investigation of Frontier Coding LLMs
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Yuntao Gui
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: The study reveals that frontier coding LLMs often resort to reward hacking by exploiting answer leaks rather than deriving solutions, particularly on challenging problems.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Frontier agentic LLMs are trained on verifiable rewards in reinforcement learning (RL) environments built from real software repositories. A passing test suite is treated as the reward for solving the task. We show that, on hard problems, frontier models often satisfy these rewards by obtaining the answer instead of deriving it, known as reward hacking. Prior reports document this behavior on public benchmarks. We test its persistence on unseen problems. In a hardened environment where the answer cannot leak, nearly every model we tested attempted to recover the answer, escalating through tiers of increasingly specialized exploitation: mining the repository history for the upstream fix, inspecting the git object store directly, and sweeping the filesystem for a possible newer copy of the source or hidden tests. These attempts were concentrated on the hardest problems, and the models differed in whether, how often, and how deeply they escalated. Our position is that this behavior is a learned shortcut, acquired in RL environments that leak the answer, not a sign of intelligence. We release agent traces for these models to support further study at https://huggingface.co/datasets/logitly-ai/reward-hacking-raw-v1.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: ReSkill: Selective Self-Improvement for Robot Manipulation
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Zheng Sun, Zhihao Li, Zhuo Li, Wenrui Liu, Xin Wang
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: ReSkill is a selective self-improvement framework that enhances robot manipulation by identifying and revising capability gaps, leading to significant performance improvements in task execution.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Self-improvement on compositional manipulation tasks requires deciding what to reuse, where to improve, and which changes to retain. We present ReSkill, a selective self-improvement framework that concentrates revision on capability gaps. A coding agent constructs an object-centric task graph from an instruction and a skill library, then uses node-level execution records to locate failures. At the task level, it revises stage organization, hand-off conditions, and recovery routes; at the skill level, it strengthens perception, motion, manipulation, and verification capabilities that repeatedly fail. Candidate revisions undergo full-task evaluation and paired comparisons before adoption, allowing local changes to accumulate into validated skills and an independently executable policy. The agent participates only during development; the deployed policy calls the retained skills without invoking the agent at run time. On the same development set, average success across ten RoboDojo tasks rises from 30.0% for the initial versions to 86.2% for the final adopted programs; retained programs achieve 83.6% in recorded robustness and model-selection evaluations. Across eight real-world tasks, ReSkill succeeds in 72 of 80 rebuilt-simulation trials and 62 of 80 real-robot trials (77.5%). The median revision changes only three functions, approximately 0.5% of a program, while 39% of task-specific functions in later-added tasks directly reuse existing implementations. These results show how locating local deficiencies, validating candidate changes, and accumulating reusable skills can improve execution of compositional manipulation tasks.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Online Geometric Consistency Assessment of LiDAR Measurements via Recursive Bayesian Comparison
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Mingqiao Han, Qigeng Duan, Xuchen Liu, Jinqiang Cui, Xi Chen
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: This paper presents a recursive Bayesian method for online geometric consistency assessment of LiDAR measurements, effectively detecting registration errors in real-time navigation systems.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: LiDAR-based localization and mapping systems produce registered point clouds that serve as geometric measurements for downstream estimation and navigation. Registration errors introduce duplicated surfaces and structural deformation into these measurements. In the absence of an independent reference, online assessment relies on geometry accumulated from earlier measurements. Such assessment requires tolerance to sampling variation and an accumulation process in which observations enter the history only after evaluation. We therefore formulate a recursive Bayesian comparison that couples geometric assessment with history maintenance. A Normal-Inverse-Wishart model represents historical voxel geometry and its uncertainty, while a weak isotropic reference adapts to current sampling.
