Existing video MLLMs usually verbalize intermediate future reasoning in text space: once visual evidence is verbalized, fine-grained motion, geometry, and interaction cues can be lost, leading to plausible but visually ungrounded hallucinations. We introduce Future-L1, an interleaved latent visual reasoning framework that lets an MLLM alternate between language tokens and continuous latent visual spans during autoregressive decoding. To train this capability, we construct Future-L1-50K by selecting examples where future visual hints help prediction and align latent states to future-frame embeddings, then further optimize sampled latent trajectories with LA-DAPO, a latent-aware RL objective with outcome-contrastive and temporal-diversity rewards. Future-L1 achieves new state-of-the-art results on both benchmarks: on FutureBench, it improves Qwen3-VL-8B from 61.0 to 85.4 and exceeds the previous best Video-CoE by 10.4 points; on TwiFF-Bench, it improves the average score from 2.44 to 3.04. These results suggest that future-oriented video reasoning benefits from preserving intermediate visual semantics in latent space rather than translating every reasoning step into text.

潘佳老师实验室.title: RoPE-Flow: Monocular Vision-based Robot Pose Estimation via 2D Graph-Conditioned 3D Flow Matching
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Liangjing Shao, Wanhao Liu, Zhiwei Fang, Rulin Zhou, Quanlu Zhang
潘佳老师实验室.summary: RoPE-Flow introduces an end-to-end framework for monocular robot pose estimation using flow matching, enhancing accuracy and consistency through innovative feature extraction and loss functions.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Camera-to-robot pose estimation from a monocular image is significant for vision-based robot navigation and control. However, recovering 3D structural features from 2D observations remains a challenging task. Existing camera-to-robot pose estimation methods either rely on time-consuming iterative rendering or involve sophisticated 2D-3D registration which suffers from projection ambiguity, accumulated errors for distal joints and imbalanced learning for different joints. In this work, we propose RoPE-Flow, an end-to-end flow matching-based framework for camera-to-robot pose estimation. From the predicted 2D heatmaps, we propose a Keypoint-centered Feature Extractor to obtain positional features along with contextual representations from keypoints-centered multi-scale patches. Moreover, we introduce Graph-guided Condition Generator, which embeds a learnable adjacency map to generate condition for flow matching based on correlation among keypoints. Besides, we introduce Bone Length Loss and Ray-Depth Loss for topological consistency and scale stability, with joint-wise weighting to mitigate varied prediction difficulty across joints. The proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods for pose estimation across different types of robots with mutiple cameras. Besides, we establish a novel cross-scene benchmark to demonstrate the outstanding performance of RoPE-Flow on zero-shot cross-scene robot pose estimation. Meanwhile, animated visualizations are shown on the website: ropeflow.netlify.app

潘佳老师实验室.title: AVALON: Zero-Shot Indoor Navigation with Human-Seeded Topological Memory
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Jing Xia, Changyan Li, Yuduo Wang, Guiyin Tian, Bo Wang
潘佳老师实验室.summary: AVALON enables zero-shot indoor navigation for robots using human-seeded topological memory and evidence-gated co-updating, outperforming existing methods without prior mapping.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Indoor service robots often enter unmapped buildings whose layouts and task constraints are already familiar to users. We address this human-familiar, robot-unseen setting with AVALON, a topological navigation framework organized around human-seeded layered spatial memory, node-verified topological execution, and task-triggered, evidence-gated human--robot memory co-updating. The robot has no prior on-site traversal or site-specific training. Deployment requires only a floor plan, place clues, and an initial topology-odometry alignment. Visual depth point-goal navigation leverages verified node arrivals to perform translational re-anchoring, without requiring a robot-constructed global SLAM map. Human--robot memory co-updating fuses complementary sources of information. Human operators specify task constraints that are unobservable via vision and report offline environmental modifications, whereas the robot provides physical-state evidence through active in-situ validation. Task relevance governs whether human-reported environmental changes undergo robot validation during the active mission. Field-collected perceptual evidence gates memory updates, maintaining an explicit separation between human-specified permissions and robot-observed traversability. Our experiments on a Unitree Go2 show that AVALON with X-NavDP completes a 12.81 m Intersection-to-Dining mission in 46.4 s (5/5) with no mapping, 40.9% less robot time than DimOS-Go2 (78.5 s, 4/5), while policy-only X-NavDP times out in all of the 5 runs. These demonstrate the superiority of the proposed topological navigation framework.

潘佳老师实验室.title: SPEAR: Selective Preference Elicitation with Adaptive Rewards for VLM-Guided Robotic Manipulation
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Zewen Wu, Ruizhe Liu, Pei Zhou, Feng Chen, Yanchao Yang
潘佳老师实验室.summary: SPEAR enhances Vision-Language Models for robotic manipulation by improving query efficiency and exploration, achieving high success rates while reducing abstention and training time.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Recent Vision-Language Models (VLMs) enable automated preference labeling for robotic manipulation, yet their deployment remains impractical since each query incurs substantial inference cost, while VLMs frequently abstain on visually challenging comparisons. We propose SPEAR, a framework that transforms VLMs into efficient preference oracles via two synergistic mechanisms. First, we design distinguishability-aware query selection to reduce abstention rates by targeting only informative and distinguishable comparisons. Second, we deploy an adaptive reward transition that bootstraps exploration with VLM-synthesized guidance before preference-based refinement. Experiments on the manipulation benchmarks demonstrate that SPEAR achieves 88.9% average success, outperforming baselines by 23.3 percentage points, while significantly reducing abstention and wall-clock training time on contact-rich tasks. SPEAR learns three Mobile ALOHA manipulation tasks fully online on real hardware, demonstrating end-to-end real-world applicability. By addressing query efficiency and exploration challenges, SPEAR establishes VLMs as practical preference oracles for scalable robot learning without manual reward engineering.

潘佳老师实验室.title: Seeing Both the Forest and the Trees: Reusing Holistic 3D Priors for Part-Decomposed Generation
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Yiqun Zhao, Binbin Huang, Haobin Duan, Zibo Zhao, Shenghua Gao
潘佳老师实验室.summary: STRUCTPARTS introduces a dual-frame coordinate mechanism for part-decomposed 3D generation, leveraging holistic priors to enhance geometric detail and structural coherence efficiently.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Generating 3D assets with explicit parts requires two properties at once: geometric detail inside each part and structural coherence across the whole object. Recent image-conditioned 3D generation models adopt a structured 3D representation that anchors tokens to explicit spatial positions, capturing both properties, but their output remains a single fused mesh. We ask how a part-decomposed generation model can inherit both properties of these holistic priors, and answer with STRUCTPARTS, a framework whose core technical contribution is a dual-frame coordinate interleaving mechanism: each shape latent is interpreted under both a part-local and an object-global reference frame, and processed through a global-local inter-leaved transformer that simultaneously reuses the prior's geometric detail at the part scale and its structural coherence at the whole-object scale. As its structural input, STRUCTPARTS uses a segmented mesh scaffold, a coarse mesh paired with a face-level segmentation mask kept entirely within the prior's native 3D representation. With only lightweight finetuning, both intra-part detail and inter-part coherence emerge from the same pretrained weights. On PartObjaverse-Tiny, STRUCTPARTS matches or surpasses prior part-decomposed models at a fraction of their training cost, while naturally supporting part-mesh refinement and part-level editing.

潘佳老师实验室.title: Anvil: Scaling Embodied Spatial Intelligence through Knowledge Recirculation
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Weilin Ruan, Bohan Zhou, Jinghao Li, Yangkai Wei, Wenqian Li
潘佳老师实验室.summary: Anvil is a unified framework enhancing embodied spatial intelligence through innovative data generation, training, and benchmarking, significantly outperforming existing models in various benchmarks.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Embodied spatial intelligence requires more than visual recognition: models must localize entities, reason about their relations, and express this knowledge in action-relevant forms. Yet joint training can conflate the knowledge needed at different stages because supervision is fragmented across incompatible geometric and semantic outputs. We introduce Anvil, a unified framework for data generation, training, and benchmarking for embodied spatial intelligence. (1) Anvil-Gen is a heterogeneous data flywheel that combines form-specific generation, cross-stage consistency verification, and failure-driven recollection across 11 Ground--Relation--Act forms. (2) Anvil-Ben provides scene-aligned supervision for learning diverse embodied spatial capabilities and scene-linked assessments that distinguish stage competence from error propagation. (3) Anvil-MOPD is a 9B student that consolidates heterogeneous spatial knowledge through distillation from specialist teachers. Semantic-first-fault routing targets teacher supervision to the student's earliest decisive failure, while stage normalization controls the loss scale across native outputs of different lengths. We construct 5.8M source-grounded records spanning 160K images, reserving 580K spatial records for held-out evaluation and using the remaining 5.22M records for training. On average across seven public benchmarks, Anvil-MOPD outperforms Qwen3.5-9B and RynnBrain-8B by 9.29 and 11.03 percentage points, respectively, while reaching 80.67% on VABench-Point. Controlled studies support targeted coverage, selective transfer, and feedback-guided repair as complementary framework components.

潘佳老师实验室.title: VeriVLA: Adaptive Test-Time Verification for Flow-Based VLAs with Latent World Models
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Xueli Sun, Yuxiang Lu, Yantong Liu, Xianzhe Fan, Xi Chen
潘佳老师实验室.summary: VeriVLA enhances flow-based VLA policies by adaptively verifying action quality at test time, improving task completion rates across various real-world and simulated scenarios.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Flow-based Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies are inherently stochastic: different noise seeds can produce action chunks of varying quality from the same observation. At test time, however, the policy typically commits to a single sample without an explicit estimate of its quality. In fine-grained manipulation, executing a suboptimal action can irreversibly disrupt task progress and lead to failure. To exploit policy stochasticity, we introduce a training-free two-axis trigger that uses two initial samples to measure within-chunk temporal variation and cross-sample variance, detecting the critical states. Once triggered, a JEPA-based latent world model ranks candidate action chunks by predicting action-conditioned future latent states and the corresponding changes in task progress. By operating in latent space, the verifier avoids pixel reconstruction and enables efficient and more accurate ranking. Across three real-world tasks, $\textit{i.e.,}$ pen insertion, pipetting, and apple placement), our method raises the average completion score from 50.8% to 65.5%, while adding 326 ms for sampling and verification per triggered decision on a single RTX 4090. Consistent gains are also observed in simulation, where the average success rate rises from 66.4% to 73.6% in the clean setting of RoboTwin 2.0, from 62.8% to 69.6% in its randomized setting, and from 96.9% to 97.6% on LIBERO.

潘佳老师实验室.title: Mosaic: Multi-Session Agentic Reinforcement Learning
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Yilong Xu, Minrui Xu, Xinyu Zhou, Xiang Long, Haochen Tan
潘佳老师实验室.summary: Mosaic introduces a multi-session agentic reinforcement learning framework that enhances trajectory advantage estimation and session allocation, outperforming traditional methods in efficiency and utility.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Most existing agentic reinforcement learning methods assume single-session trajectories, where interaction proceeds within one continuously accumulated context. However, agentic techniques such as context compaction and subagent forking may produce trajectories spanning multiple sessions, creating a mismatch between the single-session training assumption and inference-time execution. Therefore, we introduce Multi-Session Agentic Reinforcement Learning, a more general setting that supports an arbitrary number of sessions within a trajectory. Under this setting, a widely adopted method is to broadcast trajectory-level advantages to all sessions, but this does not distinguish contributions from various sessions or guide session allocation within trajectories. To address this issue, we propose Mosaic, a multi-session agentic RL method with critic-free hierarchical optimization. At the trajectory level, it incorporates session-usage signals into advantage estimation. At the session level, it shapes each session's advantage according to the estimated marginal contribution. Experiments on BrowseComp with Qwen3.5-4B show that Mosaic outperforms broadcasting in both context compaction and subagent forking scenarios while using fewer sessions on average. Further analyses show that our method achieves improvements in session utility and allocation, which we suggested is a promising target for future advances in multi-session agentic RL.

潘佳老师实验室.title: OS-Helix: Unifying GUI Interaction and Code Execution in Native Computer-Using Agents
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Bowen Yang, Kaiming Jin, Zichen Ding, Zhenyu Wu, Zehao Li
潘佳老师实验室.summary: OS-Helix is a multimodal agent that integrates GUI interaction and code execution through hybrid training, achieving significant performance improvements in desktop automation tasks.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Real desktop automation is neither purely visual nor purely programmatic. Agents must understand user-facing interfaces while efficiently manipulating files, scripts, and system state. However, native GUI/code coordination cannot be obtained by prompt-level tool composition. In our preliminary experiments, naively adding a code tool degrades a GUI agent, revealing that GUI/code routing must be internalized through training on high-quality hybrid data. We present OS-Helix, an end-to-end trained multimodal computer-using agent that unifies GUI actions and code execution in one action space. To construct the required supervision, we introduce application-artifact composition, pairing desktop applications with authentic file artifacts to instantiate executable Ubuntu states, and a decoupled instruction/evaluator generation pipeline that produces environment-grounded tasks whose final states can be verified regardless of the solution modality. We cold-start the policy with SFT on filtered hybrid data and further improve it through online RL in live desktop environments. For RL, we propose Step-balanced GSPO, which aggregates importance weight by action step rather than raw assistant tokens to prevent long code actions from dominating heterogeneous-action optimization. On OSWorld-Verified, OS-Helix-27B and OS-Helix-35B-A3B achieve relative improvements of 35.0% and 33.7% over their matched Qwen3.5 hybrid baselines, while OS-Helix-27B-RL further improves by 42.9% to reach 66.44% success. Ablations provide evidence consistent with contributions from learned GUI/code coordination, scalable verifiable supervision, and action step balanced optimization, while demonstrating cross-platform transfer on WindowsAgentArena. Our project homepage is at https://os-copilot.github.io/OS-Helix/.

潘佳老师实验室.title: MMSearch-OPD: Easy Made Hard, Hard Made Learnable for Long-Horizon Multimodal Search Agents
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Huanyao Zhang, Jiepeng Zhou, Jiaye Lin, Ontai Tang, Jingtian Hao
潘佳老师实验室.summary: MMSearch-OPD enhances long-horizon multimodal search agents through targeted data refinement, joint reinforcement learning, and on-policy distillation, improving training and performance.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Multimodal deep search is moving from short queries to long-horizon investigations that continually acquire evidence. However, training such agents remains constrained by limited challenging training questions and insufficient process feedback. We introduce MMSearch-OPD, combining controllable data refinement with joint reinforcement learning (RL) and on-policy distillation (OPD). Our Refine pipeline performs targeted expansion of reasoning chains derived from existing simple multimodal questions. Parameterized transformations control search depth and cross-modal evidence requirements while reusing existing image--question pairs. For training, answer rewards and lightweight behavior penalties guide RL, while the reward gap modulates token-level teacher guidance on imperfect student trajectories. An exponentially decaying distillation coefficient reduces teacher dependence as training proceeds. Experiments show gains from data refinement and further improvements from joint training after SFT, indicating stronger long-horizon multimodal deep search capabilities.

潘佳老师实验室.title: CoDA: Co-Evolution of Data Engines and Action Policies
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Tianjiao Yu, Zhilin Ou, Yifan Shen, Xinzhuo Li, Yuanzhe Liu
潘佳老师实验室.summary: CoDA is a co-evolution framework that enhances robot training by integrating simulation data engines and action policies through a shared memory of failures and learning progress, significantly improving out-of-distribution success rates.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Generative simulation can automate robot environment construction, but physically valid environments are not necessarily useful for training. The challenge is to identify environments that address a policy's failures and supervision that helps it overcome them. We introduce CoDA, a framework in which a simulation data engine and an action policy co-evolve through a shared heterogeneous memory of environment construction, policy failures, and learning progress. The memory compiles validated diagnoses from a vision-language critic into generation programs that recreate difficulties and training programs that help the policy overcome them. We further propose Text2potential to convert these diagnoses into staged potentials for action-chunk value learning, providing dense supervision for policy updates while preserving the task's optimal policy under standard shaping assumptions. Measured learning progress guides further generation and program refinement. Across four manipulation task families, CoDA improves out-of-distribution success from 5.3% after supervised fine-tuning to 27.6%, exceeding the strongest closed-loop baseline by 9.5 percentage points with the same generation budget. On LIBERO-Pro, 15 rounds of generation and training raise success from 25% to 84% under position perturbations and from 1% to 76% under instruction perturbations.

潘佳老师实验室.title: UniFGVC: Universal Training-Free Few-Shot Fine-Grained Vision Classification via Attribute-Aware Multimodal Retrieval
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Haiyun Guo, Hongyu Guo, Xiangzhao Hao, Jiarui Guo, Jinqiao Wang
潘佳老师实验室.summary: UniFGVC introduces a training-free retrieval framework for few-shot fine-grained visual classification, leveraging multimodal attributes to enhance recognition without overfitting.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Few-shot fine-grained visual classification (FGVC) aims to discriminate between subtly different categories with very limited data. While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLM) exhibit strong capabilities in both fine-grained visual understanding and open-world category recognition, directly fine-tuning them on few-shot FGVC tasks typically leads to overfitting on sparse samples, which erodes their valuable open-world knowledge and compromises generalization. To fundamentally overcome this limitation, we present UniFGVC, a universal training-free framework that shifts the paradigm from parameter fine-tuning to training-free retrieval-based inference. UniFGVC reframes few-shot FGVC as a multimodal retrieval problem using predefined category templates. Its core is the Category-Discriminative Visual Captioner (CDV-Captioner), an attribute-aware module designed to leverage MLLM for generating structured textual descriptions that explicitly pinpoint discriminative visual attributes between similar classes. By integrating chain-of-thought reasoning and visual references, CDV-Captioner mitigates hallucination and maximizes the discriminative power of textual captions, thereby converting images into attribute-enriched image-description pairs. Subsequently, utilizing arbitrary pre-trained visual and textual encoders in a plug-and-play manner, UniFGVC extracts features from both modalities and computes their similarity with all category templates for recognition. Extensive experiments on 12 FGVC datasets demonstrate UniFGVC's universal compatibility and consistent superiority. It not only outperforms existing few-shot CLIP-based methods but also surpasses several fully-supervised MLLM-based approaches, confirming the general advantage of the proposed retrieval paradigm.

潘佳老师实验室.title: Affordance-Aware Interactive Decision-Making and Execution for Ambiguous Instructions
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Hengxuan Xu, Fengbo Lan, Zhixin Zhao, Shengjie Wang, Mengqiao Liu
潘佳老师实验室.summary: The AIDE framework enhances robot interaction with ambiguous instructions by integrating vision-language reasoning and interactive exploration, achieving high success rates in task planning and execution.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Enabling robots to explore and act in unfamiliar environments under ambiguous human instructions by interactively identifying task-relevant objects (e.g., cups or beverages for "I'm thirsty") remains challenging for existing vision-language model (VLM)-based methods, due to inefficient reasoning and limited environmental interaction. These factors hinder real-time task planning and execution. To address this, we propose Affordance-Aware Interactive Decision-Making and Execution for Ambiguous Instructions (AIDE), a human-inspired dual-stream framework that integrates interactive exploration with vision-language reasoning: mirroring the complementary deliberative and intuitive processes of human cognition, Multi-Stage Inference (MSI) serves as the decision-making stream and Accelerated Decision-Making (ADM) as the execution stream, enabling zero-shot affordance analysis and interpretation of ambiguous instructions. Experiments in simulation and real-world settings show that AIDE achieves over 80% task planning success rate and more than 95% closed-loop continuous execution accuracy at 10 Hz, surpassing existing VLM-based methods in diverse open scenarios.

潘佳老师实验室.title: LIBERO-Industry: Benchmarking Robotic Manipulation under Industrial Process Constraints
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Ming Shin Cindy Sung, Duan Leijiahao, Haoxiang Wang, Boning Tan, Liangna Fu
潘佳老师实验室.summary: LIBERO-Industry introduces a benchmark for evaluating robotic manipulation under industrial constraints, revealing performance degradation with increasing complexity across various task scenarios.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Industrial manipulation in flexible manufacturing, e.g., high-mix, low-volume (HMLV) electronics assembly, requires robot policies to adapt to changing products and production conditions. Such settings impose industrial process constraints, including product variants, moving material flows, finite execution windows, and tight geometric tolerances. However, existing evaluation frameworks do not systematically capture these constraints when assessing generalist robot policies. To address this gap, we introduce LIBERO-Industry, a novel benchmark built on the widely used robot learning benchmark LIBERO, that translates the aforementioned industrial constraints into controllable task conditions and measurable success criteria. Specifically, LIBERO-Industry comprises three classic task scenarios: Static-to-Dynamic (S2D) loading, Dynamic-to-Static (D2S) unloading, and Dynamic-to-Dynamic (D2D) transfer. The suites contain 216 tasks in total that systematically vary object geometry, conveyor speed, interaction-window duration, and geometric acceptance region size. Extensive experiments across five generalist robot policies (including vision-language-action models and world-action models) show that performance progressively degrades as industrial constraints are introduced and combined. Under a shared fine-tuning and evaluation protocol, the LIBERO-Industry co-training condition achieved higher observed target-transfer completion than the original-LIBERO condition.

潘佳老师实验室.title: Provably Efficient Risk-Sensitive Offline Reinforcement Learning via Optimized Certainty Equivalents
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Hanzhen Wang, Boxiang Lyu, Zhongxiang Dai, Siyang Gao, Dake Zhang
潘佳老师实验室.summary: This paper presents novel offline reinforcement learning algorithms using optimized certainty equivalents, establishing theoretical bounds and addressing risk sensitivity in decision-making under uncertainty.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Risk-sensitive reinforcement learning (RL) addresses decision-making under uncertainty and adverse outcomes. Learning risk-sensitive policies from fixed datasets is important when additional interaction with the environment is costly. Existing work on risk-sensitive RL focuses on online settings or specific risk measures, leaving a general theoretical understanding of its offline setting underdeveloped. In this work, we investigate efficient offline risk-sensitive RL using the optimized certainty equivalent (OCE), a general class of risk measures. We consider two formulations: dynamic-OCE RL, which applies OCE recursively at each step, and static-OCE RL, which applies a single OCE to the cumulative rewards. Under the tabular setting, we develop pessimistic value-iteration algorithms for both formulations and establish tight sublinear suboptimality bounds, explicitly capturing how risk sensitivity, encoded by utility functions, affects learning difficulty. Moreover, we establish minimax suboptimality lower bounds to characterize the problem's fundamental limits. To handle large state spaces, we further develop pessimistic least-squares value-iteration algorithms that incorporate the general OCE risk criterion into linear function approximation. We establish utility-dependent sublinear guarantees with explicit dependence on the feature dimension $d$. To our knowledge, we provide the first offline algorithms along with the first upper and lower suboptimality bounds for both dynamic- and static-OCE RL.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: Distill to Think, Foresee to Act: Cognitive-Physical Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Driving
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Yang Wu, Qiang Meng, Zhaojiang Liu, Youquan Liu, Jian Yang
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: The CoPhy framework enhances autonomous driving by integrating cognitive understanding and foresight through a dual-reward reinforcement learning approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance and improved safety.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: Current end-to-end autonomous driving models are fundamentally constrained by the behavioral cloning ceiling of imitation learning. While reinforcement learning offers a path to smarter autonomy, it demands two missing pieces of infrastructure: (1) a cognitive foundation that understands traffic semantics and driving intent, and (2) a foresighted physical environment that can anticipate the consequences of candidate actions. To this end, we propose CoPhy, a CognitivePhysical reinforcement learning framework for autonomous driving. To distill to think, we distill VLM knowledge into the BEV encoder and then discard the VLM entirely, retaining cognitive ability at zero inference cost while releasing the cognitive channel as a pluggable interface for optional human language commands. To foresee to act, we build an auto-regressive BEV world model that explicitly predicts future semantic maps conditioned on candidate actions, serving as an interpretable physical sandbox from which safety metrics are directly derived. Built upon this dual infrastructure, we optimize the driving policy via GRPO with a novel dual-reward mechanism: a physical reward derived from BEV rollouts enforces hard safety constraints, while a cognitive reward from a language-aligned scorer ensures intent compliance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CoPhy not only achieves state-of-the-art results on NAVSIM v1 and v2 benchmarks, but also enables safer driving via cognitively informed scene compliance and flexible intent control through user-defined language instructions. Project page: https://wuyang98.github.io/CoPhy/.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: GTAGym: Real AAA Game Tasks Environment for Evaluation and Reinforcement Learning
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Jiajun Chen, Shicheng Fang, Jiahao Lu, Yuxin Wang, Xipeng Qiu
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: GTAGym introduces a framework for evaluating and training reinforcement learning agents on diverse tasks in GTA V, achieving notable performance improvements across various task categories.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: AAA games offer a rich testbed for evaluating agent perception, reasoning, and control. However, evaluating whether agents can complete tasks in AAA games is challenging and often human-annotated because task outcomes are often difficult to verify automatically, let alone applying it for Reinforcement Learning (RL). We introduce GTAGym, an environment and framework for evaluation and RL on GTA V tasks. Its evaluation benchmark, GTAVBench, derived from GTA V main-story missions, contains 103 online tasks reconstructed across nine task families, alongside 47 image-based shooting and sniping tasks using GTA V imagery. A web server provides access to the online environment and evaluation interface, supporting parallel testing through screenshots and keyboard-mouse actions with automatic engine-state outcome checks. We evaluate six frontier LLMs on GTAVBench with textual task instructions and on its GTAVBench-AGI branch, where instructions appear only in the first screenshot and a harness automatically compresses interaction history. The best configuration achieves 70.9% overall accuracy in GTAVBench-AGI, yet aerial navigation, evasion and interception remain difficult. GTAGym also provides a scalable generator that samples task parameters within user-specified ranges and option sets under fixed templates, creating batches of 3D and image-based shooting environments for RL with automatic reward and termination signals. LoRA RL of Qwen3.8-27B on generated on-foot navigation tasks improves the in-domain performance and transfers to out-of-domain task categories, and native GTA V tasks from 15% to 23%.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: Reward Shaping to Mitigate Reward Hacking in RLHF
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Jiayi Fu, Xuandong Zhao, Chengyuan Yao, Heng Wang, Qi Han
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: The paper presents Preference as Reward (PAR), a novel reward shaping method that mitigates reward hacking in RLHF by stabilizing training and enhancing data efficiency.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) is widely used to align large language models with human preferences, but it remains vulnerable to \emph{reward hacking}, whereby a policy exploits flaws in the reward function at the expense of the intended behavior. Reward shaping can stabilize training and partially mitigate reward hacking, yet its design principles remain underexplored. Our systematic study of common shaping methods suggests that shaped rewards should be bounded and should rise rapidly before gradually saturating. We introduce \emph{Preference as Reward} (PAR), which applies a sigmoid to centered rewards to produce a signal that reflects the reward model's latent preferences. We show that PAR has a variance-reduction property that stabilizes training and substantially widens the window for effective early stopping. Using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and Gemma2-2B, PAR consistently outperforms the other shaping methods evaluated and demonstrates high data efficiency and robustness. Comparisons with unshaped rewards across four base models and four reinforcement learning algorithms show that PAR is effective across models and particularly beneficial for actor--critic methods when value estimates become unstable. The code is available at https://github.com/PorUna-byte/PAR.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: DroneSegEdit: Adapting Pretrained Generative Editors for UAV Segmentation with Language-Grounded Verification
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Dehua Chen, Long Xin, Jiangtao Wei
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: DroneSegEdit enhances UAV segmentation by addressing the Grounding-Rendering Gap through language-grounded verification, achieving state-of-the-art performance on RIS-LAD and competitive results on other datasets.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: Recent work has shown that pretrained image generators can support diverse visual tasks. Yet directly applying them to language-guided unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) segmentation exposes a key limitation: a plausible mask may correspond to the wrong instance among small and repeated objects. We call this mismatch between mask rendering and expression-level target selection the Grounding-Rendering Gap. We present DroneSegEdit, which combines RGB proposal rendering with language-grounded, proposal-constrained verification to select supported foreground while retaining rendered geometry. DroneSegEdit adapts the open-weight LongCat-Image-Edit model using task-specific LoRA and fixed color-to-label decoding. For referring segmentation, a Language-Grounded Spatial Verifier (LGSV) reads hierarchical states from the frozen multimodal large language model backbone to derive expression-conditioned spatial evidence, which is mapped back to the rendered proposal without introducing foreground outside it. On RIS-LAD, DroneSegEdit reaches a new state of the art at 52.78 mIoU, 7.16 points above the previous best. It remains competitive overall on UAVid-RIS and VDD-RIS, with its clearest class-wise gains on compact, application-relevant categories, notably vehicles and humans. A separate verifier-free experiment extends the RGB interface to full-scene parsing: a task-specific adapter jointly renders all classes from one task-level instruction without enumerating class names or palette colors.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: Partition, Refine, and Detect: Preserving Novel Category Capacity in Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Wei Zhang, Zhu Teng, Zhixiang Chi, Junnan Zou, Yi Liu
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: PR-OVD enhances open-vocabulary object detection by partitioning and refining representations to better accommodate novel categories, achieving significant performance improvements over existing methods.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: Open-vocabulary object detection (OVD) expects the model trained on base classes to recognize both base and novel classes at inference. Typical methods rely on CLIP-style vision-language embeddings, yet the learned space is often biased toward base categories, with limited effective capacity preserved for novel concepts. Such a base-dominated representation can compress novel semantics, leading to semantic collapse and mis-calibrated confidence at inference. To address this issue, we present PR-OVD, a partition-and-refine framework that explicitly reserves capacity for novel categories and strengthens category separation, while being seamlessly integrated into different detector architectures. Specifically, PR-OVD first performs coarse partitioning to build global divisions for base, novel, and an explicit background partition in both visual and textual modalities, preventing object-irrelevant embeddings from leaking into category-specific representations. It then applies category-level refinement within each partition to sharpen decision boundaries and alleviate the lack of fine-grained region-level pretraining in CLIP. To further provide reliable visual anchors for novel categories, we design a cognitively inspired Structure Prompt (SP) that encodes both egocentric attributes and allocentric context, facilitating stable partition-and-refine learning. Extensive experiments on two OVD benchmarks show that PR-OVD delivers an average 6.5\% proportional improvement on novel categories over the state-of-the-art methods. Notably, PR-OVD also benefits other open-vocabulary tasks, including segmentation and classification, further confirming its effectiveness and generality.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: RedDiffuser: Auditing Multimodal Safety Failures in Vision-Language Models via Reinforced Diffusion
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Ruofan Wang, Xingjun Ma
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: RedDiffuser introduces a reinforcement-based framework for auditing multimodal safety failures in Vision-Language Models, revealing significant vulnerabilities under harmful contextual exposure.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are increasingly deployed in open-ended environments, where ensuring reliable safety under multimodal inputs is critical. However, existing evaluations remain largely instruction-centric, focusing on explicit malicious queries while overlooking a more realistic and underexplored risk: whether safety alignment remains robust under harmful contextual exposure. This limitation is particularly important for multimodal systems, where visual inputs can substantially steer model behavior and render text-only auditing insufficient. In this work, we study multimodal safety auditing under harmful contextual exposure, asking whether VLMs can maintain safe behavior when partial toxic text is paired with visual context. To enable systematic auditing, we propose RedDiffuser (RedDiff), a reinforcement-based framework that leverages diffusion models to generate semantically coherent visual inputs for black-box safety testing. By combining greedy prompt search with reinforcement optimization, RedDiffuser uncovers high-risk multimodal inputs that expose latent safety failures. Extensive experiments on both open-source and commercial VLMs show that such context-conditioned failures are widespread. On LLaVA, RedDiffuser increases unsafe response rates by up to 10.69% on the original set and 8.91% on a hold-out set, with strong transferability to Gemini and LLaMA-Vision. These vulnerabilities persist even under external safety guardrails, suggesting that current system-level safety mechanisms remain insufficient for realistic multimodal risks. Our findings reveal a critical blind spot in existing safety evaluations and establish context-aware multimodal auditing as an essential paradigm for diagnosing hidden vulnerabilities in modern VLM systems.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: ODEAction: From Predicting Chunks to Evolving Actions
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Qishen Wang, Pengxiang Ding, Shifeng Bao, Mingyang Sun, Hengtao Li
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: ODEAction introduces a continuous action evolution framework using ODEs to enhance vision-language-action models, improving task performance and trajectory quality over traditional chunk-based methods.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models typically generate actions in chunks, dividing continuous robot execution into separately predicted action chunks, which can introduce discontinuities at chunk boundaries. We propose ODEAction, a chunk-free action generation paradigm that replaces action chunk prediction with Continuous Action Evolution. We use an ordinary differential equation (ODE) to describe the continuous evolution of actions, and define the vector field of this ODE as the Action Transition Field to characterize how actions evolve with respect to evolution time. During inference, the model takes the current action as the initial condition and numerically solves the ODE defined by the learned Action Transition Field, thereby recursively generating subsequent actions with explicit dependencies. ODEAction is implemented as a modular action head that can be integrated with different vision-language backbones. Experiments on LIBERO, EBench, RoboTwin, and real-robot tasks show that, compared with action-chunk-based baselines, ODEAction improves both task performance and trajectory quality, with particularly pronounced gains on fine manipulation tasks.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: Adaptive Visual KV Cache Reuse for Efficient Multi-Turn Iterative Multimodal Reasoning
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Mengzhao Wang, Yanli Ji, Wangmeng Zuo, Chongjun Tu
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: The paper presents an adaptive visual KV cache reuse framework that enhances multi-turn visual reasoning efficiency by optimizing visual encoding and interaction without additional training.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: Multi-turn visual reasoning acquires evidence through repeated cropping and local inspection, but overlapping observations lead to redundant visual encoding and prefill. We propose an adaptive visual KV cache reuse framework that reduces repeated processing while retaining access to additional image detail. The central difficulty is that skipping visual prefill also removes the interaction between a new observation and the current reasoning: historical keys remain bound to old positions, while historical values have not incorporated the intent formed between crops. Our framework first selects full re-encoding or regional reuse according to crop size and cache availability. On the reuse path, Positional Key Rebinding (PKR) corrects attention matching at the new positions, and Intent-guided Value Enhancement (IVE) uses pre-crop reasoning attention to strengthen content relevant to the current objective. Source states from fully re-encoded crops are retained for subsequent retrieval and reuse. The framework requires no additional training on reuse hits, it bypasses the visual encoder and prefill for the selected visual tokens, then resumes normal text reasoning. Experiments show that our method reduces inference time while preserving the overall accuracy of multi-turn visual reasoning that relies on intermediate crop images.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: LAFP: Preserving Latent Action Structure in Latent Policy Learning via Flow Matching
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Jiexi Lyu, Xizhou Bu, Qingqiu Huang, Chufeng Tang, Xiaoshuai Hao
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: The LAFP method enhances latent policy learning by using flow matching and interpolation to preserve action structure, outperforming existing techniques in imitation learning tasks.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: Learning high quality latent actions from large-scale unlabeled videos, coupled with limited real-world interaction data for training an action decoder, has emerged as a promising paradigm for scalable latent policy learning. However, existing approaches typically rely on behavior cloning, which tends to collapse inherently multimodal action distributions into unimodal ones, thereby degrading the pretrained latent action structure. While flow matching provides a potential alternative, directly applying it leads to a misalignment between latent actions and physical actions during action decoder training, due to the stochastic nature of the learned policy. To address these, we propose Latent Action Flow Policy (LAFP), which leverages flow matching for latent policy learning and introduces an inference-time interpolation mechanism to mitigate stochasticity-induced misalignment. Experimental results demonstrate that LAFP consistently outperforms prior methods on most downstream imitation learning tasks, achieving an 8.2\% improvement in average success rate while incurring less than 1x additional inference overhead.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: BAT-WAM: Bridging Action and Touch in World-Action Models for Dexterous Hands
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Dong Fang, Feixuan Huang, Yuanxin Zhong, Yuxiang Gao, Qi Song
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: BAT-WAM is a novel framework that enhances dexterous manipulation by integrating visual, joint-state, and tactile information, significantly improving tactile reconstruction and prediction accuracy.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: Dexterous manipulation with world action models (WAMs) relies on hand configuration and contact information, yet joint-state and whole-hand tactile observations may be partially or entirely missing. RGB images provide scene context and hand-object geometry but are insufficient to reliably recover these missing modalities. We further observe a correlation between hand state and tactile information. Motivated by this observation, we introduce BAT-WAM, a framework that bridges visual, joint-state, and tactile representations for WAMs. BAT-WAM learns separate codebooks and decoders for the tactile and action streams. An RGB-conditioned continuous latent bridge connects the two streams for bidirectional learning, while visual information serves as continuous context. Under the HTBench evaluation protocol, BAT-WAM reduces the root mean squared error (RMSE) of tactile reconstruction by 34.73% under fully masked conditions and 38.84% under partially masked conditions, relative to an image-conditioned HandTouch checkpoint. For future tactile prediction conditioned on target-time RGB and historical actions, it reduces mean RMSE by 85.56% relative to OpenWAM with HandTouch. Real-robot experiments further show that BAT-WAM consistently outperforms related WAM baselines in dexterous manipulation. Generalization experiments on unseen objects and scenes also demonstrate substantial improvements over baseline models. These findings support joint modeling of visual context, hand state, and touch as a representation approach for multimodal WAMs.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: When Coding Agents Get Arms: Safety Risks Across the Digital-Physical Boundary
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Yiming Sun, Mi Zhang
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: The paper introduces ArmedAgent, a benchmark assessing safety risks of coding agents controlling robot arms, revealing significant vulnerabilities in frontier models like GPT-6-Astra.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: Advances in spatial understanding have enabled frontier models to power coding agents that control a real robot arm zero-shot and end-to-end, without task-specific demonstrations or retraining. This brings two new safety challenges. First, the extensive knowledge of frontier models lets these agents perform tasks that earlier VLA and WAM paradigms could not, opening the door to new forms of capability misuse. Second, coding agents can access digital resources such as web pages and emails. Threats in these resources, such as indirect prompt injection, can carry over into the physical world when the agent controls a robot. We therefore introduce ArmedAgent, the first systematic benchmark to evaluate both risks for coding agents performing zero-shot robot control. It covers robustness, malicious use, and indirect injection across 36 tasks in 5 scenarios, evaluated in simulation and validated on a physical robot arm. A distinctive portion of the tasks target harmful behaviors that earlier VLA paradigms could not perform. Testing several frontier models, including GPT-6-Astra, under widely used agent frameworks, we find substantial safety risks in current systems.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: Review the Episodes, Refine the Lessons: Simple Memory Evolution for Embodied Agents
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Yifei Yao, Yude Zou, Xing Gao, Guanbo Jiao, Yukai Wang
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: The paper introduces SimplEvo, a memory evolution framework for embodied agents that enhances performance without weight updates, achieving significant success rate improvements in task execution.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: Recent studies of embodied agents based on frontier multimodal large language models (MLLMs) develop harness engineering around the MLLM, such as harnesses with post-trained policies and recursive self-improvement loops. Yet whether these additions exceed the native capability of the MLLM remains unexplored. We introduce SimplEvo to explore how far an MLLM can improve under direct control when it retains its execution experience in self-written text memories. It requires no weight updates, post-trained policies, or privileged information. The MLLM writes a coordinate-free task memory once from a single demonstration. Under a strict train-test protocol, it then creates a bounded working memory on training episodes only and refines it after each episode with lessons on procedure, completion, and recovery. Both memories stay fixed at test time. On EBench, SimplEvo lifts the success rate (SR) of GPT-6-Astra under direct control from 46.7% to 81.7%, and tops the RoboDojo leaderboard with 69.63% SR and a score of 75.32. Compared with memories that also store past visual frames, SimplEvo reaches a similar SR with text memory alone while using fewer tokens. With its memories fixed, SimplEvo also generalizes to unseen layouts and randomized scene configurations. Moreover, the working memory transfers across models: written by GPT-6-Astra, it can be reused as is by weaker MLLMs and improve their performance without any adaptation of their own.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: Harness Matters: Measuring and Dissecting Security Resilience in Web Agents
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Xinyi Wu, Jiagui Chen, JiaYi Dong, Geng Hong, Xudong Pan
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: The paper analyzes web-agent harness security, revealing vulnerabilities across its execution workflow and emphasizing the need for harness-level design improvements alongside backend models.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: Web agents extend LLMs from text generation to real-world web interaction by relying on execution harnesses that interpret user goals, perceive webpages, plan actions, and ground model decisions into browser operations. While prior work has recognized that agent security depends on more than the backend model alone, how harness design quantitatively shapes web-agent security remains insufficiently measured. To systematically study web-agent harness security, we first characterize web-agent harnesses as a four-stage execution workflow covering goal interpretation, webpage perception, reasoning and planning, and action execution. Based on this abstraction, we build WebTrap Farm, a systematic and extensible evaluation framework covering three representative attack categories: malicious user prompts, malicious prompt injection, and deceptive web design. To avoid conflating security with task capability, we use paired usability calibration tasks to separate genuine defensive behavior from capability limitations. Our evaluation shows that existing web-agent harnesses remain vulnerable to typical attacks, with some unsafe behaviors occurring even without explicit attack content, revealing harness-intrinsic security failures (RQ1). Statistical analysis further shows that both harness and backend model significantly affect security outcomes, indicating that deployed-agent security is jointly shaped by the harness and backend model (RQ2). Finally, we localize where defensive behavior emerges across workflow stages and identify more secure design mechanisms, providing actionable guidance for building more robust web agents (RQ3). These findings highlight the web-agent harness as an important security boundary and motivate moving beyond model-centric defenses toward harness-level security design.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: Learning to Act with World Models by Valuing What Comes Next
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Chenghao Gao, Zhi Zhang, Dian Jin, Yihe Pan, Doudou Zhou
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: WM-PPO enhances reinforcement learning by integrating a world model with PPO, improving success rates significantly in ALFWorld and ScienceWorld through better action-value predictions.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: A sparse terminal reward tells an agent little about its steps. Much of the missing information is implicit in the environment's dynamics, because each state transition can change the conditions for success long before the reward arrives. A world model trained on real transitions can learn to predict what each action changes, but a predicted observation does not by itself show whether success has become more likely. With a binary terminal reward, PPO's critic makes this judgment by estimating the current policy's probability of success, but only for states the agent reaches. Our method, WM-PPO, elegantly brings the two together. For each action the policy samples, executed or not, the world model predicts the next observation and the critic values the predicted successor. In the policy channel, comparisons among these values give the policy auxiliary advantages; in the value channel, their mean gives the critic an auxiliary target. A shared gate weights both channels according to how reliably comparisons with similar margins predicted real outcomes earlier in training. The policy, critic and world model all learn from the agent's own interaction, with no teacher or privileged information, and only the policy is used at inference. With a comparable number of real environment steps, WM-PPO raises success from PPO's 63.5% to 87.5% on ALFWorld and from 39.3% to 52.9% on ScienceWorld. It matches the strongest PPO refinements we tested on ALFWorld and exceeds the best of them by 6.5 points on ScienceWorld. The trained policy more often completes prerequisite steps before placing an object or committing to an answer.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: StreamMemBench: Streaming Evaluation of Agent Memory for Future-Oriented Assistance
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Guanming Liu, Yuqi Ren, Hansu Gu, Peng Zhang, Weihang Wang
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: StreamMemBench evaluates agent memory's effectiveness in leveraging past interactions for future assistance through a two-step task sequence, revealing significant shortcomings in current systems.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: A central role of personal-agent memory is to turn stored information and prior interactions into future-oriented assistance. In daily use, useful cues come from what the agent observes and how the user interacts with the agent, and the agent must carry them forward from the current request to similar future tasks. Existing memory benchmarks usually test dialogue recall or task improvement in isolation, leaving the trajectory from streaming observations to later assistance largely untested. We introduce StreamMemBench, a streaming benchmark that constructs a two-step task sequence around each evidence anchor from EgoLife egocentric streams. The initial task tests evidence use, while the follow-up task tests whether feedback and interaction experience are reused. Four metrics diagnose evidence recall, initial evidence use, feedback incorporation, and follow-up reuse. Experiments with eight memory systems across two backbones show that current systems often fail to use observed evidence or turn feedback into reliable follow-up behavior, even when evidence is stored or feedback is incorporated locally. StreamMemBench is publicly available at https://github.com/landian60/StreamMemBench.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: WAM-Sim0.1: World Anchored Memory Meets Online RL for Consistent and Realistic Driving Simulation
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Jiahao Cui, Jiaye Li, Wenhao Zhang, Yaoyi Li, Shan Luan
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: WAM-Sim integrates a persistent hierarchical memory with online RL to enhance driving simulations, mitigating drift and improving visual fidelity and perception performance.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: Autoregressive driving world models systematically suffer from structural drift, identity drift, and quality decay over long rollout horizons due to transient conditioning signals that lack persistent state. We present WAM-Sim, a driving world model anchored by a persistent hierarchical memory and optimized via online flow-matching RL. WAM-Sim structures persistent context across three temporal and semantic scales: pose-aligned structural tokens encoding persistent road topology, read-only scene tokens supplying geolocated background appearance, and write-once instance tokens preserving individual traffic participant identities across occlusions and chunk boundaries. To restore visual sharpness and physical plausibility degraded by multi-scale conditioning, we introduce an online post-training framework that optimizes self-generated rollouts via flow-matching RL guided by hierarchy-aligned visual rewards and a vision-language model physical judge. The invariant memory empirically confines policy optimization within the anchored context, helping suppress semantic collapse and reward hacking, while online RL systematically enforces physical commonsense and fine-grained visual fidelity. On the nuScenes benchmark, WAM-Sim achieves a superior generation fidelity (FID=3.47, FVD=25.72) and strong downstream perception performance (24.16 mAP, 71.23 road mIoU). On minute-scale rollouts of self-collected data, WAM-Sim substantially mitigates structural and identity drift, preserving high scene similarity and subject identity coherence across extended horizons. Project page: https://fudan-generative-vision.github.io/WAM-Sim.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: Adaptive Test-Time Memory Allocation for Long-Tailed Human-Object Interaction Detection
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Yuqiu Jiang, Xiaozhen Qiao, Yifan Chen, Ye Zheng, Zhe Sun
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: The paper presents Adaptive Diversity Cache (ADC), a framework that enhances long-tailed human-object interaction detection by dynamically allocating memory based on interaction frequency and confidence.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: Long-tailed human-object interaction (HOI) detection remains challenging because rare interactions are sparsely represented in training data. Although test observations provide additional visual evidence, existing cache-based methods typically assign uniform memory capacity across classes, limiting their ability to capture informative features of underrepresented interactions. To address this issue, we propose Adaptive Diversity Cache (ADC), a training-free, plug-and-play framework that adaptively constructs test-time caches through frequency-aware capacity allocation and confidence-diversity joint sample selection. Specifically, Frequency-Aware Cache Adaptation assigns larger capacities to underrepresented interactions using frequency-dependent priorities and a weighted logarithmic allocation objective, and fills remaining slots with selected augmented views. Confidence-Diversity Joint Cache Selection further combines prediction confidence with local feature diversity to retain informative cache entries. Cache retrieval then refines the predictions of the frozen detector. Experiments on HICO-DET and V-COCO across three base detectors demonstrate consistent improvements. On HICO-DET, ADC improves mean average precision (mAP) for rare interactions by 4.02--8.57 percentage points, while also improving performance on non-rare interactions. Online adaptation further achieves gains of 2.87--7.36 percentage points on rare interactions. These results demonstrate that adaptive test-time memory effectively complements existing HOI detectors and improves long-tailed detection performance.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: Autonomy and Coordination in Intelligent Manufacturing: A Recursive Autonomous Agent Framework
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Yuning Chen, Hongda Zhang, Linqiang Hu, Ziqing Zhou, Yi Liu
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: The paper presents the Recursive Autonomous Agent framework, integrating individual autonomy and collective coordination for intelligent manufacturing systems to enhance decision-making and adaptability.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: Intelligent production requires systems to make decisions and organize work according to production goals and operating conditions. It also requires continuous adjustment through feedback. This paper analyzes intelligence in human production organizations from a complex adaptive systems (CAS) perspective. The analysis identifies two coupled mechanisms: individual autonomy and collective coordination. Individual autonomy enables actors to form local decisions using available information. Collective coordination aligns these decisions with shared goals and joint constraints. Learning and adaptation improve both mechanisms over time. A production-system model formalizes how local decision rules and coordination jointly form system decisions. On this basis, we propose the Recursive Autonomous Agent (RAA) framework, which combines goal-driven autonomous agents with a recursive organizational structure. Goal contracts define local objectives and operating boundaries, while capability contracts support the selection and composition of production units. Common interfaces allow coordinated groups to participate as units in larger organizations, connecting equipment, production lines, and factories. RAA thus provides an engineering approach to next-generation intelligent manufacturing, translating the requirements of intelligence, openness, and system-wide integration into mechanisms for autonomous and coordinated production.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: CoSafe: Cooperative Runtime Safety Assurance for Mixed-Traffic Autonomous Driving
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Dingji Wang, You Lu, Haowen Jiang, Yanggang Chen, Yuyang Bi
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: CoSafe is a cooperative runtime safety framework for mixed-traffic autonomous driving that enhances safety by enabling scene-level hazard monitoring and intervention through V2X communication.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: With the rapid development of autonomous driving systems (ADSes), real-world roads are evolving into mixed-traffic environments where autonomous vehicles (AVs) and other traffic participants (e.g., human-driven vehicles (HDVs), cyclists, and pedestrians) coexist and interact with each other. However, current ADSes still incur various safety violations in mixed traffic scenarios, raising a strong demand for runtime safety assurance frameworks that can continuously monitor hazards and prevent potential violations. Existing ego-centric assurance approaches are insufficient for mixed traffic, where violations often arise from locally reasonable yet jointly incompatible decisions among multiple vehicles and cannot be reliably resolved through independent takeover. To bridge this gap, we propose CoSafe, a modular and ADS-agnostic cooperative runtime safety assurance framework for mixed-traffic autonomous driving to extend runtime safety assurance from ego-centric takeover to scene-level cooperative intervention. CoSafe leverages vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication to enable roadside units (RSUs) to monitor scene-level hazards and jointly mitigate hazards involving multiple vehicles. We integrate CoSafe with seven state-of-the-art ADSes, and our evaluation on the InterDrive benchmark demonstrates that CoSafe improves the driving score of AVs by 70.03% on average, reduces safety violations by 87.80%, and accurately identifies unsafe AVs with an F3 score of 0.930, while satisfying real-time constraints.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: Turns Matter: Advancing Streaming Video RL via Turn-Level Credit
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Shuai Dong, Kanghui Tian, Linghan Chen, Wenqi Shao, Hongrui Wu
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: TurnWise introduces a turn-level GRPO framework for streaming video RL, enhancing decision-making by aligning learning with individual interactions and reducing redundant responses.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: Streaming video understanding requires models to repeatedly decide whether to respond or continue observing. Recently, Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) has been applied to this setting, with existing approaches emphasizing reward design while retaining a single trajectory-level advantage across turns. Such shared credit can reinforce redundant replies after earlier successes and discourage useful follow-ups after earlier failures. We propose TurnWise, a turn-level GRPO framework that aligns learning with individual streaming decisions. TurnWise addresses the mismatch between trajectory-level feedback and turn-level interaction, promoting informative responses and reducing redundancy. Specifically, turn-level credit assignment uses silence-completed prefix scoring to construct group-relative advantages from each decision's remaining return, separating its learning signal from earlier rewards. Turn-mean policy optimization averages token losses within each turn and then across turns, giving response and waiting decisions equal weight regardless of output length. These complementary designs improve streaming policy learning without a learned critic or additional rollouts. Extensive experiments show our method outperforms prior RL approaches for streaming video understanding.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: HiLo-WAM: Decoupling Long-Horizon Task Evolution and Local Dynamics in World Action Models
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Xingyu Wang, Yanjiang Guo, Zhijing Ding, Jiaxin Fang, Zeyu Lai
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: HiLo-WAM enhances robotic manipulation by decoupling long-horizon task evolution from local dynamics, achieving high success rates and efficiency through a dual-DiT architecture.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) improve robotic manipulation by jointly modeling visual dynamics and robot actions. However, most existing WAMs model dense short-horizon visual dynamics, capturing local interactions but providing limited long-range task context. Extending prediction horizons increases uncertainty and computation while entangling task-level evolution with fine-grained local dynamics, obscuring their dependencies and distinct roles in action generation. We propose HiLo-WAM, which decouples long-horizon task evolution from local visual dynamics while jointly modeling their interaction with robot actions. A sparse long-horizon visual stream captures historical task context and future evolution, while a dense local dynamics visual stream models short-horizon robot-object interactions. The two streams operate at different temporal scales within a unified dual-DiT architecture and guide actions through structured cross-stream attention. Progressive inference further reduces unnecessary computation through stream-wise partial denoising, joint denoising, and dynamic skipping. Experiments demonstrate strong long-horizon manipulation performance: HiLo-WAM achieves a 93.70% average success rate on RoboTwin 2.0 and a 17.43 progress score on RoboDojo long-horizon tasks, with robust in-domain and OOD performance on the Fourier GR-3 robot. Ablations confirm the complementary contributions of long-horizon task evolution and local interaction dynamics, while temporal-scale analyses highlight the importance of balancing temporal coverage and resolution. Progressive inference further achieves a 2.93x speedup while improving performance.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: SAFEVPR: Patch-Based Verification with Empirical FDR Control for Cross-Condition Sequence Visual Place Recognition
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Ha Sier, Jiaqiang Zhang, Zhuo Zou, Xianjia Yu, Tomi Westerlund
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: SAFEVPR introduces a non-trainable verification pipeline using mutual-nearest-neighbour patch scores to maintain empirical false-discovery rate control in cross-condition visual place recognition.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: Sequence-based visual place recognition (VPR) for loop closure and robot relocalization must decide whether the retrieved top-1 candidate should be accepted. Conformal calibration can set this accept/reject threshold, but its finite-sample guarantees require exchangeability between calibration and deployment, a requirement that cross-condition deployment violates. We therefore claim no formal guarantee under condition shift: this paper instead asks which verification score and calibration design keep a target false-discovery rate (FDR) empirically satisfied across realistic appearance change. We present SAFEVPR, a non-trainable pipeline that replaces the backbone cosine similarity with a mutual-nearest-neighbour (MNN) patch score from frozen DINOv2 features, and flat Learn-Then-Test (LTT) calibration with per-bin Clopper-Pearson thresholds. Across 23 cross-condition ground-vehicle setups (Oxford RobotCar, NCLT, St Lucia; three frozen backbones), SAFEVPR meets the FDR target on 23/23 setups at alpha = 0.10 (mean accepted FDR 0.014, mean TPR 0.75) and on 22/23 at alpha = 0.05 with 22 retaining non-trivial coverage (best cosine variant, cosine+LTT: 22/23 valid but 17 non-trivial); under leave-one-dataset-out calibration, validity drops to 20/23 with 14 retaining useful coverage (strongest cosine baseline: 16/23 and 10), and on texture-poor scenery (Nordland) the verifier is uninformative and the system abstains entirely, as it does everywhere at alpha = 0.01; we report these as limitations. In a pose-graph relocalization study, gating loop-closure constraints reduces erroneous constraints by 29.6x and cuts the median trajectory error from 95.5 m to 9.7 m. Code is available at https://github.com/TIERS/SafeVPR.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: CANDO: Conservative Action-Noise Directional Optimization for Residual Reinforcement Learning
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Zeyu Gao, Chengkai Hou, Chaoyue Li, Zhuangzhe Wu, Jiaming Liu
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: CANDO enhances frozen generative policies in robot control by integrating noise-space and action-space residual methods, achieving superior adaptation and performance metrics.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: Pretrained generative policies provide strong behavior priors for robot control, but adapting them efficiently with online reinforcement learning remains difficult. A central challenge is how to improve a frozen generative policy without destroying the structure learned from offline demonstrations. Noise-space residual methods address this by modifying the policy's input noise, but existing noise-space methods typically regulate adaptation through fixed latent feasible regions, which may exclude valuable noise edits. In contrast, action-space residual methods are more sample-efficient, but their efficiency can still be further improved. We propose Conservative Noise Directional Optimization (CNDO), a noise-space residual RL method that improves a frozen generative policy by learning state- and noise-conditioned directions around Gaussian latent samples. CNDO removes predefined latent feasible regions and instead regulates noise-space adaptation through the soft conservative constraint, which consists of conservative value estimation and gated execution. We further introduce Conservative Action-Noise Directional Optimization (CANDO), which adds an action-space residual, combining structured latent-space improvement with local action correction. Experiments show that, once CNDO narrows the gap between noise-space and action-space residual learning, CANDO further improves over single-space optimization, achieving 76.1 NAUC and a 91.4% final success rate, surpassing the best single-space results by 6.6 NAUC and 4.1% success rate. More demos and info are available on https://cando-rl.github.io/.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: Large Discrete Policy: Advancing Explicit Behavior Modeling with Stochastic Iterative Scoring
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Zhenxin Li, Nadine Chang, Xinglong Sun, Jingde Chen, Wenhao Yao
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: The Large Discrete Policy (LDiP) framework enhances behavior modeling by using stochastic iterative scoring to select actions from a large set of plausible candidates, outperforming existing methods.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: Behavior policies are often formulated as continuous generative models, whose iterative denoising processes are expressive but difficult to interpret and prone to producing implausible actions. We propose the Large Discrete Policy (LDiP), a fully discrete behavior modeling framework that selects actions from a large vocabulary of physically plausible candidates. Rather than perturbing actions, LDiP improves expressivity through stochastic iterative scoring: it progressively re-scores and prunes candidates with score-space stochasticity, enabling fine-grained ranking and exploration among plausible actions while preserving an explicit decision process. Across end-to-end planning, closed-loop driving, robotic manipulation, and vision-language-action settings, LDiP consistently outperforms strong discrete and continuous baselines in autonomous driving, and exceeds or matches continuous generative policies in robotic manipulation. These results show that discrete policies, when equipped with effective scoring mechanisms, offer an expressive, plausible, and interpretable alternative for behavior modeling. Project website: https://zhenxinli.net/LargeDiscretePolicy/.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: Spotter: Let the Embodied Model Lead, and the VLM Reflect for It
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Long Li, Qichao Zhao, Yue Yang, Fan Xu, Zhe Wang
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: The Spotter framework enhances embodied models by allowing them to lead while a vision-language model monitors and corrects errors, significantly improving performance and efficiency.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: Current embodied models do not respond to their own failures, although what just went wrong could inform a small adjustment on the next attempt, the kind of reflection behind the gains of thinking in language models. We test whether they can repair a known error, which requires producing a correction and judging whether it is right. Stopped at a failure and allowed to retry, they seldom repair it through their own randomness or from a language description of the error, and best-of-N selection cannot pick the successful candidate after a failure. We attribute this to training only on successful demonstrations and to inputs too narrow to show what went wrong, and conclude that reflection must come from a vision-language model (VLM), which takes in far more information, such as the episode history and text, and is more general. Prior VLM-led work has the VLM plan every step and invoke the embodied model as a tool, placing the VLM on the critical path. We propose Spotter, which reverses the roles: the embodied model leads and executes continuously, while the VLM runs in parallel, monitors through a lightweight local screener, intervenes only when an error is detected, reflects on and corrects it, and returns control. We run Spotter with Qwen and with GPT as the VLM, and both improve the embodied models; with GPT, Spotter improves Cosmos Policy and $π_{0.5}$ by 5.6 and 7.5 percentage points on RoboCasa, and raises $π_{0.5}$ from 47.2% to 57.0% on the Hard setting of RoboTwin 2.0 and from 53% to 83% on a real robot. Because the VLM steps in only when an error is confirmed, a successful episode with Qwen takes only 13 to 16 s longer than with the embodied model alone and about 70% less time than with a VLM-led baseline using the same model. Our code is available at https://github.com/zqc3117/Spotter.

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: TacMind: Benchmarking and Modeling Tactile Interaction States for Robotic Manipulation
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Jiaxin Shi, Zibin Wu, Yichi Zhang, Jianghua Duan, Siyu Zhu
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: The paper introduces TacMind, a benchmark for evaluating tactile interaction in robotic manipulation, proposing a predictive model that enhances action generation through learned tactile states.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: Tactile sensing provides robots with direct observations of contact physics, local geometry, and interaction dynamics, making it a vital source of feedback for contact-rich manipulation. However, existing tactile manipulation studies are often developed and evaluated within specific task settings, making it difficult to systematically compare how tactile information contributes under different interaction conditions. In this work, we develop a benchmark in simulation comprising 128 tasks organized around three complementary evaluation regimes: Precise, Recognition, and Dynamic. The benchmark further includes controlled static and dynamic task variants and 12 perturbation settings for evaluating robustness under changes in visual and physical conditions. These settings motivate studying tactile information as a temporally evolving interaction representation rather than only as an instantaneous observation. We therefore propose an action-conditioned latent predictive world model that integrates tactile history and learns a tactile state through prediction of future tactile latents. Building on this representation, we design a model that conditions action generation on the learned tactile state and uses predicted future tactile information to refine candidate actions through predictive tactile reflection. Experiments on the proposed benchmark show consistent gains from incorporating tactile information across the evaluated regimes. Project Page: https://tacmind-bench.github.io/

集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).title: STEER: Route-Aware Adaptive Reasoning for Autonomous Driving
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).authors_text: Yangang Zou, Pei Liu, Nan Song, Bozhou Zhang, Mingyu Guo
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).summary: STEER introduces a novel adaptive reasoning approach for autonomous driving that optimizes route-aware decision-making without requiring subjective scene-difficulty annotations, enhancing planning efficiency and performance.
集群机器人系统实验室 (MagicLab).debug_abstract: Vision-language action (VLA) models excel for end-to-end autonomous driving, yet their tendency to over-invoke chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning mirrors a human cognitive pitfall: overthinking. Just as deliberate reasoning can slow or mislead human judgment in routine tasks, excessive CoT in VLA incurs unnecessary compute overhead and can paradoxically degrade planning performance. Recent research tackles this via adaptive reasoning, which dynamically modulates inference complexity by selectively triggering CoT for complex scenes while responding directly to routine ones.
