Current solutions struggle to balance reliability and efficiency: methods based on intermediate structures are prone to error propagation, while diffusion models suffer from high inference latency and complex post-hoc candidate extraction. To address this, we present F2G-Pose, a real-time direct, single-pass framework that predicts category-level pose, metric size, and camera-frame completed shape from a single RGB-D observation in one feed-forward pass. F2G-Pose lifts dense visual foundation features to partial point clouds, encodes local geometry with DGCNN tokenization, and integrates object-level structure with a Mixture-of-Experts Transformer. Joint size prediction and camera-frame shape completion encourage metric consistency through dense geometric supervision. With its task-specific network trained only on pose-annotated synthetic SOPE data and its frozen RADIO backbone externally pretrained, F2G-Pose achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on SOPE and ROPE while running at 28 FPS for pose-only inference, and further demonstrates strong camera-frame geometry on HouseCat6D and real-object transfer on HANDAL. Analyses of latency, robustness, shape completion, and GenPose++ candidate behavior further demonstrate the efficiency and reliability of F2G-Pose, with real-world manipulation experiments demonstrating deployment potential under segmented RGB-D inputs. The project page, code, and pretrained models are made available at https://jrryzh.github.io/F2G-Pose/.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: SMR: Learning streaming motion retargeting for humanoids from human semantic
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Chun Gu, Juntong Zhang, Jingyu Li, Li Zhang
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: SMR is a streaming neural motion retargeter that converts human motion into robot-aware targets, achieving higher semantic fidelity and physical validity than traditional methods.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: Retargeting human motion to humanoids requires preserving motion semantics while accounting for the robot's physical constraints. Kinematic pipelines prescribe a robot trajectory through geometric matching, without establishing whether it can be executed under the robot's dynamics. Prior physics-supervised neural methods train bidirectional full-sequence models on physics-refined kinematic trajectories, remaining tied to prescribed kinematic solutions and requiring noncausal context. We propose SMR, a streaming neural motion retargeter learned from semantic-conditioned physics experts. We convert human motion into robot-aware task-space targets for body landmark positions, orientations, and velocities. Physics experts track these targets directly in simulation under contact, dynamics, and actuator constraints. We train a single strictly causal Transformer on their executed state trajectories that complete the motion and pass semantic and physical validity checks. At each incoming frame, the student uses only current and past human observations to generate a robot motion reference for a downstream whole-body controller. Experiments demonstrate that semantic-conditioned physics experts generate motion with higher semantic fidelity and physical validity than direct optimization-based retargeting, while the resulting streaming retargeter achieves improved closed-loop performance over kinematic and physics-refined baselines under a common whole-body controller.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: DepState-JEPA: Learning Depth-Grounded State Representation for Visual Perception and Manipulation
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Xiujian Liang, Liuyuan Na, Zehao Du, Jiacheng Xu, Weixi Song
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: DepState-JEPA introduces a dual-stream RGB-Depth architecture for robot manipulation, enhancing predictive state representation by integrating spatial understanding and action-conditioned predictions through shared latent states.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: Predictive representations for robot manipulation should connect scene geometry with the state changes induced by actions. Our intuition is that understanding what an action will change starts with understanding where things are: complementary RGB and depth observations ground a common scene representation from which to infer those changes. Guided by this intuition, we introduce \textbf{DepState-JEPA}, a dual-stream RGB--Depth joint-embedding predictive architecture that connects spatial understanding with action-conditioned prediction through a shared latent state, \textbf{DepState}. Built on V-JEPA~2.1, the framework uses depth both as a complementary observation stream and to ground both modalities in metric 3D space, aggregating shared information into DepState while retaining modality-private features for decoding. Ray-conditioned readouts predict local features without target depth; after an action-conditioned transition, the same decoders predict future RGB and depth features using the predicted state and fixed initial private features. Robot-state readouts provide recursive proprioceptive inputs; object-trajectory supervision and calibrated forward kinematics shape state learning through motion targets and joint--TCP consistency. Comparisons show stronger RGB-encoder transfer after RGB-D adaptation, feature completion, conditioned visual forecasting, and manipulation success. Within-model ablations identify contributions from depth content, metric coordinates, and future-state matching, with additional control gains from FK regularization.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: Training in Deployment: Human-in-the-loop Online Post-Training for Robot Manipulation
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Chun Gu, Xiaofei Wei, Yiming Chen, Bozhou Zhang, Juntong Zhang
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: TIDE is a human-in-the-loop online post-training system that enhances robot manipulation by rapidly adapting policies using real-time human interventions and deployment data.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: Large pretrained robot foundation models provide strong priors for manipulation, yet adapting them to target tasks with offline teleoperated demonstrations often fails to cover the contact-rich, recovery, and precision-critical states encountered during deployment. Existing methods mitigate this issue by augmenting offline demonstrations with human-in-the-loop data or online reinforcement learning. Despite this, offline post-training adapts slowly because it cannot immediately absorb deployment experience, while online RL typically relies on value functions or auxiliary actor-critic models, increasing both training complexity and instability. We present TIDE (Training In DEployment), a human-in-the-loop online post-training system. TIDE introduces a provenance-conditioned supervised learning framework that updates the policy online from human interventions and policy-generated rollouts collected during deployment, without a learned critic, reward model, or action scorer. Across four real-world bimanual manipulation tasks, TIDE improves milestone-normalized task progress and binary full-task completion over the warm-start policy and matched additional offline demonstrations, and performs comparably to the fixed-policy collection baseline while making updated checkpoints available during deployment. Each task-specific online post-training session, from the start of deployment rollouts until the final checkpoint is available, completes in less than one hour while learning and checkpoint handling run asynchronously.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: Plan First, Act Later: Streaming Reasoning for Executable Memory in Robot Control
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Qinghang Liu, Conglin Wang, Zongsheng Li, Boyong He, Han Gao
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: The PAL framework enhances long-horizon robot manipulation by proactively managing memory and subtasks, achieving superior performance in benchmarks and real-world tasks.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: Long-horizon robot manipulation requires a robot to remember task-relevant information beyond its short observation window. Existing memory-augmented policies typically retrieve relevant information from history and reason over it at execution time, placing a heavy reasoning burden on the high-level model. To address this challenge, we propose PAL (\textbf{P}lan first, \textbf{A}ct \textbf{L}ater), a hierarchical memory framework for vision-language robot manipulation. It maintains a short-term visual buffer, a semantic-event memory, and an executable \texttt{subtask\_list}. A high-level vision-language model (VLM) converts streaming visual observations into the \texttt{subtask\_list}. At execution time, the VLM selects the currently relevant subtask from the \texttt{subtask\_list} and passes it to a low-level vision-language-action (VLA) policy. To teach the model what to write to memory and when to update it, we introduce a two-stage data generation procedure that first expands sparse update supervision and then uses self-labeling with task-grounded verification to generate training data that better match the state distribution encountered during execution. We evaluate our approach on memory-dependent benchmarks and real-world manipulation tasks. On RoboMME, PAL achieves a \textbf{56.05\%} success rate, outperforming the strongest baseline, FrameSamp-Modul, at 44.51\%. In real-world experiments across four manipulation tasks, \pal{} reaches \textbf{60.83\%} overall success, surpassing MemER (45.00\%) and FrameSamp-Modul (28.33\%). These results show that proactively writing future-relevant subtasks into hierarchical memory improves long-horizon visual reasoning and robot control. Code and videos can be found on our website: https://qinghangliu.github.io/pal-webpage/

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: Let It Be Simple: One-Step Action Generation for Vision-Language-Action Models
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Yitong Chen, Shiduo Zhang, Jingjing Gong, Xipeng Qiu
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: The paper demonstrates that one-step action generation in Vision-Language-Action models is effective due to their unique condition-target structure, outperforming traditional multi-step methods.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: One-step generation from standard diffusion or Flow-Matching training is rarely effective for text-to-image or video generation without distillation or specialized one-step objectives. We find that VLA action generation behaves strikingly differently. Biasing only the training timestep distribution toward the noise endpoint yields strong one-step policies across LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, LIBERO-Pro, and real-world robot tasks. Moreover, for open-source VLA models with different architectures, simply replacing iterative decoding with a single forward pass often performs comparably to the original multi-step decoding on benchmarks such as LIBERO, CALVIN, and SimplerEnv. We attribute this difference to the condition-target structure of VLA generation, which is closer to image-to-text than text-to-image: rich observations strongly constrain a comparatively compact target. We formalize this intuition through the irreducible velocity loss $R_v(t,c)$ of standard Flow Matching, which becomes much smaller toward the noise endpoint for VLA, whereas image-generation models usually exhibit a U-shaped profile. The geometry induced by the learned generative map shows the same contrast: the Jacobian of this map with respect to the initial noise has a substantially smaller largest singular value for action generation than for image generation. Together, these results suggest that VLA's condition-target structure makes one-step generation unusually accessible to standard Flow Matching. Code and training configurations for this paper are available at https://github.com/bondtesty/let-it-be-simple.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: PRISM: Learning Realistic Depth via Physics-Grounded Noise Disentanglement with Semantic-Geometric Collaboration
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Xiujian Liang, Jiacheng Liu, Mingyang Sun, Qichen He, Anda Cheng
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: PRISM introduces a physics-grounded framework that disentangles depth noise into sensing invalidation and measurement inaccuracy, achieving state-of-the-art performance in noisy depth synthesis and real-world robotic tasks.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: Real-world physical sensing exhibits complex, heterogeneous noise patterns that deviate significantly from idealized simulation, posing a fundamental bottleneck for sim-to-real transfer. Existing sensor modelings typically treat depth noise as a monolithic black-box process, overlooking the distinct physical mechanisms that govern different error modalities. In this work, we introduce a physics-grounded paradigm that disentangles monolithic noise into two complementary modalities: \textbf{sensing invalidation} and \textbf{measurement inaccuracy}, enabling a tailored treatment of noise sources based on their physical origins. Building on this insight, we propose \textbf{PRISM}, a tripartite framework that distills 3D Visual Foundation Model features as rich spatial-semantic priors for physics-based reasoning. To address the inherent sparsity and class imbalance of invalidation regions, we develop Hierarchical Positive-Prioritized Supervision, integrating multi-scale positive-weighted objectives with a positive-preserving dynamic hard mining strategy to enforce precise artifact delineation. Extensive benchmarks demonstrate that PRISM achieves state-of-the-art fidelity in noisy depth synthesis. Furthermore, downstream robotic experiments show that PRISM facilitates a \textbf{92.1\%} average success rate in the real world, marking a significant improvement over monolithic baselines. Our project page is available at: \resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{\href{https://shawnleung-sii.github.io/prism-icml2026/}{https://shawnleung-sii.github.io/prism-icml2026/}.}

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: TARSphere: A Robot-Oriented Full-Stack Framework for Long-Horizon Embodied Agents in Evolving Physical and Social Environments
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Yicheng Xu, Zhikai Xu, Ziyuan Chen, Yuhang Dong, Tao Zhang
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: TARSphere is a comprehensive framework enabling long-horizon embodied agents to adapt and operate effectively in dynamic physical and social environments through advanced simulation and interaction techniques.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: Robots must act under physical and social constraints while adapting to changes in their environment and human needs. Existing embodied-agent systems often focus on specified goals or abstract execution into symbolic actions, limiting evaluation in an evolving world. We introduce TARSphere, a robot-oriented full-stack framework for physically and socially grounded long-horizon embodied agents. TARSphere-Infra runs robot policies in a physics simulator with embodied NPCs and constrained dialogue. An event-driven finite-state machine (FSM) uses completed actions and delivered information to update task states and evaluate outcomes. TARSphere-Harness, its embodied brain harness, lets a frozen multimodal large language model (MLLM) act through multi-level executable skills, using observations, hierarchical memory, and execution feedback to revise its decisions. On this foundation, agent-in-the-loop curation aligns task semantics, causal dependencies, and scene geometry to construct TARSphere-Bench: 360 episodes across 30 indoor scenes. Five paired conditions assess perceptual robustness, disruption adaptation, task update, human coordination, and intent understanding for navigate-and-report and fetch-and-deliver tasks. Our evaluation of 8 MLLMs shows that general-purpose models can outperform embodied models, while task updates and human interaction remain difficult. Frequent collisions and falls further motivate evaluating execution safety alongside task success, even with a shared action interface and decision budget.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: Uncertainty Gates the Gradient: Adaptive Updates for Generalized Few-Shot 3D Segmentation
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Yifei Zhao, Fanyu Zhao, Shengtang Wu, Han Zhang, Ruike Cao
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: The paper introduces Uncertainty-Gated Adaptive (UGA), a novel framework for improving generalized few-shot 3D segmentation by selectively gating updates based on episodic reliability.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: In generalized few-shot 3D point cloud segmentation, support annotations are often compromised by sparsity and occlusion. Blindly adapting to such low quality samples risks learning spurious geometric patterns rather than robust novel concepts. Although 3D Vision-Language Models have been introduced to sup plement supervision, the potential of uncertainty to actively govern adaptation dynamics remains underexplored. Existing signal-level methods like loss reweight ing fail to prevent unreliable episodes from steering the optimization trajectory. To address this, we propose Uncertainty-Gated Adaptive (UGA), to the best of our knowledge the first framework that elevates uncertainty to update-level gating for generalized few-shot 3D point cloud segmentation. The core mod ule, Uncertainty-Gated Update (UG-Update), estimates episodic reliability via intra-class dispersion over merged support and pseudo-labeled novel supervision, and selectively gates residual gradient updates. This encourages the model to learn novel semantics from reliable episodes while attenuating updates during unreliable ones. Complementing this, we introduce an Uncertainty-Based Pseudo Label Filter (UB-Filter) to enforce learning from high-confidence dense signals. On ScanNet200 and ScanNet++ (1-/5-shot), UGA sets new state of the art with an average +3.08 HM IoU over the strongest prior baseline.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: Exploration via Activation-Space Steering for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Yunan Zeng, Jinhao Jing, Xi Cheng, Yuwang Wang
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: The paper presents Activation-Space Exploration (ASE), enhancing reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards by diversifying training rollouts to improve reasoning performance on mathematical benchmarks.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) trains a language model by sampling responses, scoring them with an automatic verifier, and updating the policy from the resulting rewards. The policy therefore receives direct learning signals only from trajectories that appear in its rollouts. Yet repeated sampling from the same policy can concentrate on similar reasoning paths, leaving useful alternatives unexplored under a fixed rollout budget. We introduce Activation-Space Exploration (ASE), an online method for diversifying training rollouts. By clustering activation differences between correct and incorrect responses to the same problem, ASE builds a structured bank of latent exploration vectors. Different vectors are then applied to subsequent rollouts to explore alternative reasoning paths. On Qwen3-1.7B-Base and Qwen3-8B-Base trained on DAPO-Math-17k, ASE improves average Mean@8 across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks over GRPO by 4.87 and 1.87 percentage points, respectively, under the same rollout budget.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: M-Plan: Comprehensive Planning For LLM Agents with Memory Arrangement
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Ziyang Liu, Jiakang Yuan, Jiayuan Fan, Tao Chen
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: M-Plan is a closed-loop multi-agent system that integrates long-term and short-term memory to enhance performance in long-horizon tasks through task-specific guidance and optimized memory management.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents have recently demonstrated outstanding performance in single-turn tasks, yet they continue to struggle with long-horizon tasks, particularly in environments without prior training. A key limitation of single LLMs is their difficulty in processing long contexts, which stems from weaknesses in continuous decision-making and reasoning capabilities. Although existing multi-agent systems (MAS) equipped with long-term memory bases can partially address this gap, they mostly rely on knowledge reuse or summarization, an approach that is often constrained by directly retrieval without any adaptation for the current task, while the retrieved memory may contain much history noises waiting to be preprocessed. In contrast, MAS characterized by task-specific guidance often lack long-term memory specifically designed for the guidance. To address these challenges, we propose M-Plan, a closed-loop MAS framework that integrates long-term and short-term memory. By combining global-local and past-current guidance, M-Plan enhances agents' performance on multi-turn tasks while maintaining a plug-and-play design. During task execution, agents receive task-specific milestones and insights, and are provided with local hints only when confusion arises, which form global-local guidance together. These guidance generation and utilization construct the short-term memory as well. After task completion, relevant information about the current task is optimized or reorganized before being sent to the long-term memory storage for future retrieval. The designments mentioned above build a comprehensive framework different from other individual long-term or short-term memory works. Extensive experiments on multi-turn tasks including ALFWorld, Webshop, and PDDL across diverse models demonstrate that M-Plan outperforms multiple baseline methods in both accuracy and efficiency.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: Embodied Task Agents Can Perform Fine Manipulation through Tactile In-Context Learning
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Yubang Wang, Zezheng Huai, Yifei Zhang, Jinhao Wu, Yitong Chen
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: The study demonstrates that embodied task agents can enhance fine manipulation performance through tactile in-context learning, achieving significant success improvements without task-specific training.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: Can embodied task agents use tactile experience to perform fine manipulation without task-specific model training? We investigate this capability through Tactile-ETA, a system that incorporates tactile experience into an embodied task agent through in-context learning. Successful expert demonstrations show how contact changes during manipulation. We pair each recorded robot movement with its camera views and bilateral tactile observations. We keep tactile observations at the start and end of each movement and add two neighboring time points when the tactile images change markedly in between. The agent combines these demonstrations with current vision, tactile observations, and proprioception to select actions through general-purpose robot tools, without updating model parameters. Across four simulated manipulation tasks, adding tactile observations to the same two expert demonstrations increases average success from 15.75% to 24.00%, with current sensing and execution interfaces held fixed. Further experiments show that performance depends on the sensory content and representation of demonstrations, while comparing agent models on Lift Bottle reveals substantial differences under the same system configuration. On the real-robot tasks, demonstrations with aligned visual and tactile observations increase the task success rate from 0% to 60%. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of using tactile experience in context for fine manipulation and suggest a path toward extending embodied task agents to additional sensory inputs.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: Knowing When to Stop Thinking: A Dissection of Expected Free Energy as a Test-Time Compute Controller for Latent World-Model Planning
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Tong Zhang, Zhiyuan Shi, Yun Peng, Tao Xie
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: The paper explores using expected free energy to optimize computation in latent world-model planning, balancing goal distance and prediction disagreement to enhance decision-making efficiency.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: A planner using a learned world model can improve its predicted outcome while choosing a worse action. We study when expected free energy (EFE) can help decide how much computation to spend on a plan. An EFE-inspired objective combines goal distance with disagreement among stochastic predictions. We test candidate scoring, stopping, and online predictor updates separately. Stopping when elite cost stalls reduces refinement on tasks whose success plateaus with depth, with mean success close to fixed-depth references. At the larger tested weights, rewarding disagreement lowers success with a frozen model. Penalizing it helps at some task and weight settings but harms others. When training data omit a region needed to reach the goal, online updates recover part of the resulting loss. The tested cost-stall rule can fail when further optimization exploits model errors, because predicted cost keeps falling after task success peaks. Cost progress can guide computation on a plateau, but protecting performance after a peak requires information about the consequences of the chosen actions.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: MindView: Benchmarking Generative Multi-View Spatial Intelligence
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Yanbo Wang, Siqi Luo, Siyu Zhang, Chenming Zhu, Wenzhao Zheng
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: MindView is a benchmark for assessing generative multi-view spatial intelligence, revealing significant improvement opportunities and introducing MindCue for enhanced evidence utilization in expanded contexts.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: Spatial intelligence has recently been assessed through generative tasks such as spatially grounded image editing, yet language-guided generation of spatially consistent views from partial multi-view observations remains underexplored. We introduce MindView, a benchmark for generative multi-view spatial intelligence with 1,500 samples from 513 scenes across three indoor datasets. Its seven tasks form two families: geometry-dominant tasks specify changes in camera position and orientation, while semantics-dominant tasks require inferring target viewpoints by grounding referred objects and interpreting spatial relations and reference-frame cues. Evaluation of eleven generators reveals substantial room for improvement on MindView. A paired context analysis further shows that all eleven generators obtain lower overall scores under the expanded context setting. These findings motivate us to investigate whether task-specific supervision can improve target-view generation and whether models can use additional multi-view evidence effectively. We therefore fine-tune BAGEL on the MindView training dataset, improving its overall score by 24.3 points and yielding gains across all seven MindView tasks. Beyond these generation gains, the fine-tuned model also yields higher scores on three spatial-understanding benchmarks without training on their annotations, suggesting that learning to generate spatially grounded views may benefit spatial understanding. To improve evidence utilization under expanded context, we propose MindCue, a training-free spatial evidence selector guided by a target-view hypothesis. MindCue reverses the drop in overall score under expanded context and outperforms the standard-context baseline. Overall, MindView provides a concrete testbed for generative multi-view spatial intelligence.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: RoboCasa-Shift: Stage-Aware Robustness Evaluation of Vision-Language-Action Policies in Long-Horizon Household Manipulation
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Haocheng Wang, Youquan Liu, Weiyu Guo, Aokai Zhang, Donghang Wu
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: RoboCasa-Shift introduces a benchmark for evaluating vision-language-action policy robustness in long-horizon tasks, highlighting the complexity of failure dynamics under distribution shifts.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) robustness is commonly summarized by aggregate task success, which obscures how individual executions change under distribution shifts and where failures emerge in long-horizon tasks. We introduce \textbf{RoboCasa-Shift}, a diagnostic robustness benchmark built on RoboCasa365 that combines controlled single-factor shifts, matched clean-perturbed rollouts in which each pair shares the same underlying settings and differs only in the target shift, and simulator-grounded stage-aware diagnostics. We evaluate GR00T N1.5 on four long-horizon tasks that pass a predefined clean-performance gate under four perturbation factors and three calibrated severity levels, including conditions that drive the evaluated policy to complete task failure, totaling 1,040 formal rollouts. Robustness responses vary substantially across factors and tasks, and increasing severity does not always produce monotonic degradation. For example, one camera condition yields $Δ\mathrm{SR}=0$ despite 8 of 80 matched episodes changing outcome. Stage-aware analysis further shows that the same end-to-end degradation can correspond to different execution-depth profiles. Camera $L_2$ and Gaussian blur $L_1$ both yield $Δ\mathrm{SR}=0.188$, yet their first-stage failure rates are 19.0\% and 36.4\%, respectively. Our findings suggest that VLA robustness should be viewed as a multi-dimensional property of execution rather than a single end-to-end performance measure, motivating evaluation protocols that jointly capture outcome degradation, paired outcome sensitivity, and failure progression. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/HaochengWang23/RoboCasa-Shift.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: Do 3D Large Language Models Really Use 3D Evidence?
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Yifei Zhao, Fanyu Zhao, Han Zhang, Yixuan Lin, Yuyang Hou
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: This paper introduces UNICORNS, a benchmark for assessing 3D Large Language Models' reliance on 3D evidence, revealing performance gaps and proposing HORN to enhance accuracy.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: Recent 3D Large Language Models (3D-LLMs) have shown strong performance on scene question answering with extensive post-training. Yet, existing benchmarks rarely evaluate how 3D-LLMs respond to referential ambiguity, insufficient scene evidence, or false presuppositions, obscuring whether their responses are grounded in 3D evidence. In this work, we introduce UNICORNS, a benchmark for evaluating the reliability of 3D-LLM responses across four evidence conditions. UNICORNS contains 11,387 questions across 557 ScanNet scans, covering eight challenge categories alongside answerable controls. A response passes only if it satisfies the required response behavior and contains no scene claim unsupported by the available evidence. Evaluation of six open-sourced 3D-LLMs reveals a pronounced performance gap: even the strongest zero-shot model achieves 61.22% accuracy on answerable controls, but only 40.94% across the eight challenge categories. To address this gap, we further propose HORN, an obligation-aware post-training method combining group-relative task rewards, leaf-conditioned obligation rewards, and supervised control replay. Extensive experiments demonstrate that HORN reaches $75.1 \pm 1.0\%$ across the challenge categories and $77.2 \pm 0.8\%$ overall, outperforming all baselines without degrading answerable-control accuracy. Our findings enable a systematic evaluation and improvement of evidence-grounded 3D reasoning for 3D-LLMs (code: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/unicorns-6B38/).

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: SENRI: Understanding the Space-Event Nexus in Real-Life Videos
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Kehan Lan, Kaining Ying, Henghui Ding, Kaipeng Zhang
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: SENRI introduces a framework for understanding the space-event nexus in egocentric videos, evaluating AI's ability to connect events and spatial contexts through a comprehensive benchmark.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: Human memories are organized in a way that connects events with their corresponding spatial contexts. An AI assistant should also be able to memorize and recall the nexus of events and spaces. Thus we introduce SENRI, a task that studies this space--event connection in long, continuous real-life egocentric video. It contains six task types in two directions: Event$\rightarrow$Space, which recovers spatial knowledge from event cues, and Space$\rightarrow$Event, which retrieves events from regions and trajectories. To evaluate this, we build SENRI-Bench, containing 500 manually annotated multiple-choice questions over 10 uninterrupted self-recorded videos with around 25.3 hours of content. Also, we evaluate three typical long video understanding paradigms: direct perception, evidence seeking, and persistent memory. The task remains challenging across all three paradigms, highlighting substantial room for improvement. Then we show two representative failure modes of existing memory methods and address these evidence gaps with SENRI-Agent, a controller that uses Target-Guided Visual Check (TGVC) to propose local visual check tasks for parallel verifiers and integrate the reports into a working memory to help with reasoning. Built upon existing memory systems, SENRI-Agent improves the performance of existing baselines without modifying their stored memories. We hope SENRI will provide valuable insights into how real-life egocentric understanding should be evaluated, reveal the gaps in existing approaches, and offer a possible direction for improvement.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: Compositional Humanoid Manipulation through Isomorphic Teleoperation and Independent Skill Routing
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Yiming Wang, Peixian Yang, Lifeng Zhuo, Lai Wei, Xinling Du
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: The paper introduces HS-MoDP, a method for compositional humanoid manipulation using isomorphic teleoperation and skill routing, enhancing skill reuse and performance in robotic tasks.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: Humanoid manipulation requires reusable arm skills, yet demonstrating every possible skill combination is impractical. We present Humanoid Semantic Mixture-of-Experts Diffusion Policy (HS-MoDP), which composes separately demonstrated arm skills through independent semantic routing over a shared expert pool. This design preserves arm-specific skill control while sharing action-generation parameters across arms. A semantic scheduler integrates the learned policy with an existing locomotion controller through alternating manipulation and repositioning stages, extending the effective workspace and enabling skill reuse across location changes. To acquire demonstrations of whole-body contact manipulation, we develop G1Exo, an isomorphic exoskeleton that provides direct joint-level control of arm configurations. Experiments on a Unitree G1 show stronger skill composition than the baselines. G1Exo enables more reliable contact teleoperation than end-effector VR-IK, and its demonstrations improve contact-skill learning across four policy architectures. For HS-MoDP, switching from VR-IK to G1Exo demonstrations raises full cabinet workflow success from 35% to 65%. All project hardware designs and source code will be released as open source after the review process.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: PICA-WAM: Visual Perturbation Invariance via Cross-Appearance Self-Alignment in World Action Models
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Yude Zou, Yifei Yao, Guanbo Jiao, Jianming Ma, Guanjie Zheng
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: PICA-WAM enhances World Action Models' robustness to visual perturbations by introducing a self-supervised cross-appearance self-alignment task, improving action consistency and real robot performance.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) jointly predict future video and generate actions, yet remain sensitive to task-irrelevant visual perturbations, i.e., changes in visual appearance that should not affect robot behavior. We identify a gap in conventional WAM training: video prediction encourages representations to preserve appearance information, while action generation does not explicitly enforce invariance to task-irrelevant appearance. Data augmentation exposes WAMs to such perturbations but does not require perturbed and nominal observations to produce consistent action representations, and alignment with external pretrained features does not guarantee the desired invariance. To address this gap, we propose PICA-WAM, a self-supervised training framework that casts perturbation invariance as an auxiliary cross-appearance self-alignment task for WAMs. An exponential-moving-average (EMA) teacher processes the nominal observation to provide a deeper-layer target, while the online WAM processes a perturbed observation and aligns its shallower-layer action representation to this target through a lightweight projection head. Across four strong WAMs evaluated on RoboTwin 2.0, LIBERO-Plus, EBench, and a real robot, PICA-WAM consistently improves robustness under visual perturbations, preserves nominal performance in simulation, and raises the real robot success rate. PICA-WAM further reduces the sensitivity of video features to task-irrelevant appearance and its propagation into actions, as shown by paired layer-wise diagnostics. Code: https://github.com/YudeZou/PICA-WAM-release

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Junxi Wang, Te Sun, Jiayi Zhu, Chen Zhang, Siyuan Li
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: MemForest is a memory compression framework that efficiently partitions and merges agent memory, achieving significant storage reduction and retrieval speedup while maintaining high performance.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: Agent memory systems have demonstrated significant potential in long-term dialogue, personalized assistants, and video understanding. However, continuously accumulated memory introduces substantial storage and retrieval costs during inference. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{MemForest}, a general memory compression framework adaptable to various agent memory systems. Specifically, MemForest partitions historical memory into event-centric units by leveraging global semantic similarity and local temporal continuity. For each unit, it constructs a maximum spanning tree, termed an EventTree, and progressively merges redundant memory nodes by selecting high-weight edges, reducing storage overhead. Furthermore, we introduce an anchor-guided propagation retrieval mechanism that retrieves relevant memory nodes from the temporal neighborhoods of key nodes, improving retrieval accuracy. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of MemForest. Under the unimodal Mem0 framework, MemForest retains \textbf{97.1%} of the original performance while compressing \textbf{50%} of historical memory across three benchmarks (LoCoMo, LongMemEval, and PersonaMem), achieving a \textbf{1.89x} retrieval speedup. Under the multimodal M3-Agent framework, it preserves \textbf{99.7%} of the original performance with a \textbf{50%} compression ratio across two benchmarks (M3-Bench-robot and M3-Bench-web), achieving a \textbf{2.24x} retrieval speedup. \textcolor{RoyalBlue}{\textit{Our code is available at [https://github.com/Celina-love-sweet/MemForest.}}](https://github.com/Celina-love-sweet/MemForest.}})

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: EgoTac: In-the-wild Tactile Prediction from Egocentric Vision
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Wenkang Zhang, Chengbo Yuan, Zicheng Zhang, Zhengxue Cheng, Yang Gao
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: EgoTac is a model that predicts tactile information from egocentric videos, achieving high accuracy and enabling tactile-aware robot learning without direct tactile data collection.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: Touch is fundamental to dexterous manipulation, yet most egocentric human data increasingly used for robot learning lacks tactile information. Directly collecting large-scale tactile data is challenging due to sensor limitations, while human video data is abundant, contact-rich, and easily scalable. This motivates a natural question: can tactile signals be inferred purely from vision? To address this, we introduce EgoTac, a generalizable model that predicts rich tactile information directly from egocentric human videos. EgoTac is trained on a unified corpus of over 5.7M image-tactile pairs, covering both continuous force measurements and binary contacts. By learning from this diverse dataset, EgoTac captures nuanced touch dynamics across varied interactions. Experiments demonstrate strong performance: in-domain prediction achieves an average force error below 0.06N. On out-of-domain contact prediction benchmarks, EgoTac consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art contact estimator. It also captures the rise and fall patterns of real tactile data and enables zero-shot predictions on unconstrained real-world videos. Scaling analyses further reveal that both data diversity and volume improve performance steadily. Overall, EgoTac provides a scalable pathway to extract tactile priors from egocentric human videos, enabling broadly applicable tactile-aware robot learning. Related resources can be found at https://egotac.github.io/ .

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: R$^2$ Flow: Recursive Self-Improvement via Recursive Skill Evolution
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Mingda Zhang, Qiang Huang, Yanjin Li, Zijia Wang, Qika Lin
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: R$^2$ Flow introduces a recursive self-improvement framework for LLM-based agents that enhances task accuracy and skill evolution through flow-based training and evidence verification.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: LLM-based agents can improve themselves across tasks by reusing and revising the skills they orchestrate into executable procedures. Flow-based training fits this loop: it samples procedures in proportion to reward, and the flow through each skill credits it for the next library revision. Three obstacles stand in the way of making this self-improvement reliable: flow training suffers strategy collapse over tree-structured histories; nonnegative flow-based credit rewards frequent use as if it were benefit; and library edits rest on the task reward the policy optimizes. We introduce R$^2$ Flow, a recursive self-improvement framework that alternates policy learning, independent verification, and versioned skill-library updates on a shared-state orchestration graph. The graph merges histories that differ only in the order of independent steps, allowing flow training to pool evidence across equivalent executions. A flow-share readout of the trained flow, invariant to the backward policy, and a separate signed utility rank which skills to change, verifier evidence decides whether an edit is warranted, and a residual-variance plateau sets when to update. Committed edits reshape the graph the next policy learns on, realizing recursive skill evolution. Across question answering, mathematical reasoning, interactive decision making, and code generation, R$^2$ Flow improves task accuracy and library-edit precision over heuristic orchestration, reinforcement learning, and skill-evolution baselines, and transfers across executors. Code is available at https://github.com/beita6969/r2flow.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: EDAR: Learning Environment-Dependent Action Representations for Robotic Manipulation
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Yuecheng Xu, Tong Yang, Jingkai Jia, Chi Zhang, Xuelong Li
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: EDAR introduces an environment-dependent action representation for robotic manipulation, enhancing policy learning by linking motor commands to their contextual visual effects.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: Learning effective action representations is critical for robotic manipulation, where raw control trajectories are often noisy, redundant, and difficult to model directly. Existing methods mainly encode the structure of the action stream itself, treating the role of actions in the environment as implicit. Yet manipulation is about changing the world: the same action segment can induce different outcomes under different scene contexts, making action semantics inherently environment-dependent. We propose EDAR, an Environment-Dependent Action Representation that grounds action tokens in both executable control structure and expected visual consequences. By coupling motor commands with their environment-conditioned effects, EDAR encourages the learned action space to capture interaction semantics rather than merely command-level patterns. Experiments on simulated and real-robot manipulation benchmarks demonstrate that EDAR improves downstream policy learning, especially in long-horizon manipulation. These results highlight the importance of grounding action representations in executable control structure and environment-conditioned visual change.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: SimpleVLN: Towards Simple and Frontier Vision-Language Navigation
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Lingyi Hong, Weiren Cai, Jiayu Chen, Xinyu Zhou, Bailin He
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: SimpleVLN is a novel framework that enhances Vision-and-Language Navigation by leveraging native multimodal large language models without task-specific architectures, achieving superior success rates.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) requires embodied agents to ground language in visual observations and make long-horizon decisions. Existing methods often address these demands through task-specific architectures. As multimodal large language models (MLLMs) become increasingly capable, an important question remains: Have we truly unlocked the potential of native MLLMs for VLN before introducing task-specific architecture? We present SimpleVLN, an architecture-preserving framework developed through studies of navigation formulation, data construction, and optimization. At the formulation level, SimpleVLN combines single-turn decision inputs with fixed-budget global-local memory to efficiently use navigation history without unbounded context growth, while action chunks enable efficient output of multiple primitive actions per model invocation. For data construction, we combine expert demonstrations with policy-dependent DAgger experience and develop a scalable synthesis pipeline that generates large-scale tasks for reinforcement learning. At the optimization level, a progressive IL-DAgger-RL pipeline advances from action imitation to task-level outcome optimization. Comprehensive experiments validate the effectiveness of these three aspects. We instantiate SimpleVLN across multiple MLLM backbones and model sizes, demonstrating its generality. SimpleVLN achieves 76.7% and 80.1% success rates on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE splits, respectively, substantially outperforming existing methods. These results show that the navigation capabilities of native MLLMs can be effectively unlocked without task-specific architectural designs.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: Look Before You Act: Bridging Active Perception and Vision-Language-Action Models via Observation-Aligned Data Adaptation
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Jiawei Geng, Zhenyang Liu, Yuzheng Wu, Yongchong Gu, Yanwei Fu
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: The paper presents ActiveAlign, a framework that enhances robot manipulation success by aligning active perception with training distributions, achieving significant performance improvements in cluttered environments.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: Robots manipulating objects in clutter must decide not only how to act, but also where to look. Although active camera motion can expose an occluded target, it may move the robot into an initial observation-state distribution that differs from the manipulation policy's training distribution. We identify this problem as first-frame distribution sensitivity: under perturbed starts in LIBERO, naively prepending camera repositioning to pi_0.5 reduces success from 46.3% to 11.5%. We introduce ActiveAlign, a data-adaptation framework that trains a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policy from the states at which active perception terminates. A learned viewpoint module first generates a camera trajectory. Offline, ActiveAlign uses closed-loop alignment to connect the trajectory endpoint to an existing demonstration, replays the remaining manipulation trajectory, and retains successful continuations for fine-tuning. At deployment, the same viewpoint module precedes the adapted VLA without modifying its architecture. Across 40 LIBERO tasks, ActiveAlign achieves 70.7% success with pi_0 and 72.7% with pi_0.5, outperforming their standard-training baselines by 40.0% and 26.4% respectively. Matched-state and data-matched controls support gains beyond prefix shortening and generic viewpoint augmentation; OpenVLA and GR00T N1 also show the same trend. Success rate under physical occlusion in real world increases from 35/90 to 83/90. These results show that active perception benefits manipulation when policy training is aligned with the observation and robot-state distribution induced by viewpoint selection.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: AWAM: Active Trajectory-Conditioned View Imagination for Robust Robot Manipulation
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Jiawei Geng, Zhenyang Liu, Yuzheng Wu, Yanwei Fu
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: AWAM enhances robot manipulation in cluttered environments by actively planning observation trajectories and integrating imagined views with real-time data for improved action prediction.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: Rapid progress in embodied intelligence has enabled increasingly capable robots to follow language instructions and manipulate diverse objects. However, strong results in structured environments do not automatically transfer to open-world conditions, where clutter, occlusion, and changing viewpoints can obscure the spatial relationships required for action. To address this perceptual gap, a virtual active-perception paradigm is introduced. AWAM, an Active World-Action Model actively plans where to observe and imagines what will be seen along the planned trajectory before acting. Task-related virtual camera motion is predicted and used as a structured query into a geometry-conditioned world model, producing a reusable spatial prior for manipulation, which is later compressed into a fixed memory and fused with live observations through cross-attention for diffusion-based action prediction. AWAM achieves competitive success rates with 75.9% on LIBERO-Occ, 62.4% on LIBERO-Plus, 76.5% on RLBench-OG Occlusion1, and 94.4% in real-robot trials. These results support improved robustness to the evaluated occlusions and distribution shifts, addressing part of the gap between structured manipulation and less controlled environments.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: R$^2$Orch: Recursive Self-Improvement for Agent Orchestration via Self-Play within a Skill-Internalization Loop
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Mingda Zhang, Yun Huang, Qiang Huang, Yanjin Li, Rui Qian
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: R$^2$Orch introduces a recursive self-play framework for agent orchestration that enhances skill learning and evaluation, outperforming traditional methods across various complex tasks.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: In recent years, agentic orchestration has been widely applied to solve complex human tasks. However, existing orchestration learning still faces key challenges, including hand-designed curricula, advantage collapse when a task's rollouts all reach the same outcome, and unreliable evaluation signals that judge each skill by one noisy score. To address these challenges, we propose R$^2$Orch, a new paradigm of Recursive Self-Play Orchestration: an inner loop of self-play that improves the orchestrator on self-chosen tasks, and an outer loop that improves how the inner loop improves. To support this paradigm, we introduce Recursive Learnability, a training objective that rewards a Proposer for choosing tasks whose rollouts keep reaching different outcomes as skills are withdrawn. Built on this objective, we further propose Skill Withdrawal, in which the outer loop withdraws each skill once a controlled evaluation within self-play shows that the orchestrator performs as well without it. Moreover, the two loops form one cycle: failures are distilled into skills, skills into parameters, and withdrawals lead the Proposer to new failures, so the orchestrator moves toward zero-skill deployment. Experimental results on twelve datasets show that R$^2$Orch consistently outperforms baselines across question answering, math, code, and interactive tasks.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: QREF: Improving DeepSearch Agents by Aligning Search with Reasoning via Query Refinement and Evidence Filtering
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Yujia Chen, Yuhui Wang, Junzhe Wang, Shihan Dou, Di Liang
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: The QREF framework enhances DeepSearch agents by refining search queries and filtering evidence, significantly improving retrieval effectiveness without altering existing architectures.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: DeepSearch agents achieve strong performance on complex information-seeking tasks through iterative search and reasoning. However, they often issue intent-misaligned, under-constrained, or redundant search queries, resulting in poor evidence coverage and accumulating retrieval noise. To mitigate these limitations, we propose QREF, a plug-and-play Query Refiner and Evidence Filter. Specifically, the Query Refiner rewrites search queries according to the current reasoning intent while ensuring complementary coverage across each search batch. The Evidence Filter retains evidence relevant to both the current search batch and the reasoning objective, reducing distracting retrieval results. We initialize the Query Refiner with supervised fine-tuning and optimize it through reinforcement learning based on interactions with a real-world web search environment, reducing ineffective queries. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that our approach improves the performance of DeepSearch agents across four challenging benchmarks, achieving average relative Pass@1 improvements of 33.55% on WebSailor and 11.04% on TongyiDeepResearch without modifying architectures or retraining their reasoning policies. Compared with the original DeepSearch backbone without QREF, the RL-trained refiner reduces the fraction of query batches that lack discriminative retrieval anchors by 95%. Compared with the SFT-trained refiner, it also lowers the filter-based ineffective query ratio.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: Revisiting Embodied Chain-of-Thought for Generalizable Robot Manipulation
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Nan Sun, Yuan Zhang, Yongkun Yang, Wentao Zhao, Peiyan Li
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: This paper introduces ERVLA, a vision-language-action model that enhances robot manipulation by integrating grounded linguistic reasoning, achieving state-of-the-art performance while addressing autoregressive instability.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: Embodied chain-of-thought (CoT) aims to bridge linguistic reasoning with robotic control, yet its effective form and integration remain underexplored. In this paper, we revisit embodied CoT for robotic control at an unprecedented scale. We curate the largest embodied CoT corpus to date, comprising 978,743 trajectories, 226.3M samples, and 2592.5 hours of data. Through extensive experiments, we show that effective CoT must ground high-level semantic understaning in concrete linguistic action guidance -- such as end-effector movement and image-space trajectories -- whereas high-level reasoning alone yields marginal gains. More importantly, we identify that explicit CoT does not scale reliably as an autoregressive action prefix, suffering from compounding errors during inference. To address these challenges, we propose ERVLA, a vision-language-action (VLA) model that effectively leverages linguistic reasoning in generalizable robot manipulation. ERVLA is trained using a CoT-dropout strategy, allowing the model to leverage rich reasoning traces during training while predicting actions directly without CoT during inference to bypass autoregressive instability. This approach enables reliable scaling with increasing pre-training data. ERVLA achieves state-of-the-art results on LIBERO-Plus with an 86.9\% success rate and reaches 53.2\% on VLABench, showcasing superior performance in out-of-distribution settings. Furthermore, ERVLA outperforms competitive state-of-the-art baselines in real-robot experiments, especially in handling semantic ambiguity and long-horizon tasks. Code, data, and model checkpoints are available on the project website: https://taoshuaiz.github.io/ERVLA/.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: All-in-One Memory: Process-Rewarded Reinforcement Learning for Memory Agents
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Bingbing Wang, Jingjie Lin, Weiming Qiao, Jing Li, Ruifeng Xu
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: The All-in-One Memory (AiO-Mem) framework integrates retrieval and memory construction in reinforcement learning, enhancing answer accuracy in long-context tasks through a unified reward system.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: Large language models increasingly rely on external memory to answer queries grounded in long-horizon histories such as multi-session dialogues and lengthy documents. However, existing memory methods often optimize retrieval and memory construction separately, without a shared reward space for evaluating search, writing, and stopping decisions. To address this, we propose All-in-One Memory (AiO-Mem), which organizes these operations as transitions over a shared evidence state and directly evaluates the semantic quality of each action in a unified reward space. AiO-Mem compiles heterogeneous histories into source-traceable multi-view events, providing a shared substrate for retrieval and memory writing. A unified memory policy actor then rolls out complete interaction trajectories over this shared evidence state. A separate trajectory-conditioned process reward model is trained through evidence-grounded supervised fine-tuning and trajectory-level DPO to assign process scores to the collected trajectories. These scores are aggregated into an action-balanced trajectory reward and used by Process-Aligned DAPO (PA-DAPO) to optimize the memory policy. Across long-context memory benchmarks, AiO-Mem consistently improves answer accuracy over both static memory systems and RL-trained memory agents.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: EPIC-Bench: A Perception-Centric Benchmark for Fine-Grained Embodied Visual Grounding in Vision-Language Models
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Haozhe Shan, Xiancong Ren, Han Dong, Yingji Zhang, Haoyuan Shi
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: EPIC-Bench is a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating vision-language models' grounding capabilities in embodied scenarios through 6.6k annotated tuples across 23 tasks.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: While large vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly adopted as the perceptual backbone for embodied agents, their fundamental vision-language grounding (VLG) capability in embodied scenarios remains unexplored. We present \textbf{EPIC-Bench}, \textbf{E}mbodied \textbf{P}ercept\textbf{I}on Ben\textbf{C}hmark, a fine-grained grounding benchmark designed to systematically evaluate the VLG capabilities of VLMs in real-world embodied environments. EPIC-Bench comprises 6.6k meticulously human-annotated tuples (Image, Text, Mask) spanning three core stages of the embodied interaction pipeline: Target Localization, Navigation, and Manipulation. With 23 fine-grained tasks, multi-dimensional settings and evaluation over 80 leading VLMs, EPIC-Bench provides a diagnostic analysis.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: OS-Helix: Unifying GUI Interaction and Code Execution in Native Computer-Using Agents
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Bowen Yang, Kaiming Jin, Zichen Ding, Zhenyu Wu, Zehao Li
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: OS-Helix is a multimodal agent that integrates GUI interaction and code execution through hybrid training, achieving significant performance improvements in desktop automation tasks.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: Real desktop automation is neither purely visual nor purely programmatic. Agents must understand user-facing interfaces while efficiently manipulating files, scripts, and system state. However, native GUI/code coordination cannot be obtained by prompt-level tool composition. In our preliminary experiments, naively adding a code tool degrades a GUI agent, revealing that GUI/code routing must be internalized through training on high-quality hybrid data. We present OS-Helix, an end-to-end trained multimodal computer-using agent that unifies GUI actions and code execution in one action space. To construct the required supervision, we introduce application-artifact composition, pairing desktop applications with authentic file artifacts to instantiate executable Ubuntu states, and a decoupled instruction/evaluator generation pipeline that produces environment-grounded tasks whose final states can be verified regardless of the solution modality. We cold-start the policy with SFT on filtered hybrid data and further improve it through online RL in live desktop environments. For RL, we propose Step-balanced GSPO, which aggregates importance weight by action step rather than raw assistant tokens to prevent long code actions from dominating heterogeneous-action optimization. On OSWorld-Verified, OS-Helix-27B and OS-Helix-35B-A3B achieve relative improvements of 35.0% and 33.7% over their matched Qwen3.5 hybrid baselines, while OS-Helix-27B-RL further improves by 42.9% to reach 66.44% success. Ablations provide evidence consistent with contributions from learned GUI/code coordination, scalable verifiable supervision, and action step balanced optimization, while demonstrating cross-platform transfer on WindowsAgentArena. Our project homepage is at https://os-copilot.github.io/OS-Helix/.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: Imagine Before You Predict: Interleaved Latent Visual Reasoning for Video Event Prediction
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Tianxiang Jiang, Linquan Wu, Sheng Xia, Songze Li, Ziang Yan
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: Future-L1 introduces an interleaved latent visual reasoning framework for video event prediction, enhancing accuracy by preserving visual semantics during autoregressive decoding.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: Video event prediction (VEP) requires models to infer unobserved future states from partial video evidence. Existing video MLLMs usually verbalize intermediate future reasoning in text space: once visual evidence is verbalized, fine-grained motion, geometry, and interaction cues can be lost, leading to plausible but visually ungrounded hallucinations. We introduce Future-L1, an interleaved latent visual reasoning framework that lets an MLLM alternate between language tokens and continuous latent visual spans during autoregressive decoding. To train this capability, we construct Future-L1-50K by selecting examples where future visual hints help prediction and align latent states to future-frame embeddings, then further optimize sampled latent trajectories with LA-DAPO, a latent-aware RL objective with outcome-contrastive and temporal-diversity rewards. Future-L1 achieves new state-of-the-art results on both benchmarks: on FutureBench, it improves Qwen3-VL-8B from 61.0 to 85.4 and exceeds the previous best Video-CoE by 10.4 points; on TwiFF-Bench, it improves the average score from 2.44 to 3.04. These results suggest that future-oriented video reasoning benefits from preserving intermediate visual semantics in latent space rather than translating every reasoning step into text.

智能感知与无人系统实验室.title: Reinforcement Learning-driven Diffusion Models: Language, Vision, and Beyond
智能感知与无人系统实验室.authors_text: Zhiyuan Ma, Jiabao Wei, Tianyu Wang, Hanqing Wang, Jiadong Pan
智能感知与无人系统实验室.summary: This paper reviews and analyzes the integration of reinforcement learning into diffusion models, addressing limitations and proposing strategies for improved goal-directed generation across various applications.
智能感知与无人系统实验室.debug_abstract: Diffusion models (DMs) have steadily demonstrated outstanding performance in high-fidelity, controllable generation across diverse scenarios, following the "pretraining-finetuning" paradigm established in LLMs. Despite these advances, conventional DMs still face critical limitations in sophisticated reasoning, autonomous exploration of generation pathways, and adaptability to complex, human-aligned objectives. Inspired by RLHF's success in LLMs, RL has recently emerged as a pivotal post-training mechanism to iteratively refine DMs through reward-driven trajectory optimization. This paper presents the first comprehensive review of RL-driven DMs and an empirical analysis of how RL reshapes the diffusion process towards experience-centric, goal-directed generation. We propose a novel technical panorama elucidating RL's multifaceted roles in diffusion-based language, multimodal, robotic, and scientific models, with a granular focus on diffusion trajectory optimization and reward engineering. Through extensive experiments on multiple task-specific benchmarks, we systematically evaluate representative methods to intuitively highlight the advantages of different RL post-training strategies. Furthermore, we reveal and dissect three crucial bottlenecks that currently hinder the real-world deployment of RL-driven DMs: reward design fragility, exploration-exploitation trade-off in high-dimensional generation spaces, and training instability under sparse rewards. Based on these perspectives, we provide a principled roadmap for the integration of RL into DMs and outline promising future research directions for robust, interpretable RL-diffusion systems. We also construct a public repository to continuously track the latest developments in this rapidly evolving field: https://github.com/MAIR-Lab-HUST/Awesome-RL-for-Diffusion-Models.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: Distill to Think, Foresee to Act: Cognitive-Physical Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Driving
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Yang Wu, Qiang Meng, Zhaojiang Liu, Youquan Liu, Jian Yang
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: The CoPhy framework enhances autonomous driving by integrating cognitive understanding and foresight through a dual-reward reinforcement learning approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance and improved safety.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: Current end-to-end autonomous driving models are fundamentally constrained by the behavioral cloning ceiling of imitation learning. While reinforcement learning offers a path to smarter autonomy, it demands two missing pieces of infrastructure: (1) a cognitive foundation that understands traffic semantics and driving intent, and (2) a foresighted physical environment that can anticipate the consequences of candidate actions. To this end, we propose CoPhy, a CognitivePhysical reinforcement learning framework for autonomous driving. To distill to think, we distill VLM knowledge into the BEV encoder and then discard the VLM entirely, retaining cognitive ability at zero inference cost while releasing the cognitive channel as a pluggable interface for optional human language commands. To foresee to act, we build an auto-regressive BEV world model that explicitly predicts future semantic maps conditioned on candidate actions, serving as an interpretable physical sandbox from which safety metrics are directly derived. Built upon this dual infrastructure, we optimize the driving policy via GRPO with a novel dual-reward mechanism: a physical reward derived from BEV rollouts enforces hard safety constraints, while a cognitive reward from a language-aligned scorer ensures intent compliance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CoPhy not only achieves state-of-the-art results on NAVSIM v1 and v2 benchmarks, but also enables safer driving via cognitively informed scene compliance and flexible intent control through user-defined language instructions. Project page: https://wuyang98.github.io/CoPhy/.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: GTAGym: Real AAA Game Tasks Environment for Evaluation and Reinforcement Learning
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Jiajun Chen, Shicheng Fang, Jiahao Lu, Yuxin Wang, Xipeng Qiu
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: GTAGym introduces a framework for evaluating and training reinforcement learning agents on diverse tasks in GTA V, achieving notable performance improvements across various task categories.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: AAA games offer a rich testbed for evaluating agent perception, reasoning, and control. However, evaluating whether agents can complete tasks in AAA games is challenging and often human-annotated because task outcomes are often difficult to verify automatically, let alone applying it for Reinforcement Learning (RL). We introduce GTAGym, an environment and framework for evaluation and RL on GTA V tasks. Its evaluation benchmark, GTAVBench, derived from GTA V main-story missions, contains 103 online tasks reconstructed across nine task families, alongside 47 image-based shooting and sniping tasks using GTA V imagery. A web server provides access to the online environment and evaluation interface, supporting parallel testing through screenshots and keyboard-mouse actions with automatic engine-state outcome checks. We evaluate six frontier LLMs on GTAVBench with textual task instructions and on its GTAVBench-AGI branch, where instructions appear only in the first screenshot and a harness automatically compresses interaction history. The best configuration achieves 70.9% overall accuracy in GTAVBench-AGI, yet aerial navigation, evasion and interception remain difficult. GTAGym also provides a scalable generator that samples task parameters within user-specified ranges and option sets under fixed templates, creating batches of 3D and image-based shooting environments for RL with automatic reward and termination signals. LoRA RL of Qwen3.8-27B on generated on-foot navigation tasks improves the in-domain performance and transfers to out-of-domain task categories, and native GTA V tasks from 15% to 23%.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: Reward Shaping to Mitigate Reward Hacking in RLHF
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Jiayi Fu, Xuandong Zhao, Chengyuan Yao, Heng Wang, Qi Han
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: The paper presents Preference as Reward (PAR), a novel reward shaping method that mitigates reward hacking in RLHF by stabilizing training and enhancing data efficiency.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) is widely used to align large language models with human preferences, but it remains vulnerable to \emph{reward hacking}, whereby a policy exploits flaws in the reward function at the expense of the intended behavior. Reward shaping can stabilize training and partially mitigate reward hacking, yet its design principles remain underexplored. Our systematic study of common shaping methods suggests that shaped rewards should be bounded and should rise rapidly before gradually saturating. We introduce \emph{Preference as Reward} (PAR), which applies a sigmoid to centered rewards to produce a signal that reflects the reward model's latent preferences. We show that PAR has a variance-reduction property that stabilizes training and substantially widens the window for effective early stopping. Using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and Gemma2-2B, PAR consistently outperforms the other shaping methods evaluated and demonstrates high data efficiency and robustness. Comparisons with unshaped rewards across four base models and four reinforcement learning algorithms show that PAR is effective across models and particularly beneficial for actor--critic methods when value estimates become unstable. The code is available at https://github.com/PorUna-byte/PAR.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: DroneSegEdit: Adapting Pretrained Generative Editors for UAV Segmentation with Language-Grounded Verification
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Dehua Chen, Long Xin, Jiangtao Wei
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: DroneSegEdit enhances UAV segmentation by addressing the Grounding-Rendering Gap through language-grounded verification, achieving state-of-the-art performance on RIS-LAD and competitive results on other datasets.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: Recent work has shown that pretrained image generators can support diverse visual tasks. Yet directly applying them to language-guided unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) segmentation exposes a key limitation: a plausible mask may correspond to the wrong instance among small and repeated objects. We call this mismatch between mask rendering and expression-level target selection the Grounding-Rendering Gap. We present DroneSegEdit, which combines RGB proposal rendering with language-grounded, proposal-constrained verification to select supported foreground while retaining rendered geometry. DroneSegEdit adapts the open-weight LongCat-Image-Edit model using task-specific LoRA and fixed color-to-label decoding. For referring segmentation, a Language-Grounded Spatial Verifier (LGSV) reads hierarchical states from the frozen multimodal large language model backbone to derive expression-conditioned spatial evidence, which is mapped back to the rendered proposal without introducing foreground outside it. On RIS-LAD, DroneSegEdit reaches a new state of the art at 52.78 mIoU, 7.16 points above the previous best. It remains competitive overall on UAVid-RIS and VDD-RIS, with its clearest class-wise gains on compact, application-relevant categories, notably vehicles and humans. A separate verifier-free experiment extends the RGB interface to full-scene parsing: a task-specific adapter jointly renders all classes from one task-level instruction without enumerating class names or palette colors.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: Partition, Refine, and Detect: Preserving Novel Category Capacity in Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Wei Zhang, Zhu Teng, Zhixiang Chi, Junnan Zou, Yi Liu
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: PR-OVD enhances open-vocabulary object detection by partitioning and refining representations to better accommodate novel categories, achieving significant performance improvements over existing methods.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: Open-vocabulary object detection (OVD) expects the model trained on base classes to recognize both base and novel classes at inference. Typical methods rely on CLIP-style vision-language embeddings, yet the learned space is often biased toward base categories, with limited effective capacity preserved for novel concepts. Such a base-dominated representation can compress novel semantics, leading to semantic collapse and mis-calibrated confidence at inference. To address this issue, we present PR-OVD, a partition-and-refine framework that explicitly reserves capacity for novel categories and strengthens category separation, while being seamlessly integrated into different detector architectures. Specifically, PR-OVD first performs coarse partitioning to build global divisions for base, novel, and an explicit background partition in both visual and textual modalities, preventing object-irrelevant embeddings from leaking into category-specific representations. It then applies category-level refinement within each partition to sharpen decision boundaries and alleviate the lack of fine-grained region-level pretraining in CLIP. To further provide reliable visual anchors for novel categories, we design a cognitively inspired Structure Prompt (SP) that encodes both egocentric attributes and allocentric context, facilitating stable partition-and-refine learning. Extensive experiments on two OVD benchmarks show that PR-OVD delivers an average 6.5\% proportional improvement on novel categories over the state-of-the-art methods. Notably, PR-OVD also benefits other open-vocabulary tasks, including segmentation and classification, further confirming its effectiveness and generality.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: RedDiffuser: Auditing Multimodal Safety Failures in Vision-Language Models via Reinforced Diffusion
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Ruofan Wang, Xingjun Ma
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: RedDiffuser introduces a reinforcement-based framework for auditing multimodal safety failures in Vision-Language Models, revealing significant vulnerabilities under harmful contextual exposure.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are increasingly deployed in open-ended environments, where ensuring reliable safety under multimodal inputs is critical. However, existing evaluations remain largely instruction-centric, focusing on explicit malicious queries while overlooking a more realistic and underexplored risk: whether safety alignment remains robust under harmful contextual exposure. This limitation is particularly important for multimodal systems, where visual inputs can substantially steer model behavior and render text-only auditing insufficient. In this work, we study multimodal safety auditing under harmful contextual exposure, asking whether VLMs can maintain safe behavior when partial toxic text is paired with visual context. To enable systematic auditing, we propose RedDiffuser (RedDiff), a reinforcement-based framework that leverages diffusion models to generate semantically coherent visual inputs for black-box safety testing. By combining greedy prompt search with reinforcement optimization, RedDiffuser uncovers high-risk multimodal inputs that expose latent safety failures. Extensive experiments on both open-source and commercial VLMs show that such context-conditioned failures are widespread. On LLaVA, RedDiffuser increases unsafe response rates by up to 10.69% on the original set and 8.91% on a hold-out set, with strong transferability to Gemini and LLaMA-Vision. These vulnerabilities persist even under external safety guardrails, suggesting that current system-level safety mechanisms remain insufficient for realistic multimodal risks. Our findings reveal a critical blind spot in existing safety evaluations and establish context-aware multimodal auditing as an essential paradigm for diagnosing hidden vulnerabilities in modern VLM systems.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: ODEAction: From Predicting Chunks to Evolving Actions
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Qishen Wang, Pengxiang Ding, Shifeng Bao, Mingyang Sun, Hengtao Li
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: ODEAction introduces a continuous action evolution framework using ODEs to enhance vision-language-action models, improving task performance and trajectory quality over traditional chunk-based methods.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models typically generate actions in chunks, dividing continuous robot execution into separately predicted action chunks, which can introduce discontinuities at chunk boundaries. We propose ODEAction, a chunk-free action generation paradigm that replaces action chunk prediction with Continuous Action Evolution. We use an ordinary differential equation (ODE) to describe the continuous evolution of actions, and define the vector field of this ODE as the Action Transition Field to characterize how actions evolve with respect to evolution time. During inference, the model takes the current action as the initial condition and numerically solves the ODE defined by the learned Action Transition Field, thereby recursively generating subsequent actions with explicit dependencies. ODEAction is implemented as a modular action head that can be integrated with different vision-language backbones. Experiments on LIBERO, EBench, RoboTwin, and real-robot tasks show that, compared with action-chunk-based baselines, ODEAction improves both task performance and trajectory quality, with particularly pronounced gains on fine manipulation tasks.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: Adaptive Visual KV Cache Reuse for Efficient Multi-Turn Iterative Multimodal Reasoning
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Mengzhao Wang, Yanli Ji, Wangmeng Zuo, Chongjun Tu
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: The paper presents an adaptive visual KV cache reuse framework that enhances multi-turn visual reasoning efficiency by optimizing visual encoding and interaction without additional training.
