Ablations provide evidence consistent with contributions from learned GUI/code coordination, scalable verifiable supervision, and action step balanced optimization, while demonstrating cross-platform transfer on WindowsAgentArena. Our project homepage is at https://os-copilot.github.io/OS-Helix/.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: Imagine Before You Predict: Interleaved Latent Visual Reasoning for Video Event Prediction
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Tianxiang Jiang, Linquan Wu, Sheng Xia, Songze Li, Ziang Yan
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: Future-L1 introduces an interleaved latent visual reasoning framework for video event prediction, enhancing accuracy by preserving visual semantics during autoregressive decoding.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: Video event prediction (VEP) requires models to infer unobserved future states from partial video evidence. Existing video MLLMs usually verbalize intermediate future reasoning in text space: once visual evidence is verbalized, fine-grained motion, geometry, and interaction cues can be lost, leading to plausible but visually ungrounded hallucinations. We introduce Future-L1, an interleaved latent visual reasoning framework that lets an MLLM alternate between language tokens and continuous latent visual spans during autoregressive decoding. To train this capability, we construct Future-L1-50K by selecting examples where future visual hints help prediction and align latent states to future-frame embeddings, then further optimize sampled latent trajectories with LA-DAPO, a latent-aware RL objective with outcome-contrastive and temporal-diversity rewards. Future-L1 achieves new state-of-the-art results on both benchmarks: on FutureBench, it improves Qwen3-VL-8B from 61.0 to 85.4 and exceeds the previous best Video-CoE by 10.4 points; on TwiFF-Bench, it improves the average score from 2.44 to 3.04. These results suggest that future-oriented video reasoning benefits from preserving intermediate visual semantics in latent space rather than translating every reasoning step into text.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: Reinforcement Learning-driven Diffusion Models: Language, Vision, and Beyond
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Zhiyuan Ma, Jiabao Wei, Tianyu Wang, Hanqing Wang, Jiadong Pan
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: This paper reviews and analyzes the integration of reinforcement learning into diffusion models, addressing limitations and proposing strategies for improved goal-directed generation across various applications.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: Diffusion models (DMs) have steadily demonstrated outstanding performance in high-fidelity, controllable generation across diverse scenarios, following the "pretraining-finetuning" paradigm established in LLMs. Despite these advances, conventional DMs still face critical limitations in sophisticated reasoning, autonomous exploration of generation pathways, and adaptability to complex, human-aligned objectives. Inspired by RLHF's success in LLMs, RL has recently emerged as a pivotal post-training mechanism to iteratively refine DMs through reward-driven trajectory optimization. This paper presents the first comprehensive review of RL-driven DMs and an empirical analysis of how RL reshapes the diffusion process towards experience-centric, goal-directed generation. We propose a novel technical panorama elucidating RL's multifaceted roles in diffusion-based language, multimodal, robotic, and scientific models, with a granular focus on diffusion trajectory optimization and reward engineering. Through extensive experiments on multiple task-specific benchmarks, we systematically evaluate representative methods to intuitively highlight the advantages of different RL post-training strategies. Furthermore, we reveal and dissect three crucial bottlenecks that currently hinder the real-world deployment of RL-driven DMs: reward design fragility, exploration-exploitation trade-off in high-dimensional generation spaces, and training instability under sparse rewards. Based on these perspectives, we provide a principled roadmap for the integration of RL into DMs and outline promising future research directions for robust, interpretable RL-diffusion systems. We also construct a public repository to continuously track the latest developments in this rapidly evolving field: https://github.com/MAIR-Lab-HUST/Awesome-RL-for-Diffusion-Models.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: ExRL: Sample-Efficient Online Adaptation of Long-Chunk Policies via Execution Length Control
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Xu Luo, Jiaying Yang, Hao Wu, Junlin Xie, Zijin Hong
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: ExRL enhances long-chunk policy adaptation by optimizing execution lengths instead of actions, achieving sample efficiency in real-world robotics with minimal tuning.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Predicting long action chunks, often spanning dozens of timesteps, has become a key ingredient in increasingly capable robot policies. In this paper, we find that adapting these long-chunk policies with existing reinforcement learning (RL) methods can require many online samples due to the high dimensionality of the action chunks being optimized, making such adaptation impractical in real-world scenarios where interaction data are costly to collect. Our key insight is to shift adaptation from optimizing actions to optimizing how long to execute each predicted action chunk. This keeps the adaptation space low-dimensional while its expressivity grows with the chunk size. We thus introduce Execution at the Right Length (ExRL), a simple approach which augments the base policy with a lightweight adapter that predicts the execution length of each chunk and is trained using off-policy RL algorithms. Across simulation benchmarks and real-world robotic tasks, ExRL enables sample-efficient adaptation of a diverse range of long-chunk policies with minimal task-specific hyperparameter tuning.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: From Egocentric Human Video to Robot Manipulation in the Era of Embodied Intelligence
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Yi Wang, Jingqiu Wu, Lei Yao, Zhaoshuo Li, Haoyu Zhu
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The paper introduces Ego2Robot learning, leveraging egocentric human video to develop robot manipulation policies through four distinct learning paradigms while addressing associated challenges.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Egocentric human video (EHV) records close-range hand-object interaction (HOI) and the temporal structure of everyday activities, offering a potentially scalable source of experience for robot manipulation. Using this experience for robot control requires recovering useful supervision without recorded robot actions and accounting for differences in morphology, viewpoint, and action space. We define Ego2Robot learning as the process of learning or adapting robot manipulation policies from EHV, organized into four learning paradigms: explicit embodiment transfer, explicit action and task supervision, egocentric video representation pretraining, and latent action and dynamics modeling. The four paradigms differ in what they derive from human video: robot-format demonstrations, interpretable supervision, visual representations, or predictive models of actions and dynamics. For each paradigm, we trace what EHV information is extracted, how robot policies use it, and when the additional data is required. Besides, we review the benchmark datasets that cover EHV, robot demonstrations, and synthetic and simulated resources. This paper links EHV data's contribution to the task information preserved and the robot-specific grounding used during training or deployment. Finally, we identify challenges in physical feasibility, agent coordination, in-context adaptation, controlled evaluation, and predictive control.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: EgoHMP: Achieving Precise Human Motion Prediction in 3D Scenes via Egocentric Cues
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Xin Zhao, Pengzhan Zhou, Ziyi Li, Riheng Jia, Zhida Qin
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: EgoHMP leverages egocentric views and head motions to enhance human motion prediction accuracy in 3D scenes, achieving state-of-the-art performance through innovative feature alignment and motion synthesis techniques.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: The complex interactive dependencies between human behavior and 3D scenes make accurately predicting human intent a major challenge for human motion prediction (HMP). While recent studies use human gaze to infer intent, gaze signals suffer from ambiguity, drift, and a reliance on eye-tracking hardware. Research in cognitive science indicates that egocentric views inherently encode potential interactions, while head motion serves as a crucial precursor in motion planning. Motivated by this, we propose EgoHMP, a novel framework that uses egocentric views and head motions as robust carriers of interaction intent. By translating this intent into an envisioning of future interactions, EgoHMP achieves precise HMP in 3D scenes. EgoHMP first employs a vision-motion alignment encoder to align the visual and motion feature spaces. Based on these aligned features, an egocentric intent predictor with a modality-aware modulation mechanism adaptively suppresses invalid interaction cues to predict an accurate interaction probability map. Furthermore, to enhance the stability and realism of the generated motions, we propose a contact-aware motion decoder. Specifically, inspired by the human cognitive process of planning trajectories prior to action execution, we first predict a global trajectory to serve as a self-prompt, effectively mitigating the optimization conflict in diffusion models. Subsequently, we introduce a multi-stage denoiser, which relieves motion artifacts by incorporating human contact modeling through a multi-stage optimization strategy. Finally, a GCN-based motion decoder is employed to synthesize physically plausible and semantically consistent motions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EgoHMP achieves state-of-the-art performance.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: A 10K drone image dataset with component-level annotations for rooftop photovoltaic inspection
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Penglei Zhang, Wan Zhang, Ruizhe Deng, Bo Chen, Wenhao Duan
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The PVIS-10K dataset consists of 10,065 annotated drone images for precise component-level inspection of rooftop photovoltaic systems, enhancing localization and counting capabilities.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Component-level information supports rooftop photovoltaic (PV) inspection, but recognizing individual components across complex scenes remains challenging. We present PVIS-10K, a dataset of 10,065 drone images with component-level annotations covering 63,632 physical PV modules across 22 rooftop installations. The high-resolution red-green-blue (RGB) images were acquired by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs, also known as drones) in Ningbo, Shaoxing and Shenzhen, China. Multi-angle oblique observations capture installation-height and scale variation, dense arrangements, occlusion, shadows and reflections. Three-dimensional delineation, reprojection and image-by-image review produced 3,516,675 image-level polygon annotations, stored in Common Objects in Context (COCO) format. Station-disjoint partitions support evaluation on unseen stations within and across cities. Four supervised models and text-prompted zero-shot Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3) provide full-resolution benchmarks of instance matching and foreground coverage. PVIS-10K supports component localization, delineation and image-based counting for drone-based rooftop PV inspection research.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: ReACT: Reflection-Consistent Modulation and Cross-Load Consistency for Humanoid Velocity Tracking Under Asymmetric Loads
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Xianghui Wang, Aoran Fu, Liyou Luo, Shanze Wang, Xiaoyu Shen
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The ReACT framework enhances humanoid velocity tracking under asymmetric loads by using disturbance modulation and cross-load consistency training, improving navigation accuracy and safety.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: In recent years, humanoid loco-manipulation has progressed to whole-body grasping, lifting, and transport. A basic requirement underlying these tasks is carrying the object to its destination, which depends on the locomotion controller accurately executing velocity commands from the navigation policy. However, carrying an object in one hand introduces a persistent asymmetric upper-body load that can degrade velocity tracking. Persistent tracking biases can accumulate into position and heading deviations, increasing the risk of collisions and navigation failure. To address this problem, we present ReACT, a framework for accurate velocity tracking under asymmetric upper-body loads. Reflection-consistent disturbance modulation uses the estimated wrench to modulate actor features for load compensation while preserving action correspondence under reflected observations. Cross-load tracking consistency training compares loaded and unloaded conditions under the same velocity commands to promote consistent velocity tracking across loading conditions. Simulation experiments on a Unitree G1 humanoid robot show improved velocity tracking and reduced directional bias under varying asymmetric loads. Real-world experiments demonstrate collision-free goal reaching in all 40 tested navigation trials under unilateral hand loads with a fixed mapless navigation policy.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: REINS: A Self-Evolving Agent Harness for Real-Time Trajectory Planning
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Zhihong Cui, Hengyu Liu, Haoran Tang, Shijun Liu, Amir Taherkordi
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: REINS is a self-evolving agent harness that enables real-time trajectory planning by integrating LLM outputs with a dynamic model, verification, and indexed memory for efficient decision-making.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Agent harnesses -- runtime scaffolds that wrap an LLM's reasoning loop with tool dispatch, verification, and persistent memory -- have become the standard substrate for deploying LLMs as autonomous agents, as demonstrated by Claude Code and Codex in software engineering. In trajectory planning, however, this paradigm has not taken hold: existing LLM-based trajectory planning methods either keep the LLM in the decision loop, exceeding the millisecond-level control budget, or offload it to offline rules or training-time supervision -- leaving the runtime planner non-evolving. Intermediate hybrids still lack the verification-and-consolidation loop that makes harnesses reliable. We ask: what runtime harness would let an LLM planner meet real-time constraints while self-evolving into a deployable one? We propose REINS, a harness built on three LLM-planner couplings: LLM outputs are (i) grounded to a learned variable-level dynamics model, (ii) verified via calibrated predicates and forward rollout, and (iii) consolidated into an indexed rule memory that serves future scenes in O(log n) without re-invoking the LLM. The harness closes a self-evolution loop: familiar scenes resolve by memory lookup; novel scenes invoke the LLM, whose verified outputs enrich the memory. Without modifying LLM weights, REINS attains 98%+ compliance, nearly 50% collision reduction, and 1.9-4.6 ms latency on simulated and real-world benchmarks at the tactical decision layer, with LLM invocation rate monotonically declining as memory matures. Code: https://github.com/ZhihongCui/REINS

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: SituRecBench: Evaluating Frontier Models as Situated Recommendation Assistants in 3D Environments
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Jingtong Yang, Dongding Lin, Jian Wang, Wenjie Li
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: SituRecBench is a benchmark for assessing vision-language models as interactive recommendation assistants in 3D environments, addressing challenges in spatial navigation and user interaction.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Recommender systems are transitioning from static retrieval engines into interactive assistants grounded in physical environments. However, current studies largely neglect the combined complexities of spatial navigation, visual grounding, and multi-turn social interaction. To bridge this gap, we introduce SituRecBench, an interactive benchmark for evaluating frontier vision-language models (VLMs) as situated recommendation assistants within high-fidelity 3D environments. We reformulate recommendation as a situated assistance process in which an assistant interacts with a user while sharing the user's egocentric view. Our benchmark simulates real-world shopping environments (e.g., supermarkets and home furnishings stores), requiring assistants to elicit preferences, ground recommendations in the environment, and guide the user to relevant locations through dialogue. The benchmark evaluates dialogue quality, recommendation utility, and navigation effectiveness through a unified interactive protocol. Extensive experiments reveal persistent challenges in spatial grounding and preference elicitation, highlighting limitations in their ability to integrate global contextual information with local observations. SituRecBench provides a rigorous foundation for advancing the development of situated assistants in the real world.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: MoT3DVG: A Benchmark for Outdoor 3D Visual Grounding with Motion-Aware Descriptions and Temporal Cues
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Shijia Zhao, Xusheng Guo, Qiming Xia, Xun Huang, Kezheng Xiong
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: MoT3DVG introduces a comprehensive dataset and DynaVG framework for outdoor 3D visual grounding, enhancing localization of dynamic objects using motion-aware descriptions and temporal cues.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: 3D visual grounding (3DVG) localizes language-referred objects in 3D scenes, with broad applicability in both indoor and outdoor environments. However, existing 3DVG research focuses on static indoor objects, limiting its use in dynamic outdoor autonomous driving. Motion descriptions, which capture the temporal dynamics of moving objects, offer a promising way to address this challenge. We therefore introduce MoT3DVG, a large-scale dataset for dynamic-aware outdoor 3DVG with temporally evolving motion descriptions. It contains 850 scenarios with 31,128 frames from nuScenes dataset, and provides 144,568 language prompts with motion-aware descriptions for dynamic objects across time. We further propose DynaVG, a novel framework that effectively leverages temporal cues for outdoor 3DVG. In addition to the standard modality-specific encoders, DynaVG introduces a Short-Long Integrated Dynamic Encoding (SLIDE) module before the language-point cloud alignment. SLIDE models both local motion cues and global temporal context via short-term window encoding and long-term window shifting. Extensive experiments demonstrate its state-of-the-art performance on MoT3DVG, validating the effectiveness of motion-aware encoding. Our work reveals open challenges and promising directions for future research in outdoor 3DVG.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Preference-Guided Adversarial Policy Optimization for Long-Tail Robust Driving
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Tong Nie, Yihong Tang, Junlin He, Yuewen Mei, Jie Sun
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The paper introduces ADV-0, a closed-loop optimization framework that aligns adversarial training with driving policy objectives to enhance robustness against rare, safety-critical driving scenarios.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Deploying autonomous driving systems requires robustness against long-tail scenarios that are rare but safety-critical. While adversarial training offers a promising solution, existing methods typically decouple scenario generation from policy optimization and rely on heuristic surrogates. This leads to objective misalignment and fails to capture the shifting failure modes of evolving policies. This paper presents ADV-0, a closed-loop min-max optimization framework that treats the interaction between driving policy (defender) and adversarial agent (attacker) as a zero-sum Markov game. By aligning the attacker's utility directly with the defender's objective, we reveal the optimal adversary distribution. To make this tractable, we cast dynamic adversary evolution as iterative preference learning, efficiently approximating this optimum and offering an algorithm-agnostic solution to the game. Theoretically, ADV-0 converges to a Nash Equilibrium and maximizes a certified lower bound on real-world performance. Experiments indicate that it effectively exposes diverse safety-critical failures and greatly enhances the generalizability of both learned policies and motion planners against unseen long-tail risks.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: World Models as Adversaries: Multi-Agent Self-Play Fine-Tuning for Robust Motion Planning
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Tong Nie, Yuewen Mei, Junlin He, Yihong Tang, Jian Sun
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The paper presents Adversarial World Modeling (AWM), a multi-agent self-play framework enhancing robust motion planning for autonomous vehicles in rare, critical traffic scenarios through adversarial training.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Robust motion planning in dense traffic requires autonomous vehicles to interact in rare and safety-critical scenarios that are underrepresented in naturalistic driving data. Although adversarial training offers a feasible solution, existing methods often rely on external scenario generators, heuristic perturbations, or simulator-heavy rollouts, which makes them difficult to integrate with modern autoregressive planners. Here, we cast adversarially robust planner learning as a constrained min-max game and propose Adversarial World Modeling (AWM), a theoretically grounded multi-agent self-play fine-tuning framework. Since solving the exact game is intractable, AWM introduces a principled decoupled solver. In the inner minimization, the planner's predictive world model is converted into a role-conditioned adversary that learns sparse, scene-adaptive attack coalitions via counterfactual credit assignment. In the outer maximization, the ego planner optimizes a regret-aware robust best response against the frozen AWM, utilizing tail-risk weighting and reference-anchored trust regions to improve hard-case recovery while preserving nominal driving behavior. Experiments on the nuPlan and InterPlan benchmarks demonstrate that our method generates transferable adversarial interactions and yields a robust planner that achieves competitive closed-loop performance in both nominal and highly interactive long-tail scenarios. Theoretical analysis justifies the decoupled solver and the main optimization components.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: SurgEye: Instruction Tuning-Free Perception-Reasoning Framework for Surgical Scene Understanding
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Qing Xu, Xiechen Shen, Xianjian He, Guqiao Liang, Zixiao Chai
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: SurgEye introduces a novel instruction tuning-free framework for surgical scene understanding, leveraging Routed Multi-Task Perception and Agentic Compositional Reasoning to enhance reasoning without extensive data curation.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Surgical scene understanding is pivotal for computer-assisted intervention, yet demands compositional reasoning across instruments, anatomy, and workflow. Existing surgical vision-language models rely on instruction tuning with large-scale question-answer pairs, entailing laborious data curation and costly retraining. To bridge this gap, we propose SurgEye, a perception-reasoning framework that grounds reasoning in a vision foundation model without instruction tuning. Specifically, we devise Routed Multi-Task Perception (RMP) that routes the vision foundation model through task-specific pathways learned from public perception labels, producing spatial and temporal evidence. We further introduce Agentic Compositional Reasoning (ACR) that employs a frozen large language model to coordinate RMP specialists and temporal memory as callable tools, composing evidence across tasks and time into grounded answers. Moreover, we construct SurgEye-Bench spanning eight surgical procedures, pairing each question with perception labels for verifiable evaluation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SurgEye outperforms state-of-the-arts in surgical reasoning. The source code will be available.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: ResponsibleRobotBench: Benchmarking Risk-Aware Task-Level Decision Making for Robotic Manipulation with Large Multimodal Models
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Lei Zhang, Ju Dong, Kaixin Bai, Minheng Ni, Yu Fu
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: ResponsibleRobotBench evaluates risk-aware decision-making in robotic manipulation, highlighting discrepancies between safety predictions and task success across multimodal models.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Safe task-level manipulation requires a planner to recognize hazards, select appropriate mitigation actions, and satisfy their execution prerequisites without abandoning the original goal. We introduce ResponsibleRobotBench, a benchmark of 23 manipulation task configurations with separately specified goals and safety conditions. It connects hazard-category predictions, planned actions, execution feedback, and terminal outcomes at the episode level. Across evaluations of five large multimodal models, terminal safety and safe task completion can diverge: defense prompts increase terminal safety for three tested models but affect safe success in different directions. Correct hazard-category predictions also fail to ensure executable mitigation. In a cutting task under the default configuration, GPT-4o mini identifies the human hazard in all 100 episodes but never requests assistance, and every episode ends unsafe. Offering a help action and actually requesting it lead to different comparisons: outcomes differ between action menus even for a model that never requests help, and repeated requests can leave execution failures unresolved. Imitation-learning evaluations and physical robot sequences illustrate the need to coordinate mitigation with goal actions. Together, these results motivate evaluating mitigation selection, action prerequisites, and recovery alongside hazard recognition and terminal outcomes. The appendix provides task definitions, checker conditions, and prompts. Project website: https://responsible-robot-benchmark.github.io/.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Toward Counterfactual Learning for Selective Re-Examination in Agentic Visual Search
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Ao Chen, Shengchao Chen, Yan Luximon
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The paper introduces ReSee, a benchmark for re-examination in visual search, and proposes CARE, a reinforcement learning method that enhances decision-making accuracy and selectivity in agentic visual search tasks.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Visual search over high-resolution images requires a vision-language model (VLM) not only to determine where to inspect, but also whether another observation is warranted before committing to an answer. Existing prompting, demonstrations, and outcome-based reinforcement learning can encourage re-examination, yet do not directly supervise whether it is beneficial at a particular search state. We introduce ReSee, a benchmark of re-examination decisions comprising 3,227 visual-search trajectories and 8,827 explicit commit-or-re-examine decisions, with counterfactual adjudication that distinguishes states where additional inspection is warranted from those where commitment is preferable. Building on this formulation, we propose CARE (Counterfactual Advantage for Re-Examination), a decision-level reinforcement learning method that compares paired continuations under commit and re-examine verdicts from the same search state. Their cost-aware return difference estimates the counterfactual value of an additional observation and is assigned only to the corresponding verdict tokens, providing localized credit for whether search should continue. Experiments expose limited re-examination selectivity in existing VLMs and show that CARE significantly improves accuracy and decision selectivity over GRPO across two backbones, with higher accuracy and fewer visual requests on six unseen OOD benchmarks.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: ReWorld: Multi-Dimensional Reward Modeling for Embodied Video Generation
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Baorui Peng, Wenyao Zhang, Liang Xu, Bohan Li, Hu Zhu
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: ReWorld introduces a reinforcement learning framework that enhances embodied video generation by aligning it with physical realism, task logic, and visual quality through a multi-dimensional reward model.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Current embodied video generation models primarily emphasize visual generative quality while overlooking physical fidelity, dynamic consistency, and task logic, especially for contact-rich manipulation tasks, which limits their applicability to downstream tasks. In this paper, we introduce ReWorld, a framework aimed to employ reinforcement learning to align the video generation with physical realism, task completion capability, embodiment plausibility and visual quality. Specifically, we first construct a large-scale (~235K) video preference dataset and employ it to train a hierarchical reward model designed to capture multi-dimensional reward consistent with human preferences. We further propose a practical alignment algorithm that post-trains flow-based video generators using this reward through a computationally efficient PPO-style algorithm. Comprehensive experiments and theoretical analysis demonstrate that ReWorld significantly improves the physical fidelity, logical coherence, embodiment and visual quality of generated rollouts, outperforming previous methods.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: SurgStream: A Workflow-Anchored Proactive Streaming Framework and Benchmark for Real-Time Surgical Video Understanding
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Ruipeng Ma, Qing Xu, Jie Liang, Zhen Chen
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: SurgStream introduces a proactive framework for real-time surgical video understanding, enhancing memory retention and timely responses through Workflow-Anchored Memory and Deadline-aware Transition Learning.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Surgical video understanding is essential for intraoperative assistance such as workflow monitoring, instrument preparation and procedural documentation. Delivering such assistance in real time requires a model to jointly perceive the ongoing scene, remember past surgical events, and respond before clinically relevant moments pass. Existing approaches provide limited support for jointly retaining procedural evidence and deciding when to respond in streaming surgical video. In this work, we propose SurgStream, a workflow-anchored proactive streaming framework for real-time surgical video understanding. We first introduce Workflow-Anchored Memory (WAM) to record structured instrument-action-target observations and fold them into phase-level summaries, providing compact and queryable surgical memory. Deadline-aware Transition Learning (DTL) is then devised to supervise response states within clinical windows, enabling timely responses before procedural deadlines. We further introduce SurgStream-Bench, comprising 11.7K streaming interactions across various tasks covering real-time perception, backward memory queries, forward proactive QA, proactive alerts and caption memory. Experiments on SurgStream-Bench show gains over state-of-the-art methods, especially in memory and forward proactive QA. The source code will be available.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: DiffWBC: Unlocking Steerable General Humanoid Motion Tracking via One-Step Diffusion Whole-Body Control
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Yifei Huang, Yazhao Yang, Weijia Li, Zhiheng Ma, Dian Shen
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: DiffWBC introduces a one-step diffusion model for humanoid motion tracking, enabling adaptive control, zero-shot steering, and failure discovery without simulations, outperforming existing methods.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: General humanoid motion trackers typically rely on deterministic policies that cannot adapt online without brittle reference editing or costly retraining. We present DiffWBC, shifting whole-body control to a generative paradigm via a one-step diffusion model. By modeling distributions over future trajectories, DiffWBC unifies general tracking, test-time steering, and simulation-free failure discovery within a single controller: (1) Generative general tracking: DiffWBC requires a single forward pass per 50 Hz control step and can be distilled from an RL teacher or trained from scratch via model-based RL, achieving the lowest local tracking error among six general trackers on held-out benchmarks (20.1 mm on BONES) and deploying on a physical Unitree G1. (2) Zero-shot test-time steering: differentiable cost gradients and body-group masks modulate the frozen controller online, substantially outperforming kinematic reference editing (0.84 clean pass at 1.25 m ceiling vs. 0.10) and zero-shot generalizing across hurdles, spatial reaching, actuator faults, and tray balancing. (3) Simulation-free failure discovery: plan dispersion across generation noise effectively identifies physical tracking failures (91% precision in top 2%) without physics simulations; targeted fine-tuning on flagged clips resolves 50% of failure cases. Videos and interactive demonstrations are available at https://diffwbc.github.io/#selfassess.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Beyond Trial-and-Error: A Geospatial-Guided Active Reasoning Framework for Robust Aerial Vision-and-Language Navigation
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Jiawei Ge, Wenkang Gong, Jiuxin Cao, Bo Liu, Lei Cui
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: GeoReasoner introduces a geospatial-guided active reasoning framework for Aerial Vision-and-Language Navigation, enhancing goal localization accuracy in urban environments beyond reactive methods.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Aerial Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) requires UAVs to locate language-specified goals in large-scale urban environments, where objects often appear small and visually ambiguous from high-altitude viewpoints. Existing methods largely follow a reactive paradigm common in indoor VLN, repeatedly updating navigation states from local observations while underutilizing the geospatial structure that remains stable during navigation. As a result, visually similar distractors can cause a reactive goal search to repeatedly reinforce locally plausible goal hypotheses based on passively accumulated evidence, leading to unreliable localization. To address this, we propose GeoReasoner, a robust framework that shifts the paradigm of Aerial VLN from reactive trial-and-error to geospatial-guided active reasoning. Specifically, GeoReasoner first performs pre-search geospatial reasoning to derive region-level priors and constrain the goal hypothesis space. Building on these, it further conducts hypothesis-driven exploration to actively acquire discriminative evidence and refine competing goal hypotheses. Finally, consistency-aware goal verification adversarially assesses complementary evidence sources before stopping, hence reducing premature or erroneous goal confirmations. Experiments on the real-world CityNav benchmark demonstrate that GeoReasoner sets a new SOTA among zero-shot Aerial VLN methods while competing favorably with supervised approaches.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: What Should a Navigator Remember? Spatiotemporal Memory for Zero-Shot Vision-Language Navigation
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Yuhang Peng, Zhikai Wang, Ziyi Wang, Jiaru Zhong, Xiaoji Zheng
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: This paper presents a zero-shot vision-language navigation system that optimally organizes spatiotemporal memory to enhance navigation performance without specific training, achieving superior real-world success rates.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Zero-shot vision-and-language navigation (VLN) requires an agent to use past observations without navigation-specific training. We study what information an 8B-scale navigation system should retain and how it should be organized for subsequent decisions. Our agent combines instruction progress, hierarchically compressed observation history anchored to poses, and accumulated geometry in complementary task, temporal, and spatial memories. An 8B observer summarizes observations, and an 8B reasoner uses the memories to select waypoint intents or request additional views, a geometric controller executes the selected targets. A semantic information perspective motivates the distinction between retaining evidence, making it accessible to the reasoner, and acquiring further observations. On R2R-CE val-unseen, the complete system achieves the highest among the evaluated Qwen3-based zero-shot baselines. Removing temporal memory reduces SR and sharply increases average path length from 16.9 to 39.1m, removing the spatial-map and planning component reduces SR as well. Real-world experiments on a Unitree Go2 show that our zero-shot method achieves higher success rates than the post-trained baseline in both corridor and office environments, suggesting better transfer to the evaluated real-world settings. As a complementary evaluation, LAW2 uses paired instruction interventions to examine behavioral responses, instruction following ability beyond endpoint success. These results support preserving task progress, observation history, and geometry in structured memory for zero-shot navigation with smaller open models.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Rotation Equivariant Mamba for Vision Tasks
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Zhongchen Zhao, Qi Xie, Keyu Huang, Lei Zhang, Deyu Meng
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The paper introduces EQ-VMamba, a rotation equivariant architecture that enhances robustness and performance in vision tasks while reducing parameters by 40-70%.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Rotation equivariance is an important structural prior for a broad range of vision tasks, particularly in domains such as remote sensing and medical imaging where objects have no canonical orientation, yet it remains notably absent from current Mamba-based vision architectures. Despite the success of Mamba in natural language processing and its growing adoption in computer vision, existing visual Mamba models fail to account for rotational symmetry in their design. This omission renders them sensitive to image rotations, thereby constraining their robustness and cross-task generalization. To address this limitation, we incorporate rotation symmetry, an important geometric prior in many visual domains, into Mamba-based architectures. Specifically, we introduce EQ-VMamba, the first rotation equivariant visual Mamba architecture for vision tasks. The core components of EQ-VMamba include a carefully designed rotation equivariant cross-scan strategy and group Mamba blocks. Moreover, we provide a rigorous theoretical analysis of the intrinsic equivariance error, demonstrating that the proposed architecture enforces end-to-end rotation equivariance under the p4 rotation group. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks---including high-level image classification, mid-level semantic segmentation, and low-level image super-resolution---demonstrate that EQ-VMamba consistently improves rotation robustness and achieves superior or competitive performance compared to non-equivariant baselines on most benchmarks, while requiring 40-70% fewer parameters. These results indicate that embedding rotation equivariance not only effectively bolsters the robustness of visual Mamba models against rotation transformations, but also improves accuracy on data exhibiting rotational symmetry, with substantially improved parameter efficiency. Code is available at https://github.com/zhongchenzhao/EQ-VMamba.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Seeing and Imagining as One: Unified Video Generation and 4D Perception for Embodied World Modeling
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Haitang Feng, Zhuoman Liu, Zhennan Wang, Sheng Wang, Juelin Li
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: GenSight integrates future video generation and dense perception into a unified model, enhancing embodied world modeling through shared representations and optimized predictions across modalities.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Embodied world models should not only imagine plausible futures, but also perceive the geometric, semantic, and motion structure of the evolving world. We present GenSight, a unified embodied world model that brings future video generation and dense perception into a single pretrained video diffusion transformer. GenSight uses a unified spatiotemporal representation for video, depth, embodiment segmentation, and first-frame-relative 2D flow. Built on a shared DiT backbone, GenSight uses lightweight task modulation to predict all modalities within the same architecture. All tasks are jointly optimized within a unified velocity prediction space. At inference, GenSight supports two complementary modes: multi-step future video generation with aligned dense predictions and single-step dense perception from an observed video. By unifying modality representation, model architecture, and prediction space, GenSight avoids separate modality-specific pipelines and couples appearance, geometry, semantics, and motion in a shared representation. It promotes cross-modal consistency and allows dense perception to benefit from the spatiotemporal priors learned through video generation. Trained on embodied manipulation data spanning multiple robot embodiments and human-hand interactions, GenSight demonstrates strong performance in both video generation and dense 4D perception, highlighting the effectiveness of unifying seeing and imagining for embodied world modeling.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: RoboSeed: Multidimensional Evaluation of Vision-Language-Action and World-Action Models: Capability, Resource Affordability, and Research Evidence
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Xin Ma, Furong Chen, Xinlong Man, Bo Zhang, Yalong Guo
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: RoboSeed introduces a multidimensional evaluation framework for comparing vision-language-action and world-action models based on capability, affordability, and research reliability, aiding informed robot action model selection.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Choosing a robot action model requires evidence about task capability, adaptation cost, deployment requirements, and the reliability of reported conclusions. Success rates alone offer limited guidance to researchers with different computing budgets and goals. We propose RoboSeed, a multidimensional evaluation framework for vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action models (WAM), within a continuing program to train, evaluate, and openly release robot models with verifiable evidence for model selection. The framework defines five dimensions: capability, downstream training affordability, deployment affordability, locally verified research value, and reproduction evidence. It maps empirical measurements and audit criteria to 0-100 profiles using fixed normalization anchors, with balanced, training-constrained, and deployment-constrained preference settings. Interface and protocol checks establish when comparisons are appropriate. Missing measurements remain explicit, incomplete aggregate scores are withheld, and weighted input coverage identifies evidence gaps. We apply the framework to representative VLA and WAM models, drawing on local training, released-weight evaluation, task-level audits, and an evaluation-system study. The results reveal budget-dependent backbone choices, sensitivity to adaptation recipes, and differences between language and visual task interfaces. Reproducible scoring code and machine-readable evidence support extension to additional models. The study provides dimension-level assessments and priorities for further measurement, while incomplete serving traces and heterogeneous protocols preclude overall numerical rankings.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: From Solver Trajectories to Teaching Trajectories: Cognition-Aligned Reasoning Distillation
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Yashuo Luo, Qianren Mao, Ziqi Qin, Junnan Liu, Haitao Li
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The paper introduces Cognition-Aligned Reasoning Distillation (CARD), an RL-based method that optimizes teacher trajectories for effective knowledge transfer to smaller models.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Knowledge distillation from large reasoning models (LRMs) often uses raw teacher trajectories as supervision. However, this practice creates a mismatch between the goal of distillation and the nature of teacher trajectories. Advanced LRMs typically improve their reasoning capabilities through reward-driven post-training, such as RLHF. This training optimizes them as strong solvers, rather than as teachers that produce reasoning processes smaller models can easily learn. Since smaller models have different "cognitive capacities" compared to their larger teachers, directly imitating raw teacher trajectories can sometimes be ineffective and often requires a substantial number of high-quality samples. To bridge this mismatch, we propose Cognition-Aligned Reasoning Distillation (CARD), an RL-based framework that transforms solver trajectories into teaching trajectories aligned with the student's cognition. Avoiding expensive resampling, our framework directly transforms existing trajectories. We optimize CARD with two reward signals: (1) a Distribution Alignment Reward that matches the student's predictive distribution, and (2) a Logical Coherence Reward that reduces misleading failed reasoning steps. Comprehensive evaluations across multiple student models and settings demonstrate that CARD outperforms distillation from raw teacher trajectories in in-domain settings while achieving substantial gains in out-of-distribution performance. Code is available at https://github.com/LiteSSLHub/CARD.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Evaluation-Guided Demonstration Refinement for Vision-Language-Action Policies: The Winning Entry in the MetaFine Open Competition
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Lifan Zheng, Guotao Chen, Zhenyang Li, Shujie Cui, Qiang Huang
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The paper presents a refined vision-language-action policy that improved task performance in the MetaFine Open Competition by addressing failures through demonstration revisions and expert continuations.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: We fine-tuned a separate $π_{0.5}$ policy for each of the five tasks in the MetaFine Open Competition, with a task-specific training mixture and number of actions executed per prediction. Training started from the official demonstrations and expert procedures. Local evaluation exposed recurring grasping, pushing, and insertion failures. We addressed them by revising the demonstrated motions and by adding expert continuations from states the policy reached, while keeping nominal demonstrations in training. Checkpoints were compared on every instruction, so that a gain on one instruction could not hide a loss on another. Our submission, MAI, ranked first overall with a score of 96.66.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Trace-WAM: Learning to Act via 3D Motion Prediction for World Action Models
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Xu Hu, Changjie Wu, Linzhe Shi, Hang Zhang, Chen Yang
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: Trace-WAM enhances robot control by integrating future 3D motion prediction with video-action learning, improving manipulation performance and generalization across diverse tasks.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) learn representations for robot control by coupling future visual prediction with action generation. Successful manipulation depends primarily on how the robot and task-relevant objects evolve, whereas future-video prediction must also reconstruct the appearance and background of the entire scene. We therefore propose Trace-WAM, which augments video-action learning with future 3D motion prediction as an auxiliary objective. This objective supervises temporal point correspondence together with image-plane displacement and depth change, directly describing the interaction dynamics and spatial changes involved in manipulation. To this end, we adopt a three-branch Mixture-of-Transformer (Tri-MoT) architecture to jointly learn video prediction, motion prediction, and action generation. The motion expert predicts future trajectories from current visual features, allowing motion supervision to shape the representations used for action generation. Because the action expert does not consume predicted trajectories, inference retains the current-observation policy path: a single visual forward pass followed by action denoising. Experiments on RoboCasa-GR1, LIBERO, and LIBERO-Plus demonstrate strong in-distribution performance and out-of-distribution generalization, with particularly clear gains over Fast-WAM under limited demonstrations and distribution shifts.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: HoloRecon: Incremental Reconstruction of Long-Range Panoramas with Global Consistency
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Zhuoxiao Li, Xinyi Liu, Hongye Hou, Jing OU, Kang Du
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: HoloRecon presents a novel framework for incremental panoramic reconstruction that integrates sparse mapping and feed-forward models to ensure global consistency and accurate localization over long sequences.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Long-sequence panoramic reconstruction requires detailed scene geometry and globally consistent camera poses across distant revisits. Panoramic SLAM and incremental SfM rely on feature correspondences, but repeated, similar structures and small partial overlap make reliable long-range connections difficult to establish, leaving accumulated drift unresolved. Feed-forward models offer detailed local geometry, but their high computational costs limit inference window size, necessitating additional constraints for global consistency. This motivates combining continuous feature-based tracking and sparse mapping with rapid, high-quality local reconstruction from feed-forward models to achieve accurate localization and globally consistent dense mapping over long sequences. We therefore propose a panoramic reconstruction framework that couples an ORB-based sparse panoramic mapping frontend with a fine-tuned feed-forward model. Our key insight is that predicted local geometry enables 3D verification of feature matches across distant revisits, yielding long-range camera constraints even between regions. We calibrate predicted depths with sparse landmarks and use verified connections to optimize the global pose graph, updating dense geometry with the corrected camera poses. We also introduce PanoRecon, a seven-scene benchmark with repetitive architecture, large and small loops, and reference camera poses and LiDAR geometry for evaluating global consistency. Our method achieves the lowest mean absolute trajectory error and high F-1 Score among the evaluated methods. Project Page:https://zhuoxiaoli.github.io/HoloRecon_page/

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Algorithm Modelization: Transforming Optimization Algorithms into Evolvable Intelligence
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Jian Yao, Zhiyao Zhang, Yichen Li, Xingyu Wu, Kay Chen Tan
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The paper introduces Algorithm Modelization, a paradigm that transforms iterative optimization algorithms into trainable models capable of evolving and generalizing through learned computational experiences.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Can algorithms be learned and evolved as models, rather than repeatedly redesigned as programs? We explore this question by introducing Algorithm Modelization, a new paradigm that turns iterative algorithms into trainable models. Its central idea is to regard algorithm execution trajectories as computational experience: by learning how algorithmic states evolve over iterations, a model can internalize the knowledge embodied in existing algorithms, reproduce their computational behaviors, and further evolve beyond them through training. As a first realization of this paradigm, we modelize iterative optimization as an autoregressive process, where preceding generations constitute the computational context for generating the next population. We develop a dimension-independent population-temporal architecture to capture both population interactions and iterative dynamics, together with an imitation-to-surpassing learning framework that first acquires algorithmic knowledge from heterogeneous teachers and then improves the resulting optimizer directly through optimization feedback. The modelized optimizer consequently goes beyond reproducing individual algorithms: it consolidates heterogeneous search knowledge into a single trainable model, achieves stronger optimization capability through subsequent improvement, and generalizes its acquired knowledge across problems and substantially larger unseen dimensions. More fundamentally, Algorithm Modelization makes algorithmic capability accumulable through learning, where new algorithms and problem-solving experience can become training resources for progressively improving the model. Our results establish a promising path from manually designed algorithms toward general algorithm models that learn, generalize, and evolve from computational experience.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: UAV-SwarmAgent: Scalable Multi-UAV Reconnaissance and Task Allocation via Code Generation and Vision-Language Reasoning
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Oleg Sautenkov, Yasheerah Yaqoot, Muhammad Ahsan Mustafa, Grigorii Kalinin, Chih-Yung Wen
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: UAV-SwarmAgent enables efficient multi-UAV reconnaissance through natural language commands, automated route generation, and vision-language reasoning, achieving high mission success rates in simulations.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Supervising a multi-UAV reconnaissance mission usually means plotting waypoints and watching every drone. We present UAV SwarmAgent, a hierarchical multi-agent system in which an operator states the mission in one natural-language sentence and a ground-station agent writes and executes code that turns it into per-UAV routes. The agent grounds inspection targets in an aerial map with a vision-language model, splits them among N UAVs by balancing route length, and dispatches worker agents that verify incidents with a compact onboard decision model. In simulation over 4 incident types and 3 foundation models, the swarm located the incident in 244 of 255 missions (95.7%). A paired scaling study with one to 5 UAVs shows that flight time follows an Amdahl-type law. The second UAV delivers half of the attainable saving and the speedup is bounded at 1.52x. We discuss what this predictability, and the false alarms we observed, imply for an operator who supervises the swarm, and outline the user study needed to test it.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Initialization-Free LEO Doppler Positioning via Semidefinite Relaxation: A Cold-Start Approach
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Baoshan Song, Weisong Wen, Qi Zhang, Bing Xu, Penggao Yan
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: This paper presents an initialization-free LEO Doppler positioning method using semidefinite relaxation, achieving accurate positioning without prior location knowledge in cold-start scenarios.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite Doppler measurements offer an alternative source of positioning information for Internet of Things devices when Global Navigation Satellite System signals are unavailable. Conventional local optimisation methods depend on an accurate initial position and can fail during a complete cold start. We propose an initialization-free LEO Doppler positioning framework based on semidefinite relaxation. The method reformulates the nonlinear positioning problem into a semidefinite programme to obtain a receiver position estimate without prior location knowledge. We analyse relaxation tightness under noiseless conditions and derive sufficient noise bounds under parameter disturbances. Simulations and field experiments using opportunistic Iridium-NEXT signals evaluate initialization sensitivity, positioning accuracy and computational cost. In the field experiment, the proposed method achieves a three-dimensional positioning error of 140 m without an initial position, whereas local solvers converge to poor solutions under large initial offsets. Using the semidefinite estimate to initialise Gauss-Newton or Dog-Leg reduces the positioning error to 130 m. The framework provides a cold-start initialization stage for subsequent local refinement in opportunistic LEO positioning. The implementation and datasets are publicly available to support reproducibility and further research.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: PATH: Preference-Aware Traversability Estimation for Robotic Teleoperation in Off-Road Navigation
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Xianghao Meng, Wenshuo Wang, Cheng Shao, Lewei Feng, Qingxiao Liu
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: PATH-Net enhances robotic teleoperation by integrating operator preferences into traversability estimation, optimizing cost maps and speed profiles for off-road navigation.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Traversability estimation is critical for ground vehicle teleoperation, yet existing methods often neglect the human operator's preferences for speed and risk tolerance. To address this gap, we propose PATH-Net, a Preference-Aware Traversability estimation Hierarchical Network that adaptively generates preference-conditioned traversability cost maps and speed profiles for off-road teleoperation. Our framework integrates visual and geometric bird's-eye-view features with short-term historical vehicle states through a multi-head shared-backbone architecture. Our PATH-Net infers traversability cost maps while optimizing speed recommendations by using maximum entropy inverse reinforcement learning and sparse speed supervision. Our method incorporates operator preference via an asymmetric feature aggregation mechanism, splitting inference into a cost branch that prioritizes high-risk traversability regions and a speed branch that outputs preference-adjusted recommended speeds. Experiments with 15 operators across 225 teleoperated trajectories show alignment with user-specific navigation strategies, achieving modified Hausdorff distance of 0.17 m (aggressive) and 0.15 m (conservative). In the questionnaire assessment, participants reported lower NASA-TLX workload scores with PATH-Net recommendations than without recommendations, decreasing from 34.7 to 22.2. These results support preference-conditioned trajectory and speed recommendation for off-road teleoperation.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: AgentDP: Towards Automated Model Deployment for Heterogeneous Embedded AI Applications
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Leming Shen, Qiang Yang, Xinyu Huang, Zijing Ma, Yuanqing Zheng
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: AgentDP automates model optimization and adaptation for heterogeneous embedded AI applications using LLMs, significantly reducing adaptation time by 80% and improving task accuracy by over 13%.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: This paper presents AgentDP, which aims to deploy pre-trained AI models on heterogeneous embedded devices by fully automating model optimization and adaptation (O&A) with Large Language Model (LLM) agents. AgentDP not only significantly reduces human effort via automation but also enhances model inference efficacy by integrating LLMs with device-specific domain knowledge. To deliver a robust automation framework, AgentDP develops novel solutions to address three key technical challenges: 1) To help users elicit clear requirements, we propose a user requirement standardization module; 2) To mitigate the execution environment mismatch between AI models and heterogeneous embedded devices, we design an operator-aware model partition paradigm that enables different parts of the model to be efficiently executed on distinct inference engines. 3) To avoid re-searching optimization hyperparameters for new tasks, we propose a configuration reuse module that heuristically retrieves previous hyperparameter configurations for efficient reuse. Extensive experiments demonstrate that by fully automating the entire O&A process, AgentDP reduces entire model adaptation time by up to 80% compared with manual O&A while achieving higher task accuracy (more than 13% on average) than the baselines. Additionally, a comprehensive user study also exhibits the robust generalizability of AgentDP in adapting to different user requirements for heterogeneous embedded devices.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Dual Exam: Controlled Evaluation of Multimodal Agents and World Models
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Zhefan Rao, Meng Chu, Xuan Zhang, Jingfan Chen, Guohao Cai
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The paper presents Dual Exam, a framework for evaluating the interaction between Multimodal Agents and World Models across various domains, revealing performance inconsistencies and challenges in reciprocal learning.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: World Models (WMs) can support Multimodal Agents (MAs) through simulated experience, while Agent trajectories can inform World Model refinement. Evaluating this interaction requires separate evidence about action selection and state evolution. We introduce Dual Exam, which tests Agents under fixed environment response mechanisms and World Models under fixed action interventions across physical, digital, social, and scientific domains. The Agent track compares 10 configurations on 1,088 items in 15 reporting categories. The World Model track contains 400 cases across eight scenarios; 15 configurations have full coverage and one covers six scenarios. GPT 6 Astra leads the case-weighted Agent Index at 31.3, and GPT-Image-2 leads the full-coverage WM Overall at 21.7. These scores use different tasks and metrics and are not directly comparable. A 150-case pilot of one coupled pairing records zero task successes and motivates component-level diagnosis. Results reveal uneven task performance and failures to preserve task-relevant state. Their value for predicting coupled success or sustained reciprocal learning remains to be established.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: PhyMo: Learning Physical Dynamics with Accurate and Continuous Motion from Multi-View Videos
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Shangjia Liu, Jinxi Li, Siyuan Zhou, Bo Yang, Bing Wang
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: PhyMo is a framework that accurately learns physical dynamics and continuous motion from multi-view videos by employing a Motion-Aware Trajectory Representation and a Continuous Motion Evolution module.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Recovering dynamic 3D scene geometry, appearance, and the physical motion states that govern scene evolution from multi-view videos is important yet challenging. A key difficulty is that appearance can be deceptive. Under rendering supervision alone, a model may fit the observed images by changing color or opacity to compensate for inaccurate deformation, rather than recovering the true evolving geometry and motion. This issue is especially severe in scenes with fast or locally complex motion, where inaccurate trajectories can still produce plausible images over the observed frames, but lead to unreliable reconstruction and discontinuous future prediction. In this paper, we propose PhyMo, a framework for learning evolving dynamics from multi-view videos. We introduce a Motion-Aware Trajectory Representation that drives the model to recover accurate motion from deformation, rather than relying on appearance shortcuts to explain observed motion. On top of this, we propose a Continuous Motion Evolution module with bidirectional kinematic continuity constraint to promote temporally consistent evolution of displacement, velocity, and acceleration. Together, these designs yield geometrically faithful interpolation and continuous motion extrapolation. Experiments on four dynamic scene benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art performance.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Preserving Operator Intent Under Actuation Constraints: Teleoperation of Manipulators with Coupled Transmissions
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Xuhan Miao, Zijin Han, Yutong Shen, Haidong Huang, Shanliushui Gao
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The paper presents a novel teleoperation method for manipulators that addresses actuation constraints and preserves operator intent through coordinated motor saturation and advanced feedback mechanisms.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Teleoperation enables intuitive control of remote engineering robots for precision tasks. Existing direct joint-mapping methods have two limitations: independent motor saturation disrupts pitch-roll coordination in differential wrists, while fixed mappings struggle with abrupt tracking changes caused by gravitational loads and actuation constraints. We propose an actuator-constraint-aware leader-follower teleoperation method that jointly models leader gravity compensation, leader-follower joint mapping, and follower differential-wrist control. Specifically, we perform coordinated saturation in motor space according to the available gravity margin and integrate continuous angle unwrapping, feedback-state monitoring, and feasible-reference updates. This preserves the operator's motion direction, reduces coordination distortion, and suppresses recovery transients during saturation or brief communication failures. Real-robot experiments demonstrate smoother wrist trajectories and more continuous recovery than direct mapping.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: AtomicRL: Atomic Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Likui Zhang, Zhe Zhu, Zhihao Zhan, Yibo Bai, Hanlin Wang
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: AtomicRL enhances long-horizon robotic manipulation by optimizing credit assignment and exploration through atomic task structures, achieving significant performance gains in both simulation and real-world applications.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown promise in robotic manipulation, but imitation learning (IL) alone often struggles to master complex long-horizon skills. Reinforcement learning (RL) offers an effective avenue for further improving VLA policies. However, existing VLA-RL methods typically suffer from delayed and biased credit assignment due to trajectory-level sparse rewards, while imbalanced subtask mastery creates bottlenecks that limit overall performance. To address these challenges, we propose AtomicRL, an RL post-training framework that leverages atomic task structures for reliable credit assignment and adaptive exploration. AtomicRL introduces Semantic-Aware Policy Optimization (SAPO), which uses semantic-aware gating to constrain TD residuals from failed atomic subtasks from propagating across task boundaries, mitigating credit contamination while preserving intra-subtask credit assignment and value bootstrapping. In addition, Bottleneck-Adaptive Target Exploration (BATE) dynamically coordinates task sampling and local exploration incentives based on the mastery of individual atomic subtasks, directing learning toward the remaining bottlenecks. Finally, we develop a Real2Sim2Real pipeline that bridges online RL in simulation with real-world deployment, facilitating practical transfer to physical robots. On LIBERO-LONG, AtomicRL achieves absolute performance gains of 3.6% and 4.0% over PPO across two VLA architectures. On CALVIN ABC-D, it improves full-task performance by up to 9.5% over PPO. Combined with the Real2Sim2Real pipeline, AtomicRL further improves real-world task performance by an average of 21.3%. These results demonstrate that AtomicRL effectively improves the learning efficiency and manipulation performance of VLA policies on long-horizon tasks.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Joint-Angle Invariance of Jacobian-Based Performance Indices for Serial Robotic Manipulators
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Yaohua Zhou, Mingdao Lin, Jiayu Song, Xixin Zhao, Haidong Huang
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The paper explores joint-angle invariance of Jacobian-based performance indices in serial robotic manipulators, enhancing efficiency in performance evaluation and optimization while reducing computational demands.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: This article investigates the joint-angle invariance (JAI) of Jacobian-based performance indices for serial robotic manipulators. We identify kinematic conditions under which representative performance indices, including manipulability, stiffness, and other Jacobian-derived indices, remain independent of the first and last joint angles. This property allows a systematic reduction in the effective configuration-space dimensionality, thereby simplifying the performance evaluation. The utility of JAI is demonstrated through two application scenarios: workspace performance map construction and task layout optimization. Comparative results show that the proposed JAI-based strategy reduces computational effort and storage requirements without compromising the effectiveness.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: GPT-6-Astra Understands Touch and Outperform Vision--Tactile--Language--Action Models
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Ziyong Wang, Yupei Lin, Runxuan Huang, Liang Lin, Dongyu Zhang
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: GPT-6-Astra effectively utilizes tactile feedback and multimodal context to enhance robotic manipulation success, outperforming traditional models without extensive pretraining or task-specific fine-tuning.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: General-purpose multimodal models have shown promise as direct robot action policies, yet whether they grasp the physics underlying real-world interactions and can apply that understanding to guide action remains underexplored. We investigate this question using contact-rich manipulation as a representative testbed, examining tactile understanding as a concrete instance of this broader capability. Contact-rich manipulation requires interpreting tactile feedback and adjusting actions after obstruction. Existing learned tactile policies acquire these capabilities through specialized pretraining and per-task optimization, with substantial data and training costs. We present GPT-as-Tactile-Policy, which summarizes expert demonstrations into task guidance and tactile references for contact assessment and corrective action. GPT-6-Astra combines this context with multimodal observations and interaction history to generate control commands and adjust actions through contact feedback. Without additional robotics-specific pretraining or per-task policy fine-tuning, our method achieves 93.8\% mean success across five UniVTAC tasks. Overall performance is comparable to state-of-the-art policies, with higher success on selected tasks. On Insert Hole, tactile feedback improves success from 31\% to 99\%. Execution analysis further demonstrates contact-guided probing and correction, supporting manipulation progress through explicit expert experience and online feedback.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Exploring Temporal Context-Aware Physical Grounding in Latent World Models
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Yilei Man, Yang Chen, Jingcai Guo
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The paper introduces $\mathcal{G}$-JEPA, enhancing Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures by integrating temporal context for improved action planning in latent world models.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Learning latent dynamics is fundamental to building action-conditioned world models for planning. Among existing families, Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) offer a natural framework by modeling transitions directly in latent space rather than at the pixel level. However, two issues remain in JEPA-based world models: (i) physical grounding lacks explicit aggregation of temporal context and (ii) action planning always overly relies on generic sampling distributions. To this end, we propose $\mathcal{G}$-JEPA, which incorporates temporal context into physical grounding for latent world models and couples the learned models with prior-guided action planning. Specifically, during learning, we incorporate a shared causal temporal module that aggregates temporal context within observation and prediction sequences under physical state supervision, grounding both in task-relevant physical states. When planning, we further introduce action inference through stepwise conditioning of a generative action distribution on the current and goal latent representations together with their evolving discrepancy, yielding anchored proposals that guide model-based online refinement. Together, physical state supervision guides temporal representation learning, while the action prior guides search through the learned world model. Experiments demonstrate improved planning performance on manipulation tasks, including tasks with increasing temporal separation between initial and goal observations. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/myl11045/G-JEPA.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Difference-in-Differences on a Censored Rating Scale Can Manufacture an Effect: Evidence from a Pre-Registered LLM-Judge Audit
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Shuyi Fan, Boyuan Deng, Mengyu Xu, Xinhong Xie, Chenyang Li
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The study reveals that bounded rating scales in LLM-judge audits can create misleading effects, as evidenced by a significant interaction that doesn't reflect true preferences.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: LLM-judge audits assess bias by comparing ratings across matched conditions. Difference-in-differences designs compare two candidate responses within each item and then compare that contrast across a manipulated attribute, with an endpoint read off a bounded rating scale. Building on prior work on nonlinear difference-in-differences, we show in closed form that when ratings are bounded, a severity shift common to both responses produces an observed interaction whenever the scale bounds attenuate it unequally. We examine this problem in a pre-registered audit comprising 990 calls to a frozen pedagogy judge. The registered primary analysis did not detect an effect of a stated novice or advanced profile on scaffolding preference. The only nominally significant secondary interaction concerned the productive-struggle sub-score ($+0.378$ points; $p = 0.002$). A post-hoc construction with zero differential preference reproduced 79 to 85% of this interaction using the observed severity shift and the scale floor alone. The observed interaction therefore does not identify differential preference on the latent scale.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Cross-Visibility-Gap Identity Persistence for 4D Scene Graphs
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Jiahui Hu, Li Gao, Yu Liu, Pengzhan Zhou
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The paper presents CVG-SGM, a method for maintaining object identity in 4D scene graphs through historical relational memory, achieving high accuracy in identity recovery despite visibility gaps.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: 4D scene graphs require persistent object identity when an object disappears inside an opaque carrier and later reappears as a fresh detection. When appearance and target-centric motion are unavailable, identity recovery must rely on relational history. We formulate cross-visibility-gap identity persistence as historical-node recovery through a remembered target--carrier binding. We introduce CVG-SGM, a perception-frontend-compatible transfer--maintain--read memory. Geometry-weighted cross-node interaction transfers target-specific evidence into carrier states, a shared per-node GRU maintains this information during transport, and a two-time readout combines stored carrier--identity compatibility with current detection--carrier geometry to recover the historical identity. In the controlled one-identity-per-carrier setting, CVG-SGM achieves 1.000 re-link accuracy, compared with 0.570 for both no-memory and parameter-count-matched no-write controls. It also generalizes to scene-disjoint, unseen longer visibility gaps. On real RGB-D/SAM2 feature-level episodes, it correctly re-links 36/36 held-out detections, compared with 28/36 for the strongest fixed carrier--identity control. Counterfactual carrier-memory swaps redirect predictions according to the swapped bindings, supporting the role of stored relational information in identity recovery. The current approach remains limited by shared-carrier identity ambiguity and does not provide end-to-end raw-video re-identification.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Provisioning Robust and Efficient LiDAR Perception for Autonomous Driving
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Tingxu Han, Zijie Shen, An Guo, Lyuke Wang, Chunrong Fang
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: This paper presents a method for enhancing LiDAR perception in autonomous driving by improving robustness to point-cloud corruption while reducing latency and memory usage.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: LiDAR-based 3D object detection is a core perception service for autonomous driving, but deployment requires robustness to point-cloud corruption while meeting latency and memory requirements. Existing approaches address robustness and resource efficiency separately, resulting in compact detectors that are fragile under corruption or robust detectors that remain costly to deploy. We therefore formulate LiDAR perception provisioning as constructing a detector that remains accurate under point-cloud corruptions while meeting constraints on inference latency and peak GPU memory. To achieve robustness, we first craft corrupted samples that mimic extreme weather conditions. Then we train candidate detectors offline by ordering clean and corrupted samples by perturbation sensitivity, through which detectors learn more from hard corrupted samples. We estimate perturbation sensitivity using an ensemble of seven heterogeneous 3D detectors by tracking changes in confidence, BEV overlap, and unmatched detections. To improve efficiency, we narrow the network and use offline neighborhood-density measurements to determine how many points and neighbors each sampling stage processes. We evaluate our method using AP (Average Precision) under clean and corrupted conditions, inference latency, and peak allocated GPU memory. On KITTI for Car detection with PointRCNN, our method improves Moderate AP under corruption by 3.32 points over the original detector while reducing mean latency by 19.8% and peak allocated GPU memory by 53.9%. Across two datasets, two detector architectures, and three object classes, our method improves AP under corruption by 4.03 points on average over the corresponding original detectors, while reducing mean inference latency and peak allocated GPU memory by 14.4% and 38.0%, respectively.
