机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Hang Zheng, Nan Jiang, Zichen Zhu, Zixu Yang, Zhiyang Tang
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: ARGUS is a neuro-symbolic user simulator that enhances reliability in interactive environments through agenda-driven goal tracking and a novel training pipeline, outperforming existing models.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: High-fidelity user simulators are essential for evaluating and training agents in interactive environments. However, current LLM-based simulators struggle with reliability issues, such as goal omission and policy non-compliance. We propose ARGUS (Agenda-dRiven Goal-oriented User Simulator), a neuro-symbolic framework that maintains the user's goal state using a dynamic agenda stack manipulated via symbolic operations. By rigorously decoupling state tracking from natural language generation, ARGUS facilitates strict goal progression and constraint-aligned interactions. For cost-efficient deployment, we distill ARGUS into compact models using a unified pipeline: evaluator-guided SFT followed by online RL with dense step-level rewards. To rigorously evaluate behavioral fidelity, we introduce a rubric-based metric Composite Behavioral Score (CBS). Evaluations on $τ^3$-Bench and MultiWOZ demonstrate the significant superiority of the ARGUS architecture and the efficacy of our training pipeline. Code and data will be released soon.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: Robo2Process: Benchmarking and Learning Process-Aware Understanding in Vision-Language Robotic Manipulation
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Dayu Xia, Yue Shi, Yao Mu, Huiting Ji, Chaofan Ma
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: Robo2Process introduces a framework for process-aware supervision in robotic manipulation, enhancing vision-language models' understanding through structured QA and diagnostic benchmarking.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) used as robotic critics, reward generators, and failure detectors must understand how manipulation unfolds, not only whether it succeeds. Yet fine-grained process supervision is not readily available in a unified form, and existing evaluations do not systematically diagnose these abilities. We introduce Robo2Process, a trace-grounded framework for scalable construction of process-aware supervision from heterogeneous robotic execution data. It aligns visual observations with source-native signals and annotations, extracts local process units (LPUs), and generates structured QA supervision through task-specific sampling, deterministic label construction, and ambiguity filtering. We instantiate this framework as RoboProcessBench, a diagnostic benchmark with 12 question families spanning \emph{static monitoring} and \emph{dynamic reasoning}, and ProcessData, a corpus of 57,892 QA pairs across four data sources and 260 manipulation tasks, split into ProcessData-SFT and ProcessData-Eval. Evaluation of a broad suite of VLMs reveals uneven process understanding. Supervision from ProcessData-SFT improves \textit{Qwen2.5-VL-7B} and \textit{InternVL-3-8B} on local state, motion, progress, and primitive-aware cues. External evaluation on RoboRewardBench shows Robo2Process enables out-of-distribution process-aware reasoning abilities. Overall, Robo2Process provides a source-aware pipeline, diagnostic benchmark, and learnable substrate for process-aware understanding in robotic manipulation.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: MAIA: Anticipating Interaction Anomalies in Contact-Rich Manipulation via Multimodal World Models
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Yi Qiao, Maolin Zheng, Haoran Sun, Lujia Dong, Wenzhao Lian
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: MAIA is a multimodal framework that anticipates interaction anomalies in contact-rich manipulation, improving detection and task success through predictive modeling of physical consequences.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Reliable contact-rich manipulation requires detecting execution deviations early enough for corrective action. Yet most monitoring methods are reactive, identifying anomalies only after they become observable. Anticipating such anomalies is challenging because visual observations only partially reveal physical interaction, while planned actions describe intended motion rather than their actual physical consequences. We address this problem with MAIA, a multimodal framework for anomaly anticipation. Its vision-action-force world model learns nominal interaction dynamics and predicts the visual and force responses of planned actions, while a lightweight anomaly head predicts impending interaction anomalies. To enable systematic evaluation, we introduce CRIA, a real-world multimodal dataset of 2,852 trajectories spanning 18 contact-rich manipulation tasks, with frame-level annotations of anomaly onset and evolution. Experiments on both seen and novel tasks show that MAIA achieves more accurate anomaly discrimination than representative baselines while providing earlier warnings, with bACC scores of 0.765 and 0.710 and median anticipation lead times of 28.0 and 25.1 steps, respectively. Moreover, using these predictions for anomaly-aware action selection improves end-to-end task success from 52.6% to 61.5% without retraining the underlying manipulation policy. These results highlight the value of modeling future physical consequences for proactive anomaly anticipation.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: OS-Helix: Unifying GUI Interaction and Code Execution in Native Computer-Using Agents
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Bowen Yang, Kaiming Jin, Zichen Ding, Zhenyu Wu, Zehao Li
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: OS-Helix is a multimodal agent that integrates GUI interaction and code execution through hybrid training, achieving significant performance improvements in desktop automation tasks.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Real desktop automation is neither purely visual nor purely programmatic. Agents must understand user-facing interfaces while efficiently manipulating files, scripts, and system state. However, native GUI/code coordination cannot be obtained by prompt-level tool composition. In our preliminary experiments, naively adding a code tool degrades a GUI agent, revealing that GUI/code routing must be internalized through training on high-quality hybrid data. We present OS-Helix, an end-to-end trained multimodal computer-using agent that unifies GUI actions and code execution in one action space. To construct the required supervision, we introduce application-artifact composition, pairing desktop applications with authentic file artifacts to instantiate executable Ubuntu states, and a decoupled instruction/evaluator generation pipeline that produces environment-grounded tasks whose final states can be verified regardless of the solution modality. We cold-start the policy with SFT on filtered hybrid data and further improve it through online RL in live desktop environments. For RL, we propose Step-balanced GSPO, which aggregates importance weight by action step rather than raw assistant tokens to prevent long code actions from dominating heterogeneous-action optimization. On OSWorld-Verified, OS-Helix-27B and OS-Helix-35B-A3B achieve relative improvements of 35.0% and 33.7% over their matched Qwen3.5 hybrid baselines, while OS-Helix-27B-RL further improves by 42.9% to reach 66.44% success. Ablations provide evidence consistent with contributions from learned GUI/code coordination, scalable verifiable supervision, and action step balanced optimization, while demonstrating cross-platform transfer on WindowsAgentArena. Our project homepage is at https://os-copilot.github.io/OS-Helix/.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: Value as Memory: Online Value-Guided Post-training for General Robot Policies
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Wenye Yu, Yijin Chen, Kaiyi Xiong, Wenbo Han, Wendi Chen
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: The Value as Memory framework enhances general robot policies by integrating value caching and online reinforcement learning, significantly improving task success rates and training efficiency.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Real-world post-training of generalist robot policies faces two challenges: partial observability makes action selection ambiguous, while offline post-training methods delay feedback from deployment experience. We present Value as Memory (VaM), a framework that addresses these challenges through value caching and online real-world reinforcement learning (RL). Value caching conditions actions on recent value predictions as task-progress memory, while online updates enable timely policy improvement by combining offline demonstrations, off-policy interventions, and on-policy rollouts for sample-efficient adaptation. As a result, VaM transitions from offline RL warmup to online autonomous learning with sparse rewards. Across long-horizon tasks involving deformable objects and contact-rich manipulation, VaM yields a mean absolute success-rate gain of $29.4\%$ with value caching, while achieving a $32.8\%$ gain with online autonomous learning over matched offline training. The evaluated online schedule performs $8\times$ as many policy iterations under the same gradient-step budget, with more than $2\times$ lower recorded time per gradient step with concurrent data collection and training.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: SceneReVis: A Self-Reflective Vision-Grounded Framework for 3D Indoor Scene Synthesis via Multi-Turn RL
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Yang Zhao, Shizhao Sun, Meisheng Zhang, Yingdong Shi, Xubo Yang
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: SceneReVis introduces a self-reflective framework for 3D indoor scene synthesis that utilizes multi-turn reinforcement learning to resolve spatial conflicts and enhance generation fidelity.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Current one-pass 3D scene synthesis methods often suffer from spatial hallucinations, such as collisions, due to a lack of deliberative reasoning. To bridge this gap, we introduce SceneReVis, a vision-grounded self-reflection framework that employs an iterative "diagnose-and-act" loop to explicitly intercept and resolve spatial conflicts using multi-modal feedback. To support this step-wise paradigm, we construct SceneChain-12k, a large-scale dataset of causal construction trajectories derived through a novel reverse engineering pipeline. We further propose a two-stage training recipe that transitions from Supervised Fine-Tuning to Agentic Reinforcement Learning, evolving the model into an active spatial planner. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SceneReVis achieves state-of-the-art performance in high-fidelity generation and goal-oriented optimization, with improved transfer to underrepresented room categories in the dataset and promising potential for extension to out-of-distribution room types.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: KODA: Kinematics--Observation Data Alignment for Humanoid Learning from Human Egocentric Demonstration
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Zibo Zhou, Yueru Chen, Junsong Wu, Weiji Xie, Qingyao Xu
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: KODA effectively aligns egocentric human demonstrations with humanoid VLA training data, enhancing performance across multiple controllers while reducing reliance on costly robot data.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Training humanoid whole-body vision-language-action (VLA) policies requires costly robot demonstrations with aligned robot-view observations and controller-compatible whole-body state-action labels. Egocentric human demonstrations offer scalable supervision but have misaligned views and sparse motion cues. Existing approaches either pretrain policies that still require robot data for adaptation or generate controller-specific commands that limit reuse. Conversion also requires robot-view observations aligned with the generated whole-body motion. We present KODA (Kinematics-Observation Data Alignment), which converts egocentric RGB demonstrations into whole-body VLA training data using a reusable canonical trajectory to guide robot-view synthesis and generate controller-specific whole-body state-action supervision. KODA first generates a simulator-checked whole-body trajectory using a sparse tracker with sampling-based command optimization. This generated trajectory directly determines the onboard camera poses used to synthesize corresponding robot-view observations. The motion, observations, and task instruction form a canonical record. For each deployment controller, KODA optimizes commands to track the stored motion and records the corresponding action labels and proprioceptive states. When switching controllers, KODA retains this canonical record and regenerates whole-body state-action supervision for co-training with matching robot demonstrations. We evaluate KODA on four Unitree G1 loco-manipulation tasks using two whole-body controllers, SONIC and HEFT. With robot data held fixed, macro-average success on conditions covered by human demonstrations but absent from robot data improves by 45.0 and 46.25 percentage points, respectively. Under both controllers, this metric shows an upward trend across the evaluated human-data budgets, suggesting potential for further scaling.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: Evo-DexBench: Benchmarking Generalization across Related Tasks for Dexterous Manipulation
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Bing Cheng, Yiran Mao, Zewei Ye, Yifan Jin, Xinyi Chen
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: Evo-DexBench introduces a benchmark for evaluating dexterous manipulation policies' generalization by controlling task relatedness and exposure, revealing significant challenges in knowledge transfer.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: General-purpose dexterous manipulation requires policies to transfer knowledge from related tasks to new tasks with only a few target demonstrations. Existing benchmarks often provide too many target demonstrations. They also leave the differences between source and target tasks uncontrolled. As a result, they cannot clearly distinguish knowledge transfer from task memorization. Our key insight is the Core-Gen principle. Core tasks are related tasks that share a functional interaction and provide source knowledge, while a Gen task is a novel target within the same functional family that has only a few demonstrations. This setup tests whether a policy can reuse functional interaction knowledge. Based on this principle, we propose Evo-DexBench, which controls both source-task relatedness and target-task exposure. It comprises 30 tasks in six functional families and a VR teleoperation pipeline. The resulting dataset covers three everyday scenes per task. It contains 1,248 multimodal demonstrations collected with simulated Shadow Hands equipped with 123 taxels. Experiments show that even the best-performing method achieves an average success rate of only 38.5%, highlighting the challenges existing methods face in transferring functional interaction knowledge. Further analysis shows that, across the two tasks, joint Core+Gen training improves performance by 12% and 38%, respectively, over training on Core followed by fine-tuning on Gen. This indicates that joint training makes better use of Core knowledge and that functionally matched Core data yields greater gains in success rate than mismatched data. We release the Evo-DexBench dataset and benchmark to support the evaluation of dexterous manipulation policies' generalization across related tasks.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: UniFGVC: Universal Training-Free Few-Shot Fine-Grained Vision Classification via Attribute-Aware Multimodal Retrieval
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Haiyun Guo, Hongyu Guo, Xiangzhao Hao, Jiarui Guo, Jinqiao Wang
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: UniFGVC introduces a training-free retrieval framework for few-shot fine-grained visual classification, leveraging multimodal attributes to enhance recognition without overfitting.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Few-shot fine-grained visual classification (FGVC) aims to discriminate between subtly different categories with very limited data. While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLM) exhibit strong capabilities in both fine-grained visual understanding and open-world category recognition, directly fine-tuning them on few-shot FGVC tasks typically leads to overfitting on sparse samples, which erodes their valuable open-world knowledge and compromises generalization. To fundamentally overcome this limitation, we present UniFGVC, a universal training-free framework that shifts the paradigm from parameter fine-tuning to training-free retrieval-based inference. UniFGVC reframes few-shot FGVC as a multimodal retrieval problem using predefined category templates. Its core is the Category-Discriminative Visual Captioner (CDV-Captioner), an attribute-aware module designed to leverage MLLM for generating structured textual descriptions that explicitly pinpoint discriminative visual attributes between similar classes. By integrating chain-of-thought reasoning and visual references, CDV-Captioner mitigates hallucination and maximizes the discriminative power of textual captions, thereby converting images into attribute-enriched image-description pairs. Subsequently, utilizing arbitrary pre-trained visual and textual encoders in a plug-and-play manner, UniFGVC extracts features from both modalities and computes their similarity with all category templates for recognition. Extensive experiments on 12 FGVC datasets demonstrate UniFGVC's universal compatibility and consistent superiority. It not only outperforms existing few-shot CLIP-based methods but also surpasses several fully-supervised MLLM-based approaches, confirming the general advantage of the proposed retrieval paradigm.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: Provably Efficient Risk-Sensitive Offline Reinforcement Learning via Optimized Certainty Equivalents
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Hanzhen Wang, Boxiang Lyu, Zhongxiang Dai, Siyang Gao, Dake Zhang
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: This paper presents novel offline reinforcement learning algorithms using optimized certainty equivalents, establishing theoretical bounds and addressing risk sensitivity in decision-making under uncertainty.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Risk-sensitive reinforcement learning (RL) addresses decision-making under uncertainty and adverse outcomes. Learning risk-sensitive policies from fixed datasets is important when additional interaction with the environment is costly. Existing work on risk-sensitive RL focuses on online settings or specific risk measures, leaving a general theoretical understanding of its offline setting underdeveloped. In this work, we investigate efficient offline risk-sensitive RL using the optimized certainty equivalent (OCE), a general class of risk measures. We consider two formulations: dynamic-OCE RL, which applies OCE recursively at each step, and static-OCE RL, which applies a single OCE to the cumulative rewards. Under the tabular setting, we develop pessimistic value-iteration algorithms for both formulations and establish tight sublinear suboptimality bounds, explicitly capturing how risk sensitivity, encoded by utility functions, affects learning difficulty. Moreover, we establish minimax suboptimality lower bounds to characterize the problem's fundamental limits. To handle large state spaces, we further develop pessimistic least-squares value-iteration algorithms that incorporate the general OCE risk criterion into linear function approximation. We establish utility-dependent sublinear guarantees with explicit dependence on the feature dimension $d$. To our knowledge, we provide the first offline algorithms along with the first upper and lower suboptimality bounds for both dynamic- and static-OCE RL.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Distill to Think, Foresee to Act: Cognitive-Physical Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Driving
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Yang Wu, Qiang Meng, Zhaojiang Liu, Youquan Liu, Jian Yang
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: The CoPhy framework enhances autonomous driving by integrating cognitive understanding and foresight through a dual-reward reinforcement learning approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance and improved safety.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Current end-to-end autonomous driving models are fundamentally constrained by the behavioral cloning ceiling of imitation learning. While reinforcement learning offers a path to smarter autonomy, it demands two missing pieces of infrastructure: (1) a cognitive foundation that understands traffic semantics and driving intent, and (2) a foresighted physical environment that can anticipate the consequences of candidate actions. To this end, we propose CoPhy, a CognitivePhysical reinforcement learning framework for autonomous driving. To distill to think, we distill VLM knowledge into the BEV encoder and then discard the VLM entirely, retaining cognitive ability at zero inference cost while releasing the cognitive channel as a pluggable interface for optional human language commands. To foresee to act, we build an auto-regressive BEV world model that explicitly predicts future semantic maps conditioned on candidate actions, serving as an interpretable physical sandbox from which safety metrics are directly derived. Built upon this dual infrastructure, we optimize the driving policy via GRPO with a novel dual-reward mechanism: a physical reward derived from BEV rollouts enforces hard safety constraints, while a cognitive reward from a language-aligned scorer ensures intent compliance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CoPhy not only achieves state-of-the-art results on NAVSIM v1 and v2 benchmarks, but also enables safer driving via cognitively informed scene compliance and flexible intent control through user-defined language instructions. Project page: https://wuyang98.github.io/CoPhy/.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Synapse-Control: Making Agent Experience Actionable with Lightweight Runtime Control
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Zhiyuan Huang, Shengan Zheng, Chenghu Yang, Song Zhang, Lingyun Li
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: Synapse-Control enhances agent performance by efficiently selecting and scoring advice with a lightweight classifier, significantly reducing inference costs and improving task success rates.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Large language model agents reuse execution experience to improve reliability on complex tool-based tasks. Systems such as Sentry call large models to generate failure diagnoses before retrieving advice, adding inference cost to experience reuse. We present Synapse-Control, an agent runtime whose lightweight control plane selects advice and determines when to send it to the task-executing model. Rules shortlist relevant advice, and a lightweight 1.7B classifier fine-tuned on teacher-labeled state-suggestion pairs scores those candidates instead of generating a diagnosis. Micro-contracts encode reusable interface checks, such as required arguments or valid options, without prescribing complete task programs. A Prompt Value Table records earlier guidance and feedback to limit repeated suggestions through cooldown and token-budget checks. Across 1,308 attempts per method in AppWorld and WebShop, Synapse-Control achieves 270 successes (29.8% more than Base), replaces 4,987 generative diagnosis calls, and reduces auxiliary control time relative to Sentry by 50.2% and 51.0%, respectively.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: ForeseeDrive: Future-Token Conditioning for Anticipatory Generative Driving
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Shaokai Wu, Xunchu Zhou, Pinzhi Wang, Bo Dong, Yuting Hu
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: ForeseeDrive introduces a future-token conditioning method for generative driving planners, enhancing candidate generation and safety through predictive tokenization and reduced drift.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Generative driving planners can represent diverse ego futures, but a downstream scorer can choose only among sampled candidates; it cannot recover an absent maneuver. We present ForeseeDrive, which turns future scene evolution into a deployable interface for shaping candidate generation. Rather than reconstructing dense future states or scoring a fixed menu, ForeseeDrive derives query-indexed tokens from logged actor motion, occupancy evolution, route interactions, and TTC margins, and predicts the same token space from present context at deployment. The tokens condition trajectory geometry before candidates materialize. A zero-token-gated residual path and candidate-preservation loss limit unnecessary drift, while a TTC-margin guard targets brittle safe-to-unsafe boundary crossings. Under their respective benchmark protocols, ForeseeDrive reaches 89.2 PDMS on NAVSIM navtest, 0.41\,m average L2 and 0.05\% collision rate on nuScenes validation, and a 76.50 driving score on Bench2Drive. Controlled DiffusionDrive/NAVSIM diagnostics show an exact zero-token no-op, a small aligned-over-shuffled selected-PDM advantage under preservation, mixed oracle-best quality, and localized TTC-boundary failures. Together, the benchmark results and bounded mechanism tests support future-conditioned generation as a practical interface for anticipation. Code is included in the supplementary materials.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Embodied Science Agents: Making Embodied Experimental Design Learnable
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Yihang Che, Zhongwei Yu, Yang Li, Xingyu Lu, Hongxia Yu
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: The paper presents the Embodied Science Agent (ESA), integrating cognitive, experimental, and embodied learnability to enhance autonomous scientific discovery in self-driving laboratories.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Recent advances in large models have accelerated AI for Science toward agentic science, where AI agents autonomously conduct scientific discovery. Realising this vision requires closing the loop between computational reasoning and physical experimentation, positioning self-driving laboratories (SDLs) as critical enablers. However, existing SDLs exhibit a fundamental paradox: foundation model integration has increased linguistic sophistication while severing physical grounding. By treating models as disembodied planners that output symbolic workflows for separate robotic systems, current architectures inherently block the development of embodied experimental intuition. We argue that overcoming this paradox requires embedding \emph{learnability} along three interdependent axes: cognitive learnability (learning what to investigate), experimental learnability (learning where to search), and embodied learnability (learning how to act). Building on this view, we introduce the Embodied Science Agent (ESA), which unifies digital intelligence with physical embodiment through three synergistic components: a Digital Agent that provides cognitive and experimental learnability via memory-based reasoning and Bayesian optimisation, an Embodied Agent that provides embodied learnability via generalisable instrument control, and an Embodied Unified Interface for seamless coordination. We validated ESA in autonomous wastewater treatment experiments, navigating over 200 million possible conditions. Through 15 continuous rounds, ESA raised the final solution transmittance from 82\% to 99.7\%, corresponding to a 98.5\% reduction in residual dye concentration and near-complete decolourisation, while its learned visuomotor policies generalised across varying instrument placements, a promising step toward next-generation SDLs for autonomous scientific discovery.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: LSRP*: Scalable and Anytime Planning for Multi-Agent Path Finding with Asynchronous Actions
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Dachuan Liu, Shuai Zhou, Shizhe Zhao, Zhongqiang Ren
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: LSRP* is an improved anytime planner for Multi-Agent Path Finding that enhances solution quality and scalability, accommodating more agents and reducing costs compared to LSRP.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) seeks collision-free paths for multiple agents from their respective starting locations to their respective goal locations while minimizing path costs. Although many MAPF algorithms were developed, most of them rely on a common assumption on synchronized actions, where the actions of all agents start at the same time and always take a time unit. This assumption may limit the use of MAPF planners in practice. To get rid of this assumption, recently, an algorithm called Loosely Synchronized Rule-based Planning (LSRP) was proposed, which can find sub-optimal solutions for many agents. However, LSRP often finds poor quality solutions due to its unbounded sub-optimality. This paper develops a new anytime planner called LSRP* that can keep improving solution quality after the initial solution is obtained until the runtime budget depletes. We analyze the properties of LSRP* and test it against several baselines with up to 1000 agents on various maps. LSRP* can handle up to 25% more agents than LSRP and can reduce up to 40% of the solution cost found by LSRP.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Tac-DINO: Learning Tactile Features with Patch Alignment
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Hong Li, Yankang Dong, Yue Xu, Yihan Tang, Jiamin Qiu
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: Tac-DINO introduces a novel dataset and learning framework that enhances tactile perception in robotic manipulation through improved patch-level alignment and geometric supervision.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Multisensory perception is essential for robotic manipulation, with tactile sensing providing critical information for fine-grained, contact-rich interactions. Although prior work integrates tactile and spatial signals to improve perception, vision-tactile learning commonly relies on object-level alignment. Addressing this limitation requires systematically aligned 3D vision-tactile data. We develop a data collection system and introduce Touch3D, a dataset comprising 505 real-world objects and 20,025 tactile contacts. Building on this dataset, we establish the Contact-Centric Multimodal Tactile Representation Benchmark (CoMT-Bench), which expands evaluation from object-level retrieval and tactile properties to include patch-level contact evaluation. We further propose Geometry-Relation Distilled Tactile-Centric Cross-Modal Learning (GeoTAC), which explores tactile learning across all multisensory data. In experiments on the Touch3D test set, patch-level alignment improves the average score by 5.32 over object-level alignment, with GeoTAC's geometric supervision improving it by a further 4.48. In robotic manipulation, GeoTAC improves TP by 19.14 and 11.34 over DINOv2 (Vision-only) and DINOv2 (Vision-Tactile), respectively. Project page: https://lihongcs.github.io/tacdino.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: WARP-JEPA: World-Model-in-the-Loop Amortized Rollout Planning for Frozen Hierarchical Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Junjie Li, Zhaojiacheng Zhou, Kaixiang Wang, Zihan Wang, QingSong Zhao
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: WARP-JEPA enhances long-horizon visual control by replacing costly gradient descent with efficient learned trajectory proposers, achieving significant speed and success improvements in planning.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Hierarchical Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (H-JEPA) enable long-horizon visual control but rely on costly test-time gradient descent for planning. Our analysis reveals that iterative optimization consumes up to 97.7% of episode runtime and that low predicted rollout costs do not necessarily translate into successful control. We further identify a planning-horizon asymmetry between long-horizon top-level composition and short two-step subordinate planning. To address these challenges, we propose WARP-JEPA, a hierarchical amortized planning framework that replaces online gradient optimization with learned multi-candidate trajectory proposers while keeping the world models frozen. WARP-JEPA combines a lightweight world-model-in-the-loop causal Transformer at the top level with parallel residual MLPs at subordinate levels. The proposers are trained using model-based rollout costs and best-of-K behavior cloning, enabling efficient candidate selection without test-time gradient optimization. Across 30 frozen H-JEPA models on four benchmarks, WARP-JEPA achieves 9.6-18.8x faster episode inference on long-horizon tasks (2.9-3.0x on Cube) and improves task success by up to 33.3 percentage points. These results demonstrate that amortized planning can substantially improve both inference efficiency and control performance without retraining the world models. Code is available at https://github.com/hideinsewer/WARP-JEPA.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Efficient VLA Inference via Retrieval-Based Speculation and Hardware Acceleration
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Zhengyang Cheng, He Zhu, Zeyu Guo, Zihan Liu, Anbang Wu
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: Zora is a hardware-software framework that accelerates vision-language-action inference by utilizing a lightweight retrieval model and optimizing action verification, achieving significant speedups on edge platforms.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to understand and execute complex instructions, but their autoregressive (AR) action generation introduces significant latency on resource-constrained robotic platforms. Speculative decoding can accelerate AR-based inference by parallelizing action generation and verification; however, existing approaches rely on costly draft models, which are inefficient on edge platforms. In this paper, we propose Zora, a hardware-software co-design framework for accelerating AR-based VLA inference. Specifically, Zora introduces a lightweight retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-based draft model that exploits robotic dynamics without additional neural draft models. We further reduce batch verification overhead through a kinematics-guided action-acceptance strategy and a KV-cache-sharing attention mechanism. To address the retrieval overhead introduced by RAG-based drafting, we co-design dedicated hardware support, Zora core, to address the memory irregularity in RAG-based drafting. We evaluate Zora on four VLA models with the LIBERO benchmark. Zora retains comparable accuracy while achieving up to 3.4$\times$ speedup with software-only optimization and up to 7.6$\times$ speedup with hardware support over GPUs.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Review the Episodes, Refine the Lessons: Simple Memory Evolution for Embodied Agents
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Yifei Yao, Yude Zou, Xing Gao, Guanbo Jiao, Yukai Wang
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: The paper introduces SimplEvo, a memory evolution framework for embodied agents that enhances performance without weight updates, achieving significant success rate improvements in task execution.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Recent studies of embodied agents based on frontier multimodal large language models (MLLMs) develop harness engineering around the MLLM, such as harnesses with post-trained policies and recursive self-improvement loops. Yet whether these additions exceed the native capability of the MLLM remains unexplored. We introduce SimplEvo to explore how far an MLLM can improve under direct control when it retains its execution experience in self-written text memories. It requires no weight updates, post-trained policies, or privileged information. The MLLM writes a coordinate-free task memory once from a single demonstration. Under a strict train-test protocol, it then creates a bounded working memory on training episodes only and refines it after each episode with lessons on procedure, completion, and recovery. Both memories stay fixed at test time. On EBench, SimplEvo lifts the success rate (SR) of GPT-6-Astra under direct control from 46.7% to 81.7%, and tops the RoboDojo leaderboard with 69.63% SR and a score of 75.32. Compared with memories that also store past visual frames, SimplEvo reaches a similar SR with text memory alone while using fewer tokens. With its memories fixed, SimplEvo also generalizes to unseen layouts and randomized scene configurations. Moreover, the working memory transfers across models: written by GPT-6-Astra, it can be reused as is by weaker MLLMs and improve their performance without any adaptation of their own.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: InfCoiL: Coordinated Planner-Controller Learning for Closed-Loop Physics-Based Human-Object Interaction
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Yude Zou, Yifei Yao, Yiwei Hao, Hanqing Wang, Xing Gao
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: InfCoiL introduces a closed-loop framework for human-object interaction that integrates a morphology-aware planner and a multi-morphology controller, enhancing performance through coordinated learning and reinforcement.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Text- and goal-conditioned human-object interaction (HOI) provides an intuitive interface for specifying high-level intents in physics-based character animation. Mapping such intents to physically plausible, contact-rich behaviors naturally calls for a generative planner and a physics-based controller, yet existing planner-controller systems either execute plans open-loop or close the loop while keeping the planner fixed, so execution feedback never reshapes what is planned. We present InfCoiL, a closed-loop framework for physics-based HOI from coordinated planner-controller learning. InfCoiL couples a morphology-aware flow-matching planner with a unified multi-morphology controller through a shared morphology interface in an autoregressive plan-and-execute loop, and alternately fine-tunes both components with reinforcement learning from the same physical rollouts. To optimize the flow-matching planner online, we introduce Semantic Flow Policy Optimization (SFPO), which stochasticizes selected denoising transitions with channel-wise semantic covariance over heterogeneous HOI features and assigns group-relative, sequence-level rewards from complete closed-loop executions. On held-out OMOMO sequences, InfCoiL outperforms open-loop hierarchical baselines in goal-reaching task success and physical tracking accuracy. Project page: https://infcoil.github.io/

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Towards Rotation-Only Imaging Geometry: Multi-View Pose Estimation
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Xinrui Li, Qi Cai, Yuanxin Wu
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: The paper presents GRAM and MORE, novel methods for estimating global rotations and translations in multi-view pose estimation by minimizing rotation-only algebraic residuals, enhancing accuracy and efficiency.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Global structure-from-motion (SfM) commonly refines relative poses on individual image pairs and then estimates global rotations by rotation averaging. Pairwise refinement does not explicitly combine feature-level constraints with multi-view consistency during rotation initialization. We introduce Global Rotations from Aggregated Matches (GRAM), which estimates global rotations directly from initial relative rotations and inlier matches by minimizing edge-wise rotation-only algebraic residuals. GRAM replaces two-view relative-pose optimization and rotation averaging with a single stage. We further extend rotation- only imaging geometry to multiple views and develop Multi-view Optimization with Rotation-only Reprojection Error (MORE) for nonlinear global rotation refinement. Analytical Rotation-guided Translation (ART) derives locally scaled triplet translations from Linear Global Translation (LiGT) constraints and recovers global translations using weighted least squares. Synthetic and real-world experiments demonstrate the accuracy, robustness, and efficiency of the proposed methods.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: MotionCore: A Latent Neural Simulator for Video Generation with Rigid-Body Dynamics
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Zheng Wang, Zhengwei Gong, Yuanzhi Liang, Haibin Huang, Chi Zhang
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: MotionCore is a latent neural simulator that enhances video generation by integrating learned rigid-body dynamics with visual modeling for improved physical consistency and trajectory fidelity.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Video generation models can produce highly realistic videos while generating physically inconsistent object motion. This limitation suggests that visual modeling alone may not provide a transferable representation of physical dynamics. We introduce MotionCore, a framework for learning physical dynamics via a learnable partial differential equation solver and focuses on rigid-body motion. We introduce a latent neural simulator learning to predict the evolution of object-level physical states from observed motion. Its predictions are then converted into spatially aligned latent controls for a controllable video diffusion model. The generator serves as a visual interface: it provides appearance and scene detail, while the learned dynamics model specifies the physical trajectory. To preserve this trajectory through the interface, MotionCore combines a diffusion-matching objective with a low-capacity decodability constraint on object identity and position. We evaluate MotionCore on public physical-consistency benchmarks and on paired data with known trajectories. Results indicate that MotionCore improves physical consistency and trajectory obedience in the evaluated rigid-body settings, while maintaining comparable visual quality. A controlled ablation protocol compares learned dynamics with an analytic prior and studies the choice of latent evolution processor.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: SWAM: Scaling World Action Models with Cross-Modal Alignment
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Yu Zhou, Xinyuan Xia, Xuankun Yang, Yinghao Yang, Wendi Chen
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: The SWAM paper presents a scalable world action model that enhances language-video-action alignment through extensive data curation and optimized training strategies, achieving significant performance improvements in real-world tasks.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: World action models jointly predict video and actions conditioned on language. Existing studies focus primarily on architectures and training mechanisms, typically treating language-video alignment acquired through video pretraining as an established foundation. However, introducing action learning may impair this alignment. Principled guidance on data and supervision design for maintaining language-video alignment during action learning remains limited. To investigate this, we curate a pool of approximately 47,000 hours of general videos, egocentric videos, UMI demonstrations, and robot demonstrations. Building on this, we systematically study how language-video supervision, language-video-action supervision, and the joint use of these two forms affect WAM performance. In particular, we examine how language annotation quality affects pretrained language-video capabilities, and how action supervision from UMI and robot demonstrations extends these capabilities to language-video-action modeling. To better scale the model, we further conduct detailed studies on joint training recipe and model architecture. Under a fixed training budget, mixing egocentric videos and UMI demonstrations improves control generalization. Model architecture affects how effectively these experiences are used, while scaling pretraining under the selected configuration brings further gains. The resulting recipe, post-trained on RoboTwin Clean demonstrations only, achieves success rates of 88.10% and 61.56% under Easy (Clean-to-Clean) and Hard (Clean-to-Random) conditions, respectively. Our model achieves 40.00% SR across three real-world tasks, compared with 23.33% for the strongest baseline, indicating better generalization under unseen conditions. We release the curated data, training code, and model weights.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: HuMI: Humanoid Whole-Body Manipulation from Humanoid-Free Demonstrations
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Ruiqian Nai, Boyuan Zheng, Junming Zhao, Haodong Zhu, Sicong Dai
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: HuMI is a portable framework that enhances humanoid whole-body manipulation by efficiently learning from humanoid-free demonstrations, achieving significant improvements in data collection and task success rates.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Current approaches for humanoid whole-body manipulation, primarily relying on teleoperation or visual sim-to-real reinforcement learning, are hindered by hardware logistics and complex reward engineering. Consequently, demonstrated autonomous skills remain limited and are typically restricted to controlled environments. In this paper, we present the Humanoid Manipulation Interface (HuMI), a portable and efficient framework for learning diverse whole-body manipulation tasks across various environments. HuMI enables humanoid-free data collection by capturing rich whole-body motion using portable hardware. This data drives a hierarchical learning pipeline that translates human motions into dexterous and feasible humanoid skills. Extensive experiments across five whole-body tasks--including kneeling, squatting, tossing, walking, and bimanual manipulation--demonstrate that HuMI achieves a 3x increase in data collection efficiency compared to teleoperation and attains a 70% success rate in unseen environments.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: DAPointRWKV: Domain Adaptive Vision RWKV for Point Cloud Completion
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Yinghui Li, Qianyu Zhou, Hao Yang, Richard Dazeley, Ye Zhu
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: DAPointRWKV introduces a novel RWKV-based framework for domain adaptive point cloud completion, addressing geometric discrepancies and enhancing performance through geometry-aware learning and structural regularization.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Domain adaptive point cloud completion (DA PCC) aims to bridge the geometric discrepancy between labeled source domains and unlabeled target domains for accurate 3D shape completion. Existing methods based on CNNs, Transformers, and Mamba-like sequence models still face challenges from limited receptive fields, high computational complexity, insufficient geometric bias, and serialization sensitivity. Recently, Receptance Weighted Key Value (RWKV) provides a linear-complexity alternative for long-range sequence modeling. However, adapting RWKV to DA PCC remains challenging due to the lack of explicit geometric priors, the mismatch between recurrent modeling and coarse-to-fine generation, and unstable target-domain adaptation. To address these challenges, we propose DAPointRWKV, a novel RWKV-based framework for DA PCC. DAPointRWKV consists of three components: Geometry-Aware RWKV (GA-RWKV) Backbone, RWKV-Oriented Progressive Decoder (RWKV-PD), and Dual Structural Regularization (DSR). Specifically, GA-RWKV introduces geometry-aware recurrent representation learning, RWKV-PD bridges RWKV token representations with coarse-to-fine reconstruction through local token-guided refinement, and DSR stabilizes target-domain transfer through visible-structure anchoring and complete-shape hypothesis stabilization. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmarks demonstrate that DAPointRWKV consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Beyond Action Residuals: Real-World Robot Policy Steering via Bottleneck Latent Reinforcement Learning
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Dongjie Yu, Kun Lei, Zhennan Jiang, Jia Pan, Huazhe Xu
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: The paper presents Z-Perturbation Reinforcement Learning (ZPRL), which enhances pretrained robot policies through a compact bottleneck latent interface, improving adaptation and performance in real-world tasks.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Pretrained imitation policies have become a strong foundation for robot manipulation, but online adaptation can further improve policy performance within their pretrained behavioral support. A central question is therefore how reinforcement learning (RL) should adapt policies after offline pretraining. Existing lightweight methods commonly apply residual corrections directly in action space. We investigate how the steering interface affects online RL. In this work, we propose Z-Perturbation Reinforcement Learning (ZPRL), an approach that steers pretrained policies through a compact bottleneck latent rather than through policy weights or output actions. Building on an offline-learned bottleneck policy interface introduced by previous work, ZPRL turns this representation into an online RL control space through reward-driven residual perturbations while freezing the pretrained policy. We instantiate ZPRL on flow-matching policies and evaluate it on eight simulation tasks and four real-world tasks. Across diverse manipulation settings, ZPRL improves sample efficiency with competitive or better final performance. In the real world, ZPRL improves the average success rate on four tasks by 33.7 percentage points over imitation base policies. Our qualitative and quantitative results also indicate that ZPRL combines task success with smooth actions without explicit temporal filtering or smoothness regularization. These results suggest that a compact, task-aligned bottleneck latent provides an effective interface for online RL adaptation. Videos and code can be found at https://manutdmoon.github.io/ZPRL/.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: AetheRock: An Arm-Worn Robot Teaching System for Force-Guided Vision-Tactile Learning
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Hong Li, Yue Xu, Yihan Tang, Yankang Dong, Chenyuan Liu
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: AetheRock is an arm-worn robot system that enhances force-guided vision-tactile learning through improved sensor integration and a novel multimodal representation framework.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Force and tactile sensing are essential for contact-rich manipulation, but their integration into handheld or wearable devices is constrained by cost, size, and mechanical compatibility. Tactile signals are also sensitive to manufacturing variations and wear during use, posing further challenges to policy learning. To address these hardware and learning challenges, we introduce AetheRock, an arm-worn device for collecting gripper-force, visual, and tactile data. AetheRock incorporates GelSlim-Mini, our improved version of GelSlim 4.0 designed for low-cost, easy manufacturing, at the gripper fingertip, together with a resistive pressure sensor at the human finger contact area. To learn robust representations from the collected data, we propose ForceVT, a framework that aligns multimodal representations and uses force and vision to guide tactile learning, mitigating the effects of manufacturing variations and sensor degradation. Real-world experiments demonstrate efficient data collection with AetheRock. ForceVT improves average performance by 13% over the vision-tactile baseline and maintains an average task progress of 55.0% under reduced tactile fidelity, compared with 58.0% at full fidelity. Project page: https://lihongcs.github.io/aetherock.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: SurgTAP-3D: A Large-Scale Cross-Surgery Video Dataset with Contact-Aware 3D Motion Tracking
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Jiaxin Guo, Wenzhen Dong, Taoyu Wu, Haomin Kuang, Mengya Xu
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: SurgTAP-3D is a comprehensive dataset for 3D motion tracking in minimally invasive surgery, addressing tool-tissue interactions and enhancing autonomous surgical system development.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Understanding 3D scene dynamics in minimally invasive surgery (MIS) is a fundamental step toward physically intelligent and autonomous surgical systems. However, existing public datasets offer limited scalability and diversity in real-world clinical scenarios. Moreover, annotations typically focus on either tissue or instruments alone, overlooking tool-tissue interactions. This gap limits applications such as augmented reality guidance and autonomous surgery driven by vision-language-action (VLA) models or world models, which demand large-scale, high-quality 3D supervision. In this work, we construct SurgTAP-3D, a large-scale in-vivo pseudo-3D surgical motion tracking dataset and benchmark, comprising 520K frames, 4,549 action clips, and 1.4M 2D/3D point trajectories from diverse robotic and manual procedures under unified action categories. To make annotation scalable, we design a unified framework for surgical 3D point tracking that converts uncalibrated monocular surgical videos into structured 4D annotations through contact-region prompting, active-tool segmentation, dynamic bundle adjustment, and global 4D refinement. This pipeline adapts foundation priors to surgical videos and produces temporally consistent trajectories, pseudo-scale geometry, camera poses, and instrument masks. The dataset captures realistic challenges inherent to surgical environments, including occlusions, smoke, bleeding, and rapid instrument motion. We establish a comprehensive benchmark on SurgPose, SurgT, and STIR, covering both instrument and tissue tracking. We demonstrate instrument displacement estimation, deformable surface reconstruction, and foundation-model fine-tuning. Extensive experiments and analysis demonstrate the effectiveness of our dataset and annotation framework for 3D surgical point tracking, reconstruction, and surgical action understanding. Homepage: https://wrld.github.io/surgtap-3d/

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: VTAM: Efficient Visuo-Tactile World-Action Models for Contact-Rich Manipulation without Tactile Pretraining
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Haoran Yuan, Weigang Yi, Zhenyu Zhang, Wendi Chen, Yuchen Mo
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: VTAM is an efficient visuo-tactile world-action model for contact-rich manipulation that eliminates the need for tactile pretraining while achieving superior performance and reduced inference latency.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Tactile vision-language-action models (VLAs) and tactile world-action models (WAMs) are a promising new paradigm for contact-rich manipulation, but existing models either underutilize touch, rely on large-scale tactile pretraining, or incur high inference latency due to iterative video generation. We present VTAM, an efficient visuo-tactile world-action model for contact-rich manipulation that requires no tactile or action pretraining. RGB and tactile observations share a frozen video VAE and the pretrained video transformer weights. VTAM first adapts the video backbone to jointly predict future visual and tactile latents, then fine-tunes it end-to-end with a randomly initialized action expert that predicts actions, proprioceptive states, and a light flow-force proxy computed from tactile optical flow. Trained only on task demonstrations, VTAM outperforms all baselines on four real-robot tasks across two platforms with different tactile sensors, outperforms all baselines without tactile pretraining in average success on eight UniVTAC simulation tasks, and is comparable to tactile VLAs and WAMs pretrained on over 30K hours of largely visuo-tactile robot data (83.4% vs. 84.5% for N0-TWAM). Without full video denoising at inference, VTAM is approximately 6x and 16x faster than N0-TWAM and LingBot-VA without compilation, with compiled latency comparable to Fast-WAM. Ablations show that feeding frozen-VAE tactile features directly to the action expert, bypassing tactile world modeling, fails on every tested task, that Stage I visuo-tactile world-model fine-tuning improves UniVTAC success on most tasks, and that flow-force proxy keeps the policy from fully ignoring touch. The tactile encoder transfers zero-shot across GelSight Mini and Xense Photon sensors.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: MetricTrail: Revisiting the Power of Metric Depth and Local Optimization for Long-Sequence Streaming 3D Reconstruction
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Jingnan Gao, Jiahui Huang, Sven Elflein, Jianhao Zheng, Bingxin Ke
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: MetricTrail is a streaming 3D reconstruction system that enhances camera motion estimation and dense reconstruction from long monocular videos using single-image metric depth and efficient local optimization.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: We present MetricTrail, a streaming system for accurate camera motion estimation and dense reconstruction from long monocular videos. To keep inference efficient over long sequences, we revisit DPVO's sparse local estimator. We find that single-image metric depth substantially improves its trajectory accuracy, without retraining the correspondence network or enlarging the optimization window. Metric predictions initialize patch depths and remain as soft constraints during optimization. We further improve correspondence estimation through learned adapters that augment matching features and recurrent context with frozen DINOv3 representations. The correspondence estimator and adapters are trained on diverse short clips without additional long-sequence training. This modular design also allows the depth provider to be independently upgraded and supports supplied camera intrinsics and calibrated stereo observations without retraining. Under the reported RGB-only protocols, MetricTrail achieves the lowest average trajectory error among evaluated methods on KITTI, Oxford Spires, and VBR. Pairing the estimated poses with single-image depth predictions also produces strong dense reconstruction on indoor and outdoor benchmarks and coherent reconstructions of in-the-wild videos. With supplied intrinsics, the system processes KITTI-02 at 12.70 FPS with 3.21 GB peak GPU memory.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: AnyDexRT: Calibration-Efficient Dexterous Hand Retargeting with Few-Shot Human Guidance
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Chenxi Wang, Ying Feng, Hongjie Fang, Shangning Xia, Lixin Yang
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: AnyDexRT enhances dexterous robotic hand teleoperation by improving retargeting efficiency and intuitiveness through self-supervised learning and few-shot human guidance, minimizing manual calibration.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Teleoperation is a key interface for controlling dexterous robotic hands and collecting demonstrations for imitation learning. Its effectiveness largely depends on kinematic retargeting, which maps operator hand motions to feasible and intuitive robot hand motions. Existing methods often require hand-crafted objectives, precise calibration, or global shape matching between human and robot hand spaces, making them sensitive to hand-specific tuning and less reliable across different dexterous hands. We propose AnyDexRT, a calibration-efficient retargeting method for intuitive dexterous teleoperation across human-like dexterous hands. AnyDexRT combines self-supervised fingertip correspondence learning with few-shot human guidance to anchor the mapping in task-relevant regions, and further refines pinch-related poses using a contact classifier. Experiments on diverse dexterous hands and real-world teleoperation tasks show that AnyDexRT improves retargeting quality, reduces manual tuning, and provides more intuitive and efficient control than prior retargeting methods. Project website: https://chenxi-wang.github.io/projects/anydexrt

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: WorldAct: Activating Monolithic 3D Worlds into Interactive-Ready Object-Centric Scenes
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Jichen Hu, Jiawei Guo, Jiazhong Cen, Chen Yang, Sikuang Li
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: WorldAct transforms static 3D worlds into editable, interactive scenes by decomposing them into actionable objects and enhancing them with geometrically aligned meshes and inpainting.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Recent 3D world modeling systems based on generative scene synthesis, such as Marble, can create coherent and explorable 3D environments, yet their outputs are typically static monolithic assets with limited editability and physical interaction. This restricts their use in immersive content creation and embodied simulation, where generated worlds must be actively modified and manipulated. To tackle this challenge, we present WorldAct, a framework that converts static generated 3D worlds into editable and interaction-ready scenes. WorldAct uses a multimodal agent to guide scene decomposition, identify actionable objects, reconstruct geometrically aligned object-level meshes for interaction, and restore the residual background via 3D inpainting. The resulting scenes support object-level editing, collision-aware manipulation, and embodied task execution while preserving global scene coherence. Experiments show that WorldAct enables richer interaction scenarios than the original generated scenes, suggesting a practical path toward editable and interactive 3D world models. Project page: https://sjtu-deepvisionlab.github.io/WorldAct

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: DenseReward: Dense Reward Learning via Failure Synthesis for Robotic Manipulation
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Yu Fang, Wanxi Dong, Jiaqi Liu, Yue Yang, Mingxiao Huo
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: DenseReward introduces a novel framework for generating diverse failure data and providing dense, frame-level rewards in robotic manipulation, enhancing reinforcement learning efficiency.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning holds great promise for improving robot policies beyond the limits of imitation learning. However, its practical adoption remains bottlenecked by the lack of reliable vision-language reward models that provide dense and informative feedback. Two key challenges remain: acquiring diverse failure data at scale and obtaining fine-grained reward signals beyond sparse trajectory-level success labels. Existing approaches reuse successful trajectories to construct negative or suboptimal examples through trajectory truncation, instruction relabeling, or trajectory comparisons, without generating new trajectories where physical interaction failures such as collisions, missed grasps, object drops, and recovery actually occur. Meanwhile, many existing reward models predict sparse binary or trajectory-level rewards, which provide limited guidance for efficient policy optimization. We introduce DenseReward, a dense robotic reward model that addresses both challenges. To train DenseReward, we develop an automated failure data generation pipeline that synthesizes physically realistic failure trajectories in simulation without manual annotation, covering diverse failure modes such as collisions, missed grasps, object drops, and recovery behaviors. DenseReward predicts dense frame-level reward scores from visual observations and language instructions, enabling fine-grained estimation of task progress throughout an episode. Experiments show that DenseReward outperforms general-purpose VLMs and existing robotic reward models in dense reward prediction across both simulated and real-world manipulation. We further demonstrate that DenseReward provides effective reward guidance for downstream model predictive control and reinforcement learning.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: OmniOPSD: Rationale-Privileged On-Policy Self-Distillation for Affective Computing
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Zebang Cheng, Shuimu Chen, Boxue Yang, Yuanshen Guan, Jingyi Chen
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: OmniOPSD introduces a novel on-policy self-distillation framework for multimodal affective reasoning, enhancing generalization through evidence-rich supervision without requiring additional human annotations.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have advanced affective computing by enabling nuanced reasoning over visual, acoustic, and linguistic evidence. A key approach to improving their generalization is outcome-based reinforcement learning, which converts existing label-level annotations into rewards for final-answer correctness. However, its sparse sequence-level supervision provides limited fine-grained guidance for interpreting multimodal affective cues and may reward correct labels even when those cues are misinterpreted. To address this challenge, we introduce OmniOPSD, the first on-policy self-distillation framework for omni-modal affective reasoning. At its core, OmniOPSD transforms label-level supervision into evidence-rich, teacher-only rationales by leveraging reference affective judgments as semantic priors for offline multimodal evidence elicitation from frontier MLLMs. Through rationale-privileged self-distillation, it couples on-policy student rollouts with dense, evidence-informed token-level supervision from a local self-teacher, allowing the student to learn along its own trajectories rather than imitate fixed reasoning traces. This decoupling of offline evidence acquisition from local policy learning enables training without additional human annotation, frontier-model logits, or online frontier-model calls, while preserving student-only inference from the original task input. At both 3B and 7B scales, OmniOPSD outperforms supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and group relative policy optimization (GRPO) in mean macro-F1 on both in-domain and out-of-domain evaluations. Among the compared models, it ranks first by MER-UniBench mean across all three input-modality settings, reaching 84.13 with audio--video--text input, and achieves the highest MME-Emotion recognition score (Rec-S) of 42.4.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: PhySA: Decoupling Aesthetic and Physical Rewards for Humanoid Locomotion
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Yunwan Fu, Sicheng He, Jiageng Mao, Yue Wang
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: PhySA effectively decouples aesthetic and physical rewards in humanoid locomotion, significantly reducing joint acceleration while maintaining independent control over each reward channel.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Humanoid locomotion policies trained without an explicit smoothness objective tend to produce jerky, high-energy gaits that stress actuators. Vision-language models (VLMs) offer an appealing reward source: given a rendered rollout, a VLM returns an aesthetic quality score on [0,10] without task-specific feature engineering. We find, however, that aesthetic preference and physical smoothness point in opposite directions: across four production VLMs, clips with higher joint acceleration receive higher aesthetic scores (mean Pearson r=+0.66). We study PhySA (Physical Smoothness and Aesthetics), which keeps the two on separate, independently removable reward channels: a sparse, asynchronous VLM score and a phase-triggered correction channel that adjusts physical penalty weights from simulator state. Ablations attribute the smoothness gain to the correction channel. On MuJoCo Humanoid-v5 at 2.6M steps, PhySA lowers joint acceleration by 26 to 32% relative to vanilla PPO, Text2Reward, and Eureka (three seeds), at the cost of shorter episodes. In a single extended run it lowers joint acceleration by 59.5% relative to Prompt2Policy, while a three-seed replication shows a smaller, non-significant reduction (7.2%). The gain does not transfer to IsaacLab or the Unitree G1, even after rescaling the smoothness term.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Reinforcement Learning in GUI Agents: A Survey Toward Digital Inhabitants
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Junan Hu, Jian Liu, Jingxiang Lai, Jiarui Hu, Yiwei Sheng
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: This survey explores the integration of reinforcement learning in GUI agents, proposing a taxonomy and roadmap to enhance automation and address challenges in long-horizon tasks.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Graphical User Interface (GUI) agents have emerged as a promising paradigm for intelligent systems that perceive and interact with graphical interfaces visually. Yet supervised fine-tuning alone cannot handle long-horizon credit assignment, distribution shifts, and safe exploration in irreversible environments, making Reinforcement Learning (RL) a central methodology for advancing automation. In this work, we present the first comprehensive overview of the intersection between RL and GUI agents, and examine how this research direction may evolve toward digital inhabitants. We propose a principled taxonomy that organizes existing methods into Offline RL, Online RL, and Hybrid Strategies, and complement it with analyses of reward engineering, data efficiency, and key technical innovations. Our analysis reveals several emerging trends: the tension between reliability and scalability is motivating the adoption of composite, multi-tier reward architectures; GUI I/O latency bottlenecks are accelerating the shift toward world-model-based training, which can yield substantial performance gains; and the spontaneous emergence of System-2-style deliberation suggests that explicit reasoning supervision may not be necessary when sufficiently rich reward signals are available. We distill these findings into a roadmap covering process rewards, continual RL, cognitive architectures, and safe deployment, aiming to guide the next generation of robust GUI automation and its agent-native infrastructure.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: MASBench: Benchmarking LLM-based Multi-Agent Collaboration under Partial Observability
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Qizhi Chu, Zekai Yu, Sijie Wen, Yang Liu, Chen Qian
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: MASBench is a benchmark for evaluating LLM-based multi-agent collaboration under partial observability, featuring structured tasks and metrics to assess collaboration mechanisms.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have progressively evolved into the core of autonomous agents. Building on this progress, LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) coordinate multiple agents into a synergistic team to accomplish complex tasks that exceed the capabilities of individual agents. The effectiveness of such systems depends not only on the agents themselves, but also on how collaboration mechanisms are designed and organized. Note that real-world collaboration is typically partially observable, where each agent can only access partial information about the environment due to physical or privacy-related constraints. However, many existing multi-agent benchmarks assume global observability, and leave limited support for systematically evaluating collaboration mechanisms. To bridge this gap, we introduce MASBench, a multi-agent collaboration benchmark designed under partially observable constraints. It is organized into three progressive task categories: Reasoning, Scheduling, and Game. Through this structure, we progressively evaluate three representative collaboration mechanisms: Protocol, Memory, and Routing. MASBench further provides deterministic evaluation metrics, including performance score, communication cost, and cost effectiveness, to characterize both collaboration outcomes and communication overhead. Experiments across diverse LLM backbones and mechanism configurations offer empirical guidance for effective MAS design. Code is available at: https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/MASBench

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: GREP: Grounding Generated Room Evaluation in Principles
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Mohan Cao, Yongsen Mao, Chucheng Xiang, Zhongyuan Liu, Zhihang Zhong
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: GREP introduces a three-tier evaluation framework for assessing generated room designs, enhancing scene quality through autonomous issue identification and alignment with human-use logic.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Recent LLM-centric advances can generate attractive furnished rooms by selecting and arranging assets. Yet evaluation remains limited to specific perspectives or predefined questions, failing to reflect overall scene quality. To address this pressing need, we introduce GREP. Its core is a focus shift from defining specific questions to establishing a three-tier evaluation philosophy: basic physical validity checks whether a scene obeys physical constraints; visual coherence concerns compatibility in object scale, style, and composition; and, at the highest level, human-use logic requires object arrangements to align with everyday human habits. Guided by these principles, an evaluation agent autonomously and adaptively identifies issues from scene context, gathers evidence, and produces scores and reports. This supports scene-specific issue discovery and reliable judgments. Experiments show that (1) GREP achieves 87% agreement with human majority preferences, substantially outperforming baseline evaluators. (2) GREP reports improve scene quality through refinement, whereas score-only and no-feedback baselines show slight declines. (3) GREP suggests that as planning ability improves, recent models such as GPT-5.6 Sol can move from relying on pipelines and harnesses to challenging their guidance and constraints, but still lack the ability to resolve the resulting conflicts. Stronger models are therefore expected not only to plan well, but also to adapt to external guidance and constraints more flexibly. Project page: https://han-808.github.io/GREP/

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Playing Soccer Like Humans Do: Learning Versatile and Agile Humanoid Soccer via Latent Motion Priors
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Haoyu Shao, Yunshen Wang, Jingze Zhang, Shaohang Zhu, Yong-Lu Li
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: The paper presents "soccerbot," a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that enables humanoid robots to perform versatile, agile soccer skills with human-like motion using latent motion priors.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Humanoid soccer requires a robot to seamlessly combine agile locomotion, ball manipulation, and impact-rich contact dynamics across a continuous, dynamic behavioral spectrum. Yet existing approaches either cover only a limited set of skills, or forego motion priors entirely and produce unnatural behaviors, leaving the combination of a unified skill set and human-like motion quality unaddressed. We present soccerbot, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that resolves both limitations through a structured latent motion prior distilled from large-scale human soccer motion capture data. By constraining policy learning within this dynamically plausible motion manifold, a single skill-conditioned policy naturally learns to perform moving, dribbling, trapping, and kicking in a unified formulation, while inherently producing human-like motion and fluid transitions during commanded skill switching. Augmented by robustness-oriented simulation design, soccerbot transfers zero-shot to the Unitree G1 humanoid robot, demonstrating agile, natural, and robust execution of the full soccer skill repertoire under real-world conditions.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: When Debate Amplifies Risk: Social-Bias Vulnerabilities in Multi-Agent Safety Deliberation
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Qinghua Mao, Xi Lin, Yuxin Qi, Zihao Xu, Jinze Gu
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: This paper reveals that multi-agent debate systems can amplify safety risks due to social biases, proposing RiskTrace-Debias to mitigate these vulnerabilities without retraining.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Retrieval-augmented Web applications increasingly employ multi-agent debate (MAD) to aggregate conflicting, noisy, and heterogeneous information, yet deliberation is fundamentally a social process susceptible to interpersonal dynamics. When retrieved Web sources contain latent hazards alongside safe factual content, social biases such as conformity pressure and authority deference can override evidence-grounded safety boundaries. In this work, we investigate whether the social structure of deliberation can paradoxically amplify latent Web safety risks. We introduce SafeConflict-Bias, a controlled counterfactual diagnostic protocol spanning six core Web risk categories, which holds queries and retrieved evidence strictly invariant while isolating conversational majority sway, authority cues, and confidence asymmetry. Empirical evaluation across diverse proprietary and open-source backbones reveals that while isolated models reliably reject unsafe guidance, standard MAD catastrophically capitulates to social pressure---surging unsafe adoption from 0.0\% up to 100.0\% and systematically silencing safe minority evidence. To resolve this systemic fragility without retraining or debate regeneration, we propose RiskTrace-Debias, an inference-time auditing framework uniting evidence-first precommitment, social-metadata masking, and consistency-gated arbitration. RiskTrace-Debias suppresses worst-case unsafe adoption to $\le 2.0\%$ across all architectures without inducing over-refusal, while generating verifiable provenance traces to audit interpersonal manipulation in Web deliberation.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: G$^2$TR: Generation-Guided Visual Token Reduction for Separate-Encoder Unified Multimodal Models
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Junxian Li, Kai Liu, Zizhong Ding, Zhixin Wang, Zhikai Chen
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: G$^2$TR is a training-free framework that reduces visual tokens in separate-encoder unified multimodal models, enhancing efficiency while preserving reasoning accuracy and editing quality.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: The development of separate-encoder Unified multimodal models (UMMs) comes with a rapidly growing inference cost due to dense visual token processing. In this paper, we focus on understanding-side visual token reduction for improving the efficiency of separate-encoder UMMs. While this topic has been widely studied for MLLMs, existing methods typically rely on attention scores, text-image similarity and so on, implicitly assuming that the final objective is discriminative reasoning. This assumption does not hold for UMMs, where understanding-side visual tokens must also preserve the model's capabilities for editing images. We propose G$^2$TR, a generation-guided visual token reduction framework for separate-encoder UMMs. Our key insight is that the generation branch provides a task-agnostic signal for identifying understanding-side visual tokens that are not only semantically relevant but also important for latent-space image reconstruction and generation. G$^2$TR estimates token importance from consistency with VAE latent, performs balanced token selection, and merges redundant tokens into retained representatives to reduce information loss. The method is training-free, plug-and-play, and applied only after the understanding encoding stage, making it compatible with existing UMM inference pipelines. Experiments on image understanding and editing benchmarks show that G$^2$TR substantially reduces visual tokens and prefill computation by 1.94x while maintaining both reasoning accuracy and editing quality, outperforming baselines on almost all benchmarks. Code is at: https://github.com/lijunxian111/G2TR.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: An Axiomatic Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Open Multi-Agent Systems
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Jianhong Wang, Yang Li, Samuel Kaski, Jonathan Lawry
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: This paper presents an axiomatic framework for reinforcement learning in open multi-agent systems, leveraging Shapley axioms to enhance learning efficiency and generalization in ad hoc teamwork scenarios.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Open multi-agent systems, where only a subset of agents are controllable, are central to real-world domains such as smart grids, yet lack a principled foundation for reinforcement learning algorithm design. We study this setting through n-agent ad hoc teamwork (NAHT), a recent framework for learning in open multi-agent environments.
